attorneys.name: Matthew D. Besser
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Discrimination Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Matthew D. Besser is a Principal at Bolek Besser Glesius LLC, where his practice focuses on representing individuals in employment and civil rights cases. Prior to joining the firm, he worked for several years at a large Cleveland law firm representing companies in employment disputes, which helps him offer a unique perspective to individuals with employment law claims. Besser has experience in every aspect of employment law, from negotiation to trial, and then final appellate review.

Besser holds the prestigious “AV Preeminent”® rating from Martindale-Hubbell, reflecting that his peers in the legal community rate him as possessing the highest level of legal skill and ethics. For 2014 and 2015, Ohio Super Lawyers Magazine named him to its list of Cleveland “Super Lawyers” in Employment Law. Before that, the publication named him a “Rising Star” in the field several different times.

Besser is active in the legal community. He is frequently invited by legal groups to speak on employment law topics. He is also a member of the Judicial Selection Committee and the Certified Grievance Committee of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association. In addition, Besser serves a member of the Ohio State Bar Association’s Counsel of Delegates. In 2013, he received the Ohio State Bar Foundation’s Community Service Award for Attorneys 40 & Under in the Cleveland District. Previously, Besser taught appellate advocacy at Case Western Reserve University School of Law.

Besser is a summa cum laude graduate of The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law, where he received awards for the highest grade in Trial Advocacy, Civil Litigation, Disability Discrimination, and Evidence. Immediately after law school, Besser worked as a Law Clerk for the Honorable Richard L. Nygaard on the United States Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Mohammed Bidar
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mohammed J. Bidar, a Shareholder, has substantial experience in all aspects of a sophisticated business practice with a concentration in estate and trust planning, business succession planning, charitable giving, asset protection, and probate and trust administration.

His clients include high net worth individuals, corporate executives, exempt organizations, and closely held businesses and their owners. Areas in which Mo has advised clients include revocable trusts planning to obtain tax advantages, generation skipping trusts, and trusts designed to avoid probate or to provide for management of assets. He also has experience with irrevocable trust and gift planning, including life insurance trusts, grantor retained annuity trusts, qualified personal residence trusts, and sales to intentionally defective grantor trusts.

Mo has helped clients with charitable planning, including organization of tax-exempt entities, creation of charitable remainder and lead trust, and establishing private foundations. He frequently deals with issues related to entity formation and organization of family limited partnerships and limited liability companies, and trusts for S corporation ownership.

Mo is a frequent author and has written articles including: Avoiding Probate - More Important Than Ever, Probate Law Journal of Ohio, March/April 2009; Problem Solved? Title Insurance Coverage for Real Property Transfers, Probate Law Journal of Ohio, January/February 2007; One Step Forward and Two Steps Back? Mortgage Acceleration and Title Insurance Issues in Real Property Transfers, Probate Law Journal of Ohio, January/February 2003; Applying Ohio's New Income Tax on Trusts, Cleveland Bar Journal, November 2002; The Latest Estate Planning Consideration: When Should I Die?, Probate Law Journal of Ohio, November/December 2001; How a QTIP Marital Trust Can Save Ohio Taxes, Probate Law Journal of Ohio, November/December 1999; Time to Face - Estate Planning and Estate Planning 2;Personal Decisions, Family Times of Cleveland, April/May, 1993. Mo is a much sought-after speaker on issues related to estate planning, particularly for physicians and business owners. Some of the organizations Mo has spoken before include physician groups, hospitals, assisted living communities, corporations and professional societies.

He is a member of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association's Estate Planning and Trust Law Section and a member of the Estate Planning Advisory Council for Case Western Reserve University. Mo is also a member of the Estate Planning Council of Cleveland, the FBI Citizen's Academy Foundation, a Life Member of the Judicial Conference of the Eighth Judicial District, and has served on the boards of many corporations and charities.

He received his Juris Doctor degree from Case Western Reserve University School of Law in 1984 and graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Science degree from Case Western Reserve University in 1981.

attorneys.name: Rebecca M. Black
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Green, OH
attorneys.bio:
Rebecca M. Black practices law in the areas of criminal defense, criminal appeals, expungements, family law, and bankruptcy. She earned her law degree from the University of Akron School of Law and excelled in her coursework, achieving the Dean's List and above a 3.0 GPA.

While in law school, she successfully competed for highly selective internships at the U.S. Coast Guard's legal offices in Cleveland, Ohio, and at the Cleveland Clinic's in-house legal department in Beachwood, Ohio. These diverse internships enhanced her research skills and taught her how to learn new areas of law quickly and thoroughly.

Rebecca gained experience in criminal defense work and appellate law during the two years she worked at the Appellate Review Office at the University of Akron School of Law. Her writing skills impressed the supervising attorney so much that she immediately started drafting and researching appeals, which most interns were not assigned to do until their second year of practice at the office.

Rebecca graduated magna cum laude from Ohio University in four years with two degrees: one in English literature and another in journalism. The E.W. Scripps School of Journalism was ranked seventh in the nation by news professionals in 2013. She independently directed and edited 20 student journalists' daily news coverage of city, state, and federal government events as a staff editor at the student-run newspaper at Ohio University.

These experiences trained her to use clear, every-day language to explain complicated situations and events. Rebecca can write compelling motions on your behalf because of her experience writing argumentative scholarly papers. Additionally, she can quickly ascertain the facts of your case because of her experience interviewing people from all walks of life-from public officials and poet laureates to indigent inmates.

With these skills and experiences, Rebecca is able to effectively apply her knowledge of the law to the facts of your case to make the strongest possible arguments on your behalf. She too is known for the kind of compassionate straight talk and tireless advocacy that Attorney Melissa Graham-Hurd has always dedicated to her clients.

Although her education and work experiences have taken her all across Ohio, Rebecca's true home is Summit County. She is a volunteer CASA/GAL (Court Appointed Special Advocate/Guardian Ad Litem) through the Summit County Juvenile Court, where she advocates for the best interests of abused, neglected, or dependent children of Summit County. Rebecca also volunteers with the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) of Summit County.

Rebecca is an active member of the Akron Bar Association and is the Secretary/Treasurer of the New Lawyer's Section, in addition to participating in the Criminal Law section, the Family Law Section, the Bankruptcy & Commercial Law Section, the Solo and Small Firm Practitioners' Section, and the Lawyer's Assistance Committee. She also is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Ohio Women's Bar Association, the Ohio Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the American BarAssociation. Through these organizations, she has developed a wealth of resources and a network of contacts who can contribute their experience and advice to her work on your case.

Rebecca can write compelling motions on your behalf because of her experience writing argumentative scholarly papers. Additionally, she can quickly ascertain the facts of your case because of her experience interviewing people from all walks of life-from public officials and poet laureates to indigent inmates.

With these skills and experiences, Rebecca is able to effectively apply her knowledge of the law to the facts of your case to make the strongest possible arguments on your behalf. She too is known for the kind of compassionate straight talk and tireless advocacy that Attorney Melissa Graham-Hurd has always dedicated to her clients.

Although her education and work experiences have taken her all across Ohio, Rebecca's true home is Summit County. She is a volunteer CASA/GAL (Court Appointed Special Advocate/Guardian Ad Litem) through the Summit County Juvenile Court, where she advocates for the best interests of abused, neglected, or dependent children of Summit County. Rebecca also volunteers with the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) of Summit County.

She also is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Ohio Women's Bar Association, the Ohio Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and the American BarAssociation. Through these organizations, she has developed a wealth of resources and a network of contacts who can contribute their experience and advice to her work on your case.

attorneys.name: David R. Boldt
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning -Wills, Trust, POA's - Elder Law Lawyers in North Royalton, OH
attorneys.bio:
David Boldt co-founded Kirner and Boldt with Paul T. Kirner in 1989 and has been the managing partner ever since. A lifelong Ohio resident, David earned both his undergraduate degree and J.D. from Cleveland State University, graduating from the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law in 1986. Before establishing the firm, he gained valuable experience working at the law offices of Paul W. Cassidy in Parma Heights.

David has been an active member of the legal community since his admission to practice in Ohio in 1986. He served as Trustee and Director of the Parma Bar Association for over 20 years and currently holds the positions of Director and Secretary. Additionally, he is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association and the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association. David’s practice areas include Estate Planning, Business and Real Estate Law, Probate of Estates and Guardianships, and Trust Administration.

Recognized for his high professional achievement and ethical standards, David has received the Martindale-Hubbell peer review AV Preeminent Rating. He is also listed among the Best Cleveland Probate and Estate Planning Attorneys on expertise.com and has been honored with the Parma Bar Association’s Don Reiman Professionalism Award.

Outside the office, David enjoys spending time with his family—his wife Judy and their two sons, Matthew and Michael, both of whom have followed in his footsteps to become attorneys. Matthew recently joined the firm, while Michael resides in Chicago, practicing in the area of intellectual property law. David also enjoys golfing with friends, hiking, and appreciating the Ohio outdoors.

attorneys.name: Matthew Boldt
attorneys.practice_type: Estate & Trust Planning Lawyers in North Royalton, OH
attorneys.bio:
Matthew Boldt, a native of Cleveland, Ohio, received his undergraduate education from Duquesne University with a Bachelor of Science degree in Environmental Science & Management and a Bachelor of Science degree in Biology. Matthew is a distinguished alum of Western Michigan University’s Thomas M. Cooley Law School, graduating Cum Laude. Matthew’s legal background is strong and diverse: he has spent the last decade preparing for his role as an attorney.

As the son of one of Kirner and Boldt’s founding partners, David Boldt, Matthew’s interest in the legal field started early and he spent eight years helping support Kirner and Boldt Co., L.P.A. in areas such as client intake, legal research and document drafting. While earning his Juris Doctor from WMU, Matt picked up considerable experience in mediation from Paula K. Manis of Paula K. Manis PLLC, as well as in civil and domestic litigation and defense at Loomis, Ewert, Parsley, Davis & Gotting, PC, where he worked full-time during law school. He also honed his talents in pretrial and trial advocacy as well as negotiations at the Michigan Trial Skills Academy. Matthew’s extensive background in law has helped to prepare him for the estate and trust planning, estate and trust administration, business law, and civil litigation cases he currently takes on.

Matthew is an active member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association, and the Parma Bar Association. He has been admitted to practice law in both Ohio and South Carolina. He has also been admitted to practice in Federal Court through the Ohio Northern District. When he is outside of the office and professional environment, Matthew loves spending time with his dog Rosie, a sweet Australian Shepard Border Collie mix that he rescued during his time at Duquesne. He also enjoys spending time outdoors attempting to develop his golf game, skiing, fishing, and hiking.

attorneys.name: Edgar Boles
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Claims and Disputes Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Edgar Boles is an accomplished attorney with 42 years of experience in public law and private practice, primarily in the areas of civil litigation and dispute resolution, representing small and medium sized business entities and individuals. Immediately after graduating from Case Western Reserve University's School of Law, Edgar Boles served as a Law Clerk to Judge John V. Corrigan and Judge Thomas J. Parrino on the Eighth Appellate District Court of Appeals of Ohio for Cuyahoga County. Thereafter, he served as an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney in the Civil Division of the Cuyahoga County Prosecutor's Office. Since 1976, Mr. Boles has worked in private practice with law firms in Greater Cleveland before joining Dinn, Hochman & Potter in July 2015. Mr. Boles is experienced in commercial disputes, business torts, shareholder claims and business dissolutions, personal injury claims, employment disputes representing both employers and employees, commercial, business and individual tort claims, and construction, real estate and real property claims and disputes including arbitration. Edgar Boles has experience representing individuals in Estate, Probate and Trust disputes and Domestic Relations matters including divorce, dissolution of marriage and post-decree proceedings. Mr. Boles also has experience in FINRA proceedings representing securities investment claimants and securities industry employment claimants.

attorneys.name: Phyllis G. Bossin
attorneys.firm_name: Phyllis G. Bossin & Associates, A Legal Professional Association
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Phyllis Bossin is a dedicated and passionate family law attorney. She cares deeply about her clients and brings her passion, caring and skill to every case she and her associates handle.

Phyllis knows that the best path to resolution occurs outside of the courtroom where people can control their own outcomes. She brings her experience and expertise to settlement negotiations. When appropriate, Phyllis takes her cases to mediation. As a trained mediator herself, she can apply her expertise to help achieve resolution. Phyllis is also trained in collaborative law, another form of dispute resolution that involves a commitment by the parties to resolve their differences outside of the courtroom. Finally, as a trained arbitrator, Phyllis can serve parties and their counsel by arbitrating and deciding their cases.

However, when reasonable alternative paths to resolution fail, Phyllis is ready to litigate. As an experienced, persuasive, and successful litigator of family law, she brings decades of highly-honed trial skills to bear.

The Practice

Phyllis is the principal and founder of Phyllis G. Bossin and Associates. Her practice includes all aspects of family law, including

Divorce and dissolution of marriage

Marital settlement agreements

Spousal support

Child custody and support

Equitable division of property

Prenuptial and cohabitation agreements

Business valuations

Phyllis drafts highly detailed and nuanced settlement agreements involving complex cases, which may involve intricate business valuations and complicated tax issues. To assist in the resolution of these issues, Phyllis has developed long-standing relationships with highly competent experts in related fields, including forensic accountants and tax and estate planning attorneys, all of whom are ready to provide specialized support whether the case is resolved outside of the courtroom or in litigation.

Ms. Bossin is licensed to practice in the state of Ohio, and admitted to practice in the federal courts of the Southern District of Ohio, the Eastern District of Kentucky, and the United States Supreme Court.

Certification

Phyllis is a certified as a Family Relations Law Specialist by the Ohio State Bar Association.

Organizational Leadership

ACFTL – Phyllis is a Diplomate of The American College of Family Trial Lawyers. The College is a select group of “100” of the top family law trial lawyers from across the United States. Diplomates are chosen based upon their recognized litigation skills and courtroom abilities

AAML – Phyllis is a long-standing fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers and has served as the President of the Ohio Chapter

ABA – As an active member of the American Bar Association, Phyllis has served in many capacities, including

Chair of the Section of Family Law

Member of the Commission on Domestic and Sexual Violence,

Member of The Justice Kennedy Commission on Criminal Justice Reform,

Liaison to the Commission on Women in the Profession

Faculty of the ABA Family Law Section Trial Advocacy Institute, an intensive trial skills program for attorneys

Member of the Section of International Law

Ms. Bossin graduated from the University of Cincinnati, where she received both her undergraduate degree and a master’s degree. She received her law degree from the Salmon P. Chase College of Law.

attorneys.name: Hannah L. Botkin
attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Hannah was born and raised in Columbus, Ohio. She first felt called to pursue the practice of law as a teenager after witnessing her parents spend years and many thousands of dollars dealing with legal matters. This difficult experience inspired her to become a resource for other families struggling to navigate the complicated realities of the legal system in Ohio.

At seventeen, Hannah joined the United States’ ARMY Reserve Officer Training Corps to serve her country and have the opportunity to attend Capital University. She received a Bachelor of Arts degree with honors in 2006, and double majored in both Sociology and Criminology, and minored in Military Science.

Hannah went on to attend Capital University Law School and while taking classes, she signed up for the Adoption Legal Clinic, Foster Youth Legal Clinic, Veteran’s Wills Clinic and Family Advocacy Legal Clinic and spent more than 200 pro bono hours honing her craft working directly with clients in preparation for her future legal career.

She received her Juris Doctorate degree in 2013. Later that same year, she took and passed the Ohio State Bar Exam and was issued her license to practice law by the Supreme Court of the State of Ohio.

In recent years, Hannah has been recognized for her hard work and dedication to the practice of law receiving Capital University Law School’s “Graduate of the Last Decade Award”, Capital University’s “Distinguished Young Alumnus Award”, and the Legal Aid Society of Columbus’ “Expanding Our Impact Pro Bono Award”.

Today, Hannah owns and operates Hannah’s Legal Help, providing personal and affordable 'Legal Help with Heart.' She focuses her practice on helping clients with uncontested legal matters and offers flat fees with payment plans for those in need.

attorneys.name: Courtney Bow
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Litigation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Courtney Bow’s experience includes employment litigation, civil litigation, personal-injury litigation, and civil-rights investigations. She has litigated in state and federal court and conducted corporate internal investigations.

Courtney’s heart has always been with serving the community in which she lives.

Before she moved to Cleveland, Courtney worked closely with refugees to assist with their resettlement in the Buffalo, New York area. She also was the president of her law school’s Public Interest Law program, an organization that allowed law students to dedicate their time and skills to providing legal assistance to those in the Buffalo community.

After graduating from the University at Buffalo’s School of Law with honors,

Courtney moved to Cleveland in 2021 and joined a mid-sized, defense-side law firm. During her service there, Courtney handled employment-discrimination investigations and litigation, as well as fair-housing investigations.

Since being admitted to practice, she has fostered a relationship with the Legal Aid Society of Cleveland and has regularly handled cases on their behalf during her career.

She is admitted to practice in Ohio, New York, and the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio.

Courtney and her husband live in Cleveland.

attorneys.bio: Jeffrey W. Bowling was a founding partner of Rapier & Bowling Co. LPA, and a lifelong resident of Hamilton, Ohio. Jeff earned his high school diploma from Hamilton High School in 1986. He enlisted in the United States Army his senior year. After serving in the 515th Transportation Unit in Stuttgart, Germany, Jeff earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in History and Political Science from Miami University, Oxford, Ohio. He then earned his Juris Doctorate in Legal Letters (law degree) from the University of Dayton School of Law in 1998. He returned to Hamilton, Ohio and served his community until his death.

attorneys.name: Patricia A. Brandt
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Independence, OH
attorneys.bio:
Patricia A. Brandt is Partner at Spitz, The Employee's Law Firm. Before becoming an attorney, Patricia held multiple positions in a Louisiana sheriff's office, the most notable of which was as the first female member of SWAT in the parish. She was selected for the FBI Instructor Development Course which entitled her to teach anything within the state's police training curriculum. Patricia's duties included holding an interior perimeter on missions and instructing officers in subject matters such as firearms, less than lethal munitions and hand to hand combat.

In 2018, Patricia graduated from Southern University Law Center in Louisiana. While in law school, Patricia gained valuable legal experience through an internship with the public defender's office and as a law clerk for Louisiana's First Circuit Court of Appeals. Upon earning her Juris Doctor, Patricia relocated to Ohio where she passed the Ohio Bar Exam and opened a private practice representing clients in the Cleveland area. Since being recruited by Spitz, The Employee's Law Firm, Patricia has continued to represent clients focusing her practice on employment law. Patricia is currently a deputy marshal in the training and grant writing division who teaches conceal carry classes and self-defense in her spare time.

attorneys.name: Tyler Bridenstine
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Leveraging a Lifetime of Helping Others in a Career as a Workers’ Compensation Attorney

Tyler Bridenstine is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Throughout his life, Tyler has embodied an ethos of service in his many career roles, philanthropic endeavors, and volunteer activities. Today, Tyler helps injured Ohio workers obtain the compensation they need to get their lives back.

Building on a Background in Service

“There’s a lot that brought me to where I am today, but two things stand out the most,” Tyler said, describing how he became a workers’ compensation attorney. “I joined the workforce as a teenager, and I took jobs at McDonald’s, local factories, and industrial cleaning outfits.” Tyler went on to describe that his work in jobs with high injury rates combined with his family’s core value of always seeking to help others led him to pursue workers’ compensation law shortly after passing the bar in 2023.

Before joining NRS Injury Law in 2024, Tyler leveraged his skill set in a number of ways to help others. While pursuing his undergrad at Kent State and then Ohio State, Tyler realized he wanted to help people via the legal profession. He quickly shifted his employment focus from factory work to any legal internship he could find. For example, his role as President of the Health Law Society and his Health Law Certificate made him a natural asset in internships and clerking roles at Community Legal Aid and similar organizations.

Working-Class Roots Led to a Role Representing Working Ohioans

“Most people in the communities where I’m from don’t have the resources they need when confronted with a legal issue connected to healthcare, real estate, or employment,” Tyler said, ticking off on his fingers the various legal areas where he’s spent time helping people, mostly in rural Ohio communities. “I decided early on I wanted to be an attorney so I could help the hardworking Ohioans I grew up with.”

Tyler continued. “I joined NRS Injury Law because this firm puts client results as the ne plus ultra objective—which isn’t always the case with law firms. The NRS Injury Law ethos is that results matter, and when you focus on getting results for clients, you’ll always have an office with your name on it waiting for you come Monday. But it’s the client results that’s the critical point. You have to focus on putting the client first, delivering for them, and ensuring their trust in you is well-deserved. NRS Injury Law does that.”

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working or volunteering, Tyler spends his free time bowling with friends, family, or colleagues. He enjoys exercising at the gym, frequenting local restaurants, and catching flicks at the movie theater with his wife. The pair live in Columbus with their two dogs. When they’re not exploring the sights and sounds of the city, they’re taking annual anniversary vacation trips or quick weekend getaways to Chicago, Vegas, D.C., or Toronto, to name a few.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Tyler Bridenstine

Tyler’s background, his ability to relate to his clients, and his knack for problem-solving combined with his compassion-forward approach align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Tyler and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Tyler believes strongly in not just preaching a value system of service but also living one. Since joining NRS Injury Law, he’s been active with the firm’s philanthropic and volunteer activities, including the Toys for Tots campaign and numerous food and clothing drives. Building on his work during his college years where he helped young people from disadvantaged communities, Tyler continues to host bowling clinics on nights and weekends, giving local youths an opportunity to develop an interest in a healthy, cooperative activity.

Tod Brininger — Veteran Criminal Defense Attorney in Ohio

Tod Brininger is an experienced criminal defense attorney with nearly 30 years of trial experience representing clients in more than 40 counties across Ohio. Known for his trusted legal advocacy, practical courtroom skill, and consistent results, Tod has successfully secured dismissals, charge reductions, and acquittals in a wide range of criminal and traffic cases.

Tod’s practice focuses on DUI/OVI defense, theft crimes, domestic violence and assault, and both misdemeanor and felony drug charges. His approach combines deep knowledge of Ohio’s criminal courts with strategic, client-focused representation designed to protect each client’s rights and future.

Throughout his career, Tod has earned a reputation as a skilled and respected trial lawyer who brings professionalism, preparation, and integrity to every case — from local municipal courts to complex felony trials.

attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jim began his career at Lindhorst & Dreidame as a law clerk in 1979. Upon his admission to the bar in 1981, he was hired by the firm and has been there ever since. His is a litigation practice. He has represented all the railroads in Cincinnati in FELA, trespasser, crossing and all other litigation. His practice also includes representing parties in products liability, personal injury, wrongful death, class action and toxic exposure cases. He represents real estate brokers and agents in civil litigation and administrative proceedings in Ohio. He also represents trucking companies in litigation throughout the State of Ohio.

attorneys.name: Tamara Brooks
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Utilizing a Knack for Litigation to Help Injured Workers Secure Justice and Compensation

Tamara Brooks is an Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. As a first-generation attorney with rich experience in both prosecutorial and defense litigation, Tamara’s understanding of Ohio law, combined with her unique abilities in the courtroom, all culminate in an attorney who can proudly stand up for working people and help them win.

A Pathway to Law and Advocacy for Working People

“I can trace my interest in the legal field back to the fourth grade,” Tamara said when asked to reflect on the moments and milestones that led her to a career in workers’ compensation law. “During my childhood, there were times where I was in the foster care system. I remember attending hearings and listening to all these big people talk about me and make decisions about my life. I realized, one day, I wanted to be the one making the decisions, the one helping others have the final say in their future. I decided to become an attorney so I could help others who were put in difficult situations through no fault of their own.”

Born in Maple Heights and raised by her grandparents, Tamara has lived and worked in northeast Ohio for most of her life. She worked multiple jobs starting at age 15, including at the Geauga Lake amusement park and McDonald’s. Sadly, her academic career at the University of Toledo was interrupted when her grandmother, who had been a mother to Tamara and her brother, passed away suddenly, and Tamara had to move back to her hometown to be the legal guardian of her younger brother.

Determined, Tamara went back to college and graduated from the University of Akron and later the Akron School of Law. Since passing the bar, Tamara has worked as both a public defender and a county prosecutor, earning rare, highly valuable experience practicing law on both sides of the judicial aisle. She has gained experience from labor union and employee representation to defending tenants in eviction cases, representing police officers being denied workers’ comp claims, and prosecuting felony offenders, Tamara has excelled through it all.

Helping the Underdog Obtain Justice

“When I was a county prosecutor, my role was to obtain justice for victims and ensure the community was safe from violent offenders, I also had a duty to Defendants to get them the rehabilitation they needed so they would not reoffend,” Tamara said. “I see my role in civil law as a workers’ compensation attorney very similarly. My job is to keep families safe and secure by helping injured workers, often the breadwinners of families, in securing the compensation they need to get their lives back, to get their houses back in order, and put a spotlight on areas that employers can improve, so they are not continuously liable for injuries that occur on their watch.”

To Tamara, representing plaintiffs in workers’ compensation cases is about helping them attain justice, but it’s also about holding employers accountable and bending the arc of employment practices towards policies that are safer and more equitable for all. “Every time I win a case against an employer and secure benefits for my client, I know I’m incentivizing employers to implement better safety measures so future workers don’t experience life-altering workplace injuries.”

Work/Life Balance

When she’s not working at the firm’s Cleveland office, Tamara spends time with her son, Parker. “He’s my little bestie,” Tamara says. The two spend nights and weekends together practicing music, gaming, attending drama club, going to the movie theater, and checking out the local restaurant scene. “If there’s a new mom-and-pop restaurant or grassroots establishment nearby, you can bet I will be one of the first customers in there,” Tamara says.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Tamara Brooks

“You have to think outside the box to consistently win workers’ compensation cases,” Tamara said when asked how she represents her clients. “It’s about breaking down the legalese into its most basic and relatable structure, working hand-in-hand with your client, and building a case based on their story. You have to work together, as a team, and when you do, nothing can stop you from attaining justice.”

To Tamara, nothing embodies the definition of out-of-the-box thinking better than NRS Injury Law. “Everyone at the firm is highly accessible. The partners have an open door policy for attorneys and our clients. There is no baseless hierarchy traditionally found in law firms. We are a legal team that’s dedicated to helping workers across Ohio. All the poisonous office politics you sometimes see in law firms? That doesn’t exist at NRS Injury Law. It’s just the necessities of helping people, and that distinguishes the firm from others, and makes us highly effective.”

Tamara’s compassion, empathy, litigation skills, and client camaraderie are traits that align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Tamara and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Tamara embodies the core tenets of NRS Injury Law during her free time. She is deeply involved in showing up for her community and giving back. Tamara is a member of Torchbearers Akron, where she takes an active role in improving the community via environmental volunteering campaigns. Tamara serves as First Vice President of the Akron Canton Barristers Association, where she works on civil rights and social action issues. She has also been a member of the Akron Urban League of Young Professionals since 2018.

As she was earning her law degree, Tamara received an honors chord for providing over 500 hours of community service while in law school, a feat recognized by the Ohio State Supreme Court. In her free time, Tamara helps people who need legal help but who can’t afford it. She also volunteers to end food insecurity by working with People Feeding People to deliver 10,000 pounds of food monthly to communities across northeast Ohio. In the future, Tamara would like to take the lead on new community action campaigns. She seeks to implement an initiative she started during her time at the Summit County Prosecutor’s Office within the law firm, a NRS Injury Law Costume Drive and a safe “Trunk-or-Treat” event to help families from disadvantaged communities receive free Halloween costumes and access safe Trick-or-Treating opportunities.

attorneys.bio:
Eric grew up in Worthington, Ohio. He graduated with honors (cum laude) from The Ohio State University in 2002 with a Bachelor of Arts. Eric then graduated with honors (magna cum laude) from Capital University Law School in 2007.

Eric is admitted to practice law in all Ohio state courts and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. Eric has been practicing domestic relations law, exclusively, since 2007. Accordingly, he handles matters in all areas of family law including divorce, dissolution, custody proceedings, post-decree matters, child and spousal support cases and appellate matters. Eric is an OSBA Certified Specialist in the practice of Family Relations Law, which requires passage of a written examination in the field of family relations law, demonstration of a high level of substantial involvement in family relations law and favorable evaluations by colleagues and judges / magistrates familiar with his work. Eric has also been selected to the National Academy of Family Law Attorneys “Top 10 Under 40 Attorney Award for the state of Ohio,” which is by invitation and is extended to those attorneys who have demonstrated exceptional knowledge, skill, experience, expertise and success in their practice of family law. Eric has presented at a number of seminars, including the Fifth Annual Family Institute in 2017 and the Domestic Relations Judge & Magistrate Winter Conference in 2016. Eric is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Samantha J. Brush
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Leveraging a Lifetime in Workers’ Compensation Law to Help Injured Workers Find Their Voice

Samantha Brush is an Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Samantha has practiced workers’ compensation law since passing the bar, always seeking to help Ohio workers who have been injured through no fault of their own. Her rich background across multiple legal fields and professional categories adds value to her client representation, and her commitment to giving Ohio workers a voice aligns perfectly with the NRS Injury Law mission and vision.

Born and Raised in a Workers’ Compensation Law Firm

“In 1937, my great-grandfather, Clarence Scott Knisley, was elected as State Treasurer; and in his term, worked closely with the Board of Industrial Commission to shape their policies and procedures,” Samantha said when asked about the life chapters that led to her pursuing a career in workers’ comp law. “He advised my grandfather, Scott M. Knisley, to become a workers’ compensation attorney. My grandfather established Knisley Law Office and years later his four sons joined him at the practice.

Samantha recalled being a young ten-year-old girl assisting in the mailroom at the Knisley Law Office. She spoke about weekends at her grandparents’ house, where she’d watch her grandpa meet with his clients on Sundays from 8:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. “I watched grandpa work on weekends to ensure his clients, all of whom were injured workers, were getting the representation they needed to secure fair compensation,” Samantha said. “From a very young age I saw the positive effect my grandpa had on folks within our community, and I decided I wanted to be that person some day.”

Helping the Underdog Get the Justice They Deserve

“CEOs are collecting millions upon millions per year while their employees are terrified of reporting a workplace injury because they’re worried they’ll miss a paycheck as a result, or worse,” Samantha said. “I got into workers’ comp law not just because it’s what I grew up knowing, but because workers are at an inherent disadvantage, and it's our job as attorneys to level the playing field and ensure workers get the justice they deserve. I was raised with an ideology that you make a career out of something that makes you happy, and taking care of people makes me happy. I’ve practiced in numerous professional and legal areas, but because of my upbringing, workers’ compensation law has always felt like home to me.”

To that point, in addition to her lifetime commitment to helping injured workers, Samantha has focused her legal career on dispute resolution, negotiation, mediation, and professional responsibility. She holds a Mediation Certification from Capital University Law School. Samantha has held leadership roles in academia, business, and the legal profession and she has lived abroad. These life-changing decisions and roles gave her opportunities to study how other legal systems worked, giving her a nuanced perspective and a strategic edge back at home.

Work/Life Balance

“Gosh we are busy,” Samantha says with a chuckle when asked what she does when she’s not being an attorney. “Our weekends consist of sports, social gatherings at our home, and community activities throughout Columbus. The whole family is very active outside of work and school. We go skiing together, host parties, and each season of the year at least one or more of our three boys are involved in sports.” Samantha and her family are also members of athletic and social clubs, and they like to travel abroad whenever possible. Samantha also enjoys running and has competed in several half-marathons.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Samantha Brush

Compassionate, loyal, and someone who listens with intent to her client’s story, Samantha believes that successful workers’ compensation cases are built on empathy and a desire to learn about and advocate for “the person sitting right in front of you.” Quoting Samantha, “We as attorneys will represent thousands of injured workers in our careers. But each case is unique. It’s someone who has seen their entire life change overnight due to a workplace injury. Each case deserves to be treated like it’s the first and last case an attorney will ever have, one where failure is not an option.”

Samantha’s lifetime commitment to Ohio workers who have been injured in the line of work aligns perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Samantha and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Samantha is involved with Ohio Women Against Domestic Violence, an organization centered around helping women break free from abusive situations at home and in shelters. Samantha was also granted the title of Guardian Ad Litem (a neutral party who advocates for a child's best interests in legal cases) by the Supreme Court of Ohio in 2018. She is also an active parent in youth sports teams.

attorneys.name: Christopher Bucio
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Dayton, OH
attorneys.bio:
Christopher Bucio is a trial lawyer with a history of success in Criminal Defense cases. Chris’ trial history includes “Not Guilty” verdicts in several high profile criminal cases, which include: Attempted Murder, Rape, Kidnapping, Abduction, Felonious Assault, Domestic VIolence, and Child Pornography.

Chris is willing to take on tough cases and zealosuly represent his clients. This is one of the distinctions that sets him apart from other lawyers. Although Chris can not guarantee any outcome he does guarantee he will work hard for his clients.

Chris has been selected by AVVO.com for the Client Choice Award for his consistent high marks, and also reviewed highly by former and current clients. Additionally, Mr. Bucio has been selected as Ohio’s Business Man of the Year for his dedication and leadership of his law firm.

As a result of his experience, Chris has appeared on national and local television. He has also served as a moderator for various functions and has also been invited to speak to schools and other public audiences.

After graduating from Newton High School and earning All State Honors in basketball. Upon graduating High School, Chris enrolled at Bluffton University where he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in Criminal Justice and Sociology in less than three years while playing college basketball. After graduating with honors from Bluffton University, he earned a law degree from the University Of Cincinnati College Of Law. At the time of being sworn in, he was one of the youngest member admitted to the Ohio Bar. Following Law School, Chris opened up his own law practice in Troy, Ohio in 2004. Chris then eventually partnered with OSBA Certified Specialist in Family Law, Roberta S. Roberts and partner Scott Kelly and has grown a boutique firm into several offices which are spread throughout Ohio.

When he is not working on cases, Chris still enjoys attending church, playing basketball and spending time with his wife and five children.

Holmes Cuyahoga Jefferson

Hamilton Belmont Coshocton

His colleagues credit him with being a compassionate professional, with patience and concern to work diligently for his clients as a strong advocate in courtroom litigation. He has 36 years of experience in matters in Domestic Relations and Juvenile Courts. He also counsels clients to avoid potential pitfalls which may occur when a marriage or a relationship between parents ends, and is available to speak on any family law topics.

Ray is a member of the American, Ohio State and Stark County Bar Associations, and is admitted to practice in Ohio courts and the U.S. District Court, Northern District of Ohio.

After 32 years of building a regional family law practice throughout Northeastern and East Central Ohio, Ray joined Mills, Mills, Fiely & Lucas in opening the firm's Canton office in May 2013.

Frank grew up in rural Northwest Ohio. He graduated with honors (cum laude) from Ohio University in 2012 with a Bachelor of Science. Frank then graduated from The Ohio State University's Moritz College of Law in 2020.

Frank has been serving the public in high-stress situations before he ever became an attorney. Ronald Burdge retired in 2025, and was a leading lemon law attorney known nationally for fighting for the rights of RV owners and helping them get rid of their lemon RVs of all types. As the founder and managing partner of Burdge Law Office, Ron has practiced exclusively in the areas of RV lemon law, Lemon law, and Consumer law since 1978.

Ronald L. Burdge is consumer Law Trial Attorney in private practice in Dayton, Ohio since 1978. A sizeable percentage of the reported cases under Ohio’s Consumer Sales Practices Act (the Ohio UDAP law) come from Mr. Burdge’s years of representing thousands of consumers in Auto-Fraud and Lemon cases in three states and numerous federal courts. He is Board Certified in Civil Trial Law and has extensive trial and appellate experience in individual and class action cases involving lenders, car dealers and manufacturers, and is one of the few Consumer Law Trial Attorneys who has tried a class action case to a jury.

In 2004, he was named Trial Lawyer of the Year by the National Association of Consumer Advocates.

attorneys.name: Amanda M. Burgess
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Portsmouth, OH
attorneys.bio:
Amanda M. Burgess’ legal experience began during college when she worked full-time as a law clerk for a business law firm representing clients of all sizes, from small start-up companies to Fortune 100 corporations in Cincinnati, Ohio. At the same time, Amanda attended college at the University of Cincinnati where she graduated cum laude in 2003 with a B.A. in English. After graduation, Amanda continued her legal experience at one of the nation’s leading providers of residential and civil litigation.

In 2005 Amanda attended law school at the University of Dayton School of Law. At the same time, Amanda worked as a law clerk at a full-service personal injury law firm including serious injury, complex medical malpractice, worker’s compensation and Social Security Disability and complex personal injury cases in Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky. Amanda graduated from the University Of Dayton School Of Law in the top 22% of her class earning the CALI Awards in Civil Trial Practice, Contracts II, and Intellectual Property. Amanda served as the President of the Law Students for the Arts and through this position raised money to benefit various causes in the local and national community. Amanda passed the Ohio bar exam scoring in the top 5% of the July 2008 Ohio bar examinees.

Amanda began practicing law immediately upon graduation and has successfully represented clients in not only personal injury cases but in a multitude of practice areas including consumer and business bankruptcy, debt settlements, loan modifications, contracts, real estate transactions, business matters, divorce, juvenile law, custody, child support, spousal support, domestic violence, civil protection orders, adoptions, wills, estate planning, probate administration, and other legal needs. Just two years later, Amanda passed the Kentucky bar to meet the needs of her growing client base and expanded her practice.

Amanda utilizes her diverse background to cater her practice to meet the individual needs of her unique clients. Amanda treats every client with the care and compassion of a small firm while bringing to the table the clout and experience of a large firm. When the insurance company is unwilling to negotiate a fair settlement, Amanda is prepared to litigate your case.

While Amanda is not practicing law she stays busy with her three-year-old son, Bradley, in New Albany, Ohio. They enjoy traveling, riding bikes, swimming, coloring, and fishing!

attorneys.name: Kristopher D. Burgess Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lebanon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Ohio, Kris Burgess is exactly where he belongs—fighting for injured Ohioans and pursuing full compensation and real accountability. As an injury attorney with Rittgers, Rittgers & Nakajima, Kris stands up for people who’ve been hurt because someone else didn’t take safety seriously, making sure they feel heard, supported, and never left guessing about what comes next.

Kris’s diverse life experiences shape how he shows up for clients. Before he was ever a lawyer, he played rock shows in hole-in-the-wall bars until closing time, toured Japan as a musician, taught math to students of all ages, and learned what it means to be part of a great team—on the field and in the courtroom. Those chapters built the perspective and discipline he brings to his practice today: steady under pressure, direct with opponents, and human with clients.

With years of courtroom experience in high-stakes injury cases, Kris represents individuals and families navigating some of the hardest moments of their lives—from serious and catastrophic injury cases to wrongful death claims after a tragic loss. He works to uncover the full story, build the strongest case possible, and put his clients in the best position to win.

Whether he’s standing up to insurance companies, large corporations, or determined opponents in court, Kris thrives in high-stakes disputes and brings a seasoned, relentless approach to every case. Backed by the team at RRN, he’s proud to serve the Cincinnati community and fight every day to make sure injured Ohioans and their families are heard—because seeing someone’s pain acknowledged, their story respected, and their future protected is what makes the hard work worth it.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Lillie Burkons brings a rich background in journalism, law, and public service to her practice at Zashin Law. Graduating from Northwestern University with a Bachelor of Science in Journalism, Lillie’s journey into law began with an impressive transition from a committed student to a D-1 walk-on athlete for the women’s tennis team, showcasing her determination and resilience.

Her legal education was pursued at Case Western Reserve University School of Law. She not only excelled academically, earning Cali awards for her outstanding performance in Trademarks, but she also dedicated her time to student government in her 2L year.

Professionally, Lillie’s career has been characterized by her commitment to serving her community. Starting as a prosecutor, she later channeled her expertise into the nonprofit sector, providing both brief advice and representation to those in need. Her legal practice now focuses on family law, including divorce and custody matters, where she is passionate about tailoring parenting plans to meet the unique needs of each family.

In her personal time, Lillie continues to embody the spirit of balance and wellness, enjoying yoga and spending quality time with her family and friends. Her journey from the tennis courts of Northwestern to the legal courts of Cleveland encapsulates a dedication to excellence, justice, and the well-being of others.

attorneys.name: Alec C. Burkhart Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Alec has spent his entire career in a courtroom. Prior to joining Lindhorst and Dreidame, Alec worked as a staff attorney in the Hamilton County Court of Common Pleas for over twelve years. He began as a staff attorney for the Common Pleas Magistrate in one of the busiest courtrooms in the State of Ohio. In that role, he got exposure to a wide range of cases including foreclosures, collection cases, civil protection orders, administrative appeals, and real property disputes.

Alec went onto clerk for Common Pleas Judge Lisa C. Allen. Judge Allen’s docket included personal injury cases, construction cases, insurance disputes, complex litigation, and felony criminal cases. Alec played an integral role in the day-to-day operations of the courtroom including legal research, drafting entries and jury instructions, and overall case management of both civil and criminal cases. He has seen all types of cases play out in the courtroom from the very beginning all the way through trial.

At Lindhorst and Dreidame, Alec utilizes the skills he has learned over the years for the benefit of his clients. Alec explains the law in a way ordinary people can understand. Given his experience, Alec focuses on the issues that matter and advises clients how courts are likely to rule. Alec uses the research and writing skills he honed as a law clerk to tell the client’s story with legal precedent to support the client’s position. Going to the courthouse and litigating cases in the courtroom is where he is most comfortable.

Alec lives on the Westside of Cincinnati with his wife and two children. In his free time, Alec enjoys taking his kids to parks throughout the city, grilling out with friends and family, and taking in a high school football game on a Friday night.

attorneys.bio:
Protect Your Rights.

Call 740-353-2363 for an Appointment Today.

Hello, my name is Attorney Jeremy Burnside. I was born and raised in Cleveland, Ohio, and have since moved to Scioto County to provide valuable legal care in the areas of personal injury, wrongful death and criminal law. I'm located in the historic Bourgholtzer House (Est. 1849), directly across the street from the Scioto County Courthouse in downtown Portsmouth, Ohio. You can easily reach my office from US Rt. 23 and US Rt. 52 for all of your legal needs. I'm readily available for consultation and my clients are comforted by having direct contact with their lawyer. In cases involving wrongful death, medical malpractice and serious injury, home, weeknight and weekend visits are available. On these cases, I work on a contingency fee basis. This means if you don't get paid, I don't get paid.

DON'T trust the insurance companies.

Many people who are involved in car accidents don't realize that they're injured until several days after the collision. The longer these victims wait before getting treated by a medical provider, the more likely it is that an insurance company will not pay out on medical bills. Don't be victimized twice. Call me today. If you don't know where to look for treatment, contact me and I can possibly point you in the right direction to proper medical care and treatment.

DO speak to someone who can help you.

This does not include insurance adjusters. They are paid by their billion-dollar bosses to minimize your recovery. Many adjusters are paid bonuses for the amount of minimal recoveries they are able to convince victims to accept. Many such victims have permanent injuries and were either pressured to accept the settlement or simply didn't take the time to know and understand their rights. The more insurance adjusters are successful in settling potentially large claims for minimal amounts, the more money the insurance companies save from the billions and billions they receive from premiums and can therefore use to buy naming rights to ballparks, fancy commercials and ultimately place large bonuses in the pockets of their executives. Talk to a lawyer to ensure you're not helping the insurance industry pad its pockets by settling your claim for less than it is worth.

Free Consultation

My hours are tailored to meet my client's needs. I'm available for weekend, weeknight, home and hospital visits. Please call 740-353-2363 to set up an appointment that will suit your needs. If I am not available, I'm probably in court. As a proud trial lawyer, I pride myself in my courtroom and litigation experience. Hopefully that will not be necessary in your potential case.

I look forward to speaking with you!

attorneys.name: Alonda Bush
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Sandusky, OH
attorneys.bio:
Alonda Bush is an experienced criminal defense lawyer with a lengthy history of trials, dismissals, and not guilty verdicts.

With a decade of experience in the criminal defense world, she's another of our women to see for private criminal defense in the Cuyahoga County and the surrounding areas.

Alonda Ann Bush joined Ohio Legal Group in May 2025, bringing nearly a decade of criminal defense experience and a deep commitment to advocating for underserved and vulnerable populations.

Ms. Bush serves as a criminal defense attorney, with a career distinguished by high-stakes litigation, appellate advocacy, and dedication to justice reform.

Ms. Bush is licensed to practice law in the State of Ohio and is admitted to all Ohio state courts. She has appeared in Municipal, Common Pleas, and Appellate Courts throughout the state.

Experience.

Prior to joining the firm, Ms. Bush served as an Assistant Public Defender in Portage County, where she managed a felony court docket and the Drug Court docket. Her caseload included trial litigation in matters involving murder, rape, felonious assault, weapons charges, DUI/OVI, domestic violence, and trafficking offenses. She also researched, briefed, and argued appellate issues before the Eleventh District Court of Appeals.

From 2018 to 2020, she worked as an Assistant Public Defender in Cuyahoga County, where she managed both municipal court and felony arraignment dockets, focusing on domestic violence, DUI/OVI, and vehicular homicide. Ms. Bush also worked in academia, serving as an Academic Support Specialist at Cleveland State University’s College of Law, assisting law students with legal skills and academic development.

Earlier in her legal career, she operated a solo practice focused on criminal defense, child custody, and small business litigation. She also previously served as a Senior Law Clerk at Milano Attorneys at Law, preparing motions and legal memoranda in both civil and criminal matters.

Before practicing law, Ms. Bush worked in social services as a Case Worker for Frontline Services, where she provided outreach and care coordination for individuals with co-occurring mental health and substance use diagnoses.

Education & Training.

Ms. Bush earned her Juris Doctor, cum laude, from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law at Cleveland State University in 2016, where she served as Co-Editor-in-Chief of The Gavel and received the Suggs I. Garber Award. She also received CALI Excellence for the Future Awards for her performance in Taxation of Business Enterprises and Agency and Partnership.

She holds a Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice with dual minors in Psychology and Sociology from Baldwin-Wallace College.

Ms. Bush is certified in Standardized Field Sobriety Testing by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (2019) and is a trained mentor through the Ohio Supreme Court Mentor Program.

Brian Butler has practiced civil litigation for more than 15 years since graduating cum laude from the University of Cincinnati College of Law in 2007. He lives with his wife Amy and their dogs, Phil and Carl, in East Walnut Hills.

Brian has represented a wide variety of clients in various areas of civil litigation, including employment, personal injury, and commercial. He has significant experience representing employees and executives in litigation involving wrongful termination, discrimination, retaliation, whistleblowing, and non-compete agreements. He has also represented clients in complex financial disputes and contractual disputes. Brian has also represented clients in complex personal injury matters, where he has secured several recoveries in excess of $2,000,000.

Brian is licensed to practice law in the State of Ohio, the Southern District of Ohio, the Northern District of Ohio, the Southern District of Indiana, and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. He has also represented clients in federal course in other jurisdictions, including Kentucky.

attorneys.name: Amanda M. Buzo
attorneys.firm_name: Hickman Lowder Lidrbauch & Welch Co., L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Special Needs Estate Planning Lawyers in Independence, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Amanda M. Buzo has devoted her career to serving individuals with special needs and their families. Her legal practice is concentrated in the areas of special needs estate planning, guardianships, elder law, estate administration, and other probate matters.

Amanda was an associate attorney at Hickman Lowder from 2005 through 2013 and returned to practicing law at Hickman Lowder in August 2024. During her time away from the firm, she served as the Executive Director of Community Fund Ohio. Co-founded by Hickman Lowder attorney Janet L. Lowder, Community Fund Ohio strives to enhance the lives of individuals with disabilities by protecting their eligibility for government benefits and funding their current and future needs through pooled special needs trusts, grants, community education, and related services.

Her experience with Community Fund Ohio and her previous work as a practicing attorney have provided her with an in-depth knowledge of estate planning for people with special needs, including special needs trusts, establishing guardianships, and maintaining government benefits. Amanda advises guardians and special needs trust trustees on their respective fiduciary responsibilities. She works with individuals or their attorneys to provide advice regarding the impact of settlements on government benefits, such as Medicaid and Supplemental Security Income, to establish minor and adult guardianships, and administer wrongful death settlements. Amanda advises clients on the necessity of guardianship, special needs trusts, wrongful death trusts, qualified settlement funds, and/or Medicare and Medicaid lien resolution. She also counsels domestic relations attorneys and their clients regarding the legal impact of divorce on government benefits for spouses or children with disabilities.

Amanda graduated from the University of Akron School of Law. She is a member of the Ohio State, Cleveland Metropolitan, and Lorain County Bar Associations, as well as a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA) and the Estate Planning Council of Cleveland. Amanda has been recognized as a 2010 and 2016 Rising Star by Ohio Super Lawyers; a distinction offered to only 2.5% of Ohio attorneys. She is also a 2015 Best Lawyers® award recipient.

Amanda resides in Lorain County with her family and dogs. When she is not enjoying a good book or listening to a podcast, you can find Amanda exploring the Metro Parks, attending high intensity interval training classes, or watching The Ohio State University football.

attorneys.name: Christopher D. Byers
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Christopher D. Byers has worked with our firm for 15 years, first as an assistant while he was in law school and then as an associate attorney since 2005. During his tenure at our firm, Chris has resolved over 3,000 cases and successfully recovered in excess of $30,000,000 for his clients in out of court settlements and at trial.

Chris comes from very modest means. He was born in a small town in southern Kentucky, and raised by a single parent. This background gives Chris true insight to the financial struggles that many of his clients often face after an accident due to medical bills and lost wages. Therefore, Chris is passionate in fighting for his clients in order to obtain the maximum recovery for their losses.

Chris was the first in his family to attend college, and he graduated from Berea College in 2000. Berea is a unique college as every student is on 100% academic scholarship based solely on financial need. In exchange, Berea requires its students participate in a work study program. Chris moved to the greater Cincinnati area in 2002 to attend law school at Northern Kentucky University, Chase College of Law. Chris chose Chase because it was the only law school in Kentucky that offered a part-time program. Chris worked 40 hours per week during the day while attending law school at night in order to fund his education. Chris knows the value of hard work and perseverance, and devotes these qualities to his clients.

Chris currently lives in Mt. Adams with his wife and their young daughter. Chris loves Cincinnati and enjoys attending Reds and Bengals games. However, he is a blue blood by heart, and is an avid Kentucky basketball fan. Chris believes in giving back to the community and supports charities including St. Jude Children Research Hospital, Goodwill, and the Stray Animal Adoption Program (SAAP). His family currently has two stray puppies that they adopted from SAAP, Barkley and Calvin Byers.

Chris loves his job as he truly enjoys helping people. He finds satisfaction in the fact that he can help an injured party recover for their loss. Chris promises not to charge any fee unless his client has been compensated, and he will always work hard to obtain the best possible outcome that they deserve.

attorneys.name: Thomas Cafferty
attorneys.practice_type: Admiralty & Maritime Law Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
I served over 20 years on active duty with the U.S. Coast Guard, which included 5 years aboard Coast Guard Cutter ACACIA, working as the navigator on this World War II era, seagoing buoy tender and ice breaker. In addition to my shipboard experience, I investigated marine casualties, prosecuted suspension & revocation cases and served as the chief of the Great Lakes Regional Exam Center. This background provides me with the experience to evaluate and advise you on your maritime matter quickly and professionally.

I began my legal practice in northwest Ohio in 2006, where I work in bankruptcy, consumer and maritime law. I am a frequent lecturer on bankruptcy matters for attorneys earning continuing education credits, with topics ranging from the implications of divorce and bankruptcy, consumer bankruptcy fundamentals, claim litigation and preferential property transfers. I earned my law degree from the University of Toledo (with honors), I’m a member of the Ohio and Toledo Bar Associations, and I’m admitted to the Eastern District of Michigan and the Northern and Southern District of Ohio federal courts.

Since my Coast Guard career concluded, I’ve been an active volunteer with my local American Legion post, which includes performing with the color guard to ensure that our veterans are provided proper honors. I devote a significant portion of my legal practice to pro bono activity, which includes referrals from the Toledo Bar Association and Operation Legal Help Ohio for veterans, advising callers on the Ask the Attorney program, and assisting homeowners in foreclosure.

attorneys.name: John Calabrese
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
After eleven years representing individuals and families in civil litigation matters, John Calabrese joins Cavitch, Familo & Durkin as a Shareholder in their business litigation practice group. His national litigation practice focuses on representing individual and business clients in complex commercial and business tort actions, shareholder litigation cases, construction defects, insurance disputes, breach of contract claims, employment and compensation matters, conversion of property, and probate/will contests.

John has extensive trial experience trying cases before judges and juries. Additionally, he has successfully briefed and argued multiple appellate claims before the Eighth District Court of Appeals and has navigated and handled complex administrative and regulatory matters on behalf of clients. John brings extensive experience to Cavitch to assist individuals, employers and businesses develop and improve communications, increase efficiencies, and decrease litigation risks through an analytical and innovated approach to the specific needs of his clients. In collaboration with clients to understand their goals and objectives, John is able to assess risks and devise strategic plans to guide and promote advantageous outcomes through dispute resolution and out of court solutions. If resolution requires litigation, John and the Cavitch team of lawyers stand ready and prepared to aggressively assert your interests and advocate on your behalf.

Cleveland has undeniably become home for John and his two golden retrievers, Rigley and Cru. He is a proud Cleveland resident and actively engaged within the greater Cleveland community and Tremont neighborhood where he resides. John grew up in Erie, Pennsylvania, attended Cathedral Preparatory Catholic High School, and shares a great relationship with the Erie community, most importantly his loving family and lifelong friendships. Often remembered as an avid nationally ranked junior golfer, he now enjoys the fun and camaraderie of the game of golf as a member of The Kahkwa Club. He attended Florida Gulf Coast University, in Fort Myers, Florida, for his undergraduate education earning a degree in finance and minor in economics. John remains connected with FGCU and the southwest Florida community visiting his home and interacting with friends and neighbors in the area. After returning north to Cleveland, Ohio, he earned his law degree at Cleveland State University College of Law. John has been involved in many Cleveland-area civic organizations and currently serves on the CSU Law Alumni Association Board of Trustees. He ascended to President of the Board of Trustees during 2019-2020 and remains active in the organization.

attorneys.name: Sean P. Callan
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Real Estate Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Sean's practice areas include commercial real estate, corporate (in both the for-profit and non-profit sectors) and litigation, including administrative hearings before planning commissions, boards of zoning appeals, and taxing authorities. An AV-rated attorney who is also listed in The Best Lawyers in America, Sean also has extensive national experience representing Greek letter organization such as fraternities/sororities, foundations and house corporations.

In the commercial real estate arena, Sean advises owners and developers on the full range of issues confronting them from initial land acquisition, through permitting and right-to-build challenges, to financing, leasing, and ultimately disposition. Sean frequently speaks and writes on real estate issues, and is a member of the International Council of Shopping Centers. He is also listed in The Best Lawyers in America in Real Estate.

In the corporate world, Sean advises closely held for-profit companies as well as non-profit and tax exempt entities. His advice covers a broad spectrum of issues including corporate governance, corporate "best practices", mergers and acquisitions, employment issues, grant-making and maintaining tax-exempt status.

Finally, Sean represents clients in the courtroom and before administrative agencies. He has litigated a variety of cases including contract disputes, boundary and real estate disputes, franchise disputes, and land use and zoning disputes. On an administrative level, Sean represents clients at planning commissions and boards of zoning appeals throughout Ohio and northern Kentucky, including the NKAPC. He also represents property owners before taxing authorities in Ohio and Kentucky including county Boards of Revision and the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals. This broad and long litigation experience enhances Sean's handling of real estate and corporate transactional matters.

attorneys.name: John Camillus Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Securities Fraud and Class Action Matters Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
John Camillus is a trial lawyer. His trial experience includes securities fraud and class action matters, consumer protection and commercial disputes, personal injury and medical malpractice cases, and civil rights and employment matters.

He has broad experience trying civil cases in federal and state court, including arbitrations, bench trials, and jury trials.

In addition to being Of Counsel to Meyer Wilson Werning, John is a principal with his own firm, the Law Offices of John C. Camillus, LLC. Previously, John was an attorney at Cooper & Elliott, where his practice focused on representing plaintiffs in a broad range of civil matters. Prior to joining Cooper & Elliott, John was a litigator with the international law firm of Jones Day. While at Jones Day, John worked on civil and criminal matters at both the trial and appellate levels. His experience at Jones Day included the successful representation of clients in various tort, contract, criminal, and securities matters. Before joining Jones Day, John served as a law clerk for the Honorable R. Guy Cole, Jr., of the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit.

John received his law degree from Yale Law School. At Yale, John was an editor for the Yale Law & Policy Review and was named a Schell fellow. John also served as the President of the Initiative for Public Interest Law at Yale and worked with the South Asia Human Rights Documentation Centre in New Delhi, India. John received his B.A. in Philosophy from Ohio Wesleyan University, graduating first in his class. He graduated phi beta kappa and summa cum laude and was a First-Team All-Conference and First-Team Academic All-American basketball player. At OWU, John was the recipient of the Easton Prize given to the outstanding senior philosophy major and graduated with University and Departmental Honors.

attorneys.name: Spencer Campbell
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
In everything he does, Spencer is an advocate. From his fifth-grade speech preaching the value of America's public libraries to his continued work with the University of Cincinnati College of Law as a coach and mentor, Spencer has always found a way to blend his love for public speaking with his passion for knowledge and education.

In 2018, Spencer won the American Mock Trial Association's National Championship with Miami University's Mock Trial team. In 2019 he was the only returning team member from the National Champion roster and, as President of the program, he won his second All-American award and helped the team defend that Champion title. Spencer remains one of the most decorated competitors in AMTA history.

In 2019, Spencer graduated from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio with a degree in Music. The years he spent on stage and in practice rooms, as well as studying under the very best mentors and coaches, have yielded a rare but tempered confidence and comfort standing in front of judges and juries alike.

Spencer's competitive spirit and winning record followed him to UC Law, where Spencer competed for the college's Moot Court and Trial Advocacy teams. In his first semester of law school, he was named Best Attorney at the Ohio Attorney General's Trial Team Competition. That award was followed by numerous others on the national level in both trial and appellate settings. Upon graduation, Spencer was awarded the Order of the Barristers, the Neil Weil Service Award for National Excellence in Moot Court, and the John W. Peck Award for Excellence in Trial Practice.

Today, Spencer rigorously fights for the firm's clients in class action cases, bringing an empathy and a humanity that often surprises and reassures his class representatives and other class members. Every day, Spencer is thankful for the opportunity to bring his battle-hardened advocacy skills to bear for people who deserve justice.

When he isn't in the office working for his clients, or at the College working for his students, you can find Spencer around the Queen City taking in as much live music as he can find, out on the golf course with his dad, or preparing a nice home cooked meal.
