attorneys.name: Duane E. Cox
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
A Trailblazing Attorney Serving Ohio Clients Since 1979

Duane Cox is an Attorney of Counsel at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Now semi-retired, Duane’s passion for helping injured workers drives him to continue providing essential counsel to the firm’s practicing attorneys.

The Only Black Graduate of His Law School Class

“It was a radical time,” Duane said when asked to reflect on his early years as an undergraduate, law school student, legal clerk, and newly barred attorney. Duane had enrolled at Kent State University just one year after the tragic Kent State Shootings, and he was the only one from his family to go to college. Motivated to change the status quo, Duane studied political science and became involved in the Black United Students advocacy group, eventually serving as the organization’s Vice President and later President.

Quoting Kent State’s Alumni publication, “His [Duane’s] leadership had a lasting impact on the university as BUS was able to raise significant funding and helped develop the Institute of African American Affairs, now known as the Department for Africana Studies, and secured dedicated space in Oscar Ritchie Hall.”

Duane graduated from Kent State in 1975 and, on the advice of Professor Charles Greene, took the LSAT and enrolled in the nearby University of Akron School of Law. He graduated and passed the bar in 1979.

From Cleveland’s Inner City Projects to Statewide Advocacy for Working Ohioans

After brief stints as a District Hearing Officer for the Ohio Industrial Commission and an employer’s defense attorney for the Greater Cleveland Region Transit Authority, Duane decided his skills would be best used as a plaintiff’s attorney representing hardworking Ohioans who had been injured on the job. Duane opened a private practice and became the only Black workers’ compensation attorney in Cleveland.

“I was in private practice for almost 40 years before I began to wonder if it was time to throw in the towel,” Duane said. “But I really didn’t want to retire, and around 2020, my grandson was playing baseball with the son of this young fella who I took a real liking to, a man named Jerald Schneiberg. Jerry and I got to talking, and he asked if I’d like to come on over to NRS Injury Law and serve in a semi-retired Of Counsel role. Partial retirement that would still let me work and help people? Now that sounded good to me!”

“Let Providence and Good People Show You The Way”

Despite his many accomplishments, Duane insists that other people and the Lord should take credit for just about every milestone in his long and impressive career. “The folks at the community rec center gave me a job when I was in high school, which instilled in me a strong work ethic and an understanding that community roots go just as deep as family, but only if you water them and help them grow. During undergrad, Professor Charles Greene pointed me towards law school so I could stay close to my new girlfriend Jackie at the time, who is now my wife of over 40 years and the mother of my children,” Duane said.

Duane continued. “Thanks to Mr. Greene, I secured a place to live, acceptance into Akron’s law school, and a job clerking for a prominent judge. That judge, the Honorable Joseph D. Roulhac, taught me how to think and love the law. And my mother, Ernestine Cox, well she was behind the scenes every step of the way, telling me to never forget where I came from, and to work hard and be humble.”

Work/Life Balance

Not a homebody by a long shot, Duane leaves the house every morning at 10:00 a.m. for a walk or drive, no matter the weather. “I’m still a student of the 60s and 70s,” Duane says through a grin. “I’m a hippie kinda guy and I love a good nature walk.”

Tuesdays are Duane’s library days. He spends hours reading and researching for both pleasure and legal practice. Wednesdays and Sundays are church and volunteering days. On Fridays, he’s at the firm’s offices in either downtown Cleveland or Euclid.

Whenever he can, Duane spends his free time striking up conversations with strangers and loved ones, dropping nuggets of wisdom like the following: “No matter what chapter of life you’re in, you have to maintain your sense of whatever you think is right or wrong,” Duane said. “If we’re all going to get along with each other, we must refrain from criticizing each other directly. If you disagree with someone, speak your mind in a way that begs accountability for that person’s actions, not their character. We’ve come a long way since I was a young man, but we still have a long way to go, and it all starts with understanding each other and resolving our differences in a way that allows us to move forward, not backward.”

Duane Cox and NRS Injury Law

Duane’s values, principled stance, tireless work ethic, and his ability to relate to everyday working people and help them improve their material conditions are traits that align with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with the firm about your case, call 855.468.4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Duane coached youth baseball for 35 years and has been a longtime parishioner at Starlight Missionary Baptist Church. As an active member of the congregation, Duane volunteers in the church’s outreach programs and community betterment initiatives. “I’m at my best when I’m engaged in an organizing campaign or large-scale project,” Duane says. “Pastor Anthony L. Small gives me an assignment and I go do it. Yes I do love the Lord, but when the Lord comes knocking, I plan to tell him I ain’t home, because there’s still so much good work I gotta do.”

attorneys.name: Andrea L. Cozza
attorneys.practice_type: Alimony & Spousal Support Lawyers in Westerville, OH
attorneys.bio:
Andrea L. Cozza is a graduate of The Ohio State University where she attained a B.S. in Psychology. She subsequently received her Juris Doctorate from The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law along with a certificate in alternative dispute resolution from Moritz. Ms. Cozza is certified as a Specialist in Family Relations Law by the Ohio State Bar Association and is a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers. She also is certified as an arbitrator by the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers. Ms. Cozza has completed mediation training for domestic relations matters as well as additional mediation training in the area of domestic violence.

She is presently serving as vice-chair of the CLE Committee for the American Bar Association Family Law Section and assists in planning and implementing legal education programs for the section. She also serves as co-chair of the Paraprofessional Committee for the section, planning and producing a national symposium for family law paralegals annually through her role with this committee. Ms. Cozza is a member of the Delaware County, Ohio Domestic Relations Committee. In addition to representing parties in family law cases, Ms. Cozza serves as a Guardian ad Litem in domestic relations cases in Franklin County and Delaware County. In this capacity, she represents the best interests of children in divorce and juvenile custody cases.

Ms. Cozza has been honored as an Ohio Super Lawyer annually for 2017 through 2025. Ms. Cozza was also designated by Ohio Super Lawyers as one of the Top 25 Women in Columbus (2021-2024), Top 50 Columbus Super Lawyers (2022-2025), Top 50 Women Ohio Super Lawyers (2022-2025), and Top 100 Ohio Super Lawyers (2024-2025). She was previously designated as a "Rising Star" by Ohio Super Lawyers in 2010, 2012, 2013, 2015, and 2016.

In her community, Ms. Cozza is the Vice President of the Board of Citizens for Humane Action Animal Shelter ("CHA"), serves on the shelter's operations committee, and volunteers regularly with the care of the animals at the shelter. She also plays clarinet with the Westerville Community Band, enjoys spending time with her two Great Danes, and is an avid runner.

attorneys.bio:
Kyle, a Northeast Ohio native, has over 30 years of experience fighting for those seriously injured as a result of the carelessness and the negligence of others. Whether it be injuries suffered from a serious accident or wrongful death, Kyle works hard to get his clients fair and just compensation. He prides himself on treating his clients like family. "Most of those I help have never been through this process before. They know they need someone experienced who they can trust. They know they need someone to help make sure they are treated fairly. That is what I do."

Kyle has achieved significant verdicts and settlements in semi-truck accidents, motorcycle crashes and serious motor vehicle accidents, slip and fall cases and products liability cases. In his spare time, Kyle, currently and for the past several years, coaches high school travel baseball teams. Kyle has also been recognized by Ohio Super Lawyers as one of the best lawyers in Ohio.

attorneys.name: George S. Crisci
attorneys.practice_type: Employment and Labor Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
George S. Crisci joined Zashin & Rich Co., L.P.A. in March 2007. George has practiced employment and labor law in both the public and private sectors for more than 23 years. George is an OSBA Certified Specialist in Labor and Employment Law. Law and Politics and Cincinnati magazines named George an "Ohio Super Lawyer" in Labor and Employment law in 2004, 2005, 2006 and 2007.

George’s practice has encompassed a wide variety of subjects, including discrimination, retaliation and workplace harassment, unfair labor practices, collective bargaining, arbitration, wrongful discharge, and enforcement of restrictive covenants. He has extensive experience at all levels of federal and state court, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Ohio Civil Rights Commission, the Ohio State Employment Relations Board, and the National Labor Relations Board. He also has participated in more than one hundred arbitration hearings and negotiated numerous labor contracts in both the private and public sectors. In addition to an extensive private practice, George worked as in-house labor counsel for the Cleveland Public Schools.

George received his BA from the College of Wooster, where he graduated with Departmental Honors and Phi Beta Kappa, and his JD from Case Western Reserve University School of Law, where he was a member of the Case Western Reserve Law Review and graduated Order of the Coif.

George is admitted to practice law in the State of Ohio, the United States District Court for the Northern and Southern Districts of Ohio and the Eastern District of Michigan, the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court.

George has lectured frequently on many topics, including public sector labor and employment law, employment discrimination, workplace harassment, retaliation, wrongful discharge, collective bargaining, avoiding unfair labor practices, and proper evaluation, discipline and termination procedures.

George is a member of the American Bar Association’s Litigation, State and Local Government, and Labor and Employment Sections. Within the Labor and Employment Section, he is a member of the Committee on State and Local Government Collective Bargaining, where he serves as a sub-committee co-chair. Mr. Crisci also is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association and Cleveland Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Jake Michael Cropper
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jake Cropper is a trial lawyer known for taking on difficult cases and refusing to let insurance companies minimize the lives and injuries of his clients. Since 2024 alone, Jake has recovered more than $40 million in settlements and verdicts for injured people and families.

Jake represents clients in serious injury and wrongful death cases involving truck crashes, unsafe property conditions, dram shop liability, dog attacks, and other catastrophic injuries. He has helped resolve cases for $11.25 million, $11 million, $6 million, $4 million, $1.25 million, $1 million, and $1 million—results that provided stability, security, and accountability when clients needed it most.

One case best captures how Jake approaches his work. In 2025, he and co-counsel Lindsay Lawrence took a premises-liability wrongful death case to trial after the defense offered just $37,500 for the life of a 96-year-old, legally blind woman who fell from a nursing home window. Jake believed that offer was an insult to the woman and her family—and he refused to accept it. After two weeks in court, the jury returned a $3 million verdict, holding the nursing home accountable and delivering justice that the family had been denied.

Jake is also known for taking on cases where insurance companies try to blame the injured person. He has secured six- and seven-figure recoveries in heavily contested comparative-fault cases, including $1 million for a pedestrian struck while crossing the street on a dark, rainy night; $750,000 for a bicyclist accused of causing his own injuries; and $650,000 for a pregnant woman hit in a crosswalk after the insurer claimed she crossed against the signal. In each case, Jake exposed the flaws in the defense’s narrative and forced them to take responsibility.

What truly sets Jake apart is how personally he treats every client. He listens. He takes the time to understand what they are going through. Jake believes strong results come from real connection—because juries respond to truth, and truth comes from fully understanding a client’s story.

Jake’s empathy is rooted in his upbringing. His mother was a public-school teacher and union leader who taught him the importance of standing up for others. His work ethic comes from his background as a former college basketball player who grew up on a tobacco farm and spent summers working construction, pouring concrete and framing houses. He understands hard work, perseverance, and sacrifice—values that guide every case he handles.

For those facing life-altering injuries or the loss of a loved one, Jake brings not only elite legal skill, but open communication, trust, and genuine commitment. He fights to make sure his clients are treated with dignity, respect, and empathy—from the first call to the final verdict.

If you or someone you love has been seriously injured, you don’t have to face this alone. Call Jake to understand your options, what comes next, and how he can help—without pressure or obligation.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Brian Cugliari joined Neiman Law in July 2025 and brings with him six years of experience in affordable housing and community development. As Director of Operations, Brian oversees the firm’s administrative functions while also contributing to legal matters. A licensed attorney in the State of Ohio since 2013, he is excited to continue growing his practice in real estate law.

A native of east-central Ohio, Brian earned his bachelor’s degree in Accounting with a minor in Business Legal Studies from Miami University in 2010. He went on to earn both his Juris Doctor and MBA from the University of Toledo in 2013.

Before joining Neiman Law, Brian worked in public accounting with work that included a range of financial and tax credit programs, most notably the New Markets, Historic, and Opportunity Zone incentives. Brian also worked with an affordable housing developer that specialized in the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit. He is passionate about real estate projects that strengthen communities and brings that passion and expertise into his work at Neiman Law.

Outside of the office, Brian enjoys golfing, both playing and watching, and is a major fan of Cleveland sports, especially the Browns. He lives in Columbus with his two cats and relishes his role of uncle to his nieces and nephew.

Brian makes sure the Neiman Law office runs like a well-oiled machine and provides polished, knowledgeable service to the firm’s clients.

attorneys.name: Romney Cullers
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Romney Cullers is an experienced trial lawyer, trying complex cases in Ohio for over 25 years. He has obtained numerous multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements, including many on behalf of the families of children catastrophically injured during childbirth. In 2016, he obtained a settlement of $60,700,000.00 on behalf of a 16-year-old girl severely injured by a down power line. It is the largest settlement in Ohio history for injuries to an individual plaintiff.

Romney is a former president of the Cleveland Academy of Trial attorneys and is presently a Master Bencher in the Judge John M. Manos Inn of Court.

Romney is also a professor of law at Case Western Reserve University in the nationally-recognized Health Law Program. Over the 20 years that Romney has held academic appointments at Case Law School, he has taught courses in Medical Malpractice, Trial Tactics, and Appellate Advocacy.

Romney is a frequent speaker at continuing legal education seminars for attorneys, lecturing on legal topics relating to trial strategy, including cross examination of experts and use of demonstrative evidence in the courtroom.

Romney is recognized by his peers as a leader in the field, having represented the friends and families of judges, attorneys, law professors and physicians. He was born and raised in a small farming community in southwest Missouri. Romney worked his way through college and law school. He understands the value of hard work and appreciates the privilege of speaking up for those who have endured hardships.

We also want to congratulate him on becoming certified as a Civil Trial Specialist by the National Board of Trial Advocacy.

attorneys.bio:
Eddie is the newest attorney at the firm. He is a second generation lawyer. He has followed in his father's footsteps into private practice. His sister is also an attorney with the Seventh District Court of Appeals.

Eddie graduated from Youngstown State University with a Bachelor's of Science before going on to the University of Akron for Law School. During this time in law school, Eddie clerked for the Honorable R. Scott Krichbaum in the Mahoning County Court of Common Pleas. After receiving his Juris Doctorate, he successfully passed the bar in both Ohio and Georgia. attorneys.name: Juliette Gaffney Dame
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Office of Juliette Gaffney Dame
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Lebanon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Juliette Gaffney Dame is an experienced family law attorney dedicated to working with parties as they navigate through the foreign and emotional process of divorce, dissolution and custody. In this highly personal process, Juliette works to educate her clients on a multitude of options from mediation to settlement conferences to Guardian Ad Litems, with the absolute last option being litigation. Juliette is a trained mediator and former Guardian ad Litem herself so she knows the benefits of keeping a case out of the courtroom and children, especially, as far away from the contentious process. Juliette tries to put the parties more in control of the ultimate outcome. However, as a former prosecutor, Juliette is not one to shy away from taking a case to trial if that is the best option. As she will tell you in the initial consultation, "Each case is unique." While most cases will resolve by agreement, very few will go to trial and you always have to have someone that is a ready and zealous advocate for you and your children when that day comes. Juliette is trained in alternatives such as mediation and collaborative law and has a strong history of successfully complex end of marriage separation cases.

Juliette is an active member of the Cincinnati Collaborative Group which works together with financial and mental health professionals through a team-based approach to end the parties’ marriage based on goals and interests rather than through litigation.

Away from her practice, Juliette enjoys photography and running and watching her kids in whatever sports they have taken up, camera in hand. She recently completed her very first half marathon as she looks challenge herself outside of the office.

attorneys.name: Carla B. Davis
attorneys.firm_name: Carla B. Davis, Attorney & Counselor at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Child Support Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
In order to provide you with the best in service, I prefer to keep my practice local within the areas of Lucas County, Wood County, Fulton County and Ottawa County. Meeting with clients and maintaining regular contact helps me better understand their needs and how to assist in meeting those.

Family law often entails many difficult and stressful issues that tend to hit us the hardest when we are most vulnerable. Understanding the legal system and one's rights and responsibilities can help to alleviate some of the stress. A combination of a strong support system and a good family law attorney will help guide a person through what tends to be an emotional and difficult time.

For 33 years, I have practiced family law. My experience helping clients ranges from divorces and dissolutions, to premarital agreements, custody, and support. The goal is to assist clients in obtaining a reasonable and fair settlement. If an acceptable agreement cannot be obtained, then I will pursue and protect your rights in court.

Before I began practicing solo, I worked for a public interest law firm. There I advocated for basic legal equality and represented people who had been diagnosed with mental illnesses. In addition, I was a volunteer mediator for many years with the Citizens Settlement Dispute Program.

Not only am I a current member of the Toledo Bar Association, but I am admitted to practice in federal court.

I am very active in the Toledo Community. These are some of the associations I work with:

Board Member of National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI), Toldeo.

Board Member of Children's Right Collaborative: We provide safe and secure visitation and exchange services for families experiencing separation because of divorce or family break-up

Mentor through Sisters-in-Law Program, Mom's House: Sisters-in-Law is a group of female lawyers working towards the continued improvement of the lives of the moms and their children at Mom's House.

attorneys.name: Trevor R. C. Davis
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Guiding Clients to Victory Through Strategy, Compassion, and Communication

Born of humble beginnings, Trevor Davis grew up in a working-class family. He entered school and the professional world during three major nationwide events, the housing crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the tech bubble burst. All his life, he wanted to advocate for hardworking Ohioans of every stripe and background, and his lived experience showed him there was a critical need for attorneys who were willing to do just that.

The Problem-Solving of an Engineer Combined with the Strategic Acumen of a Talented Trial Attorney

Weeks after passing the bar, Trevor joined NRS Injury Law in November 2022 and immediately committed himself to the administrative and litigation aspects of workers’ compensation law. But even he couldn’t have predicted this outcome. Trevor had initially gone to school to become a computer technology engineer, though he’d dreamed of being an attorney since age 7.

“I’ve found it more than fascinating how similar these fields are,” said Trevor with a smile while reflecting on the moments that led him to today. “I’ve always had a mind for problem-solving, and in engineering we have our engineering process, which involves isolating the issue, finding information associated with the issue, coming to a conclusion, and implementing a solution. You can imagine my joy when I fulfilled my lifelong dream of going to law school and found the same strategies apply to law!”

Today, Trevor’s penchant for problem-solving, passion for the underdog, and professional ability to find common ground with anyone positions him to succeed in representing injured workers in Southern Ohio.

A Multi-Faceted Approach Wins the Day for Trevor’s Workers’ Compensation Clients

From the mock trials he excelled at in high school to the real thing today, Trevor’s greatest joy is in securing results for clients, and doing so as quickly and efficiently as possible. “The system as it stands right now doesn’t act in the injured workers’ best interests at all,” says Trevor. “It’s slow, cumbersome, and workers are up against powerful institutions. My role is to push back, and to do so as quickly and efficiently as possible. My goal is to get my clients the compensation and the care that they need and deserve.”

To Trevor, being a successful attorney is not defined by personal accolades, but by the results he gets for his clients. “That view is shared by everyone here at the firm,” Trevor added, gesturing to the offices around him. “The end goal at NRS Injury Law is to deliver results for clients. We do that by leveraging every resource we have and by utilizing a highly organized and tested team approach. It’s methodical and systematic on the backend, with no box left unchecked and no detail left undiscovered. And it’s compassionate, empathetic, and people-focused on the front end. It’s a unique, unprecedented approach, and it’s how we win for our clients.”

Community Impact

Trevor has prioritized giving back to the community since childhood. He grew up in a household that valued volunteer work, so some of his fondest memories are of working with United Way. Trevor carried those values into academia, serving as the Design and Advertising Chair for his fraternity’s involvement in Relay for Life. Trevor also founded and headed an organization called Flyers Against Drunk Driving. Trevor is still involved with United Way and Relay for Life today, and he volunteers at the Young Lawyers section of the Cincinnati Bar, who take pride in giving back to multiple organizations in Cincinnati as needs arise.

Work/Life Balance

“I’m a big walker,” Trevor says with a grin when anyone asks him what he does during his free time. But just as he is energetic and motivated in his career, Trevor also makes the most of every free minute in his “down” time. If he’s not walking the streets of downtown Cincinnati with his wife, Trevor’s playing pickleball, golfing, dining out, cooking a new meal, or writing. And always the problem-solver, Trevor can often be found doing handyman tasks around the house and at the homes of family members and loved ones.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Trevor Davis

Trevor succeeds in administrative hearings and litigation by communicating well with others and being respectful. He excels at developing cordial relationships with defense counsel and he prioritizes being prepared for every outcome. His love for problem-solving and his deep compassion for his community align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Trevor and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

My role is to push back, and to do so as quickly and efficiently as possible. My goal is to get my clients the compensation and the care that they need and deserve.”

To Trevor, being a successful attorney is not defined by personal accolades, but by the results he gets for his clients. “That view is shared by everyone here at the firm,” Trevor added, gesturing to the offices around him. “The end goal at NRS Injury Law is to deliver results for clients. We do that by leveraging every resource we have and by utilizing a highly organized and tested team approach. It’s methodical and systematic on the backend, with no box left unchecked and no detail left undiscovered. And it’s compassionate, empathetic, and people-focused on the front end. It’s a unique, unprecedented approach, and it’s how we win for our clients.”

Community Impact

Trevor has prioritized giving back to the community since childhood. He grew up in a household that valued volunteer work, so some of his fondest memories are of working with United Way. Trevor carried those values into academia, serving as the Design and Advertising Chair for his fraternity’s involvement in Relay for Life. Trevor also founded and headed an organization called Flyers Against Drunk Driving. Trevor is still involved with United Way and Relay for Life today, and he volunteers at the Young Lawyers section of the Cincinnati Bar, who take pride in giving back to multiple organizations in Cincinnati as needs arise.

Work/Life Balance

“I’m a big walker,” Trevor says with a grin when anyone asks him what he does during his free time. But just as he is energetic and motivated in his career, Trevor also makes the most of every free minute in his “down” time. If he’s not walking the streets of downtown Cincinnati with his wife, Trevor’s playing pickleball, golfing, dining out, cooking a new meal, or writing. And always the problem-solver, Trevor can often be found doing handyman tasks around the house and at the homes of family members and loved ones.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Trevor Davis

Trevor succeeds in administrative hearings and litigation by communicating well with others and being respectful. He excels at developing cordial relationships with defense counsel and he prioritizes being prepared for every outcome. His love for problem-solving and his deep compassion for his community align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Trevor and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

attorneys.name: Paul M. De Marco
attorneys.practice_type: Class Actions Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Paul M. De Marco is one of the founding members of Markovits, Stock & DeMarco. He is an Appellate Law Specialist certified by the Ohio State Bar Association and has handled more than 100 appellate matters, including cases before the Supreme Court of the United States, six federal circuits, and five state supreme courts.

Paul’s practice also focuses on class actions and other complex litigation. During his 25 years in Cincinnati, Paul has been actively involved in successful litigation related to the U.S. Department of Energy’s Fernald nuclear weapons plant, the Lucasville (Ohio) prison riot, Lloyd’s of London, defective Bjork-Shiley heart valves, Holocaust-related claims against Swiss and Austrian banks, the Bankers Trust derivative scheme, Cincinnati’s Aronoff Center, the San Juan DuPont Plaza Hotel fire, the Procter & Gamble Satanism rumor, the Hamilton County (Ohio) Morgue photograph scandal, defective childhood vaccines, claims arising from tire delamination and vehicle roll-over, racial hostility claims against one of the nation’s largest bottlers, fiduciary breach claims against the nation’s largest pharmacy benefits manager, and claims arising from the heatstroke death of NFL lineman Korey Stringer.

MOTIVATING FACTOR

“I’ve always loved crafting legal arguments and picking apart others’ arguments. MSD is great fit for me because it allows me to work on the research, writing, oral advocacy, and strategic aspects of a wide variety of complex cases with committed people who share my appreciation for the importance of paying attention to every detail, anticipating your opponents’ moves, and leaving no stone unturned in serving our clients.”

CREATING VICTORY

“Figuring out the law governing a case is like a mystery waiting to be solved. It calls upon all of a lawyer’s analytical skills and investigative instincts. I’ve won arguments because I was obsessed with reading and re-reading the language of a contract, statute, or case and noticed a word, phrase, sentence, or even a punctuation mark that no one else seemed to notice and was able to make something of it. I’m fortunate to work among people who share this obsession.”

attorneys.name: Lisa Carey Dean
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
Lisa Carey Dean joined Roderick Linton Belfance, LLP in 2008 and became a partner of the firm in 2015. Her legal work is focused primarily on family law with specialties including divorce, dissolution, prenuptial agreements, custody and support issues. She is a skilled litigator who represents clients and makes court appearances on their behalf in Summit, Portage, Stark, and Medina counties.

Lisa is a lifelong resident of Summit County, Ohio. She earned her undergraduate degree, with honors, from Kent State University and received her Juris Doctor from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law. While in law school, she received recognition for her outstanding performance in Criminal Procedure and was offered an Externship with the United States Attorney’s Office located in Cleveland. Lisa also participated in Moot Court competitions and was elected by her classmates as a Senator of the Student Bar Association.

Prior to beginning her private practice as an attorney, Lisa served the public in the appellate division of the Summit County and the Portage County Prosecutor’s Offices. While at the Portage County Prosecutor’s Office, Lisa wrote briefs in favor of the application of “Megan’s Law” (requiring sexually oriented offenders to register), and others that were ultimately argued before the Supreme Court of Ohio.

Lisa also served the public as Judicial Attorney to the Honorable Judge Judith A. Nicely (retired) of the Summit County Domestic Relations Court. She was acknowledged by Baldwin’s Ohio Practice on Domestic Relations Law for her assistance to Judge Nicely in the publication of the 2000 Edition of Chapter 19: Child Support.

After serving the public for a number of years, Lisa entered private practice as a trial attorney. She has accumulated a wealth of knowledge and experience during her past 18 years of practice handling complex litigation involving business valuations, real estate transactions, complex divisions of retirement and investment accounts, and many other multifaceted legal issues. She is also recognized in our community as a zealous and respected advocate for the rights of family members, including her noted work to advance the rights of same-sex marriage partners and parents. Lisa has also appeared and argued before the Ninth District and Eleventh District Courts of Appeals. Additionally, Lisa completed extensive training through a program created by the Supreme Court of Ohio to become a certified mediator. She uses this training to resolve countless matters by way of settlement, with the goal of saving time and money for her clients.

Lisa has remained very active in serving the Akron community throughout her legal career. Her past service to the Akron Bar Association includes: Chair of the Family Law Section, Member of the Commission of Judicial Candidates (three years), and speaker and presenter to the Akron Bar Association.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Michelle Lynn DeBaltzo earned her J.D. from Cleveland Marshall College of Law in 1997 following her 1993 graduation from John Carroll University where she had earned a B.S. degree in chemistry with a minor in political science. The analytical skills she developed in the study of chemistry help her to discover the facts in her clients' cases. Since passing the bar and becoming an associate attorney in 1997, she has gained the respect of the judges and of the district hearing officers before whom she represents her clients. That respect is earned every day based on her preparedness, honesty, and integrity. While she derives great satisfaction from the reputation she has developed, her greatest satisfaction comes from winning a case for a client.

Michelle has been assisting Social Security applicants since May 1989 in varying capacities. She began as a receptionist and secretary and advanced to law clerk while attending law school. Having worked her way up in the firm, she understands the Social Security and Workers' Compensation claim processes and their pitfalls. Additionally, working nearly every position in the firm, she understands how each staff position fits into the overall goal of winning a client's case.

Michelle is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association; the Cuyahoga County Bar Association; the National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives; and the Cleveland Marshall College of Law Alumni Association. Michelle is a passionate fan of the Cleveland Indians.

Ryan received a Bachelor of Science Degree in Economics from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio. He attended Law School at The University of Memphis, Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law, where he earned his Juris Doctorate Degree.

Ryan L. DeBra is a member of the Ohio Bar Association, Cincinnati Bar Association, Clermont County Bar Association and Warren County Bar Association. Ryan is admitted to practice law in the State of Ohio and United States District Court, Southern District Court and Southern District Court of Ohio.

attorneys.name: Max Dehn
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Max Dehn is a shareholder with Cavitch, and focuses his practice on business and employment litigation and counseling. He has represented clients in a variety of areas, including employment discrimination, wage and hour matters, non-compete litigation, business contract disputes, and class action defense in state and federal courts, as well as arbitration forums.

Max co-chairs the firm’s monthly employment law luncheon, and also provides counseling to business clients regarding their employment practices. Max has presented lectures to attorneys, business owners and human resources professionals on topics including non-compete contract litigation, and the Fair Labor Standards Act (the “FLSA”).

Max has also worked in successfully defending numerous class and collective actions. These include FLSA collective actions, Ohio Consumer Sales Protection Act class actions, and several large entitlement-based class actions brought against State of Ohio agencies, some of which were litigated over the course of ten years or more.

attorneys.name: James A. DeRoche
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
James DeRoche joined Garson & Associates in January, 2001. While attending Case Western, Jim served as an editor of the Law Review and was awarded the American Jurisprudence Awards in Civil Procedure, Evidence, Constitutional Law, Legal Research & Writing, Criminal Procedure, Real Estate Transactions & Finance, and Ethics and Labor Law.

After law school, Mr. DeRoche worked with a large Cleveland law firm, handling a variety of litigation matters including complex business litigation. He has extensive trial experience, having successfully tried cases in both federal and state courts, and argued cases before the Ohio Court of Appeals.

He also has experience representing investors in arbitration matters against brokerage firms. Jim served most recently as general counsel of a Solon company, where he assumed both business and litigation responsibilities, while maintaining an active outside litigation practice.

Jim has been practicing law since 1991, and brings extensive business litigation experience to our Firm.

My Story:

Jim DeRoche is a special kind of guy. Every June he faces the possibility of snow, rain, headwinds and blistering sunshine as he cycles swiftly and steadily around the whole state of New Hampshire for a cause he believes in.

Jim heads to the Granite State to participate in the three-day grueling Trans New Hampshire bike marathon to raise money for muscular dystrophy research. "The steep mountains we climb and the unexpected difficulties we encounter along the way are extremely challenging for a rider like me," admits Jim. "But I know these are truly insignificant compared to what children with Muscular Dystrophy face everyday of their sometimes brief lives. I'm grateful I can do some small part on their behalf each year."

Caring for people is not just something that Jim does on the open road. When he walks into his office at Seaman Garson LLC the dangerous twists and turns in Jim's path are the roadblocks put up by giant corporations and insurance companies. But he is always ready to charge into battle for his clients' best interests.

"As a business litigator my highly intense competitive nature serves me well," says Jim. "I'm at my absolute best rooting for the underdog and the downtrodden – those men and women who have been adversely affected by corporate greed. I see that they get their fair day in court and the settlement they deserve. I like winning much more than I like losing. Each case is an intellectual challenge – a testing of my wits against the other side."

Jim's sense of healthy competition has been the hallmark of his life. In high school he was an award winning wrestler and baseball star. He graduated with high honors from the University of Rochester where he was a political science major, and attended Case Western Reserve University School of Law. "I've always been interested in politics, so law school was a natural career for me," says Jim. "It's been very good fit."

When Jim is not preparing for marathon bike rides he enjoys reading literary and news magazines and novels. But family trumps everything. Jim's office is filled with pictures of his wife, daughters and family pets. "At the end of the day, my family means everything to me," grins Jim.

"I'm at my absolute best rooting for the underdog and the downtrodden – those men and women who have been adversely affected by corporate greed. I see that they get their fair day in court and the settlement they deserve. I like winning much more than I like losing. Each case is an intellectual challenge – a testing of my wits against the other side."

Jim's sense of healthy competition has been the hallmark of his life. In high school he was an award winning wrestler and baseball star. He graduated with high honors from the University of Rochester where he was a political science major, and attended Case Western Reserve University School of Law. "I've always been interested in politics, so law school was a natural career for me," says Jim. "It's been very good fit."

When Jim is not preparing for marathon bike rides he enjoys reading literary and news magazines and novels. But family trumps everything. Jim's office is filled with pictures of his wife, daughters and family pets. "At the end of the day, my family means everything to me," grins Jim.

attorneys.name: Deepak K. Desai
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Deepak was born and raised in greater Cincinnati. He graduated from Covington Latin School in 1984 and went to college at Northern Kentucky University. There, he became a leader in the University Honors Program and received the prestigious Exemplar Award his senior year.

After graduating from NKU, Deepak attended the Salmon P. Chase College of Law. As a first-year law student, he won the award for Best Oral Advocate at the annual Moot Court competition. He continued to excel throughout his law school career and graduated number one in his class.

After law school, Deepak entered the business world. There he learned the ins and outs of running a closely held business with four locations across the Midwest, and that generated seven million dollars annually in revenue.

For the past 20 years, Deepak has used the hands-on knowledge he gained in the business world to help business clients meet all their legal needs. From contract negotiation to commercial litigation, Deepak has a unique skill set that protects his clients' interests.

Deepak also practices law in the public sector and has represented multiple villages, cities, and townships throughout Ohio. His unique legal knowledge regarding real estate, zoning, eminent domain, and the legislative process provides significant value to business clients dealing with local governments, as well as public entities engaged in economic development and infrastructure improvement.

For the past 10 years, Deepak has focused his employment law practice on advising employers during the pre-termination process and counseling them on various federal and state laws such as the FMLA, the ADA, and the Equal Pay Act. He is also retained by national insurance companies to defend employers they insure against discrimination and wrongful termination claims, as well as to assist with charges filed with the NLRB, the EEOC, and the Ohio Civil Rights Commission.

attorneys.practice_type: Labor and Employment Litigation Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Michael DeWitt counsels and defends clients in a diverse range of insurance related issues with an emphasis on ERISA litigation and life, health and disability claims consulting. His experience includes representing clients in claims regarding breach of contract and bad faith as well as the pursuit of punitive damages involving both ERISA-governed and individual plans. Mr. DeWitt both defends and advises on policy wordings, business practices and regulatory matters.

Mr. DeWitt has extensive experience in representing clients in a wide range of complex litigation including, including subrogation matters, securities-related disputes and trying arbitration cases before the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (formerly the National Association of Securities Dealers). During his career, he has also assisted clients in employment matters related to the enforcement and defense of non-compete provisions. Mr. DeWitt provides clients with a unique perspective to the challenges and issues confronting the industry, having spent several years as both an insurance agent and a licensed securities broker.

In addition to his legal practice, Mr. DeWitt is an adjunct professor of legal research and writing at Capital University Law School’s ABA-accredited paralegal program. He previously served as a research editor of the university’s Law Review.

attorneys.name: Nicholas A. Dicello Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Nicholas DiCello joined the Spangenberg firm as an associate attorney in 2004. Nick graduated "magna cum laude" from the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law in 2002 where he served as managing editor of the Cleveland State Law Review. While an editor, he authored and published No Pain, No Gain, No Compensation: Exploiting Professional Athletes Through Substandard Medical Care Administered By Team Physicians, 49 Clev. St. L. Rev. 507 (2001). The article focuses on medical malpractice issues in the professional sports industries and earned Nick multiple honors for his work in the field. Prior to joining Spangenberg, Nick served as law clerk to the late Judge John M. Manos of the United States District Court of the Northern District of Ohio.

Nick is licensed to practice law in Ohio in both state and federal court and is a member of the Cuyahoga Metropolitan Bar Association. He is an active member of the Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys, the Ohio Association for Justice and the American Association for Justice. The publishers of Law & Politics® magazine named Nick a "Rising Star" in 2006, 2007, 2009 and, 2010.

Since joining the Spangenberg firm, Nick has successfully litigated and resolved a diverse spectrum of matters on behalf of his clients. In addition to cases involving personal injury, insurance bad faith and civil rights violations, Nick focuses a significant portion of his practice on business litigation... bankruptcy litigation and serving as special litigation co-counsel on behalf of debtors and unsecured creditors and on commercial insurance disputes. Nick also focuses a portion of his practice on serving as counsel in various class actions.

Nick hails from the Cleveland area and graduated from Hawken Upper School in 1994. He attended Lehigh University in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, where he obtained a B.A. in Earth and Environmental Sciences and graduated with honors. As a Division I college soccer player, Nick earned widespread recognition as a goalkeeper, including Academic All-American honors. Upon graduation, he played professional soccer with the Cleveland Crunch for three years and was a member of the 1999 N.P.S.L. championship team.

attorneys.bio:
Christopher Diedling is a Partner in the law firm of Cornetet, Meyer, Rush & Stapleton whose practice is concentrated in the areas of Estate Planning and Probate Administration. Chris offers a free consultation to get started. Please contact Mallory at 513-672-6122 to schedule your consultation.

Chris was selected by Super Lawyers as a 2024 Rising Star! Being selected to Rising Stars is limited to a small number of attorneys in each state. As one of the few attorneys to earn the distinction of Rising Stars, Chris has earned the respect of peers as one of the top-rated attorneys in the nation.

Chris is an educator to his clients when it comes to every aspect of Estate Planning. Chris counsels clients about the available Estate Planning tools and helps them make the best and most practical decisions for their circumstances.

Chris is a 2017 graduate of the University of Cincinnati College of Law where he was awarded the Judge John W. Peck Trial Practice Award for excellence in Trial Advocacy. As a member of UC Law’s Trial Practice Team, Chris won the Texas Young Lawyer’s Association’s (TYLA) Regional Trial Practice Competition in 2017 and in 2016. Chris represented UC Law at the TYLA Nation Trial Practice Competition in both years. Chris was also involved with UC Law’s Moot Court Team. While in law school, Chris worked as a law clerk for the United States Attorney’s Office in the Southern District of Ohio. Chris was also a Fellow at the Ohio Innocence Project. Through all of these experiences, Chris has developed a sharp advocacy skill set and a strong will to be an exceptional legal advocate for his clients.

Chris and his wife Casey live in Over-the-Rhine in Downtown Cincinnati. He enjoys being active, hiking in the great outdoors, playing sports, and CrossFit training. Chris loves going to Cincinnati Reds games, concerts, music festivals, exploring local breweries, and traveling.

attorneys.bio:
Jon M. Dileno joined Zashin & Rich Co., L.P.A. in 2007. Jon represents employers in the full spectrum of labor and employment matters in both the public and private sector. Jon serves as chief negotiator for some of the most high profile labor negotiations in Ohio. He has worked as management’s chief negotiator in labor contract negotiations with a wide variety of unions such as the UAW, IBEW, AFSCME, OPBA, IAFF, Steelworkers and Teamsters.

Jon’s experience in collective bargaining matters extends beyond negotiating labor contracts and covers the full gamut of collective bargaining proceedings. He has defended private employers and public entities in lawsuits involving collective bargaining agreement disputes, unfair labor practices, and other labor-related issues.

Jon’s employment law litigation experience is also extensive and varied. He has successfully defended both private employers and public entities in numerous cases involving discrimination, retaliation, wrongful discharge, intentional tort, and defamation.

Jon earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from Baldwin Wallace College, cum laude. He earned his law degree from Tulane University, cum laude, where he received the Outstanding Labor Law Student Award. He also taught Public Sector Labor Law at Cleveland State University as part of the University’s labor relations certificate program. Jon was also named as a Top Attorney in Ohio for 2009 in the Super Lawyer Section published by Cincinnati Magazine.

Jon is admitted to practice law in the State of Ohio, the United States District Court for the Northern and Southern Districts of Ohio, the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court. He is also a member of the Labor and Employment Relations Association and the Cleveland Bar Association.

The Early Years

Shawn Dingus was born and raised in Flatwoods, Kentucky, a small town located in the eastern region of the state. His father worked as a railroad employee for C&O Railroad, Chessie System and CSX Transportation, and his mother cleaned homes and businesses on a part-time basis. After graduating from Russell High School with honors in 1990, he was the first in his family to attend college, choosing to attend Morehead State University on a scholarship.

Undergraduate

As a student at Morehead, Shawn Dingus was very involved in student government, including serving as president of his fraternity, Lambda Chi Alpha; serving as executive vice-president of the IntraFraternal Council; and running for office in the Student Government Association. In 1994, he was named the university's Greek Man of the Year, for his dedication and commitment to the fraternal system at the university. He graduated from Morehead in 1994 with a bachelor of arts in government and a minor in philosophy.

Law School

In 1995, Shawn Dingus elected to attend the University of Akron School of Law, where he continued to serve in student government, first as treasurer of the Student Bar Association and next as president of Phi Delta Phi Legal Fraternity. Shawn Dingus was also appointed to serve as the law school's representative to the American Bar Association in 1997 and served as its representative at the ABA National Convention in San Francisco, California, in 1998. In that same year, he received his juris doctorate from Akron, graduating in the top 10% of his class, with a cum laude distinction.

Career

Upon graduation and passage of the state bar exam in 1998, Shawn Dingus accepted a position as an assistant prosecuting attorney in Morrow County, Ohio. He initially served the county as the prosecutor assigned to prosecute juvenile delinquency cases and represent the Morrow County Children Services Agency in cases involving abused and neglected children. He was later assigned to the adult criminal division, where he prosecuted adults charged with misdemeanors and felonies, which ranged from simple speeding violations to aggravated murder.

In 2000, Shawn Dingus left the prosecutor's office and accepted an associate position with The Plymale Partnership in downtown Columbus, where he represented individuals in civil matters, which included representation in bad faith actions against insurance companies and wrongful death actions. During his tenure at The Plymale Partnership, he served on the board of the Franklin County Trial Lawyers Association and was presented with the Association's Slugger Award in 2002 for his dedication and commitment to injured victims and their families.

In 2003, Shawn Dingus decided to set out on his own and opened his own law firm, The Law Office of M. Shawn Dingus. In 2009, Shawn Dingus joined Columbus attorney Ronald Plymale to form the firm of Plymale & Dingus, where he represents individuals and small businesses in civil and criminal matters. He has had the honor of representing hundreds of individuals and businesses in cases ranging from wrongful death actions to divorce and child custody matters.

Shawn is involved in his community by serving on numerous professional and political boards and committees as well as volunteering for various causes. He is a Board of Trustees member for the Central Community House and also serves on the Board of Directors of the American Constitution Society. He is also a member of the First Congregational Church in downtown Columbus.

attorneys.name: James J. Disantis
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jim Disantis is a valued associate at Cavitch bringing a comprehensive background in legal support and client-facing roles. With over a decade of hands-on experience as a paralegal, Jim has developed a deep understanding of legal processes, particularly in the areas of estate planning, probate administration, and business organization.

Prior to becoming an associate, Jim was a paralegal at Cavitch and previously at Smith & Condeni LLP, where he was responsible for drafting a wide range of documents including Wills, Trusts, and Powers of Attorney. Jim has extensive experience managing complex probate and trust administrations from start to finish, including preparing and filing Federal Estate and Gift Tax Returns. His skills also include direct communication with clients and courts, filing documents across Ohio, Florida, and Pennsylvania, and preparing business organization documents for entities nationwide.

Jim's practical experience is complemented by a strong academic foundation. A graduate of Cleveland State University College of Law, he also holds an ABA-approved Post-Degree Certificate in Paralegal Studies from Cuyahoga Community College and a B.A. in Communication from Cleveland State University, where he graduated cum laude. His unique blend of technical legal knowledge, communication skills, and diverse professional experience in administrative and customer-service roles provides a well-rounded perspective for addressing clients' needs.

Jim's interests outside of work include spending time with his wife and two children. He is a proud supporter of his children's passions, regularly attending their theater performances and sporting events.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Medical Malpractice: Plaintiff Lawyers in Mayfield Heights, OH
attorneys.bio:
Marilena DiSilvio joined Elk & Elk Co., Ltd., as a partner, in 2014. A former registered nurse and experienced trial attorney, Marilena's practice focuses on birth injuries, medical negligence and personal injury. Prior to joining Elk & Elk, Marilena spent 17 years with a leading Cleveland defense firm, where she was a member of the firm's Executive and Management committees and served as chair of the Health Care Law Practice group. Marilena has tried more than 50 medical malpractice cases. Her extensive experience serving the defense bar has provided her with invaluable knowledge regarding medical malpractice and health care law.

Marilena has been recognized as an "Ohio Super Lawyer" every year since 2009, listed in Best Lawyers in America, and elected to the American Board of Trial Advocates. Super Lawyers Magazine has named her to several lists, including the Top 50 Women Ohio Super Lawyers from 2010-2017; Top 25 Women Cleveland Super Lawyers for 2012-2017; Top 50 lawyers in Cleveland for 2012-2017; and Top 100 lawyers in Ohio for 2011-2017. She has also been recognized by Marquis "Who's Who of American Women."

In 2013, Marilena was named President of the Ohio Women's Bar Foundation, the charitable arm of the Ohio Women's Bar Association. She also served as the Co-Chair of the 2014-15 Leadership Institute.

Marilena is a Founding Member of the Ohio Advisory Group to the National Museum of Women in the Arts in Washington, D.C., serves on the board of The Gathering Place and as co-chair of the Development Committee.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey A. Dittmer
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Gahanna, OH
attorneys.bio:
Born in Lorain, Ohio, on April 18, 1962, Mr. Dittmer graduated from The Ohio State University (B.A. 1984), and Capital University Law School (J.D. 1988). He is admitted to practice in Ohio and the US District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.

A former bailiff and staff attorney in the Franklin County Common Pleas Court, Mr. Dittmer focuses his practice on civil and criminal litigation, including the prosecution of personal injury, products liability and wrongful death claims. Mr. Dittmer's experience in criminal defense law includes all aspects of misdemeanors and felonies - including white collar and business crime. He represents both individuals and businesses in his civil and criminal practice. As a trial attorney, he has tried many jury and bench trials to verdict throughout the state of Ohio. He has also presented oral arguments before the 5th and 10th District Courts of Appeals. Trustee of Hampsted Village Homeowners Association. Counsel to dozens of homeowner and condominium associations throughout Ohio.

Notable Engagements

Obtained $4 million jury verdict as co-counsel in a medical malpractice case for physician's failure to properly diagnose stomach cancer.

Obtained $4.3 million settlement of a product liability claim against a major automobile manufacturer.

Obtained $1.3 million jury verdict in a premises liability claim later set aside when motion for judgment notwithstanding the verdict was granted by the trial court.

Obtained $1 million settlement for plaintiff who suffered traumatic brain injury in automobile accident.

Obtained $250,000 settlement for plaintiff who suffered mild traumatic brain injury in automobile accident.

Obtained $150,000 settlement for minor plaintiff who lost finger in ATV accident.

Successfully defended a liquor control/police officer in an 11-count theft in office prosecution in state court, who was found not guilty on all counts.

Successfully defended two Delaware County corporations against claims of intentional tort and negligence for the death of an employee after the trial court granted summary judgment in favor of both corporations.

Case results depend upon a variety of factors unique to each case. Case results do not guarantee or predict a similar result in any future case.

Dittmer, Wagoner & Steele, LLC serves clients throughout Ohio.

attorneys.bio:
Mark Dlugopolsky began his law career in Colorado running a general law practice handling a variety of criminal and civil matters. Upon returning to Ohio in 2013, he began to practice exclusively in Social Security disability law.

Working for a nationwide disability law firm Mark travelled all over the United States attending administrative hearings throughout Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, New York, Maine, Indiana, Tennessee, and Maryland. attorneys.name: Michael J. Duber
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Michael Duber brings excellence to Bentoff & Duber in fields of workers' compensation and social security disability law. In his nearly 40 years of experience in litigating workers' compensation matters, which Michael would consider his forte, he has extensively explored every avenue of this legal field.

Since Michael took control of the firm in 1990, it has tripled in size, with its client base growing at even greater levels. Even with the extensive growth, Michael's focus remains on giving personal attention to his injured and disabled clients who come to him for help.

Michael's respect in the field of workers' compensation law is evident as he has served as the President of the Workers' Compensation Section of the Cleveland Bar Association (now known as the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association) and is a former professor at the Ohio Paralegal Institute where he taught administrative law. He has also served on both the Workers' Compensation and Grievance committees of the Cuyahoga County Bar Association, upholding the standards of lawyers in our community.

Michael was awarded the Ohio Super Lawyers acclaim in 2015 - 2023 consecutively and was included in the fourth edition of Marquis Who's Who in American Law. He also served as Special Counsel to the Office of the Attorney General, State of Ohio.

Active in other legal professional groups, Michael is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association where he serves on the Workers' Compensation Section committee. He is also a member of the Ohio Association for Justice, Cleveland Association of Compensation Attorneys, American Civil Liberties Union and National Organization of Social Security Claimant's Representatives (NOSSCR).

Michael received his Bachelor of Science degree from The Ohio State University in 1970 and his Juris Doctor from The University of Cincinnati College of Law in 1973 where he published numerous articles for the school paper on workers' compensation issues. He is admitted to practice law in Ohio and Colorado state courts and the United States District Court.

Michael's accomplishments extend outside of work, where he has served as Chairman of the Orange Community Schools and Recreation Commission and was instrumental in passing one of the most successful recreation levies in Orange School District history. He was also President of the Orange Community Athletic Association where he led the development of a newly created program for special needs athletes allowing them to participate in numerous sporting activities.

In his free time Michael is an avid outdoorsman. He loves to fly fish and when not representing the injured and disabled, you can find him in the rivers and streams in Ohio, Montana and Colorado looking for steelhead and trout while in the winter his attention turns to snow skiing.

attorneys.name: Brandon T. Duber
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Brandon Duber brings a wealth of both civil and criminal law experience to Bentoff & Duber. Currently he focuses his practice on workers' compensation, personal injury, criminal defense and medical malpractice. He represents those individuals accused of committing a crime, whether it be a serious felony, DUI or minor misdemeanor, as well as those who are injured through a work accident, car accident or while receiving medical treatment. His exceptional trial experience and relentless aggressive work-ethic make him an invaluable asset to the firm. He truly works tirelessly to make sure our clients receive the best results available, sacrificing all he has to his cases.

Prior to joining the firm, Brandon first worked as a Prosecutor with the Cuyahoga County Prosecutor's Office where he first-chaired complex criminal litigation. As a prosecutor he tried more than forty felony jury trials and dozens of bench trials. Spending nearly every day in the courtroom, Brandon earned the respect of judges and attorneys alike. During his tenure with the prosecutor's office, Brandon gained national media attention on Court TV and Dateline NBC while successfully prosecuting an individual accused of capital murder. He also fine-tuned his appellate experience, drafting dozens of briefs and arguing those briefs before the court of appeals.

Brandon then moved to Denver, Colorado where he joined a prominent boutique law firm, specializing in personal injury and construction defect litigation. He represented an assortment of clients in the construction industry, ranging from subcontractors to general contractors in both commercial and residential projects, and was involved in all phases of personal injury litigation, including auto accidents.

Super Lawyers, a rating service honoring outstanding lawyers, has named Brandon to its Rising Stars list for years 2013 – 2019 and to the Super Lawyers list for years 2022 – 2026.

Brandon received his Bachelor of Arts from Skidmore College in Saratoga Springs, NY in 2001, and his Juris Doctor from the Case Western Reserve University School of Law in Cleveland, Ohio in 2005. He is admitted to practice in Ohio and Colorado state courts, as well as United States District Courts. He is an active member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Ohio Association for Justice and the Cuyahoga Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

When not in the courtroom, you can usually find Brandon on the golf course, riding his Harley in the summer or searching the country for a mountain to ski in the winter. Brandon is a passionate skier, learning to ski at the age of three, and is a former professional ski instructor. He of course also enjoys spending time with his dog, Cameron.

attorneys.name: Robert M. Dumes
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law (Divorce and Dissolution) Lawyers in Middletown, OH
attorneys.bio:
Robert Dumes practices primarily in the areas of Family Law (divorce and dissolution), Personal Injury, Criminal Defense, and Probate and Adoption matters. Currently, he is “of counsel” at Hurley Law, and is licensed throughout the State of Ohio. Mr. Dumes handles legal matters not only in Butler County, but also in the surrounding counties of Hamilton, Warren, Preble, and Montgomery.

With over 42 years of experience, including working as a magistrate in the Domestic Relations Court of Butler County and serving as a prosecutor in Middletown, Mr. Dumes is committed to working and serving his clients and to providing his clients with the highest quality legal service based on understanding their needs and objectives.

Clients benefit from his experience working for and practicing with learned practitioners and Judges over the years. During his time in law school, Mr. Dumes served as the law clerk for the Honorable Fred B. Cramer, who at the time of his passing, had served as a Common Pleas Judge in the State of Ohio for more than 40 years.

Additionally, Mr. Dumes was previously engaged in the practice of law with two distinguished jurists: The Honorable James E. Walsh who served as the Fairfield Municipal Court Judge and as a Judge on Ohio Twelfth District Court of Appeals before his retirement, and the late and Honorable David J. Niehaus who served as the Butler County Probate Judge before becoming the Butler County Juvenile Court Judge.

attorneys.name: Daniel G. Dutro
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Dan practices primarily in the areas of commercial and residential real estate, contract drafting and negotiation, and not-for-profit and tax-exempt organizations. He has also assisted clients with issues involving labor and employment, bank financing documentation, foreclosure, domestic relations, and collections.

In his real estate practice, Dan has advised his clients on commercial and residential real estate transactions. He has drafted and negotiated purchase and sale agreements, development agreements, leases, easements, and covenants and restrictions, along with advising and addressing title and survey issues. In his practice, Dan has represented a large multinational retail chain on its development and redevelopment projects throughout Ohio and Kentucky, including site development for new store locations and negotiations with municipalities.

He also assists an international transportation services company in the review of requests for proposal for its operations throughout North America. In addition, as a former tax consultant with one of the large public accounting firms, Dan has advised hospitals, educational institutions, public charities, and private foundations on their tax and operational concerns, including obtaining tax-exempt status recognition with the IRS, analysis of unrelated business income concerns, and tax return compliance.

A long-time resident of Cincinnati, Dan is involved in various community service activities. He volunteers as a reader at the Cincinnati Association for the Blind and Visually Impaired, a lector at the Community of the Good Shepherd Catholic Church, a volunteer at Montgomery Community Church, and as a tutor at John P. Parker Elementary School through the Cincinnati Youth Collaborative. He also sits on the Board of his neighborhood’s homeowner’s association.

Dan earned his undergraduate degree from Yale University and his law degree from the University of Cincinnati College of Law.

attorneys.bio:
With over seventeen years of intensive courtroom experience, Attorney Heather Dyer has the expertise necessary to confidently and effectively represent Northeast Ohio clients in all aspects of family and juvenile law including prenuptial agreements, divorce, dissolution, collaborative divorce, legal separation, custody, establishment of parental rights and responsibilities, child and spousal support, Civil Protection Orders, adoption, grandparent’s rights, third-party custody, LGTBQ family rights, name changes, juvenile dependency, neglect and abuse cases and juvenile delinquency matters.

Since 2002, she has served as a Guardian ad Litem for hundreds of minors advocating for their best interest in custody matters in both family and juvenile courts. Heather serves as a mediator for any type of legal matter. Since 2015, Attorney Dyer represents less than four percent of Ohio lawyers as an Ohio State Bar Association Certified Family Law Specialist.

Heather strives to meet her clients’ goals in an efficient and cost-effective manner, providing personalized attention and individualized guidance. She can provide the best strategy for negotiated resolutions, contentious cases or collaborative matters. She will be there every step of the way, fighting for you and finding viable solutions.

Heather primarily serves clients in Summit, Cuyahoga, Medina, Portage, Stark, Lake and Geauga counties.

Heather is originally from Central Ohio. After graduating from college, she migrated to Florida to enjoy the sunshine and attend law school, eventually returning to Northeast Ohio to practice law and raise her family- Jett (20), Thalia (19) and Rory (15). She resides in Akron with her youngest son and when she isn’t following to the gym and ballfields, she can be found hiking the amazing local parks and trails or following the diverse music scene.

With over seventeen years of intensive courtroom experience, Attorney Heather Dyer has the expertise necessary to confidently and effectively represent Northeast Ohio clients in all aspects of family and juvenile law including prenuptial agreements, divorce, dissolution, collaborative divorce, legal separation, custody, establishment of parental rights and responsibilities, child and spousal support, Civil Protection Orders, adoption, grandparent’s rights, third-party custody, LGTBQ family rights, name changes, juvenile dependency, neglect and abuse cases and juvenile delinquency matters.

Since 2002, she has served as a Guardian ad Litem for hundreds of minors advocating for their best interest in custody matters in both family and juvenile courts. Heather serves as a mediator for any type of legal matter. Since 2015, Attorney Dyer represents less than four percent of Ohio lawyers as an Ohio State Bar Association Certified Family Law Specialist.

Heather strives to meet her clients’ goals in an efficient and cost-effective manner, providing personalized attention and individualized guidance. She can provide the best strategy for negotiated resolutions, contentious cases or collaborative matters. She will be there every step of the way, fighting for you and finding viable solutions.

Heather primarily serves clients in Summit, Cuyahoga, Medina, Portage, Stark, Lake and Geauga counties.

Heather is originally from Central Ohio. After graduating from college, she migrated to Florida to enjoy the sunshine and attend law school, eventually returning to Northeast Ohio to practice law and raise her family- Jett (20), Thalia (19) and Rory (15). She resides in Akron with her youngest son and when she isn’t following to the gym and ballfields, she can be found hiking the amazing local parks and trails or following the diverse music scene.

attorneys.name: Marisa Dyson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in West Chester, OH
attorneys.bio:
Marisa Dyson focuses her practice in the areas of workers compensation and domestic law. Additionally, she maintains a broad practice in other areas of the law as well with experience in Corporate Litigation, Estate Planning and Personal Injury. Marisa has experience representing both injured workers as well as employers in workers compensation disputes. Marisa enjoys advocating for families and helping clients navigate their way through complex family law issues as well.

Marisa graduated at the top of her class, magna cum laude from Salmon P. Chase College of law in 2014. During her time at Chase she was a Chase Fellow, IOLTA Fellow, research assistant and worked at the Children’s Law Center advocating for children involved in domestic disputes as well as educational rights of children in poverty. She also received the Henry Clay Merit Scholarship, competed in the Bettman Moot Court Competition, attended the Peggy Browning Labor Rights Conference and was on the Dean’s list every semester.

Marisa also works with Project HOPE, an affiliate of ACA, which is a non-profit organization that works to help victims of Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Human trafficking. In her spare time she enjoys spending time with her husband and four children, serving on school boards, volunteering with her children’s extracurricular activities as well as competing in triathlons.

attorneys.firm_name: Eadie Law Nursing Home Injury Lawyers
attorneys.practice_type: Nursing Home Abuse Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
At Eadie Law Nursing Home Injury Lawyers, we stand united in our Cleveland office with a singular purpose: Championing the rights of families affected by nursing home negligence. We are deeply entrenched in the Cleveland community, and we bring our collective skills and dedication to every case we handle. As we navigate the complexities of nursing home law, we maintain transparent and honest communication, ensuring that our clients are fully informed at every turn.

We are efficient attorneys who focus on cases of abuse, neglect and injury within nursing homes and assisted living and group home settings. We have a proven track record of securing accountability for wrongful acts leading to severe injuries or even the tragic losses of loved ones. Our experience extends to cases involving bedsores, falls, sexual and physical assault, elopement and medication errors.

Residents of nursing homes require special care as they are vulnerable and need consistent care, attention and support. Even the slightest neglect may cause fateful accidents or irreversible damage. William Eadie, our CEO, understands how corporations are selfish in their need to drive profits instead of prioritizing quality care for their consumers.

We believe in taking a personalized approach to each case, providing guidance and support that extends beyond the courtroom. Our ultimate fulfillment comes from not only achieving justice for our clients but also contributing to safer standards of care for all.

If you seek a law firm that truly understands the stakes of nursing home litigation in Ohio, Eadie Law Nursing Home Injury Lawyers will be your unwavering ally. For your convenience and ease of access, we offer free initial consultations and virtual appointments. You can contact us at any of our Ohio offices, in Cleveland, Cincinnati, Akron, Columbus, and Toledo.
