attorneys.name: Ben Eberly
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Troy, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Ben Eberly is a native to the Miami Valley having lived in Troy, Piqua and Tipp City. He graduated from Tippecanoe High School and then attended Miami University for undergraduate studies. Upon graduation from Miami University, his education continued at the University of Dayton School of Law where he earned the prestigious CALI award in the area of Civil Trial Practice.

After law school, Attorney Eberly relocated to Pennsylvania to begin his practice of law. While in Pennsylvania, Attorney Eberly honed his legal skills focusing on areas of Civil Litigation including personal injury, Workers' Compensation and Social Security Disability Claims. In 2007, Attorney Eberly joined the law firm of Edgar Snyder and Associates where he served as the firm's attorney for Workers' Compensation and Social Security for northwestern Pennsylvania. While in Pennsylvania, Attorney Eberly helped hundreds of people with injury claims, Workers' Compensation claims and Social Security Disability claims. He was three times named a Pennsylvania Super Lawyer Rising Star and was named an Ohio Super Lawyer Rising Star in 2013.

Attorney Eberly has now returned "home" to the Miami Valley and is a founding partner of Klein, Tomb and Eberly (2010-2018) and Waite, Tomb and Eberly (2018-present). Eberly has now been named an Ohio Super Lawyer Rising Star and will continue to focus on Civil Litigation, Personal Injury, Workers'Compensation and Social Security Disability Claims. He has recovered millions of dollars for his clients over his 20 plus years of practice. Ben is also an active member of the community serving as a member of both the Tipp Monroe Optimist Club and the Tipp City Rotary Club. He also sits on the Miami County Bar Association's Ethics and Grievance Committee and has served as Treasurer, Vice President and President (2017).

attorneys.name: Molly A. Ebraheim
attorneys.firm_name: Nurenberg, Paris, Heller & McCarthy Co., L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Molly Ebraheim joined Nurenberg, Paris, Heller & McCarthy during the opening of the firm’s Toledo office, bringing her deep roots in the community and a passion for helping individuals who have suffered personal injuries. Born and raised in Toledo, Ohio, Molly is committed to advocating for her neighbors and ensuring they receive the legal support they deserve during some of their most challenging times.

Molly’s academic foundation began at DePaul University, where she earned a Bachelor of Science in Biology with a focus in Pre-Medicine. She went on to earn a Master of Business Administration (MBA) with a concentration in Health Care Systems Management from the University of Toledo. She then graduated from the University of Toledo College of Law in 2017, where she concentrated on health law to further enhance her ability to navigate complex medical-related cases.

Molly’s strong science background gives her a unique ability to understand the medical intricacies of personal injury cases. Whether handling traumatic brain injuries, spinal cord damage, or complex orthopedic conditions, she excels at translating complex medical data into clear, persuasive legal arguments. This expertise allows her to collaborate effectively with medical professionals to ensure her clients receive the care they need and the compensation they deserve.

Driven by a genuine desire to make a meaningful impact on the lives of her clients, Molly combines her legal expertise with her scientific knowledge to provide personalized, strategic representation. With her deep connections to Toledo and unwavering commitment to justice, Molly is a dedicated advocate for the community she calls home.

attorneys.name: Robert Edelstein
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Collections Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
A sole practitioner in Cleveland, Ohio, Mr. Edelstein focuses his practice in the areas of commercial collections, landlord/tenant law and corporate matters. Mr. Edelstein received his undergraduate degree from Tulane University (BA 1980) and his J.D. (1983) from Case Western Reserve University School of Law. Mr. Edelstein is a member of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association and admitted to practice in the State of Ohio. After law school, Robert spent two years as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Ohio.

Upon entering private practice, Robert was appointed Special Counsel to the Attorney General's office, helping pursue collections on behalf of the State of Ohio. Since its founding in 1997, the Robert's practice has concentrated on helping businesses collect outstanding receivables & judgments. The firm also helps clients with credit applications, contracts and preparing other documents used in the course of conducting its daily business. In addition, Robert represents landlords in both residential and commercial properties in the eviction and collection process.

As many creditors know, obtaining a judgment is only the beginning of the battle. Through years of experience Robert has learned to use many tools of modern technology to help locate assets and places of employment. In addition, Robert's office uses the most up to date collection software to help keep track of your files, calculate accruing interest and allow for efficient preparation and filing of post judgment collection documents. A successful collection attorney understands the many options available to collect money, whether through bank attachments, wage garnishments or having judgment liens filed which attach to debtor's real estate.

Robert's practice focuses on handling matters throughout the State of Ohio, but he can also work with you in placing files around the country and monitoring local counsel's progress.

Collection matters can be handled on either a contingent or hourly basis, to discuss what works best for you contact Robert for a free consultation. As a sole practitioner, you will always deal with Robert directly.

attorneys.name: Carie Marsh Ehrenborg
attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Lawyers in Canal Winchester, OH
attorneys.bio:
Adoptions are emotional, sensitive, and intensely complex matters. The process is laden with rules and laws and is a paramount life decision. I strive to provide compassion while advocating through the process. Each client and case is unique. I aspire to respectfully meet the individual needs of each client.

I am a Solo practitioner focusing on Adoption and Child Welfare Law. I was an Assistant City Prosecutor from 1993-1998, with a brief stint as a defense attorney. I was a Staff Attorney at Children Services from 1998-2004, where my responsibilities included advising and representing the Adoptions Department. I opened my law practice in 2004, and have focused solely on adoptions and child welfare cases. My clients are varied in that I represent prospective adoptive parents, expectant/birth parents, and some adoption agencies. A portion of my practice involves adoption subsidy matters.

Having my own practice has afforded me the flexibility to be available for my family, while still caring for my clients.

I travel the entire State of Ohio to represent clients.

I strive to provide compassion while advocating through the process. Each client and case is unique. I aspire to respectfully meet the individual needs of each client.

I am a Solo practitioner focusing on Adoption and Child Welfare Law. I was an Assistant City Prosecutor from 1993-1998, with a brief stint as a defense attorney. I was a Staff Attorney at Children Services from 1998-2004, where my responsibilities included advising and representing the Adoptions Department. I opened my law practice in 2004, and have focused solely on adoptions and child welfare cases. My clients are varied in that I represent prospective adoptive parents, expectant/birth parents, and some adoption agencies. A portion of my practice involves adoption subsidy matters.

Having my own practice has afforded me the flexibility to be available for my family, while still caring for my clients.

I travel the entire State of Ohio to represent clients.

attorneys.name: Brian N. Eisen
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice/Wrongful Death Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Brian Eisen graduated magna cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa from Harvard College in 1988, where he majored in neurobiology. He earned his law degree from Harvard Law School in 1992, graduating cum laude. During law school, Mr. Eisen was a member of the environmental law review, and was awarded the prestigious Addison Brown Prize for Legal Writing. After graduating, Mr. Eisen earned the highest score on the following Ohio Bar Examination.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Eisen spent a year as a law clerk for the United States Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit, and then spent three years as a trial attorney for the United States Department of Justice in Washington, D.C., where he prosecuted white collar fraud cases. Mr. Eisen gained some notoriety when he took on Philip Morris in a case alleging that tobacco companies were violating prohibitions on television advertising by the strategic placement of billboards at sports venues. That case led to the removal of "The Marlboro Man" and other tobacco advertising from NFL, MLB, and NBA stadiums and venues around the country. It also whet Mr. Eisen's appetite for taking on big, well-funded litigation opponents.

Since joining the firm in 1996, Mr. Eisen has focused his practice on cases of medical negligence and wrongful death. He has been first chair trial counsel in more than 15 medical malpractice cases, and he has obtained dozens of multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements on behalf of his clients. Mr. Eisen also has won cases in the Courts of Appeals, as well as the Supreme Court of Ohio. He is licensed to practice in Ohio and Washington, D.C.

Mr. Eisen spent several years as a member of the Ohio Board of Bar Examiners, where he drafted questions and graded answers for the Ohio bar examination. Mr. Eisen also is a past chair of the Medical Negligence Committee of the Ohio Association for Justice, and past president of the Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys. As a result of his experience and success, Mr. Eisen has been invited to speak at various seminars on litigation, trial procedure, and medical negligence.

In his spare time, Mr. Eisen coaches baseball and soccer. His teams regularly are regarded as mediocre. He does not intend to "give up his day job."

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mayfield Heights, OH
attorneys.bio:
David is the Senior Partner of Elk & Elk in Cleveland, Ohio. As an Ohio personal injury lawyer, he has represented thousands of medical malpractice and wrongful death victims throughout the state for nearly 50 years. Dave believes that quality legal representation allows all people to level the playing field against the big insurance companies. He has devoted his entire professional life of almost five decades to helping injured people receive the compensation they deserve.

Dave began his professional career with one of the largest and most prestigious personal injury law firms in Ohio and spent his first seven years under the wing of Ohio's best. After practicing on his own for several years, his entrepreneurial spirit got the better of him and he ventured into a practice with his brother Art, whom together built geographically one of the largest injury practices in the state of Ohio.

When Dave isn't representing the rights of injury victims, he spends his time being an active husband, father and grandfather to his wife Marilyn, three children, granddaughters Meredith, Madison and Celia, and grandson Dylan. Dave is also a lifelong Cleveland Indians fan, and frequently attends games with family and friends.

Settlements and Verdicts

$1.3 Million Settlement – Motor vehicle accident results in multiple fractures

The Defendant went left-of-center and struck Plaintiff. The Plaintiff suffered a fractured pelvis, left knee and femur, head laceration and shattered left elbow.

$690,000 Settlement – Motor vehicle accident results in serious injury, subsequent surgery

The 72-year-old Plaintiff’s vehicle was struck by the Defendant’s pick-up truck. The Plaintiff’s ankle had crushing injuries, requiring surgery.

$500,000 Settlement – Slip and fall results in broken hip, subsequent surgery

The Plaintiff fell on a step at a restaurant and suffered a broken hip, requiring multiple surgeries.

$300,000 Settlement – Motorcycle collision results in head injury, fractures, subsequent surgery

The Plaintiff was riding a motorcycle when the Defendant traveled left in front of him. The Plaintiff suffered a closed head injury and two broken wrists, requiring surgery.

$82,000 Settlement – Motorcycle collision results in multiple fractures

The Plaintiff, who was riding his motorcycle, was rear-ended by the Defendant. He sustained bruised eyes, a fractured nose, right knee injury, sprained right ankle, fractured right toe and needed 12 stitches to the forehead.

All lawsuits are different and Elk & Elk makes no representation or promises that it can obtain the same results in other cases. These results do not guarantee, warrant, or predict the outcome of any future legal matter. You should consult an attorney for advice regarding your individual situation.

Arthur is the Managing Member of Elk & Elk in Cleveland, Ohio. As an Ohio personal injury lawyer and medical malpractice lawyer, he has represented medical malpractice and wrongful death victims for almost five decades. Art, just two years out of law school, was elected Ashland Ohio's County Prosecuting Attorney for two successive four-year terms. After having been the youngest prosecuting attorney in the state of Ohio, Art chose to leave the public sector and enter the private practice of law. Art has found great satisfaction in providing injury victims with quality legal services in all major areas of injury law.

When Art is not representing the rights of injury victims, he enjoys spending time with his wife and four children.

Read more about Arthur Elk of Elk & Elk Co., Ltd.

Settlements and Verdicts

$3.5 Million Settlement - Incorrectly holding a patient to carbon dioxide instead of oxygen

74-year-old Plaintiff underwent cardiac surgery at a hospital. Immediately following the procedure he went directly from the operating room to the ICU. Elk & Elk’s medical malpractice lawyers settled the case out of court for $3.5 million.

$1.8 Million Settlement - Botched sinus surgery results in cognitive delays and chronic headaches

16-year-old Plaintiff was suffering from pansinusitis. The Defendant physician undertook surgical correction of this problem. Plaintiff’s experts and the defense acknowledged that with appropriate surgery, this chronic and diffuse sinus problem could be corrected.

attorneys.name: Austin J. Enger
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Passionate About Labor Law, Dedicated to Helping Injured Workers

From working the family horse farm to servicing automobiles at his father's tire shop, Austin Enger developed respect and admiration for labor at a young age. While attending Cleveland State University, Austin started as a business major, but his roots quickly drew him to courses in labor relations, collective bargaining, and human relations. “Working for my father at the tire shop and then coming home every day to our horse farm, which was a full-time job in and of itself, it all really inspired me to go into a field where I could help workers,” said Austin, reflecting on his trajectory from his youth to his career at NRS Injury Law.

A Passion for Helping Workers, Realized in a Profession in Workers' Comp Law

Austin graduated cum laude from Cleveland State University in 2017. While in college, Austin realized the best way he could build on the strong foundation his upbringing had given him would be to pursue a career in labor law. So, from Cleveland State, he went on to the University of Akron School of Law, where he graduated magna cum laude with a Juris Doctorate in 2020. After receiving his Certificate in Health Law, Austin wasted no time leveraging his passion for labor to help workers who had been injured while on the job. In fact, while he was still in his graduate program, Austin got a head start on his career in law by clerking part-time at NRS Injury Law from 2018 to 2020. When he passed the bar in 2020, the firm offered him a position as Associate Attorney, and Austin immediately came aboard.

Relentless Advocacy Leads to Results for Clients

Austin thrives on discovering the details and specifics of his client's unique situation and then building a case from there. “The legal system so often tries to lump labor law and workers’ comp cases into one-size-fits-all categories,” says Austin. “My mission as a workers’ comp attorney is to overcome that. My clients’ stories matter. Their goals matter. Their injuries matter. Their love for their job’s matters. I feel like I am doing my best by them when I am able to listen, learn, understand their situation, and then tirelessly advocate for them until we get the result they want.”

A Personal Mission Aligned with the NRS Injury Law Vision

Austin's mission is to find unique and effective ways to represent his clients. Known for asking questions and showing true interest in his clients, Austin's first question is always, “What are your goals for this case?” Austin fits right in at NRS Injury Law because his attitude, approach, work ethic, and passion for helping clients align perfectly with the firm's vision of “An elite team zealously advocating for justice for every client by practicing the art of constant compassion, striving for excellence, and acting with integrity, patience, and professionalism.”

Work/Life Balance

Passionate About Labor Law, Dedicated to Helping Injured Workers

From working the family horse farm to servicing automobiles at his father's tire shop, Austin Enger developed respect and admiration for labor at a young age. While attending Cleveland State University, Austin started as a business major, but his roots quickly drew him to courses in labor relations, collective bargaining, and human relations. “Working for my father at the tire shop and then coming home every day to our horse farm, which was a full-time job in and of itself, it all really inspired me to go into a field where I could help workers,” said Austin, reflecting on his trajectory from his youth to his career at NRS Injury Law.

A Passion for Helping Workers, Realized in a Profession in Workers' Comp Law

Austin graduated cum laude from Cleveland State University in 2017. While in college, Austin realized the best way he could build on the strong foundation his upbringing had given him would be to pursue a career in labor law. So, from Cleveland State, he went on to the University of Akron School of Law, where he graduated magna cum laude with a Juris Doctorate in 2020. After receiving his Certificate in Health Law, Austin wasted no time leveraging his passion for labor to help workers who had been injured while on the job. In fact, while he was still in his graduate program, Austin got a head start on his career in law by clerking part-time at NRS Injury Law from 2018 to 2020. When he passed the bar in 2020, the firm offered him a position as Associate Attorney, and Austin immediately came aboard.

attorneys.name: Bryn Ericksen
attorneys.practice_type: Mechanical/Aerospace Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Bryn Ericksen combines her background in mechanical engineering with her legal training to counsel clients on protecting and leveraging their intellectual property. She focuses her practice on patents and related IP strategies, drawing on both her technical insight and her experience assisting businesses with legal and compliance needs.

Bryn earned her J.D. from the University of Cincinnati College of Law, where she served as Vice President of the Intellectual Property Law Club and authored an article that appeared in The University of Cincinnati Intellectual Property and Computer Law Journal (“That’s Going to Leave a Mark: The Effect of Trademark Law on Colleges and Universities,” Volume 8, Issue 1; February 6, 2023). In law school, Bryn gained valuable client-facing experience through UC’s Entrepreneurship and Community Development Clinic, assisting small businesses with transactional and compliance matters. She also externed with the University of Cincinnati’s Office of Innovation, where she conducted prior art searches, reviewed inventions, and supported technology transfer efforts—an experience that confirmed her commitment to patent law.

Before law school, Bryn earned a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Iowa State University. Her technical experience includes designing a medical device prototype as part of her senior capstone project and working as a full-time engineering co-op at Meyer Tool Inc., where she collaborated with engineers on production processes. This blend of engineering and legal training enables her to evaluate innovations from both technical and regulatory perspectives.

A former Division I varsity swimmer, Bryn brings discipline, perseverance, and focus to her practice. At Wood Herron & Evans, she works with innovators, entrepreneurs, and companies of all sizes to safeguard their intellectual property and support their growth.

attorneys.name: Christopher Carl Esker
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
PRACTICE AREA AND PROFESSIONAL EXPERTISE

Christopher C. Esker 's practice is primarily focused on insurance defense, complex litigation, commercial litigation, personal injury actions, and general appeals with Akron's Roderick Linton Belfance, LLP, and one of Northeast Ohio's most storied firms, founded in 1885.

Mr. Esker joined the firm in 2008 following a decade as a member of Buckingham, Doolittle and Burroughs’ litigation practice group and his dedicated public service as a Summit County Assistant Prosecutor, Judicial Attorney to Judge Mary Spicer, Summit County Court of Common Pleas, and Judicial Attorney to Judge John W. Reece, Ohio Court of Appeals, Ninth Judicial District. Augmenting his litigation practice, he serves as District Counsel to the Akron, Bath and Copley Joint Township Hospital District in the area of public finance.

Mr. Esker has a depth of experience in courtrooms statewide, including municipal, state, and federal courts, and has served as a hearing officer, mediator, and arbitrator. He has represented clients in Ohio’s Northern and Southern Federal District Courts, in the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, and in the United States Supreme Court, as well as many of Ohio’s common pleas and appellate courts and the Ohio Supreme Court. He has also served clients in venues beyond Ohio through pro hac vice admission in several courts and tribunals.

Mr. Esker has been honored by his peers through his Martindale-Hubbell AV® Preeminent rating, and has been tapped as an Ohio Super Lawyer® every year since 2012. He has been recognized repeatedly Recognized by "Inside Business Magazine" as Leading Lawyer in Northeast Ohio as voted by his peers, and he has also been designated a Best’s Recommended Insurance Attorney annually since 2013.

Mr. Esker has been an active member of the American, Ohio State and Akron Bar Associations, and has served on many committees, including the Attorney Grievance, Common Pleas and Appellate Court, Continuing Legal Education, and Scholarship Committees, as well as the Judicial Evaluation Commission. He is also an active member of the community at large, and has served as a member of the Bath Township Comprehensive Plan Review Committee, Bath Township Historical Preservation Committee, Copley Township Board of Zoning Appeals, Copley Township Audit Committee, Community Advisors for the Reserve, Copley, Ohio, and the St. Hilary School Board, served as president of the Summit County Farm Bureau Board of Trustees and the Weathervane Community Playhouse Board of Trustees, and recently completed a three-year term as a member of the Board of Trustees for the Habitat for Humanity of Summit County, Inc.

attorneys.name: Ellen Essig
attorneys.practice_type: Adoption Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
With over 30 years of experience, Ellen has developed a niche practice in collaborative reproduction and fertility law. She represents clients worldwide with their surrogacy and other family-building needs, including those relying on egg, sperm in embryo donation to achieve their goals. Ellen represents hopeful parents including singles, couples and LGBTQ+ clients. Ellen was proud to serve as co-counsel in the marriage equality case of Obergefell v. Hodges et.al which was successfully argued before the U.S. Supreme Court in April 2015. Over the years, Ellen has helped thousands of hopeful parents bring a child into their home, Ellen also provides legal advice to medical clinics involved in third-party reproduction. In addition, she provides legal advice to matching programs which help hopeful parents in their journey towards parenthood.

Ellen's practice began as an adoption practice at a time when IVF was still in its infancy. In 1993, Ellen became a Fellow of the American Academy of Adoption Attorneys. As IVF and other third-party reproduction technologies advanced, the landscape changed. Parents now had additional options. In 2009, Ellen was a founding member of the newly established American Academy of Assisted Reproductive Technology Attorneys. In 2016, these two Academies combined and are now known as the Academy of Adoption and Assisted Reproductive Technology Attorneys (AAAA). As a Fellow of this Academy, Ellen works with other experienced attorneys across the country and around the world.

Because of her experience and reputation, Ellen is frequently called upon to lecture to hospital personnel and physician groups about this emerging area of the law. Her assistance is often requested in developing office practices. Ellen has been called upon as a witness in cases concerning third-party reproduction and has been interviewed by various news sources when issues about surrogacy or third-party reproduction.

Ellen is licensed to practice law in Ohio and Michigan. Since 2001, Ellen has been designated as AV rated by Martindale Hubbell which recognizes the highest ethical standards and legal ability within the legal community. Ellen is proud of this accomplishment and does all that she can to maintain that reputation including returning phone calls promptly, completing projects on time and continuing her education is this developing area of law. Ellen is thoughtful about the interests of all parties involved in this process and always mindful of her clients' goals.

attorneys.name: Madalyn J. Fairbanks
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in West Chester, OH
attorneys.bio:
At the outset of her career, Madalyn worked as an Assistant District Attorney in Bristol County, Massachusetts, where she investigated and prosecuted complex financial cases throughout the county. During her tenure at the DA’s office, Madalyn assisted in building the Financial Crimes Unit from the ground-up – establishing strong connections with citizens, local businesses, legal professionals, and local and federal law enforcement.

After relocating back to Ohio, Madalyn worked for the Ohio Attorney General’s Office where she representeddivisions within Ohio EPA and the State Fire Marshall in civil environmental enforcement actions in all aspects of

litigation across Ohio. During her tenure at the Ohio Attorney General, Madalyn received a letter of recognition forher work on a high-profile case, against a Cincinnati-based company that engaged in decades-long environmentalviolations.

After a successful career in government, Madalyn entered private practice with a specialized focus in family law matters. Madalyn has successfully represented clients in courts across Butler, Warren, and Hamilton County. Madalyn sees the value in collaborative law and has experience negotiating complex and highly contested cases. However, she also has the requisite trial skills to effectively advocate for her clients in a courtroom when needed.

attorneys.name: James D. Falvey
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jim Falvey has over 20 years of experience in litigating cases. He has tried numerous cases to verdict and has also successfully negotiated multiple cases to seven figure settlements for his clients.

For the past 12 years, Jim's practice has focused on personal injury and workers' compensation cases. During that time, he has tried personal injury, wrongful death, medical malpractice and workers' compensation cases to juries in Cuyahoga, Lake, Summit, Mahoning and Licking Counties.

Jim graduated from John Carroll University in 1997, where he obtained a degree in Communications. He then graduated from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law in 2001. During law school, Jim worked as a law clerk in the Cleveland office of the Ohio Attorney General, assisting in the workers' compensation division. He is a member of the Ohio Association for Justice and the Lake County Bar Association.

Outside of work, Jim lives in Mentor, Ohio with his daughters Sadie and Sienna. He coaches his daughters' softball teams in the summer and fall.

attorneys.name: Anthony Scott Farren
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Inspired to Help Injured Ohioans Through a Career in Injury Law

Anthony “Scott” Farren is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on personal injury law. Scott has decades of experience in Ohio personal injury law and has successfully argued cases at the Eighth District Court of Appeals. Committed to advocating for people who have been wrongfully injured, Scott commits to his cases and does not let up until his clients achieve victory.

A Lifetime Dedicated to Representing Victims of Wrongful Injury

Scott grew up in Medina County, where he began working in the trades as soon as he entered high school. During summer break, Scott painted houses, churches, and fences, quickly learning the value of hard work and a job well done. He played three sports during the school year, graduated in 1988, and went to Bowling Green State University, where he worked in the cafeteria during the school year and at the Medina County Fairgrounds during summer.

“I like to say I ‘bring the news,’” says Scott, reflecting on the life experiences that shaped his approach to the legal profession. “I’ve always had a very straightforward, tactical, detail-focused approach to my work, which gives me the tools I need to represent my clients effectively in their personal injury cases.” Scott added that his early years in the trades and working-class roles gave him an appreciation for everyday Ohioans, a worldview that Scott holds to this day when working with injured people who are up against powerful insurance companies.

Building Foundations for Winning Cases with Communication, Honesty, and Strategy

Scott has won countless personal injury cases throughout his several decades in the legal profession, all the while honing his knack for communication, strategy, case-building, and a matter-of-fact, straight-shooting approach to the practice that puts his clients at ease and makes it easier for them to understand the nuances of Ohio personal injury law.

“My own abilities are magnified tenfold thanks to working at NRS Injury Law,” Scott added, pointing out that the most effective attorneys are those who are backed by a stellar firm. “The attorneys at this firm have paralegals, case managers, and assistants supporting them, and with the team support, resources, and our ability to get our questions answered and collaborate with other attorneys, plus the sheer commitment everyone at the firm has to zealous client advocacy, all of that combined leads to a firm where each attorney is able to leverage their own unique talents to the absolute max.”

Work/Life Balance

Born in Cleveland, raised in Medina County, and now back in the Cleveland area (Broadview Heights), Scott is an Ohio family man at heart. As his children love music, Scott spends his downtime going to concerts with his kids and listening to music at home. “I like to support my kids’ music interests, and of course, I’m a sports fan loyal to the Cavs, Browns, and Guardians,” Scott says. “My wife and I travel when we can, and I’ll never say no to a few rounds of golf on the weekends.”

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Anthony Scott Farren

“NRS Injury Law provides impeccable service,” Scott said in closing, reflecting on why he accepted a position at the firm. “The firm is consistent, and they put communication with the client as a top priority, which means the client is fully brought in and made a member of the team for the duration of their case. NRS Injury Law makes clients feel like they haven’t been abandoned.”

Committed to helping people who don’t have the resources or legal knowledge to advocate for themselves, Scott’s values and integrity align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Scott and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Dedicated to advocating for people who’ve been wrongfully injured, Scott understands the value of helping others and supporting his fellow community members. Throughout their sons’ upbringing, Scott and his wife took their children to food banks to show them the meaning of service. Scott also coached high school basketball while working on his undergrad.

attorneys.name: Michael J. Feldman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Willoughby, OH
attorneys.bio:
Michael J. Feldman supervises the Personal Injury and Criminal practices at Lallo & Feldman. He lives in Orange Village with his wife, Rhonda, and they have raised two children. Mr. Feldman is an active member of his community, from coaching youth sports to being a long-standing board member and volunteer for his Temple. A Cincinnati native, Mr. Feldman graduated cum laude from the University of Cincinnati in 1973. He continued his education at Boston University Law School where he received his Juris Doctorate degree in 1976.

Mr. Feldman relocated to Cleveland and was admitted to the Ohio Bar in November of 1976. Soon thereafter, he joined the Cuyahoga County Court of Common Pleas as a staff attorney for two Judges. After two and a half years, he left the Court to begin practicing law, and has been with his partner, Ernie Lallo since then.

Mr. Feldman has handled thousands of personal injury and criminal cases, gaining valuable experience in many Court trials. Experience of working in the Court system laid the foundation for a successful, professional relationship with many Cuyahoga County Judges, bailiffs and Court personnel, as well as Judges in other counties including: Ashtabula, Lake, Summit, Portage, Geauga, Lorain, and Medina. Additionally, over 27 years of handling personal injury cases has helped me develop a mutually respectful relationship with insurance defense counsel, as well as hundreds of insurance adjusters."

It is necessary to educate clients as much as possible about how the legal system works. This can eliminate many client fears, which builds trust. Trust is an important cornerstone of a positive and fruitful relationship between us and our clients.

Carol began her legal career in 1985 as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Ohio; she then served as a judicial clerk for Justice Clifford F. Brown, Supreme Court of Ohio. She then moved into the private practice of law and established a primary focus in family law. Carol’s practice includes divorce, dissolution, collaborative divorce, and custody matters for both LGBTQ and traditional clients, along with non-traditional family law matters such as formation and dissolution of LGBTQ and other unmarried relationships, parenting and custody matters unique to LGBTQ relationships, and family legal planning document preparation (wills, health care powers of attorney, and related planning).

Now that LGBTQ marriages are recognized throughout the country, Carol happily facilitates same-sex couple adoptions, stepparent adoptions, and parentage actions to confirm parentage of children born to married same gender couples (for whom a biologically based “presumption” of spouse’s parentage may not be recognized). Carol pioneered the establishment of shared custody for LGBTQ and other unmarried parents beginning in 1997, which laid the groundwork for the Ohio Supreme Court’s affirmation of that practice. In honor of that work, Carol was awarded the Stoney Award by Stonewall Union. Carol also represented the first non-biological mother to obtain shared custody over the objection of the biological-mother, despite the lack of any formal written agreement.

Carol was the first Chair of the Columbus Bar Association’s LGBT Committee, is a member of Temple Beth Shalom where she also plays piano, and formerly served as an elected member and President of the Bexley School Board. She is a frequent speaker on LGBTQ legal issues.

attorneys.name: David L. Firestine
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
Dave serves as general outside counsel for privately held businesses. In that role, he interacts with business owners and c-suite executives daily, helping them to mitigate risk, capitalize on opportunities and navigate problems when they arise.

Dave has significant experience advising clients on start-ups, mergers, acquisitions, transactions and strategic planning across a multitude of business sectors. Recognized for his candor, pragmatism and business acumen, Dave has served on the Board of Directors of both for-profit and non-profit organizations and has organized Advisory Boards for clients in multiple industries.

In addition to his business practice, Dave represents clients in residential and commercial real estate transactions and disputes, including land use planning and zoning disputes. Dave also advises clients on general estate planning including wills, trusts and business succession planning. Since 2020, Dave has served as the Law Director for Copley Township and its 17,000+ residents.

Dave is a graduate of Leadership Akron Class 24 and is a Fellow of the Akron Bar Foundation. He was selected as an "Ohio Super Lawyers" for 2022, ’23, ’24, '25 and '26 and an "Ohio Super Lawyers - Rising Star" for 2009, ‘10, ’11, ’12, ‘13 and ‘14 by Law & Politics Magazine and Cincinnati Magazine/Cleveland Magazine in the practice areas of real estate and business/corporate.

In his free time, Dave enjoys watching high school sports and spending time outdoors with his wife and two children.

attorneys.name: Emmaline R. Fisher
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Emmaline R. Fisher is a bankruptcy attorney serving the greater Cincinnati area, dedicated to helping individuals and families regain financial stability and move forward with confidence. She combines a strong analytical background with a client-focused approach, guiding clients through complex financial situations with clarity and compassion.

Emmaline earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Cincinnati College of Law. During law school, she served as Publications Editor for the University of Cincinnati Law Review, where she managed a team of editors and ensured the accuracy and quality of published legal scholarship. She was also actively involved in student organizations, including serving as Vice President of Patent Law for UCincyIP and Treasurer of Adventure JDs.

She earned her undergraduate degree in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering from the Georgia Institute of Technology. Her engineering background gives her a detail-oriented, problem-solving mindset that she now applies to helping clients navigate bankruptcy and financial challenges.

Before becoming an attorney, Emmaline gained extensive legal experience in the Cincinnati area. As a law clerk with Cummins Law LLC, she conducted legal research, drafted memoranda, and performed document review. She also worked as a legal intern with the University of Cincinnati Patent & Trademark Clinic, where she drafted provisional patent applications, conducted prior art searches, and met directly with clients to understand and protect their ideas.

Her additional legal experience includes working with the University of Cincinnati Office of Innovation, where she evaluated the commercial viability of inventions and drafted patent claims, as well as serving as a research assistant focusing on tort law, informed consent, and emerging legal issues involving artificial intelligence. She also served as a summer law clerk for Judge Molloy in Kenton Circuit Court, gaining valuable insight into both civil and criminal proceedings in the Northern Kentucky region.

Prior to her legal career, Emmaline worked in engineering and industry, where she managed projects, conducted technical analysis, and worked with clients in complex environments. This background allows her to break down complicated legal and financial concepts into clear, practical guidance for her clients.

Today, Emmaline focuses her practice on bankruptcy law, representing clients throughout the Cincinnati area and surrounding communities. She is committed to providing personalized attention, clear communication, and practical solutions to help her clients achieve a fresh financial start.

When Emmaline isn’t assisting individuals get a fresh start and financial freedom, you might find her at Ault Park walking her gorgeous pup, Penny. She also enjoys taking part in the Queen Bee marathon and the Flying Pig marathon.

attorneys.practice_type: Public Housing Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Tom Fisher is a business attorney. He provides practical advice to a wide range of clients in Kentucky and Ohio including start up and well established businesses, non-profit organizations and government entities. His guidance assists clients in assessing and prioritizing business, operational and legal issues and enabling them to make decisions to accomplish their goals. His clients seek his advice as general counsel to make business and legal decisions which have long-term implications. His experiences range from assisting start up and emerging businesses and well established business on all topics including entity selection, raising capital and financing, tax issues, mergers and acquisitions, developing compensation models, employment issues and incentives, family succession and estate planning, exit strategies for business owners, regulatory compliance, negotiating commercial leases and contracts, negotiating financing agreements, landlord tenant issues, licensing and protection of intellectual property and real estate development.

Tom also has served as general counsel to a local public housing authority in Kentucky. In this capacity he has assisted his client in all aspects of its operations under state and federal law, including the administration of a federal HOPE VI grant used for developing new housing opportunities by integrating housing into the community and redeveloping existing urban housing stock. He has negotiated and closed numerous HOPE VI/mixed public and private financing transactions, negotiated the acquisition and sale of real estate, and assisted in the creation of affiliated entities used by his client to develop affordable housing opportunities.

attorneys.bio:
David A. Fitzgerald II is a Partner at Wood Herron & Evans and focuses his practice on various areas. For his patent practice, David focuses on patent prosecution and opinion work in the technical fields of mechanical and aerospace engineering, for example, in technologies such as food preparation and handling, energy generation and drilling technologies, industrial cleaning systems, liquid dispensing, tire technologies, aircraft flight controls and air conditioning systems, cryogenic refrigeration systems, and wind turbine systems. For his trademark and licensing practice, David principally focuses on game designers and game companies in both digital and tabletop games, serving clients that range from small independent startups to larger studios. David joined Wood Herron & Evans in 2007 and has been practicing in these areas full time since 2008. In 2012, Mr. Flesher graduated from the Ohio State University with a Bachelor's Degree in Political Science.

attorneys.name: Robert J. Foley Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Heller, Maas, Moro & Magill Co., LPA
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Youngstown, OH
attorneys.bio:
The firm's chief litigator, Robert J. Foley, is a passionate champion of underdogs seeking just compensation for work-related injuries.

A Youngstown native, Foley attended Hubbard public schools and graduated from Hubbard High School. He received a B. A. degree in political science and philosophy from Youngstown State University in 1993, graduating magna cum laude. He then enrolled at the University of Akron School of Law and combined his legal studies with a full-time law clerk job at Heller, Maas, Moro & Magill. He then joined the firm as an attorney after receiving his J.D. in 1998.

Foley's practice focuses solely on representing working people seeking workers' compensation and Social Security disability benefits. He handles these claims at every step of the process, but is also the firm's primary litigator when cases make it to the hearing stage or go to court.

"I like standing up for what I believe is just," Foley says. "And I've always liked debating and trying to convince people."

A lifelong devotee of martial arts, Foley brings a well-honed fighting spirit to his work on behalf of clients. While he relishes the competitive aspects of law, however, he is equally drawn to its crucial quieter sides - analytical research and effective writing.

In his spare time, Foley maintains a longstanding interest in underground music - he once published his own music fanzine - and continues to practice martial arts. He holds Black Belts in Chinese and Japanese martial arts and works and trains on a regular basis.

attorneys.name: Paige Forwerck
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Paige is an associate attorney at Mockensturm, Ltd. with a primary focus in family law and brings a deep understanding of family dynamics to her practice.

Paige is a graduate of the University of Toledo College of Law, graduating magna cum laude and in the top 20% of her class. During law school, Paige worked as a paralegal and law clerk for various firms during the day and attended classes at night, all while being an active executive board member of the Student Bar Association and other student organizations. Her leadership and dedication to advocating for her peers earned her the Student Involvement Award, underscoring her commitment to fostering a supportive and inclusive community. Today, she channels that same dedication into providing personalized and effective legal representation to individuals and families facing a wide range of legal issues. Prior to attending law school, Paige received her Bachelor of Arts in sociology from the University of Cincinnati, where she developed a keen interest in the complexities of human relationships and societal structures.

With a focus on empathy and understanding, Paige guides her clients through some of the most challenging times with care and professionalism. Whether handling divorce, dissolution, child custody disputes, or other legal matters, she is committed to achieving favorable outcomes for her clients. Paige has practiced in domestic relations and juvenile courts throughout Northwest Ohio and argued before the Sixth District Court of Appeals. She is also a certified Guardian Ad Litem where she advocates for children in court proceedings.

Born and raised in Toledo, Ohio, Paige is committed to serving her community. She is an active member of the Toledo Bar Association, chairing the Domestic Relations Committee, and she regularly participates in their pro bono clinics. Paige has also partnered with local community groups to present valuable information sessions to those navigating the court system on their own.

Outside the office, Paige enjoys spending her free time exploring the outdoors, practicing yoga, binging reality television, and loving on her many fur children.

With a focus on empathy and understanding, Paige guides her clients through some of the most challenging times with care and professionalism. Whether handling divorce, dissolution, child custody disputes, or other legal matters, she is committed to achieving favorable outcomes for her clients. Paige has practiced in domestic relations and juvenile courts throughout Northwest Ohio and argued before the Sixth District Court of Appeals. She is also a certified Guardian Ad Litem where she advocates for children in court proceedings.

Born and raised in Toledo, Ohio, Paige is committed to serving her community. She is an active member of the Toledo Bar Association, chairing the Domestic Relations Committee, and she regularly participates in their pro bono clinics. Paige has also partnered with local community groups to present valuable information sessions to those navigating the court system on their own.

Outside the office, Paige enjoys spending her free time exploring the outdoors, practicing yoga, binging reality television, and loving on her many fur children.

attorneys.name: Norm Frankowski
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Norm Frankowski has been with the firm since its founding. He practices law primarily in the areas of commercial real estate (including purchase, sale, finance, lease and construction), business (including formation, dissolution and extensive areas of operation) and a broad spectrum of transactional law (including contracts and organizational development). With a strong desire to help each client grow, achieve and thrive, an everyday attention to detail and a mission to serve as a reliable advisor and team member, Norm assists lending institutions, individuals and businesses of all types.

In addition to his role as attorney/partner in the law firm, Norm also is the President of Allied Land Title LLC, the firm's affiliated title agency. As a licensed title agent authorized to issue title insurance policies in Ohio and Kentucky, Norm continues his emphasis on commercial real estate transactions.

Norm began practicing law in 1993. Complementing his current practice is Norm's experience in areas ranging from civil litigation, jury trial experience and title insurance defense to health care and administrative law. A 1990 graduate of the University of Toledo with a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics Magna Cum Laude with College Honors, Norm went on to earn his Juris Doctor from The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law in 1993. At Ohio State, Norm was active as one of the Managing Editors of The Ohio State Law Journal. Norm remains an avid Buckeye!

Norm is licensed to practice law in the State of Ohio, the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio, Western Division and the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit.

attorneys.name: Philip J. Fulton
attorneys.practice_type: Injured Workers Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Philip Fulton has worked tirelessly on behalf of injured workers and disability claimants since 1980. Widely recognized as a leader in his field, Mr. Fulton is listed in The Best Lawyers in America, Ohio Super Lawyers, and has received numerous other accolades and awards over a distinguished career.

He is past president of the Ohio Association for Justice and has twice been chairperson of the Ohio Academy of Trial Lawyers' Workers Compensation Section. For his commitment to injured workers, he was given the Distinguished Service Award in 1994 and 2002 by the Ohio Academy of Trial Lawyers and was inducted into the Ohio Academy of Trial Lawyers Association Workers' Compensation Hall of Fame in 1997. He has twice been selected as Lawyer of the Year for Workers' Compensation in "Best Lawyers in America."

Mr. Fulton's proudest professional achievement is his history of successfully protecting the rights of the injured and disabled.

Mr. Fulton Wrote The Book On Ohio’s Workers’ Comp Law

Frequently asked to lecture to attorneys, legal groups, and doctors all over Ohio on issues dealing with workers' comp, Mr. Fulton is also the author of the well-known treatise on workers' compensation, "Ohio Workers' Compensation Law," published by LexisNexis. Mr. Fulton's book is used by workers' compensation attorneys, doctors, the Ohio Bureau of Workers' Compensation, the Ohio Industrial Commission and the court system.

In addition to his work on behalf of injured workers, Mr. Fulton has been an adjunct professor at Capital University Law School in Ohio. He taught law to aspiring workers’ compensation attorneys.

attorneys.name: Michael K. Fultz
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Westerville, OH
attorneys.bio:
My practice includes estate planning, probate, business, and municipal work. The scope of my practice has ranged from drafting simple wills and contracts to the formation of an international foundation. I am typically engaged to draft wills and family trusts and to create LLCs, corporations, and nonprofit entities. I have experience in residential construction, remodeling, and residential rental property investing. I have litigated in civil court, criminal court, probate court, and assisted with litigation in state appellate court and the Supreme Court of Ohio.

An analytical problem-solver by nature, I capitalize on my educational background in business, as well as, my "emergency" experiences as a firefighter and paramedic. I have extensive experience resolving emergencies and difficult situations, addressing the legal, financial, and public relations aspects involved. I'm good under pressure, and I know how to manage the small details without losing sight of the overall strategy.

For recreation, I play volleyball, golf, ride my motorcycle, and play with my golden retriever, Buddy.

attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
While Mike Gabrail’s primary professional focus is Crossroads Group, a real estate investment and management firm based in Richfield, Ohio, his legal activities center around transactional law, with an emphasis on real estate, the pharmaceutical industry, and property rights in Ohio.

Crossroads Group owns and operates residential and commercial properties throughout the Midwest, as well as international holdings including vacation rental villas, giving Mike a unique position to advise on business decisions involving legal risk.

Mike also serves on the board of the 1851 Center for Constitutional Law, an organization that advocates for and litigates on behalf of Ohioans whose property rights are unlawfully violated by government entities.

Outside of work, Mike is a passionate golfer who often jokes that golf might be his real day job. He lives in Northeast Ohio with his wife and family.

attorneys.name: W. Scott Gaines
attorneys.practice_type: Electrical/Electronics Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
W. Scott Gaines is a partner in the firm’s Electrical & Electronics Practice Group. His practice focuses primarily on the preparation and prosecution of patent applications directed to electronic and electromechanical devices and systems, photonics, electromagnetics, semiconductors and semiconductor processing, control systems, signal processing, and power systems.

Scott received a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering in 1991, and a Master of Science in Electrical Engineering in 1994, both from the University of Cincinnati. His undergraduate studies concentrated on electronics and electromagnetics, and his graduate studies concentrated on electromagnetics, semiconductor physics, and semiconductor device fabrication.

After graduate school, Scott worked as an engineer in the aerospace/defense electronics and telecommunications industries for 12 years before entering the University of Cincinnati College of Law. Scott graduated with a Juris Doctor degree in 2009 and has been registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office as a patent attorney since 2010.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Galasso
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mike joined the firm in 1999 and became a partner in 2005. He is a member of the firm’s litigation practice group and his practice is devoted almost exclusively to litigation. Mike has tried numerous cases to verdict including bench trials, jury trials, arbitrations, appeals, and contested bankruptcy matters.

Prior to law school, Mike was a police officer in Knoxville, Tennessee. During college, Mike was a military police officer in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve serving on active duty in Operation Desert Storm in Saudi Arabia, Iraq, and Kuwait.

Admitted to practice in Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana, Mike’s practice extends to a wide range of civil litigation matters such as business and contract disputes, real estate disputes, employment litigation, non-compete agreements, trade secret claims, franchise litigation, consumer claims, and creditor’s rights. His creditor’s rights practice regularly involves representing banks, credit unions, and other financial institutions in foreclosures, bankruptcies, receiverships, loan workouts, and related default matters. Mike also represents outdoor advertising clients in land use, zoning, and contract matters. Mike has significant experience in personal injury matters representing both plaintiffs and defendants.

Mike is a member of The Million Dollar Advocates Forum in which membership is limited to attorneys who have won million and multi-million dollar verdicts, awards, and settlements.

Mike has made several presentations to professional organizations relating to foreclosure and real estate issues.

Judith E. Galeano (Partner) was born in New York, New York, and was raised in New York City and Toledo, Ohio. attorneys.name: William R. Gallagher
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
William Gallagher is a 1987 graduate with honors from Chicago-Kent College of Law in Chicago. After seven successful years as a trial attorney in the Lake and Cook Country Public Defender Offices in Illinois, he moved to Cincinnati in 1994. Since joining the Law Offices of Hal Arenstein, Mr. Gallagher has confined his practice to criminal cases in both state and federal courts.

In addition to the many jury trial victories, Mr. Gallagher has tried 13 Capital Murder trials in three different states with none of his clients receiving the death penalty. Currently, Mr. Gallagher is one of only a few local lawyers in private practice handling federal Habeas Corpus litigation.

Mr. Gallagher is a past president of the Greater Cincinnati Criminal Defense Lawyers Association. He is a past member of the Board of Directors of the Ohio Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and the current Chair of the CLE Institute for the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Mr. Gallagher is a frequent presenter on a variety of topics relating to criminal defense. His presentations have included topics such as "Opening Statements", "Evidentiary Issues in Drug Cases", "Professionalism", "Theories and Themes in Criminal Cases" and "The Use of Electronic and Digital Evidence in Criminal Trials."

In addition to his guest lecturing, Mr. Gallagher is a past adjunct faculty member at DePaul University Law School and is currently on the Adjunct faculty at the University of Cincinnati Law School. He has taught in the areas of Ethics, Trial Advocacy, and Forensic Sciences.

Mr. Gallagher is a founding member of the Ohio Innocence Project located at the University of Cincinnati Law School. He serves on its Advisory Board.

In 2011, Mr. Gallagher was awarded the Robert Heeney Memorial Award by the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. It is their most prestigious award given to the attorney who provides outstanding contributions to the profession.

attorneys.name: Mark Gardner
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Sandusky, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mark Gardner is an experienced criminal defense lawyer with a lengthy history of trials, dismissals, and not guilty verdicts.

With more than thirty years of experience in the criminal defense world, he's the man to see for private criminal defense in the Cuyahoga County and the surrounding areas.

Following nearly nine years of service in the United States Armed Forces, including service in the Air Force Intelligence Service and the Coast Guard as a weapons controller, Mark graduated from the Case Western Reserve University School of Law in December, 1992.

Since graduation, he has distinguished himself as a public defender (4 years) and in private practice (9+ years). During that time, he has successfully conducted numerous DUI motion hearings and jury trials, including getting across-the-board “not guilty” verdicts in a case where his client was charged with DUI, fleeing and eluding, reckless operation, speeding (105mph in a 60mph zone), and failure to wear a seatbelt.

He has testified as an expert witness on the proper administration and grading of SFSTs in DUI trials in both Pennsylvania and Ohio.

Mark was also the appointed inaugural chairman of the OACDL’s DUI Defense Task Force.

Mark has been received the AV* rating under Martindale-Hubbell’s peer review rating system.

attorneys.name: Jonathan N. Garver
attorneys.firm_name: Jonathan N. Garver, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Traffic Crimes Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Garver attended the University of Bristol, Bristol, England; graduated with honors from American University, Washington D.C. (1970); and received a juris doctorate degree from The Boston University School of Law (1973).

Mr. Garver served as an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for Cuyahoga County from 1974 to 1977. Winning his first seven jury trials may have signaled things to come, but during his tenure as an assistant prosecuting attorney, it was not simply about winning; it was about doing justice. More important than the convictions he secured was the extraordinary respect Mr. Garver earned from those he prosecuted. Mr. Garver fought hard, but tried a clean case, and the defendants he prosecuted and convicted frequently expressed their gratitude for his sense of fairness and decency.

Mr. Garver has extensive experience in both criminal and civil litigation. His chief areas of practice include criminal defense and appeals.

For approximately 15 years, until the company was acquired by Wachovia, Mr. Garver represented the investment firm of A. G. Edwards & Sons, Inc. in Northeastern, Ohio. During that period of time, Mr. Garver was the only solo practitioner in the United States to represent A. G. Edwards & Sons, Inc. His work for A. G. Edwards & Sons, Inc. included contract litigation, defense of broker defection cases, premises liability defense, securities arbitration defense, and general civil litigation. Mr. Garver has done similar work for the investment firm of Stifel Nicholas & Co.

Mr. Garver is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Ohio Association for Justice, and the Cuyahoga County Criminal Defense Lawyers Association.

Mr. Garver has taught law at an accredited university on both undergraduate and graduate levels.

attorneys.name: Grant B. Garverick
attorneys.firm_name: Hottenroth, Garverick, Tilson & Garverick, Co., L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills and estates Lawyers in Galion, OH
attorneys.bio:
Grant Garverick grew up in the Galion, Ohio area. He is a 1981 graduate of Galion High School, a 1985 graduate of Ohio State University (B.A. with honors), and 1988 graduate of the Ohio State University College of Law (J.D.).

His law practice includes wills and estates, estate planning, landlord-tenant disputes, personal injury, lawsuits, family law, divorce, dissolution, child custody and support, traffic law, criminal defense, and a number of other areas.

Grant was admitted to practice law in Ohio on November 7, 1988 and has been with our firm since then. He is a current member of the Ohio State Bar Association and the Crawford County Bar Association. Grant received the statewide 2002 Ohio State Bar Foundation Community Service Award for lawyers under 40 and also is a Life fellow of the Ohio State Bar Foundation.

He is currently a member of the local Elks Lodge No. 1191. He currently serves as a member of the Board of Trustees for the Galion-Crestline Area Chamber of Commerce. He is the Secretary for the Galion Community Education Foundation and has been since its inception. Grant has served as Treasurer of the Galion Chapter of the American Red Cross for 6 years, as a member of the Board of Directors for the Galion Center YMCA for 6 years and as a member of the Board of Directors for the Sara Beegle Day Care Center. Grant is currently serving his second four year term as a board member of Galion City Schools District and has been past president of the school board.

Grant's wife, Margaret, is a teacher for Mansfield City Schools. They have two daughters who are both Galion High School graduates. Grant enjoys playing golf and fishing, as well as spending time just relaxing at home. He is currently a member of Peace Lutheran Church. He was a coach for many years in the Galion Girls Summer Softball program.

2002 Ohio State Bar Foundation Community Service Award

Life fellow, Ohio State Bar Foundation

attorneys.name: Payton J. Genis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Payton Genis joined Leeseberg Tuttle as a law clerk in January 2022 during her second year at Capital University Law School. While in law school, Payton was the President and founding member of Capital's Tort and Injury Law Society and served as an Education Manager for the National Plaintiffs' Law Association. Payton also received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award, an award that recognizes excellence achievement by law students and is given to the highest scoring student in a particular law school course, in her Intellectual Property course at Capital Law.

Payton remained as a law clerk at Leeseberg Tuttle throughout her second and third year at Capital Law, and officially joined the firm as an associate attorney in November 2024. Payton focuses her practice on medical malpractice and catastrophic personal injury litigation and is dedicated to zealously advocating for her clients, all while maintaining empathy, patience, and compassion.

Prior to starting her legal career, Payton graduated from Creighton University with a Bachelor of Arts in Advertising and Multi-Media/Photojounalism. From 2018-2021, she worked in Des Moines, Iowa as a creative copywriter with the Meredith Corporation, drafting direct mail copy for a variety of magazines, such as People, Magnolia Journal, and Entertainment Weekly. When the Covid Pandemic hit, Payton decided to utilize her extra time indoors to study for the Law School Admission Test (LSAT) in the evenings after work, which ultimately prompted her move to Ohio, her attendance at Capital Law School, and the commencement of her journey dedicated to the love of the law and helping others. Outside of the courtoom, Payton enjoys binge-watching true crime documentaries, exploring all that Columbus has to offer, which includes trying new activities and restaurants with her fiancé, as well as attending local dog parks and corgi meetups with her two corgis.

Awards and Honors

Honors

CALI Excellence for the Future Award - Intellectual Property - 2023

attorneys.name: Meaghan Anne Geraghty
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Mayfield Heights, OH
attorneys.bio:
Meaghan A. Geraghty joined Elk + Elk in 2025 as a personal injury and medical malpractice attorney, bringing with her a background as a registered nurse. A native of Northeast Ohio, she earned her undergraduate degree from Bowling Green State University and was awarded a Fulbright Fellowship, which took her to Hong Kong. After returning to the U.S., she obtained her nursing degree from Kent State University and gained hands-on experience in various clinical settings, including top local hospitals and travel nurse assignments.

Meaghan earned her Juris Doctor degree from the University of Nebraska College of Law in 2018. During law school, she was a member of the National Mock Trial Team and received several CALI Awards for her work in Civil Clinic and Public Health Law. She was also recognized as the Outstanding Clinical Student and received the Clinical Legal Educators Association Award.

Her legal experience includes handling medical malpractice and nursing home cases in both Nebraska and Ohio. She has also served as a Guardian ad Litem and has litigated personal injury cases involving complex medical issues. Her combined experience in medicine and law provides her with unique insights into medical negligence cases, which she uses to advocate for individuals and families.

At Elk + Elk, Meaghan represents clients across Ohio in personal injury and medical malpractice cases. She is committed to ensuring those affected by medical negligence receive strong advocacy and support. Outside of work, she remains involved in community health initiatives and speaks at seminars focused on nursing and the law.

attorneys.name: Kenneth B. Germain
attorneys.practice_type: Trademarks/Unfair Competition Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ken Germain has more than 45 years of varied experience in the trademark/unfair competition field and is a former full-time law professor. He focuses his practice on expert witness work, and consulting and litigation. Ken often has been retained as an Expert Witness on issues relating to trademarks and unfair competition, working on cases involving some of the nation’s largest companies in high-stakes, cutting-edge cases. He has testified in court over 15 times.

Ken has been an active speaker on trademark and unfair competition, lecturing at national, regional and local conferences over 300 times. In addition, in 1990 Ken founded, and until 2014 chaired, the All Ohio Annual Institute On Intellectual Property seminar. This seminar is in its 33rd year, provides two-city programming (Cincinnati, Cleveland) covering all aspects of IP, and is the largest, oldest, full-day IP CLE program in and around Ohio.

Ken served as an Adjunct Professor at the University of Cincinnati College of Law for many years, teaching trademark/unfair competition courses. Later, Ken served as the Distinguished Professorial Practitioner in the University of Dayton Law School’s Program in Law and Technology.

attorneys.name: Joseph E. Gibson
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Fairborn, OH
attorneys.bio:
Drawing on Decades of Experience in Multiple Practice Areas to Secure Benefits for Clients

Joseph Gibson has practiced law for decades, working in many fields and holding several positions. Today, he leverages an unmatched arsenal of legal strategy while serving NRS Injury Law clients at the firm’s Dayton office.

A Storied Legal Career Directed at Helping Injured Workers Secure Benefits

Few attorneys can claim to have worked in as many legal fields as Joe Gibson, but his career didn’t start with law. “I cut grass and did landscaping in college and even law school in the 1970s and 1980s,” says Joe. “It started with my uncle’s yard. Before I knew it, I was cutting lawns across the neighborhood.” A Middletown, Ohio native, Joe’s working-class roots brought him to workers’ comp law when he joined NRS Injury Law in August 2023.

But there were many rungs in Joe’s career ladder between cutting grass as a teenager and joining this firm. Joe worked as a legal assistant, paralegal, and law clerk before and during law school at the University of Dayton School of Law. After passing the bar in 1990, Joe worked both corporate law (Dap Incorporated) and government law (Wright-Patterson Air Force Base Air Force Logistics Command).

After his stint at the Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Joe launched his law firm in 1994 serving defense clients, plaintiff clients, and the Ohio Bureau of Workers’ Compensation (BWC). Joe was later appointed District Hearing Officer for the BWC, where he presided over workers’ compensation hearings.

“Some lawyers can say they’ve served clients on both sides of the table,” says Joe, referring to plaintiff and defense legal work. “At various stages of my career, I’ve sat on ALL sides of the table, and believe me, there are more than two sides. My experience as plaintiff’s attorney, defense attorney, BWC attorney, and District Hearing Officer gives me a unique understanding of workers’ compensation law, an understanding I leverage in winning cases for my clients.”

A Willingness to Fight; A Commitment to Inform

“Clients want two things from their attorneys,” Joe said, shifting the conversation to his role at NRS Injury Law. “One, they want you to fight for them. Two, they want you to inform them.”

For Joe, the first is a given and an area where he’s proven himself in securing client results. But the second is an area where he stands out. “Not all attorneys take the time to inform their clients,” Joe says. “But I do. My goal is to serve and advise my clients so they have an understanding of what’s going on and so we can secure benefits and compensation together.”

According to Joe, informing clients and bringing them into the team approach NRS Injury Law has created is incredibly beneficial and puts the firm in a better position to win for the client. “In my decades, I’ve seen every type of case there is,” Joe concluded. “And while your strategy based on the case in front of you may differ from one case to the next, it is a universal truth that an informed client and a teamwork-approach significantly increase your odds for success. This is especially true in workers’ comp cases, where the fast-paced nature of the case requires all of us to be on the same page.”

Bolstered by the unprecedented resources provided by NRS Injury Law, the largest workers’ compensation law firm in Ohio, Joe brings his clients into the fold, informs them, fights for them, and helps them win.

Work/Life Balance

Joe stays busy in the office and outside of it. When he’s not representing NRS Injury Law clients, he can be found playing tennis or golf. He also jogs and bicycles on local trails. Joe is an avid chess player, a hobby he’s had for multiple decades and one he credits with boosting his legal abilities in strategy, prediction, and human psychology. Joe lives in Tipp City with his wife, Sonia. They have two daughters together.

“I take a lot of pride in helping injured workers be made whole,” Joe said in closing. “Yet my greatest achievements in life are those girls. They grew up watching me help others in my legal profession and they loved me for it. Now, they’re both in professions where they help others and they volunteer at homeless and immigration shelters. No accomplishment is more rewarding or humbling than the fact that they still see me as a role model.”

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Joe Gibson

NRS Injury Law treats every client case as unique, important, and deserving of the firm’s full array of resources. Joe embodies those principles. His willingness to educate, love for problem-solving, storied career serving in all areas of workers’ compensation law, and his commitment to community align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Joe and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Outside the law office, Joe has served his community in many ways. At law school, Joe served as the president of the Commuter Students Association. More recently, Joe became deeply involved in civil service through multiple elected positions, including City Council, City Council President, and City Mayor. He also served on the City Planning Board and the Cable Access Commission. Joe has taught political science and legal studies at Sinclair Community College in Dayton and Edison State Community College, where he encouraged students to get involved in local and state government. Joe participates in food drives, volunteers at shelters, and helps his wife’s organization in employment and family services.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Former Tipp City Mayor

Tipp City Council, President

attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Dublin, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ross A. Gillespie was born in Parkersburg, WV and grew up in Waterford, Ohio. He earned his undergraduate degree in History in 2000 from The Ohio State University. After attending the Ohio State University, he attended law school at the University of Akron, School of Law, where he received his juris doctorate degree in 2003.

He has been practicing law since 2003. Currently Mr. Gillespie is a member of the Columbus Bar Association, Central Ohio Association of Justice, Ohio State Bar Association, and Union County bar Association.

Mr. Gillespie is admitted to practice law in the State of Ohio and before the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio an the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio. Mr. Gillespie also argued before the Fifth District Court of Appeals for Ohio in Folmar v. Griffin, 2006-Ohio-1849.

Mr. Gillespie enjoys most outdoor activities, working on home improvement projects, and spending time with his family in his free time.

Mr. Gillespie practices in the areas of Adoptions, Appeals, Civil Litigation, Consumer Law, Estate Planning, Family Law (Divorce, Dissolution, Custody Cases & Post Decree Modifications), Guardianships (Adult & Minor), Medical Malpractice, Name Changes, Probate Law, Real Estate Law (Landlord/ Tenant and Residential).
