attorneys.name: Corinne Hoover
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law (Divorce, Domestic Relations, Custody, Juvenile Law) Lawyers in Cuyahoga Falls, OH
attorneys.bio:
Is the lead attorney of Hoover Kacyon, LLC’s Family Law Practice Group and is a Certified Specialist in Family Law. Corinne focuses her practice exclusively on complex family law issues, including high-asset or high-conflict divorce or child custody cases, high-net worth clients, adoptions, appeals, developing new issues of the law including surrogacy and embryo issues and same sex parenting and other cases on the cutting-edge issues of the law or cases of first impression in the State of Ohio. Because of this, Corinne has earned her place as a proud member of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers, the highest-quality organization of professional family lawyers across the United States.

Corinne knew from a very young age that she was destined to be an attorney. The daughter of Judge Kim R. Hoover and the granddaughter of the late Attorney Orval R. Hoover, Corinne grew up in a family that excelled in the legal field and taught her the value of helping others through difficult legal issues. Now, Corinne has carried on that family tradition, along with her brother, Attorney Tad Orval Hoover, practicing in the same building that her father, grandfather and other extended family practiced before her. As a former magistrate, prosecutor, and criminal defense attorney, Corinne follows her family tradition of having represented clients on all sides of the law.

As the mother of four young children, Corinne knows nothing is more important than family. Because of this, Corinne has spent her entire career honing her skills as a trial lawyer so that she is in the best position possible to advocate for families who need her most as they face the most difficult moments of their lives. Now, Corinne uses her credentials as a certified specialist in family relations law to handle the most complex family law cases including high asset or high conflict divorce of custody cases, cases of private business ownership and complex business valuations, cases involving forensic custody and psychological evaluations and competing expert reports, and cases representing professionals such as professional athletes, lawyers, doctors, dentists, politicians, CEOs and business executives and owners (and their spouses against them!).

Corinne has also had the honor of representing clients on the cutting edge of new laws and legal developments across the state. Corinne frequently argues cases of first impression in the courts of appeal and is sought after by both clients and other lawyers alike to take over complex cases once they reach the appellate court level. Notably, Corinne has even appeared in front of the Ohio Supreme Court and has additionally testified in front of the state legislature's Civil Justice Committee on controversial pending family law legislation.

Corinne also has developed a particularly niche market of her practice in the arena of complex adoption law. What sets Corinne apart from her colleagues in the family law field is her hybrid of experience in both adoption law and other family law matters. For whatever reason, most lawyers who practice in domestic relations or juvenile court do not practice adoptions, which are heard in probate court. For the same reason, a lot of probate law attorneys say they practice probate law in general but do not do adoption matters. Practically speaking, these areas of law intersect, and clients are best served with a lawyer who understands how one area of law affects the other. For example, perhaps a mother is fighting her ex-husband in domestic relations court over visitation and child support and is remarried and wishes for her new husband to adopt the child. A purely domestic relations lawyer may very well be able to assist with matters of visitation and support but not know how their actions in domestic relations court could ultimately affect the success of an adoption case later. It is for this reason that Corinne is regularly consulted as a family law specialist, not just by clients but oftentimes by other lawyers who acknowledge Corinne's unique hybrid approach can be of huge benefit to a case. Corinne is also a regular lecturer and instructor on Continuing Legal Education courses to other lawyers and judges dealing most often with the intersections of family law and adoption cases based on her experience in the fields. It is not uncommon for judges to remark that when they see Corinne on a case it involves an issue they have never seen before or something else particularly complicated. Corinne is willing to take on the messy cases such as this because her passion is protecting families because she knows nothing matters to her clients more. Her most crucial cases involve contested adoptions, adoption appeals, representing clients in situations where fraud or wrongful adoptions have occurred and oftentimes, opposing public children’s service agencies in their attempts to get involved in the private lives of families who could instead handle their own matters through private adoptions. In representing clients in these matters, Corinne cannot help but be “all in”. What sets Corinne apart from others is that she will fight for her client’s children just like she would fight for her own.

Aside from complex litigation and messy family law cases, Corinne is also a firm believer in settlement and alternative dispute resolution when it serves her clients. Some clients express that they cannot afford to have a lengthy legal battle. Other clients say that emotionally or mentally they or their children cannot handle a contested case. With prior extensive experience as a Guardian ad Litem (GAL) in both domestic relations and juvenile court, Corinne understands that sometimes the most important role a lawyer can fill is assistance with reaching a fair settlement or compromise without a long drawn-out battle.

In addition to her full-time family law practice, Corinne also serves as an attorney in governmental relations, representing individuals and political entities in complaints before the Ohio Elections Commission, advising clients on elections law and campaign finance matters and providing consulting services on intersections between legal and political matters. In the past, she has also served as Special Counsel to the Ohio Attorney General. Corinne is also a proud member of the JoAnn Davidson Leadership Institute.

Corinne is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association Grievance Committee, charged with investigating complaints filed against judges and other lawyers across the state, as well as a Ohio State Bar Foundation Fellow. She is also an active member of the Akron Bar Association and a member of the Family Law Section, an Akron Bar Foundation Fellow and a Member of Board of Directors of the Akron Bar Foundation, the charitable wing of the Akron Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Gerald R. Horning
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Leveraging Decades of Experience & Thousands of Case Victories to Get Results for Clients

The year was 1984, and on a day that Gerald Horning will never forget, he both took and passed the bar exam, and his first child was born. (It was a busy day for Gerald, though his wife, Tolisa, worked even harder that day!) Gerald has practiced law ever since, dedicating his life to representing people wronged by large, powerful companies.

A Call to Serve

“I graduated with a B.A. in 1976 and, as I always wanted to help people and make communities safer, I started working as the Assistant Director of Cleveland's Department of Public Health and Welfare,” said Gerald, reflecting on his trajectory. “I managed four divisions and 500 employees, working on things like access to healthcare, environmental health, air pollution control, and prison administration.”

But that was just the beginning of a long and storied career. Gerald has brought his passion for service, commitment to social betterment, and his love for helping others through several decades and into the present, where he today exhibits the same energy and charismatic good nature that was on display the day, he passed the bar and welcomed his firstborn into the world.

Pursuing a Career in Law

Despite his many accomplishments at the Cleveland Department of Public Health and Welfare, Gerald could not help but feel he was being called to serve elsewhere. He returned to school to seek an MBA and Juris Doctorate, which he obtained in December 1983 through a joint program at Cleveland State University. Gerald has represented thousands of injured clients since, developing a particular skill set in deftly organizing and presenting personal injury cases, including wrongful death, medical malpractice, workplace injury, insurance coverage issues, uninsured motorist cases, product liability, premises liability, and auto accidents of all types.

Gerald joined NRS Injury Law in 2012, where he quickly rose through the ranks to become Senior Associate Attorney. Particularly skilled at understanding the nuances of a case and knowing which strategy best serves that case, Gerald has resolved thousands of cases by settlement, litigation, arbitration, mediation, and trial. He has argued cases in several appellate courts, the Ohio Court of Claims, and the Ohio Supreme Court.

“When the firm gets a particularly complex case, it comes to my desk,” says Gerald. “I feel a deep sense of responsibility to my clients and their cases. It means a lot to me to represent people who have been hurt by powerful corporations. Standing up for them when other firms will not means everything to me because I firmly believe that everyone deserves an ally. Everyone has the right to have someone in their corner.”

Work/Life Balance

Gerald has few moments to spare between practicing law full-time and volunteering in his community, but when he does have a day off, he usually spends it sailing with his friends or getting together with his son and daughter, both of whom live locally. If he can line up a few days off, Gerald takes trips to faraway places like Alaska. Gerald lives with his wife and their cat in Bay Village, Ohio.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Gerald Horning

With several decades of experience in law, Gerald has found his niche in tackling particularly complicated and nuanced cases. Combining that personal dedication with a heartfelt compassion for his clients, Gerald's values align perfectly with NRS Injury Law's mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work each and every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Gerald and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Dennis E. Horvath grew up in South Bend, Indiana. He earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from Indiana University and his Juris Doctor from Capital University Law School. Dennis is admitted to practice law in the State of Ohio and before the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.

Dennis has practiced law in Ohio since 2001, dedicating his practice exclusively to domestic relations and family law. He represents clients in all aspects of family law matters, including divorce, dissolution, child custody and parenting disputes, child and spousal support, and prenuptial agreements. His practice is known for handling complex, high-conflict, and high-asset matters with precision, strategy, and discretion.

Dennis’s work has been consistently recognized by his peers. He has been selected for inclusion in Best Lawyers in America from 2018 through 2026. Best Lawyers is the oldest and one of the most respected peer-review publications in the legal profession, and selection is widely regarded as a significant professional honor conferred by fellow attorneys.

Dennis has also been recognized by Super Lawyers. He was named an Ohio Super Lawyers “Rising Star” in 2005 and from 2009 through 2013 (his final year of eligibility), and has been selected as an Ohio Super Lawyer from 2016 through 2026. Super Lawyers selects attorneys through a patented, multiphase process that includes peer nominations, peer evaluations, and independent third-party research. Only five percent of attorneys statewide are selected each year.

Based on this selection process, Dennis has further been named one of the Top 50 Lawyers in Columbus and Top 100 Lawyers in Ohio by Super Lawyers Magazine.

Dennis holds the AV Preeminent® rating from Martindale-Hubbell, the highest peer-review rating available. This distinction reflects the highest levels of professional excellence and ethical standards, as determined by confidential evaluations from members of the bar and judiciary who are familiar with his work.

In addition, Dennis has been listed as a Top Lawyer by Columbus CEO Magazine.

Dennis maintains a 10.0 out of 10.0 “Superb” rating on Avvo, has been listed in Rue Ratings’ Best Attorneys in America, and was a recipient of the 2015 Avvo Clients’ Choice Award.

attorneys.name: Barbara Horwitz
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Lawyers in Springboro, OH
attorneys.bio:
Barbara L. Horwitz, a partner with the firm, earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Butler University in Indianapolis, Indiana, and a Legal Assisting Certificate from the University of Cincinnati. She obtained a Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Cincinnati College of Law, where she served on Law Review for two years. Two of her law review articles were selected for publication in the University of Cincinnati Law Review: "The Extinction of the Peremptory Challenge: What Will the Jury System Lose by Its Demise?" and "The Duty of Schools to Protect Students From Sexual Harassment: How Much Recovery Will the Law Allow?".

Mrs. Horwitz worked for six years as a legal assistant in Hamilton, Ohio, for Carl Morgenstern, Esq. and for Michael J. Sage, Esq. She then served as a Bailiff for the Butler County, Ohio, Common Pleas Court under Judge Michael J. Sage.

Mrs. Horwitz was an associate attorney in the Offices of Myron A. Wolf for fifteen years. During that period, she practiced in the areas of bankruptcy, personal injury, insurance defense, wills, probate, civil disputes, family law and general litigation. Mrs. Horwitz has practiced extensively before the Court of Appeals for the Twelfth District of Ohio, where her arguments have generally resulted in the Court ruling in her clients' favor.

Mrs. Horwitz strongly believes that her own personal involvement in all aspects of her clients' cases provides them with the strongest possible legal representation, and has never delegated meetings with clients, drafting of pleadings, or completion of bankruptcy forms to legal staff. She further strives to keep clients informed as to the status of their case, and to educate them to understand the legal processes with which they are involved.

Mrs. Horwitz is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, Cincinnati Bar Association, Butler County Bar Association, and Warren County Bar Association. She is admitted to practice in the State of Ohio, as well as the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.

attorneys.name: Jonathan Horwitz
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Springboro, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jon Horwitz, a partner with our firm, obtained a Bachelor of Arts degree in Chemistry from Indiana University – Bloomington and a Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Cincinnati College of Law.

While attending law school, Mr. Horwitz completed an externship with the Cincinnati Chapter of the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), as well as a judicial externship with Judge Burton Perlman of the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of Ohio. Mr. Horwitz also worked part-time with the Hamilton County (Ohio) Probate Court, and was a law clerk with a Cincinnati law firm specializing in secured transactions under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC).

Upon graduation from law school, Mr. Horwitz began a distinguished career with the Montgomery County (Ohio) Prosecutor’s Office, lasting more than 10 years. During his tenure with the prosecutor’s office, Mr. Horwitz successfully prosecuted hundreds of cases in the office’s Child Support Enforcement Division, Child Protection Unit, Juvenile Delinquency Division, Grand Jury/Preliminary Hearing Division, Criminal Division as a Felony Docket Attorney, and Fraud and Economic Crimes Unit. During his last four years with the prosecutor’s office, Mr. Horwitz specialized in prosecuting complex white collar crimes, including cases involving mortgage fraud, embezzlement, food stamp fraud, workers compensation fraud, insurance fraud, contractor fraud, securities fraud, power-of-attorney fraud, tax fraud, elder abuse, and identity theft. Mr. Horwitz successfully tried a number of high-profile complex criminal cases against many of Southwestern Ohio’s preeminent attorneys. Mr. Horwitz’s trial experience is not limited to white collar crime. He has successfully tried felony cases involving DUI, robbery, burglary, rape, kidnapping, felonious assault, and drug charges.

The experience gained as a prosecutor has provided Mr. Horwitz with insight as to what the prosecution is likely to be thinking in a particular case and allows him to anticipate the prosecution’s next move. This insight helps Mr. Horwitz to obtain the best possible resolutions for his clients.

Mr. Horwitz is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, Dayton Bar Association, Warren County Bar Association, and Greene County Bar Association. He is admitted to practice in the State of Ohio and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. He currently lives in Centerville with his wife and two children. In addition to his intense passion for seeking justice for his clients, Mr. Horwitz has a passion for the game of soccer and coaches youth soccer teams through the Centerville United Soccer Association (CUSA) and the Washington Township Recreational Center.

attorneys.name: E. Richard Hottenroth
attorneys.firm_name: Hottenroth, Garverick, Tilson & Garverick, Co., L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Wills and Estates Lawyers in Galion, OH
attorneys.bio:
Dick Hottenroth was born in Galion, Ohio, in 1936. He is a graduate of Galion High School, Capital University (A.B. Degree) and the Ohio State University College of Law (J.D. Degree).

Dick's practice includes wills and estates, estate planning, real estate and other areas.

At both Galion High School and Capital University, Dick participated in a number of student government and sporting activities. He attained all-league honors in high school baseball, was captain of the baseball team, and was a recognized lineman on the football team; at Capital University, he participated in intercollegiate baseball for four years and football for one year. In high school, Dick was president of the student government, president of his sophomore and junior classes, a class officer for four years, a member of the National Honor Society, and a representative of Boys State.

At Capital University, he was president of his class for three years, was student body vice-president and was student body government representative for four years.

Dick is actively involved in legal practice in many areas including wills and estates, business and corporate law, and real estate.

Dick has been involved as a trustee or director of a number of community activities including United Appeal, Galion YMCA-Community Center, Galion Community Hospital, Galion Community Improvement Corporation, Galion Public Library and Peace Lutheran Church.

Dick and his wife Carol have three children, David, Gail, and Marc, all of whom are graduates of the University of Cincinnati. In addition to his professional, community and family pursuits, Dick enjoys fishing and woodworking.

Member, National Honor Society

attorneys.name: Barbara J. Howard
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law – Domestic Relations and Juvenile Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Serving clients throughout the greater Cincinnati metropolitan area, including Hamilton, Clermont and Warren counties, Barbara J. Howard focuses her practice exclusively on family law matters at Barbara J. Howard Co., L.P.A. She has been certified as a specialist in family relations law by the Ohio State Bar Association since 1999. Ms. Howard assists people who are facing the end of their marriage and who are dealing with divorce-related issues that can include the division of retirement accounts and other complex marital assets, child custody and visitation, alimony, and child support. A strong advocate for her clients in the courtroom, Ms. Howard often attempts to seek resolution of these matters through collaborative law. Ms. Howard has extensive experience in other areas of family law, including post-divorce order modifications and paternity disputes.

A native of Ohio, Ms. Howard graduated magna cum laude from Xavier University in 1976 with a Bachelor of Arts in political science. She then obtained her legal education from the University of Cincinnati College of Law and was awarded her Juris Doctor in 1979. Admitted to practice before all Ohio state courts, Ms. Howard is also admitted to practice before the United States Supreme Court and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. Highly respected by her fellow attorneys, she is AV Preeminent* peer-review rated through Martindale-Hubbell.

Ms. Howard is completing her two-year term as the Chair of the American Bar Association's House of Delegates, the nearly 600-person policy-making body of the ABA. She is a former president and member of the Board of Governors of the Ohio State Bar Association. She is also a past president of the Cincinnati Bar Association, and she serves on the Supreme Court of Ohio Commission on Continuing Legal Education, having previously served on its Commission on the Certification of Attorneys as Specialists. Other ABA positions include a delegate in the House of Delegates since 1986 and the Ohio State Delegate to the House. Ms. Howard will chair ABA Day in Washington for 2023. Ms. Howard was the Chair of the Board of Trustees of Xavier University from 2014 to 2019 and chaired the Presidential Search Committee from 2020 to 2021. Ms. Howard is also Chair of the Ohio Bar Liability Insurance Company, a Board on which she has served since 2005.

*AV®, AV Preeminent®, Martindale-Hubbell Distinguished and Martindale-Hubbell Notable are certification marks used under license in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell® is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the anonymous opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review RatingTM fall into two categories - legal ability and general ethical standards.

attorneys.name: C. Bradley Howenstein
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Leveraging Decades of Experience and a Competitive Drive to Win Cases for Injured Workers

A veteran workers’ compensation attorney with rich experience representing both injured workers and employers, Brad Howenstein brings forth a lifetime of victories and a breadth of knowledge to which few can lay claim. Brad has become well-versed in every facet of workers’ comp law with his on-going service of injured workers and his previous time spent representing the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation, the Industrial Commission of Ohio, and private employers. Brad’s diverse background gives him an edge and has made him one of Ohio’s best-ranked workers’ comp attorneys.

Building on Decades of Legal Experience to Win Cases for Clients

“I try to approach each claim with the eye of a tactician,” Brad said when asked how he handles workers’ comp cases. “I evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of each claim from every perspective to map out the best path for success for our clients.” Brad’s methodology works. Supported by the immense resources and hands-on ethos of the NRS Injury Law team, Brad has zealously represented injured workers in over 1,200 hearings annually before the Industrial Commission of Ohio since joining the firm in 2015.

Brad is a results-driven attorney who cares deeply about securing benefits for his clients. He has argued over 100 workers’ compensation cases before the Ohio Supreme Court and Tenth District Court of Appeals, and he has prevailed in nearly two dozen workers’ compensation jury trials throughout Ohio with one of the highest winning percentages in the State. Brad has practiced law since 1991 and has an AVVO rating of 8.7/10 (i.e., Excellent).

Making Ohio a Safer Place for Workers

The mandamus cases Brad is involved in with the Tenth District Court of Appeals and the Ohio Supreme Court help shape the laws that affect injured workers. Each mandamus victory secures benefits for that client and makes it easier for clients throughout Ohio to obtain the benefits they are entitled to receive.

Since he was a teenager, Brad knew he wanted to help others as an attorney. A moot court class in 10th grade along with classic legal movies peaked his interest in law, and since Brad has never shied away from hard work, he quickly became familiar with the field by clerking for four law firms while attending law school. During his early years as an attorney, Brad worked a series of service jobs in the evenings.

Some of Brad’s greatest strengths include his background working as Ohio’s Assistant Attorney General and his time spent representing private businesses, the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation, and the Industrial Commission of Ohio. “I started representing injured workers in 2014, and it has become my passion work,” says Brad. “But the time I spent before that representing the State and private companies gave me a deep understanding of how the defense council operates in workers’ comp cases. Your best arguments are made when you understand the opposition. Understanding the folks across the aisle gives me an edge in securing compensation for our clients.”

Community Involvement

A legal career spent representing injured workers is all about service to the community, and Brad takes that mission to heart. When he’s not wearing his hat as a workers’ comp attorney, he can often be found participating in the firm’s charitable events, including volunteering at the Ronald McDonald House, helping out at food pantries, and participating in the firm’s annual community turkey giveaway. A good neighbor to his Dublin, Ohio community, Brad has also coached local sports teams, including his son’s football, baseball, and basketball teams.

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working, Brad enjoys hiking, fishing, and gardening with his partner. He is a proud Buckeye football and Cardinals baseball fan (having grown up in St. Louis). He enjoys watching games with his dog Rudy. During the spring months, Brad can be found scouring farm fields searching for arrowheads to add to his growing collection.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Brad Howenstein

A team player and always willing to help out, Brad’s work ethic and care for his clients aligns perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Brad and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Brad has practiced law since 1991 and has an AVVO rating of 8.7/10 (i.e., Excellent).

Making Ohio a Safer Place for Workers

The mandamus cases Brad is involved in with the Tenth District Court of Appeals and the Ohio Supreme Court help shape the laws that affect injured workers. Each mandamus victory secures benefits for that client and makes it easier for clients throughout Ohio to obtain the benefits they are entitled to receive.

Since he was a teenager, Brad knew he wanted to help others as an attorney. A moot court class in 10th grade along with classic legal movies peaked his interest in law, and since Brad has never shied away from hard work, he quickly became familiar with the field by clerking for four law firms while attending law school. During his early years as an attorney, Brad worked a series of service jobs in the evenings.

Some of Brad’s greatest strengths include his background working as Ohio’s Assistant Attorney General and his time spent representing private businesses, the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation, and the Industrial Commission of Ohio. “I started representing injured workers in 2014, and it has become my passion work,” says Brad. “But the time I spent before that representing the State and private companies gave me a deep understanding of how the defense council operates in workers’ comp cases. Your best arguments are made when you understand the opposition. Understanding the folks across the aisle gives me an edge in securing compensation for our clients.”

Community Involvement

A legal career spent representing injured workers is all about service to the community, and Brad takes that mission to heart. When he’s not wearing his hat as a workers’ comp attorney, he can often be found participating in the firm’s charitable events, including volunteering at the Ronald McDonald House, helping out at food pantries, and participating in the firm’s annual community turkey giveaway. A good neighbor to his Dublin, Ohio community, Brad has also coached local sports teams, including his son’s football, baseball, and basketball teams.

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working, Brad enjoys hiking, fishing, and gardening with his partner. He is a proud Buckeye football and Cardinals baseball fan (having grown up in St. Louis). He enjoys watching games with his dog Rudy. During the spring months, Brad can be found scouring farm fields searching for arrowheads to add to his growing collection.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Brad Howenstein

A team player and always willing to help out, Brad’s work ethic and care for his clients aligns perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Brad and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

attorneys.bio:
“Businesses need to understand how IP relates to their products, their customers, and their competitors, and use that understanding to optimize their use of IP. That’s why I’m here.”

Thomas W. Humphrey is a Partner with Wood, Herron & Evans and is involved in all phases of the firm's practice, with concentration on electronic, software and computer technologies.

Tom joined Wood, Herron & Evans in 1993. He has served as Chairman of the Cincinnati Bar Association's Computer and High Technology Law Committee. Admitted to the Ohio bar in 1993 and to the U.S. District Court, Southern District of Ohio in 1994, Tom is also registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.

At the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Tom received both a Bachelor of Science degree and a Master of Science degree in Electrical Engineering in 1989, and he was a member of Tau Beta Pi and Eta Kappa Nu. He then graduated cum laude with a Juris Doctor degree from Harvard University.

Tom is an active member of the Cincinnati Bar Association and the Cincinnati Intellectual Property Law Association. He has lectured on patent, copyright and trade secret law at Xavier University's College of Business Administration, at Northern Kentucky University's Salmon P. Chase College of Law and at various legal education seminars. Tom was named as one of the Ohio Super Lawyers - 2006 Rising Stars by Law and Politics Media. He has been recognized by The Best Lawyers in America® since 2014. Tom is the Practice Group Leader for the Electrical/Software patent prosecution practice group within the firm. He resides in Glendale, Ohio with his wife Susan and their two children.

attorneys.name: Douglas Hunter
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Drawing on a Storied Legal Career to Win Cases for Injured Ohioans

Douglas (Doug) Hunter is a Partner at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation trials and hearings. Building on a career that’s already seen him successfully resolve hundreds of cases in favor of his clients, Doug’s infallible commitment to helping clients obtain compensation for their losses has made him an invaluable part of the NRS Injury Law team.

An Advocate for the Working People

Doug knew from a very young age that he wanted to pursue law, as his father was a judge and his grandfather was an attorney. As a young man, Doug worked in various fields before his first job as a lawyer, including as a laborer at a rubber plant where he saw how dangerous working-class jobs can be. As fate would have it, Doug’s first attorney role was in workers’ compensation.

“I sort of fell into workers’ comp, really,” Doug says, describing how he became a multi-decade workers’ compensation attorney with a passion for helping working people. “It was my first job out of law school, and while I really enjoyed the field, my first role was as a defense attorney representing employers. I left that job within six months to shift over and help injured workers, but those initial months helped me learn a great deal about how workers’ compensation law is set up in Ohio, and, spoiler alert, it’s not set up to benefit the worker! But my in-depth experience on both sides of the aisle, plus my passion for helping people who are thrown into a system that works against them, makes my role as a plaintiff’s attorney the best one I could ask for.”

Leveraging Decades of Trial Experience to Provide Clients with Their Best Opportunities for Success

Doug’s vast career experience helps him secure benefits for injured workers. In a phrase, he has countless hours in first-chair jury trials, arbitration, and appellate oral arguments. He has perfected the securing and defending of depositions of lay and expert witnesses. He has provided immense trial support and assistance to senior attorneys while assisting in trial preparation and drafting firm pleadings, motions, and briefs.

Throughout his career, Doug has tried civil cases in several Ohio courts, has tried arbitrations, and has argued cases before several Ohio appellate courts. He has represented parties before state and local administrative agencies, including the Industrial Commission of Ohio. Doug has negotiated hundreds of settlements for personal injury and workers’ compensation claims and has additional experience in insurance coverage law, consumer and contract law, and civil defense law. He is also deeply skilled in negotiation, torts, trial practice, third-party liability, and industrial accidents. A trial attorney by nature who focuses primarily on the litigation side of workers’ compensation cases, Doug’s best traits are on full display when he shows up for clients in court.

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working, Doug spends time with his wife and their three children. Doug is a big fan of Cleveland and Ohio State sports and enjoys golfing and traveling with family and friends. On weekends, Doug can usually be found attending swim meets or golf tournaments. During holidays, he packs the bags, rounds up the family, and hits the road for an adventure.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Douglas Hunter

“Clients choose NRS Injury Law because of the firm’s proven track record of success,” Doug said, describing what initially drew him to the firm. Beyond those sentiments, Doug also firmly believes in NRS Injury Law’s mission to provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day. To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Doug and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Doug brings his commitment to others from his work at the firm back into his personal life. A father to three children, he and his wife spend much of their free time volunteering and supporting their children’s activities, primarily their school and sports-related endeavors. The two also work together in raising money for sporting events and chaperoning extracurricular activities.

attorneys.bio:
Steven Hupp was born and raised in Youngstown, Ohio. Mr. Hupp is an Equity Shareholder and one of the founders of the firm. He has been an attorney since 1988. Mr. Hupp began trying medical malpractice cases in 1990. Over the past 28 years, Mr. Hupp has enjoyed tremendous success in the courtroom. He has been first chair counsel in over one hundred jury trials and he has won all but eight of these trials. On two occasions, Mr. Hupp won a defense verdict for his clients after admitting that they breached the standard of care.

Mr. Hupp is routinely engaged as trial counsel in cases involving catastrophic injuries and wrongful death on behalf of physicians and hospitals throughout the state of Ohio. Mr. Hupp has obtained defense verdicts in difficult cases dealing with diverse areas of medicine, such as cardiology, emergency medicine, general surgery, colorectal surgery, internal medicine and narcotic overdoses. Mr. Hupp has a special interest in cases involving strokes, heart attacks, pulmonary emboli, breast cancer and colon cancer. On two occasions, Mr. Hupp won a defense verdict for his clients after admitting that they breached the standard of care.

Mr. Hupp currently spends one-third of his time representing long-term care clients, including rehabilitation hospitals, nursing homes and assisted living facilities. Mr. Hupp has taken two nursing home negligence cases to jury trial and prevailed on both.

After law school, Mr. Hupp worked as a law clerk to the Honorable Blanche Krupansky in the Eighth District Court of Appeals. Mr. Hupp has practiced as appellate counsel in the United States Supreme Court, the Ohio Supreme Court, the Federal Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals and several Ohio District Courts.

Mr. Hupp has enjoyed an AV Preeminent rating (the highest possible) from Martindale-Hubbell since age 34. He has been named an Ohio Super lawyer for the past eleven years (2008 through 2018).

Mr. Hupp has a special interest in cases involving strokes, heart attacks, pulmonary emboli, breast cancer and colon cancer. On two occasions, Mr. Hupp won a defense verdict for his clients after admitting that they breached the standard of care.

Mr. Hupp currently spends one-third of his time representing long-term care clients, including rehabilitation hospitals, nursing homes and assisted living facilities. Mr. Hupp has taken two nursing home negligence cases to jury trial and prevailed on both.

After law school, Mr. Hupp worked as a law clerk to the Honorable Blanche Krupansky in the Eighth District Court of Appeals. Mr. Hupp has practiced as appellate counsel in the United States Supreme Court, the Ohio Supreme Court, the Federal Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals and several Ohio District Courts.

Mr. Hupp has enjoyed an AV Preeminent rating (the highest possible) from Martindale-Hubbell since age 34. He has been named an Ohio Super lawyer for the past eleven years (2008 through 2018).

attorneys.name: Dustin R. Hurley Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Lawyers in Middletown, OH
attorneys.bio:
Dustin R. Hurley has enjoyed a diverse legal career, making him uniquely qualified to effectively represent businesses and business owners. His practice is focused on Business Law, Commercial Real Estate, and Business Litigation.

He was born and raised in Middletown, Ohio, the son of a steel worker and a probation officer. After graduating from Middletown High School, he attended Miami University Farmer School of Business. He graduated from business school with a degree in Business Management. Dustin immediately attended University of Dayton School of Law.

During law school, Dustin worked in his stepfather's law practice located in Springboro, Ohio, where he learned the business side of running a law practice. It was also during law school that he interned for the prosecutor of a local municipal court, which sparked an interest in trial practice.

Following graduation from law school, Dustin accepted a position as an Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for Montgomery County, Ohio. He was immediately in the courtroom every day, handling a high volume of cases. This is where Dustin had his first trials and started to develop his strong litigation skills.

Dustin eventually left the Prosecutor's Office and rejoined his stepfather's law firm. In this role, Dustin worked directly with individuals and families in resolving debt issues, including bankruptcy. He also gained extensive experience in federal court litigation during this time, including many motions, oral arguments, and evidentiary hearings.

Always having an entrepreneurial spirit, and a business education background, Dustin wanted to use his knowledge and experience to help business owners. That was the driving force behind starting Hurley Law. Since that time, Hurley Law has grown into a law firm with multiple attorneys and staff, working in multiple office locations, and representing clients in nearly all practice areas.

Now, Dustin's practice is primarily focused on serving as outside general counsel for businesses. His diverse experience allows him to effectively advise business clients on a wide range of legal topics, from drafting simple contracts to being lead trial counsel on multi-year federal litigation. This reduces the need for business clients to work with multiple lawyers or law firms, and allows him to be more effective by having a deeper understanding of his clients' business.

Dustin is also known for being an active volunteer within the Middletown, Ohio community. He has served as a board member and officer for multiple non-profit organizations, and commission member for the City of Middletown. Dustin was previously the City Attorney for a nearby municipality. He has been an acting prosecutor in multiple courts. Dustin is also a frequent lecturer to attorneys and Judges for Continuing Legal Education seminars. He frequently plays drums for his church's music team.

He has been voted by other attorneys as an Ohio Super Lawyer Rising Star since 2016. Dustin is also rated by his peers and Martindale-Hubbell as having High Professional Achievement.

attorneys.name: Catherine H. Jackson
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Dayton, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Catherine H. Jackson is a skilled litigator at Bieser Greer in Dayton, Ohio, representing clients in complex civil and criminal matters throughout Ohio. Her practice focuses on litigation and appellate advocacy, where she brings meticulous preparation, persuasive writing and strong courtroom presence to every case. Her ability to navigate high-stakes disputes with clarity and precision has earned her the trust of both clients and colleagues alike.

Ms. Jackson earned her Juris Doctor cum laude from the University of Dayton School of Law, graduating one semester early. During law school, she served as President of the Criminal Law Association, a Dean’s Fellow and a member of the Law Review. She also received the CALI Excellence for the Future Awards in both Constitutional Law and Criminal Procedure for achieving the highest grades in those courses. She demonstrated exceptional academic performance, finishing in the top 2% on the Ohio Bar Examination. She completed her undergraduate studies at Bethany College in West Virginia, earning her Bachelor of Arts in English literature magna cum laude.

Ms. Jackson is admitted to practice in the State of Ohio, as well as the U.S. District Courts for the Southern and Northern Districts of Ohio. She is also a member of the Carl D. Kessler Inn of Court, where she engages with peers and judges to promote professionalism and excellence in advocacy. She is an active member of the Dayton Bar Association, the Ohio State Bar Association and the Clark County Bar Association. In 2023, she furthered her trial advocacy skills by completing the National Criminal Defense College’s Deryl Dantzler Trial College.

Prior to joining Bieser Greer, Ms. Jackson gained extensive private practice experience, handling a broad range of litigation matters, including domestic relations, criminal defense, negotiations and appellate work. Known for her analytical insight and composed advocacy, Ms. Jackson is committed to achieving just and effective outcomes for every client she represents.

Past Experience

Extensive prior private practice experience in litigation and motion practice, including bench trials for both domestic relations and criminal cases, appellate practice, negotiations, and jury trials.

attorneys.name: Joseph B. Jaap
attorneys.practice_type: Residential Real Estate Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Joe assists clients with a wide range of legal issues, whether personal, family, or business, developing and implementing legal strategies to achieve client goals and to avoid and resolve disputes. Joe advises clients about their real estate and family legal matters, including wills, estate planning, divorce, child support, and related issues. His real estate practice includes both commercial and residential real estate, representing and counseling clients regarding purchases, sales, leasing, condominium development and conversions, condominium management and homeowner associations, construction contracting and construction project management, construction dispute resolution, and mechanic's liens.

Joe also provides general business representation advising clients about business formation, incorporation and joint ventures, contract negotiations, and public bidding. He helps clients resolve issues related to intellectual property, clearance and registration of state and federal trademarks and copyrights, trademark and copyright infringement claim resolution, intellectual property asset transfers and licensing, trade secret protection, and electronic commerce including Internet and domain name issues.

As the BPBS community service coordinator, Joe helps BPBS help others in the community. He has tutored and served as BPBS tutor coordinator for John P. Parker School with the Cincinnati Youth Collaborative, and served as job shadowing coordinator for students from Taft and Withrow High Schools. He is active at his church in youth ministry and education, served as a trustee, and worked in various church committees and activities, including a church remodeling project. He also has served on the board of his neighborhood homeowner association.

A Cincinnati native, after graduating from Purdue with B.S. and M.S. degrees in engineering, Joe served on active duty as an officer and engineer on Navy nuclear-powered ships. His Navy service was aboard a submarine, cruiser, and aircraft carrier, and he remains active with other local Navy veterans, serving on the executive board of the Cincinnati Council of the Navy League. After leaving the Navy, Joe worked for several years as an engineer and was licensed as a professional engineer in Ohio before obtaining his law degree from the University of Michigan. Joe is married, with three children.

attorneys.name: Louis A. Jacobs
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Rights Violations Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Lou Jacobs is a professor emeritus at The Ohio State University College of Law, where he taught employment law, constitutional law, and civil rights law from 1978 through 2003. Upon his retirement from teaching, Lou became of counsel to Marshall Forman & Schlein LLC, where he litigates employment, civil rights, and Constitutional cases.

Lou also spent two years as an Assistant Attorney General for the State of Ohio, serving as Senior Trial Attorney in the Civil Rights Section. He received his B.A. from Syracuse University, his J.D. from the Washington College of Law at The American University, and his LLM from New York University.

Lou has been elected by his peers to be included in Best Lawyers in America in the field of employment law (1989-2017) and was the recipient of the Legal Education Award from the Ohio State Bar Association in 2002. He has written or co-authored numerous books on evidence, civil rights litigation, age discrimination, and equal employment opportunity law, including the Ohio Rules of Evidence Trial Book (1999) and the Employment Practices Manual (West 1995-2017). Lou is a frequent speaker on employment law at OSBA CLE’s Midwest Labor and Employment Law Seminar.

Outside of the office Wayne enjoys hunting, fishing, hiking, shooting, weight training, and Krav Maga.

attorneys.firm_name: Nurenberg, Paris, Heller & McCarthy Co., L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
With over 40 years of experience as a trial attorney, William (Bill) S. Jacobson is recognized for his compassionate advocacy on behalf of families affected by birth injuries and catastrophic medical malpractice. As a dedicated attorney at Nurenberg, Paris, Heller & McCarthy, Bill focuses his practice on representing victims of birth trauma and other severe injuries, helping them navigate complex legal challenges with skill and empathy.

A respected member of the Birth Trauma Litigation Group, Bill is part of a national network of attorneys committed to securing justice for families of children who have suffered brain injuries at birth. His legal scholarship includes a published article in the Journal of the Birth Trauma Litigation Group, where he provided strategic insights on cross-examining defense experts in birth injury cases. He has also written extensively on medical malpractice topics, including deposition techniques and pediatric, obstetrical, and adult malpractice claims.

Bill is a sought-after speaker and educator in the field of medical malpractice litigation. In November 2023, he delivered a lecture in Atlanta to an audience of over 100 attorneys at a seminar co-sponsored by the Birth Trauma Litigation Group and the American Association for Justice, focusing on cross-examining defense experts in birth trauma cases. Additionally, he presented at the Ohio Association for Justice's annual meeting on the calculation of economic loss in catastrophic injury cases. His insights have also been shared at the Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys, where he discussed a landmark birth injury case that resulted in one of the largest verdicts in the region in recent years.

A distinguished legal professional, Bill has been named Ohio Super Lawyers® every year since 2006, an honor reserved for the top 5% of attorneys in the state, as selected by their peers and Law & Politics Media. He was also recognized in Best Lawyers (2015) as one of the top 13 medical malpractice (Plaintiff’s) attorneys in Cleveland.

Beyond his litigation work, Bill served as co-chair of the annual Risk Management Seminar at one of Ohio’s largest hospitals, where he worked alongside hundreds of physicians to promote patient safety and reduce medical errors.

Bill’s dedication to advocating for the injured, educating fellow attorneys, and improving medical accountability has solidified his reputation as a leading trial attorney in birth injury and medical malpractice litigation.

attorneys.practice_type: Insurance & Bad Faith Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Steven G. Janik is the founder and Senior Partner of Janik L.L.P.

Steve graduated from Denison University with a Bachelor of Arts degree, having majored in Economics. He was actively involved in the Denison Campus Government Association, a member of Omicron Delta Epsilon (Economics Honorary), a member of the Board of Directors of the American Shorin-Ryu Karate Association, Inc., a two-year All-Conference Selection in Football, and a recipient of the NCAA Football Post-Graduate Scholarship Award.

Steve obtained his Juris Doctorate from the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law, and thereafter served as Law Clerk to the Honorable Thomas D. Lambros, Chief Judge of the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio. Upon completing his Clerkship, Steve entered private practice, and on September 1, 1988, founded the Firm.

Steve is admitted to practice before the State and Federal Courts for California, Georgia, Kentucky, Maryland, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Texas, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia, as well as the United States Tax Court and the United States Supreme Court.

Steve has served as Special Master to the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio in complex antitrust and asbestos litigation proceedings, as a member of the Federal Judicial Center Task Force on Reducing Trial Delay, and as Chairman of the Magistrate Merit Selection Committee for the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio.

Steve is a member of the California, Kentucky, Maryland, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Georgia, Texas, West Virginia, District of Columbia, Federal, American, and Lawyer-Pilot Bar Associations.

Steve is a senior life member of the Sixth Circuit and life member of the Ohio Court of Appeals Judicial Conferences. He is also a member of the International Association of Defense Counsel, Defense Research Institute, and the American College of Coverage and Extracontractual Counsel. Steve has served as a member of the Orthopedics Leadership Board of the Cleveland Clinic Foundation and is a private pilot, single engine land, instrument rated.

Steve has been listed in The Best Lawyers In America for Commercial Litigation, Insurance Law, and Personal Injury Litigation, every year from 2001 through 2024 and in Ohio "Super Lawyers", every year from 2004 through 2024.

attorneys.name: Terry Jennrich
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Combining Attorney-Client Teamwork and Legal Experience to Craft Winning Cases

Terry Jennrich is an Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Drawing on a multi-decade career representing injured clients since 1986, Terry leverages a wealth of knowledge to help his clients secure the compensation they deserve. His experience arguing cases in Municipal Court, Common Pleas Court, the Court of Appeals, the Industrial Commission, and in federal court positions Terry as one of the most knowledgeable attorneys in Ohio.

A Background Based in Service to Working Ohioans

“When I took my first job at the local grocery store in Medina back in the 1970s, I had no idea I would one day dedicate my life to the law and to helping working people,” Terry said when asked to describe how he found his way to a career as an attorney. After the grocery store, Terry put time in on factory floors and auto dealerships in Northeast Ohio. Terry worked through high school, then received the Medina Rotary Club Scholarship and used it to attend the University of Akron, where he majored in history and political science.

“But as you can imagine, there aren’t many places that hire history buffs,” Terry said. “So I took the LSAT and went to law school.” Terry continued to hold jobs in both the legal field and in computers, serendipitously combining the two skill sets right after he passed the bar by using his computer skills to secure an IT role at a law firm during a period when virtually no firms were hiring recently barred attorneys.

“That was a pretty funny time,” Terry reflected with a chuckle. “The only firms that were hiring wanted experienced attorneys. I’d just passed the bar, so I wasn’t ‘experienced’ yet. But I could fix computers, so a firm hired me to do their IT. Pretty soon, I convinced them to let me represent their clients. I ended up being with that firm for 28 years.”

Helping Ohio Workers Who Cannot Help Themselves

After joining NRS Injury Law, from 2014 through 2024, Terry argued thousands of administrative hearings at the Industrial Commission on behalf of injured workers. “I argued six to ten hearings per day, three to five days per week, for ten years,” Terry said. “All those hearings revolved around helping injured workers in their workers’ compensation cases.” Presently, Terry primarily works with the intake department, where he serves a vital role: onboarding clients, educating them about the legal process, interviewing them to learn about their injuries, asking the right questions to build a compelling case, and preparing clients for deposition.

Terry’s rich background helps him immensely in this role. He’s worked in probate, divorce, bankruptcy, Social Security disability, workers’ compensation, personal injury, slip and falls, premises liability, auto accidents, and medical malpractice. He’s argued cases at a variety of levels, including the Cleveland Municipal Court, Common Pleas Court, Court of Appeals, the Ohio Supreme Court, and in federal court. No attorney has “seen it all,” but Terry comes close. That experience enables him to interact easily with the client in front of him, administer the onboarding process, bring the client into the fold, and make the client an active member of the legal team.

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working, Terry is an avid ballroom dancer and practitioner of T’ai Chi-Ch’uan. A dancer since the 1990s, Terry used to compete in pro-am and amateur ballroom dance competitions. These days, he says ballroom dance is just a good way to socialize, relieve stress, and get a good cardio workout.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Terry Jennrich

“No matter what your particular ‘legal style’ is as an attorney, when the chips are down, you have to be a ruthless advocate for your client,” Terry said in closing. “A lot of pressure is on the injured worker. The workers’ comp system is immensely confusing. That’s why the initial meetings with the client are so important. You have to know what questions to ask and how to draw out the client’s story. Drawing on a multi-decade career representing injured clients since 1986, Terry leverages a wealth of knowledge to help his clients secure the compensation they deserve. His experience arguing cases in Municipal Court, Common Pleas Court, the Court of Appeals, the Industrial Commission, and in federal court positions Terry as one of the most knowledgeable attorneys in Ohio.

A Background Based in Service to Working Ohioans

“When I took my first job at the local grocery store in Medina back in the 1970s, I had no idea I would one day dedicate my life to the law and to helping working people,” Terry said when asked to describe how he found his way to a career as an attorney. Terry worked through high school, then received the Medina Rotary Club Scholarship and used it to attend the University of Akron, where he majored in history and political science.

“That was a pretty funny time,” Terry reflected with a chuckle. “The only firms that were hiring wanted experienced attorneys. I’d just passed the bar, so I wasn’t ‘experienced’ yet. But I could fix computers, so a firm hired me to do their IT. Pretty soon, I convinced them to let me represent their clients. I ended up being with that firm for 28 years.”

attorneys.name: Joseph S. Jeziorowski
attorneys.practice_type: Domestic Relations Law Lawyers in Dublin, OH
attorneys.bio:
As an associate attorney, Joseph Jeziorowski practices primarily in the area of domestic relations law, including divorce, dissolution, custody, post-decree modification, termination of spousal support, child support modification, and appeals.

Joseph's cases primarily consist of high income and high asset situations, with intense conflict between the parties. Joseph focuses on the unique details of every case and changes his approach based on the facts. As an attorney, he is quick thinking and able to adapt to the sudden changes in circumstances that often occur in domestic cases. Joseph is committed to providing diligent and efficient representation to his clients, with an aim to swiftly achieve the client's goals.

Joseph's method for addressing the specific problems associated with each case is extremely thorough. He combs through all the evidence available, in search of any fact which may help his clients get the edge in a case. Joseph is driven and highly capable, pushing to help create the best result possible for each and every client.

Joseph Jeziorowski graduated Summa Cum Laude from the University of Dayton honors program with a double major. Joseph was a member of the Phi Beta Kappa Honor Society and earned Dean's List all semesters. After completing his undergraduate degree, Joseph moved to Columbus to attend The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law. During law school, Joseph served as an associate editor of the Ohio State Journal of Criminal Law. He also spent a summer studying law abroad at St. Anne's College, Oxford University, in England.

Despite his busy schedule as an attorney, Joseph still finds time to enjoy exercise, reading, and watching Cleveland professional sports, all while patiently waiting for the next season of his favorite TV show to air.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey D. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Cleveland Workers Comp Attorney

Attorney Jeffrey D. Johnson is a Cleveland, Ohio, workers' compensation lawyer. With almost 10 years of experience, Jeff Johnson continuously develops strong strategies to help injured workers with their workers' comp cases. Some people injured on the job do not understand the complex system of the Bureau of Workers' Compensation. Jeff helps injured workers navigate the system to receive compensation like temporary total (TT), permanent partial impairment awards (PPI) and permanent total disability (PTD). Other benefits or types of compensation include wage loss, non-working wage loss, living maintenance, or vocational rehabilitation. Workers Comp benefits may be paid by either the BWC or the self-insured employer.

Worker's Compensation in Ohio is a very complicated system. The Managed Care Organizations (MCO), Third Party Administrators (TPA), Bureau of Worker's Compensation (BWC) and most Vocational Rehabilitation Company's all represent the interests of the employer. The largest MCO's in Ohio are: Careworks, Sheakley, CompManagement, 1-888-Ohiocomp and Corvel.

The accident and injury law firm can help determine if disabled employees with a workplace injury need an attorney. Some examples of injuries include but not limited to:

Herniated discs

RSD (Reflex Sympathetic Disorder)

Rotator Cuff Tear

Radiculopathy

Impingement Syndrome

Fractures

Amputations

Death Claims

Torn Medial Meniscus

Torn ACL (Anterior Cruciate Ligament)

Torn MCO (Medial Cruciate Ligament)

Sprains, Strains & Contusions

Head Trauma

Depression

PTSD (Post Traumatic Stress Disorder)

Second and Third Degree Burns

Chemical Inhalation

Electrocution

Construction

Factory

Assembly Workers

Motor Vehicle Accidents

Third party claims and intentional tort cases require experience, strategy and immediate response. The workplace accident lawyers led by Jeff Johnson protect your rights as a hurt worker in your workers comp case. Attorney Johnson also advises clients when to settle workers' comp cases. For more information, contact Jeffrey Johnson, the Cleveland and Akron, Ohio, workers' comp lawyer to answer your workers comp questions. In addition to the successful workmen's compensation practice, Jeff Johnson assists with other areas of practice dedicated to helping injured people in personal injury and medical malpractice cases.

My Story:

"Honesty is the best policy" is Jeff Johnson's motto, whether in a court of law or sitting in the Cleveland Brown's stadium rooting for the Steelers, the Pennsylvania born attorney always remains true to his beliefs. "My father taught me you never get in trouble if you tell the truth," he says. Both Jeff and his brother also learned from their father, an attorney, the value of serving others by choosing the practice of law as a career. But Jeff did not go to law school right out of college, even though "I was always fascinated with the law and politics," he says. "I even did an unpaid internship with Thomas Ridge, who was governor of Pennsylvania while I was a college student."

When Jeff moved to the Cleveland with his bride, Shelley, he worked as a paralegal for Stuart Garson and was given the opportunity to work in Seaman Garson LLC's workers' compensation department. "I appreciated this area of law and realized then it was time to go to law school," says Jeff. "I wanted to do everything I could to become an advocate for injured workers."

Now, as managing attorney for Seaman Garson LLC workers' compensation department, Jeff personally deals with workers' compensation clients. "I enjoy helping people and knowing if we are not there to work for them they would not be able to provide for themselves or their families," he says. "I've become very good at what I do and can quickly identify the issues. That way I can zero in on the problem and then take care of business." To relax from "troubleshooting and putting out fires," Jeff enjoys jogging and coaching his sons' sports teams, especially flag football. "On the playing field there are clear cut rules everyone can follow," he says. "That's not always the case with our tainted American judicial system that often makes it difficult for suffering injured workers to get what is legally due them under Ohio Workers' Compensation laws. But as long as there is a battle waiting to be fought ­ I'm in the game."

Cleveland Workers Comp Attorney

Attorney Jeffrey D. Johnson is a Cleveland, Ohio, workers' compensation lawyer. With almost 10 years of experience, Jeff Johnson continuously develops strong strategies to help injured workers with their workers' comp cases. Some people injured on the job do not understand the complex system of the Bureau of Workers' Compensation. Jeff helps injured workers navigate the system to receive compensation like temporary total (TT), permanent partial impairment awards (PPI) and permanent total disability (PTD). Other benefits or types of compensation include wage loss, non-working wage loss, living maintenance, or vocational rehabilitation. Workers Comp benefits may be paid by either the BWC or the self-insured employer.

Worker's Compensation in Ohio is a very complicated system. The Managed Care Organizations (MCO), Third Party Administrators (TPA), Bureau of Worker's Compensation (BWC) and most Vocational Rehabilitation Company's all represent the interests of the employer. The largest MCO's in Ohio are: Careworks, Sheakley, CompManagement, 1-888-Ohiocomp and Corvel.

attorneys.name: Nadine Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Building Winning Cases with Empathy, Communication, and Collaboration

Nadine Jones is an Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Drawing on her experience in Social Security, disability, and workers’ compensation, Nadine collaborates closely with her clients to build winning cases. A first-generation attorney, Nadine’s working-class upbringing and empathy, along with her work ethic, communication skills, and deep understanding of Ohio law, combine to position her as one of the most effective workers’ compensation attorneys in the state.

A Background in Blue-Collar Ohio

“My mom is a combat veteran and would later become a proud business owner, operating her own family bakery,” Nadine began. “Starting in the 5th grade, I’d wake up at 4:00 a.m., help Mom get the bakery ready, go to school, then come back to close the bakery in the afternoon.” Nadine insists she did not have a hard life, but she tells a story steeped in working-class roots and a blue-collar lifestyle familiar to so many in Ohio. “My dad worked manufacturing jobs, and my family has a rich history in the United Auto Workers,” Nadine said.

While helping with the family business, Nadine also worked part-time at JCPenney, and, since she did very well in high school, Nadine decided to take the LSAT, which she studied in the JCPenney stockroom during her mandated 15-minute break. “I’d do logic games with the mannequins,” Nadine said through a chuckle. Nadine did well on the LSAT and, because she excelled in speech and debate in high school, received a scholarship to attend Youngstown State University.

Helping Others Who Cannot Help Themselves

The further she progressed through her academic career, the more convinced Nadine became that she wanted to become an attorney so she could help those who could not help themselves, individuals up against powerful institutions that bent existing laws and policies to fit their agendas. For one summer, Nadine worked at Community Legal Aid, where she represented impoverished pregnant women facing eviction. “That was a crucible moment for me,” Nadine says. “I had been so naive before. Landlords just choose to ignore the medical documentation provided by tenants and threaten them with homelessness during some of the most vulnerable times of their lives – impoverished, pregnant, bedridden, and sick. Now living in an unimaginable circumstance and unable to work to pay their rent on time. That job made me realize how many people slip through the cracks in this country, and how necessary it is to advocate for those who can’t fight alone.”

As she went through law school, graduated, passed the bar, and began practicing law, Nadine saw many of her family members and friends in the clients she represented. For her, it became her life’s mission to leverage the legal protections and institutions of the state to help people who had experienced a life-changing injury at work.

Work/Life Balance

When she’s not working at the firm’s Euclid office, Nadine loves to read, cook, bake, watch documentaries, attend social events, and make needlepoint Christmas ornaments. “These aren’t just any Christmas ornaments,” Nadine says. “I make fun stuff. Recently I did a needlepoint Christmas ornament of a Celsius energy drink can and a Diet Coke can.”

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Nadine Jones

“We understand what the Civil Rights Act says, and we understand what the Americans with Disabilities Act says,” Nadine said in closing. “But people often forget that the disabled, including disabled workers, are still a protected class of people. At NRS Injury Law, this firm is wholly dedicated to representing working people. The entire ethos of the firm revolves around it, around representing this group of individuals who have been severely disadvantaged due to a workplace injury, individuals who are now wondering how on earth to move forward with their lives. This firm exists to help them solve that problem.”

Nadine’s commitment to working people, her communication and listening abilities, case-building skills, empathy, relatability, and her unmatched rhetoric talents are all traits that align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Nadine and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Nadine volunteers at the University of Akron School of Law by coaching moot court students. She assists them in drafting and delivering compelling arguments with a focus on international law. Nadine was also recently elected to the Board of Directors for Simply Slavic, a cultural heritage nonprofit based in Youngstown. “The primary intent of our organization is to encourage cultural bonds within the community through education, outreach, and public events,” Nadine says. “We promote Eastern European art, language, and food through activities like our big Simply Slavic Heritage Festival, which we put on every summer in downtown Youngstown.” The nonprofit promotes local scholarships, and Nadine and other members engage with residents of a sister city in Slovakia.

attorneys.name: Joseph A. Kacyon
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cuyahoga Falls, OH
attorneys.bio:
Is the lead attorney of Hoover Kacyon’s Estate Planning/Probate and Business Practice Groups, as well as an experienced family law litigator.

Attorney Joe Kacyon completed his undergraduate studies at the Rochester Institute of Technology. He attended the University of Akron School of Law, where he participated in Law Review and graduated Magna Cum Laude in the top 10 of his class. Joe also holds a Masters of Business Administration from the University of Akron.

Joe is licensed to practice law in Ohio and Pennsylvania and is a member of the Akron Bar Association, the Ohio Bar Association and the Pennsylvania Bar Association. Joe has been named to the top 10 best lawyers in Ohio for client satisfaction in 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018 and has been named as a Super Lawyers Rising Star in the field of Estate Planning/Probate for 2017, 2018 and 2019.

Now, Joe focuses his practice on family law litigation, business, and estate matters. Joe is an experienced litigator in courts throughout Ohio, in all of his fields of practice. Joe’s business background, both in education and business ownership experience, combined with years of representing clients in these types of matters, all make him uniquely qualified to handle the complex and various needs of clients looking to protect their families and assets.

During law school Joe gained experience working for a US Federal District Court Judge and a US Circuit Court Appeals Judge. After law school, Joe began the law firm of Joseph Kacyon and Associates, where he acquired practices of retiring lawyers, learning from their decades of experience and knowledge, and building an additional client base based on his unique passion and energy. Joe has been named to the top 10 best lawyers in Ohio for client satisfaction in 2015, 2016, and 2017 and has been named as a Super Lawyers Rising Star in the field of Estate Planning/Probate for 2017 and 2018.

Joe has a unique blend of experience in business, bankruptcy, probate, and family law that sets him apart from other lawyers in the field. Many family law attorneys do not practice business and bankruptcy law. There is a great deal of intersection between these areas of law. Very often a family law matter will include a business interest that needs to be divided or valued and having a grasp for business matters and business law is a great asset in those cases. Other times, an estate plan will require an understanding of the corporate structure of the family business. Unfortunately, other times a divorce will lead to bankruptcy or vice versa and understanding how a bankruptcy affects a divorce proceeding may be crucial to getting the desired results. Joe’s Masters of Business Administration gives him a deeper understanding of business, business valuation, corporate structure, and bankruptcy than many attorneys can offer. Hoover Kacyon prefers to attach a team of lawyers to every case. Joe is often a part of cases that involve businesses, business law, bankruptcy or complex financial issues.

Joe also has an excellent appellate record. Joe’s time as an extern for the Federal Courts, including the 6th Circuit Court of Appeals gave him an inside perspective on the appeals process. His appeals include cases in family law, child support, custody, probate estates, probate guardianships, real estate, and criminal law.

attorneys.bio:
Emily is an Attorney in the litigation group, where she represents clients in a broad range of legal matters, including insurance defense, bankruptcy, corporate business law, appropriations, and intellectual property. She has a strong passion for intellectual property law, with a particular focus on copyrights and trademarks. Emily is committed to providing strategic and innovative legal solutions, leveraging her sharp analytical skills and keen attention to detail.

Emily began practicing law in 2025 and approaches her practice with tenacity and dedication to client advocacy. She has experience handling complex litigation matters, navigating intricate regulatory frameworks, and advising businesses on risk management and compliance. Her practice also includes defending corporate clients in high-stakes disputes and guiding businesses through transactional and contractual challenges.

Emily graduated summa cum laude from the University of Alabama before earning her juris doctorate from William & Mary Law School. While in law school, she served as an Articles Editor for the William & Mary Bill of Rights Journal, refining her legal writing and research skills.

Beyond the courtroom, Emily leads an active and adventurous life. A Cincinnati native, she enjoys playing tennis, softball, and pickleball. She has a deep appreciation for the outdoors and can often be found hiking scenic trails or traveling the world, immersing herself in different cultures. An avid bibliophile and film connoisseur, she finds inspiration in literature and cinema. She also has a passion for cooking and scrapbooking, always exploring new creative outlets.
