attorneys.name: Joseph W. Kampman
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Joe joined Ziegler Metzger in 1992. He is a partner and chairman of the firm's Probate and Estate Planning Group. His practice is focused on estate planning, estate and trust administration and general corporate/business law.

His clients include high net worth individuals and families, young professionals and entrepreneurs, business owners and physicians, dentists and other medical professionals. This representation has led to many long-standing relationships consistent with the firm's culture of providing "Counsel of Good Value".

Joe's experience in estate planning, probate and estate/trust disputes enables him to bring creative ideas to the table to help heirs, beneficiaries, trustees and executors in estate and trust litigation matters. In conflict situations involving will contests, trustee removal and abuse of elderly due to undue influence, incompetency or fraud, Joe works closely with the firm's litigation team in achieving our client's goals.

Another important part of his practice is representation of business owners in the variety of legal issues that arise in the course of the operation of their business. Such matters include general contract review, resolution of shareholder disputes, buy-sell agreements, the starting, sale or acquisition of a business and business succession planning.

Joe obtained his Juris Doctorate from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law in 1980. He also graduated from the Cleveland State University Graduate School of Business attaining his Masters of Business Administration degree. He earned his undergraduate degree in Business Administration from the Cleveland State University.

Joe is a member of the Ohio, Cleveland and Lake County Bar Associations and Estate Planning Council of Cleveland. He is also a member and Past Chairman of the American Cancer Society Planning Giving Committee (Lake/Geauga/Ashtabula County Units), member of the Catholic Lawyers Guild (Speaker's Bureau) and a former member and past Chairman of the Mentor Municipal Planning Commission.

He also served on the Promoting Philanthropy Committee of the Cleveland Foundation. Joe is a well-received speaker on estate planning and charitable gifting issues at numerous Continuing Legal Education seminars and presentations for charitable organizations. He takes great pleasure in assisting clients in achieving their charitable goals.

Joe lives in Mentor, Ohio with his wife, Debbie, and has three sons, Matt, Brian and Greg. Brian is also an attorney at the firm. Joe is a sports enthusiast and also enjoys running, playing golf, travelling and spending time with family and friends.

attorneys.name: Kenneth P. Karlock
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security -- Disability Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ken has been involved in Social Security Disability since graduating from law school in 1993.

Ken began his career as a Disability Claims Adjudicator with the Bureau of Disability Determination, the entity that develops Social Security Disability claims and renders decisions. He quickly advanced into a supervisory role, training and overseeing new Claims Adjudicators.

In 1997 Ken left the Bureau and has since dedicated his legal career to representing the disabled in Social Security matters at all levels, from initial applications through federal court proceedings.

Ken has been a member of NOSSCR since 1997. He was a co-founder of the Columbus Bar Association Social Security Disability Committee, and served as co-chair of the committee from 2010-2013. In 2013 he received the Columbus Bar Association's President's Award for his work on the committee. Ken is a frequent lecturer at Social Security Disability seminars and is routinely consulted by colleagues on vocational matters.

Away from his career in the law, Ken is happily married to his business partner Julie Hall and is the father of two amazing children.

Amy Keating successfully navigates clients through all variety of family law matters, specializing in complex marital estates and international family law issues.

Amy was appointed as an adjunct professor at Case Western Reserve University College of Law in 2016 and continues to teach Family Law. She is a Fellow of the American Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers and has been recognized as a speaker and author on family law topics, including inclusion in Chambers & Partners High Net Worth rankings in 2023. Amy and her colleagues have represented clients on international family law issues before the Supreme Court of the United States, participated in briefing with the Cox International Law Center, and been consulted on international family law issues, including The Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction.

Amy is experienced in Alternative Dispute Resolution methods and aims to resolve matters through negotiation when appropriate. If that’s not possible, she is prepared to litigate effectively. Amy is also a certified family law mediator.

“She is really the up-and-comer and is known across the state. She speaks at conventions and has a lot of high-level cases. She has learned her craft very quickly.” – Chambers & Partners Ranked, Family/Matrimonial: High Net Worth client (2023)

Amy is a lifelong Clevelander and avid (long suffering) football fan. She’s always willing to try a new restaurant or recipe with a good glass of wine—or hike or run the Metroparks to burn off some of the calories.

sections.content:
Amy Keating successfully navigates clients through all variety of family law matters, specializing in complex marital estates and international family law issues.

Amy is experienced in Alternative Dispute Resolution methods and aims to resolve matters through negotiation when appropriate. If that’s not possible, she is prepared to litigate effectively. Amy is also a certified family law mediator.

attorneys.name: Daniel Gerard Keating
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Warren, OH
attorneys.bio:
Daniel G. Keating was born and raised in Warren, Ohio, graduating from John F. Kennedy High School in 1975. He obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree from Concordia University in Montreal, Canada, in 1979, and his Juris Doctor degree from the University of Toledo, College of Law, in 1982. Dan was sworn in as an attorney in November, 1982, and he then joined his Father, W. Leo Keating, in the practice of law in Warren, Ohio.

Through his career, Dan has represented clients and argued cases throughout the State of Ohio, including before the Ohio Supreme Court, and Federal Courts.

Dan's practice has been diversified through the years including extensive criminal practice, medical malpractice defense, personal injury, probate, domestic relations and business services. Over the years, Dan's client list has included Warren General Hospital, Premier Health Plan and Sony Entertainment America, among others. He currently serves as General Counsel to the Western Reserve Port Authority/Youngstown Warren Regional Airport.

Dan is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association (Member, Aviation Law Committee), the Trumbull County Bar Association and the Lawyer-Pilots Bar Association. He served as President of the Trumbull County Bar Association from 2005 to 2007, and was formerly the Chairman of the Trumbull County Certified Grievance Committee. He also served as the first Bar Counsel of the Trumbull County Bar Association. Dan is active in community affairs, serving on the Advisory Board of the Salvation Army and on the Board of the Warren Heritage Center.

attorneys.name: Stephen T. Keefe Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Catastrophic Personal Injury Lawyers in Lakewood, OH
attorneys.bio:
For more than 25 years, I have dedicated my legal career to helping injured people through their toughest of times and darkest of moments. A fundamental value I hold close to my heart is genuinely caring for my clients. I understand what it feels like when you are seriously injured or when a family member or loved one is killed due to someone else's fault. This is when you need an attorney who genuinely cares about your needs and who is committed to ethically and aggressively pursuing your legal rights. This is what my law firm does, and we do it well.

My firm represents clients not only in Cleveland, Lakewood and Northeast Ohio, but also throughout Ohio, including in Akron, Canton, Medina, Youngstown, Columbus, Toledo, Dayton and Cincinnati. We take on causes, not simply cases. We work tirelessly to investigate and pursue your claims. No stones are left unturned.

I graduated from Case Western Reserve University School of Law in 1996 and have been practicing law in Ohio ever since. Before entering private practice, I worked as a Judicial Staff Attorney for two respected Cuyahoga County Common Pleas Judges so I could learn the inner workings of Ohio's court system. Not long after entering private practice, I was elected President of the Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys. I currently serve on the Board of Trustees for the Ohio Association for Justice, a non-profit organization dedicated to fighting for the rights of Ohioans who are seriously injured through no fault of their own.

The human element I bring to my law practice extends to my personal life. When I am not practicing law, I am actively involved in my community, spending time with my family, supporting Ohio's sports teams and cultural diversity, and writing and playing original music with my band, Robbing Mary. I am beyond thankful that my family and former clients actively support what I do for a living. These strong relationships make me count my blessings on a daily basis and make me a better person and a better lawyer for my diverse clients.

Martindale-Hubbell’s highest AV Preeminent Peer Review Rating of 5.0 out of 5.0

AVVO’s highest rating of Superb, 10 out of 10

Dedicated Service Award, Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys, 2002-2004, 2008-2009

attorneys.bio:
Jay, a partner at Elk & Elk since 2011, focuses on civil trial work in state and federal courts in matters of medical negligence and wrongful death arising from birth injury, surgery; oncological, cardiac and pharmaceutical product liability causes. Jay has presented more than 70 cases to jury, including: felony prosecution, criminal defense, civil defense and civil plaintiff cases. He has been lead counsel on cases in more than 30 Ohio counties, appellate courts and the Supreme Court of Ohio.

Jay was included in the 22nd and 23rd Edition of The Best Lawyers in America® for Medical Malpractice Law and Personal Injury Litigation.

Jay has been recognized as an "Ohio Super Lawyer" for six consecutive years, maintains the highest AVVO rating and received a 5.0/5.0 AV Preeminent Martindale-Hubbell® Peer Review Rating™ by members of the Bar and Judiciary for his legal ability and professional ethical standards. He has been named to the Top Five in Cleveland by Super Lawyers from 2012-2015, Top Ten Ohio Super Lawyer’s list from 2011-2015 by Cincinnati and Columbus Super Lawyers magazines, Top 100 Ohio Super Lawyers from 2010-2017 and Top 50 lawyers in Cleveland by Super Lawyers for 2009, 2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017. Jay is a past member of the board of trustees for Ohio Association of Justice and currently serves on Board of Trustees for The Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys. Nationally, he’s a member of the American Association of Justice's “Leadership Forum.”

Jay speaks internationally to medical and legal groups on the issue of birth injury and medical liability. In 2008, Jay was reviewer for a fetal monitoring textbook used by physicians around the country on the issue of liability for birth injuries. Jay has a chapter published in the 6th edition of Comprehensive Gynecology, Medical Legal Issues (2011) and in the 7th edition of Comprehensive Gynecology, Medical-Legal Risk Management (2017.) The respect of the medical community provides access to leading experts and optimal results.

When Jay isn't working, he enjoys spending time with his family, watching his kids play sports and attending various other sporting events.

attorneys.name: Paul J. Kellogg
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Montgomery, OH
attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years Paul has helped individuals and businesses with a variety of personal and business transactions. Individuals come to Paul for assistance with wills, trusts, estate planning, probate, and residential real estate transactions, while his business clients utilize his experience to provide guidance with business strategy, contract drafting and negotiation, mergers and acquisitions, trademarks, corporate governance, and licensing. Many of Paul’s business clients see him as their outside general counsel.

Prior to joining Phillips Law Firm, Inc. Paul served as the Vice President and General Counsel for two privately held companies and as the Director of Estate and Business Planning for the Cincinnati office of Northwestern Mutual. These experiences allow him to provide proactive advice and counsel to individuals, families, entrepreneurs, and privately held businesses and their owners.

Paul is a life-long Cincinnati resident, having grown up in West Chester, Ohio and attended Cincinnati Moeller High School. Paul went on to study communications at Ohio University, where he met his wife Karen, graduating Cum Laude. After graduating from Ohio University Paul went on to the University of Dayton School of Law where his studies focused on business law, probate and estate planning.

Paul and his wife currently live in West Chester with their three children. In his time away from the office Paul enjoys exercising, bicycling, fishing, playing golf and traveling with his family.

attorneys.name: James M. Kelly
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial/Corporate Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
James M. Kelly is the firm’s senior litigation partner. With 38 years of experience, Jim focuses his practice in business litigation and counseling businesses on contract disputes, employment agreements, enforcement of restrictive covenants, and employment practices. He has represented, for example, manufacturers, franchisors, construction companies, financial institutions, and technology companies.

Jim has represented the firm’s clients in state and federal courts in many states, including Ohio, Alabama, California, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Massachusetts, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, and Texas. Jim also practices on behalf of the firm’s clients before administrative agencies such as state civil rights commissions, industrial commissions, and the EEOC.

Jim also represents injured victims in personal injury claims. In this practice area, as well as his business practice, Jim has experience representing clients in mediation and arbitration. He believes using alternative dispute resolution methods are an efficient and less costly way of resolving disputes for clients.

Martindale Hubbell has recognized Jim as AV® Preeminent Review Rated, the highest possible rating in both legal ability and ethical standards. He has been recognized as an Ohio Super Lawyer for Business Litigation since 2010. Jim brings his firm’s philosophy of service and commitment to every client’s issues and concerns. His personal goal as an attorney and counselor is to understand his clients’ needs and efficiently achieve the best result possible.

Jim lives in Madeira with his wife, Dana. They have four children. In his spare time, Jim enjoys golf, travel, history, Cincinnati sports, and most especially, his family and three dogs.

attorneys.practice_type: Consumer Bankruptcy Lawyers in Dayton, OH
attorneys.bio:
John F. Kennel attended the University of Dayton School of Law where he focused his studies on advocacy and dispute resolution. Mr. Kennel received his J.D. in May 2011, graduating in the top 15% of his class and earning concentration honors.

Prior to law school, Mr. Kennel attended Miami University as a Harrison Scholar. Named after United States President Benjamin Harrison, a Miami graduate, the scholarship has long been considered Miami's most prestigious award. Mr. Kennel earned his B.A. in Anthropology in 2007.

Mr. Kennel's practice includes the following areas of law: Consumer Bankruptcy, Foreclosure Defense, Consumer Law, and General Civil Litigation.

Mr. Kennel was admitted to the Ohio Bar in 2013, scoring in the top 3% of all candidates on the February 2013 bar examination. He is also admitted in Massachusetts and the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. Mr. Kennel is a member of the Dayton Bar Association, the National Association of Consumer Bankruptcy Attorneys and The Thomas F. Waldron American Bankruptcy Law Forum.

In his spare time Mr. Kennel enjoys spending time with his wife Dianne and their dog Loki. Mr. Kennel is an avid supporter of FC Bayern Munich, the Boston Red Sox and the Green Bay Packers.

attorneys.name: Paige Kern
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cuyahoga Falls, OH
attorneys.bio:
Paige is licensed to practice law in Ohio.

Paige graduated cum laude from Youngstown State University in 2019, earning her B.A. in Psychology. She then received her Juris Doctorate from the University of Akron in 2022.

During her time in law school, Paige worked as a law clerk and gained significant experience in juvenile and corporate law. She volunteered with the Re-Entry Clinic and Expungement Clinic at the University of Akron, helping low-income clients file clemency applications and applications to seal their criminal records. She also volunteered extensively with several non-profits, including Crisis Text Line and various animal shelters, even successfully managing a cat shelter at the height of the COVID pandemic. These experiences have helped shape Paige into an empathetic and passionate advocate for her clients.

Paige is licensed to practice law in Ohio and is a member of the Akron Bar Association and the Ohio State Bar Association. She practices primarily in domestic relations, juvenile, and adoption matters.

Paige is an avid reader and Cleveland Cavaliers fan, and you can usually find her singing karaoke with friends or enjoying time with her partner and their cats when she is not practicing law.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney James M. Kersey is the founder and principal of the law firm of the same name based in Cleveland, Ohio. Mr. Kersey's legal practice has been focused exclusively on criminal defense for more than 50 years. He has tried more than 300 jury trials, including 65 aggravated murder cases and 30 death penalty cases. He has attained more than 82 jury verdict wins, including 12 aggravated murder cases and one death penalty case.

In 2009, Mr. Kersey represented a client accused of "double murder," and won two acquittals on his client's behalf. His law firm has handled a significant number of high-profile cases, defending political figures, celebrities and sports personalities.

In his white collar criminal defense practice, lawyer James Kersey has tried several state and federal RICO cases, and has also represented lawyers, medical doctors and police officers accused of various white collar crimes.

Cuyahoga Criminal Defense Lawyers Association, member and past president

Recipient of the John Butler Lifetime Achievement Award for Excellence in Criminal Trial Work

Ohio State Bar Association

Super Lawyer Listing 2010, 2011,2012, 2013, 2014, 2015 , 2016 , 2017 , 2018 , 2019

Mr. Kersey has authored numerous articles on the subject of criminal trial practice, spoken at length on matters involving criminal law, and served as an expert in the area of firearms and ballistics.

attorneys.name: Steve Kilburn
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lebanon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Steve Kilburn is a Warren County native who lives with his wife in Morrow. He graduated from Eastern Kentucky University in 2010 magna cum laude as an honors scholar. He attended the University of Dayton School of Law on an academic scholarship where he served as a staff writer and comment editor for the University of Dayton Law Review in the 2011-2012 and 2012-2013 school years, respectively. While in law school, Steve clerked at Warren County Juvenile & Probate Court under Honorable Judge Michael Powell. He graduated from the University of Dayton School of Law in the spring of 2013 and was admitted to the practice of law that same year.

After law school, Steve acquired experience in personal injury and medical malpractice. In 2014, however, Steve joined the Rittgers firm and discovered his passion for representing clients facing criminal, traffic, and juvenile delinquency charges. His practice at Rittgers Rittgers & Nakajima is focused nearly exclusively on criminal, traffic, and juvenile delinquency defense in Southwest Ohio.

Steve has a strong record of success when defending suspects involved with criminal investigations or defending individuals charged with criminal, traffic, or juvenile offenses. For instance, he has resolved many cases favorably for clients who were facing various non-violent and violent misdemeanor and felony convictions, lengthy jail and prison sentences, OVI/DUI convictions, embarrassing sex offender registration requirements, and burdensome driver's license suspensions. In countless situations, he has either successfully prevented criminal charges from being filed against his clients, has minimized the severe impact of charges, or has achieved a not-guilty verdicts for his clients following bench trials and jury trials.

Because of his experience as a criminal defense lawyer, Steve understands the government often over-charges individuals and can rush to judgment, make unfair assumptions, and rely upon non-credible information when charging folks with crimes. He also understands that frequently, people make bad decisions due to a mental health issue or stress, a substance abuse issue, or just being at the wrong place at the wrong time. Regardless of the situation, Steve understands that every person who is either facing or is charged with a crime is a human being who needs and deserves a competent, skillful, and hard-working lawyer on their side.

Steve is thorough, treats every case as though it is own, and is willing to go the extra mile for his clients. He feels fortunate to be able to help people during what is often the most scary and uncertain time of their lives.

attorneys.name: Robert P. King
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation - Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Robert P. King has practiced law with Bugbee & Conkle since 1985, primarily representing both state fund employers and self-insured employers in workers' compensation defense throughout Ohio, including Toledo, Lima, Mansfield, Cleveland, Akron, Cambridge, Columbus, Cincinnati, Dayton, and Portsmouth, among other hearing districts. Rob successfully defends employers in workers' compensation disability and injury claims, such as claim and death allowances, permanent total disability, temporary total disability, additional and psychological condition allowances. Rob regularly appears before the Bureau of Workers' Compensation and the Industrial Commission of Ohio, including hearings before district hearing officers, staff hearing officers, and the full Industrial Commission. Rob also represents employers before the Bureau of Workers' Compensation's Self-Insured Employers Evaluation Board (SIEEB), as well as the Self-Insured Review Panel on matters regarding self-insurance compliance. Rob advises employers on issues involving compensability of claims, self-insured complaints, self-insured administrative rules, the administration of claims for injured workers, violation of specific safety requirements (VSSR), setting reserves, and proper claim management.

Rob received his Bachelor of Arts Degree from Davidson College in 1980 with a degree in Economics. He received his Juris Doctor degree, cum laude, from the University of Toledo College of Law in 1983. Rob has practiced law in Toledo continuously since 1983. Rob is a frequent lecturer throughout Ohio at various institutes and seminars presented by bar associations, the Northwestern Ohio Self-Insurers Association and the Ohio Self-Insurers Association. Rob is a former four-term President of the Northwestern Ohio Self-Insurers' Association. Rob also is a past two-term chairman and a current member of the Workers' Compensation Committee of the Toledo Bar Association and a member of the Toledo and Ohio State Bar Associations.

Outside the practice of law, Rob has been active in community affairs, including Toys for Tots. Rob has led annual toy drives collecting toys and donations for the Northwestern Ohio Toys for Tots program since 1992. Rob is married to his wife Anna and has three children, Katie, Kelly and Brian.

attorneys.name: Stephen R. King
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce - Dissolution Lawyers in Montgomery, OH
attorneys.bio:
Stephen King was born in Roswell, New Mexico. Steve received his bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering in 1985 from Wright State University, and spent a decade working in the field of engineering. He was a Licensed Professional Engineer, and holds two U.S. Patents.

He received his law degree in 1996 from the University of Cincinnati, and was admitted to the Ohio Bar in 1996. Steve has argued before the First District Court of Appeals, the Twelfth District Court of Appeals, and the Ohio Supreme Court. In 2008, Mr. King was successful in his petition to the Ohio Supreme Court on behalf of Grandparents that had been awarded custody of their grandson when he was 1 year old. The trial court returned custody to the parents when the child was 5 years old because the parents no longer exhibited the same behaviors that resulted in them losing custody. The Ohio Supreme Court ruled that a change of circumstances in the child or the grandparents had to be proven before a Trial Court could even consider returning custody of the child back to the parents.

Steve is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Cincinnati Bar Association, the Cincinnati Academy of Collaborative professionals, and the CBA Domestic Relations Committee. Steve has either presented or moderated at attorney seminars on the subjects of Child Custody and Family Law for the Ohio State Bar Association, the Cincinnati Bar Association, the Northeast Lawyer's Club and the National Business Institute.

In addition to his extensive training and experience in the area of family law litigation, Mr. King has also been trained in the field of collaborative law, an alternative approach to the traditional methods of litigating family law issues. Steve was also named as an outstanding lawyer in the Cincinnati Business Courier's edition of Who's Who in Greater Cincinnati Law.

attorneys.name: Chase T. Kirby
attorneys.practice_type: General Practice Lawyers in Springboro, OH
attorneys.bio:
Chase is an associate attorney at Smith, Meier & Webb and focuses his practice on litigation. Chase primarily handles matters involving civil litigation, criminal defense, domestic relations, appellate advocacy, and estate planning.

Chase is a Warren County native and graduate of Springboro High School. Chase attended the Ohio State University, where he graduated with a Bachelor of Arts. He then attended the University of Dayton School of Law, where he obtained a Juris Doctorate.

While attending the University of Dayton School of Law, Chase was a member of the leadership honors program, a student ambassador for the university, and a member of the moot court board. Chase competed in national moot court competitions during his second and third years of law school and was awarded best oral advocate in the 2019 Regional Competition. He received a CALI Award of Excellence for achieving the highest score in his class in Civil Procedure, Family Law Practice, and Estate & Tax Planning.

During law school, Chase worked as a law clerk at the Warren County Prosecutor’s Office, where he worked in the appellate and felony criminal divisions. He then worked for a year at Dyer, Garofalo, Mann & Schultz in Dayton, gaining experience in personal injury and catastrophic injury cases and writing appellate briefs. During his last year of law school, he worked as a judicial law clerk for the Honorable Judge Donald E. Oda II in the Warren County Common Pleas Court general division, where he assisted in civil and criminal matters and observed jury trials.

In January 2020, during his third year of law school, Chase joined Smith, Meier & Webb as a law clerk. He worked as a law clerk until he passed the bar exam in the winter of 2020 becoming a third-generation lawyer in his family.

attorneys.name: Konrad Kircher
attorneys.practice_type: Victims of Sexual Abuse Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Konrad is a former Marine Corps infantry officer (1984-1989), graduate of the U.S. Naval Academy (1984), four-time marathon finisher and 20-year triathlete including one Ironman finish (Louisville 2008), who seeks to satisfy his competitiveness in the courtroom. Konrad's passion is representing the underdog against powerful institutions, and he has built a nationwide reputation as a leader in pursuing perpetrators of child sexual abuse and those organizations which enable them. Konrad has been to the Ohio Supreme Court four times since 2005 on behalf of survivors of child sexual abuse, and he handles such cases throughout Ohio. Konrad recognizes that there is much more to validation of a survivor than just receiving money, and he strives to help address all aspects of the healing process.

Konrad has also developed a niche in representing victims of police misconduct and civil rights violations. While most police officers are honorable public servants, there are others who are bad apples. Furthermore, sometimes even well-intentioned officers make tragic mistakes, resulting in death or serious injury to innocent persons. Konrad believes that these cases must be litigated to increase the quality of policing and decrease the frequency of violations of rights.

Konrad is admitted to practice in Ohio and Kentucky and in all federal courts in both of those states. He is active in the American Association of Justice and the Ohio Association of Justice. He was the 2019 recipient of the J. Thomas Henretta Distinguished Advocate Award from the Ohio Association of Justice for his advocacy on behalf of sexual assault survivors. Konrad is currently President of the National Crime Victim Bar Association, where he has co-chaired the Child Sex Abuse Section for many years.

Konrad has five daughters, of whom he is very proud and who continue to remind him through their mere presence that there is much in the world worth fighting for.

attorneys.name: Gary W. Kisling
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Fairlawn, OH
attorneys.bio:
Gary W. Kisling was born and raised in the countryside of southeastern Iowa. At an early age he developed a strong sense of justice and anger toward injustice. He decided to become a lawyer at the age of seven, when he discovered there was actually a profession that would pay him to argue. Gary has now practiced law for over 37 years and is a founding partner of Kisling, Nestico & Redick, LLC. His broad legal experience and years of practice give him perspective and insight in helping people.

While in law school, Gary worked for one year as a judicial legal assistant in the Akron Municipal Court, then two years as a judicial legal assistant in the Summit County Court of Common Pleas. It was in the Court of Common Pleas that Gary cites as having received his real legal education. In addition to legal research, writing memorandums, and draft opinions, Gary's judge requested his presence during jury trials to assist with complex evidentiary issues. This gave Gary the opportunity to watch good and bad lawyers try cases and observe jurors' reactions.

Gary went into private practice immediately following law school and tried his first jury trial in his second week of practice. He has since tried dozens of jury trials to verdict as lead counsel and settled multi-million dollar cases. In addition to trying complicated and serious injury cases, he counts a jury verdict of nearly one million dollars in a soft tissue injury case as one of his most satisfying experiences.

Gary has also won cases in the Court of Appeals and the Supreme Court of Ohio dealing with various issues including the unconstitutionality of the Ohio Workers' Compensation subrogation statute, defeating sovereign immunity for a county owned nursing home, lack of customer's prior notice of a defective condition despite previous use in premises liability cases, the admissibility of an expert witness's testimony based partially upon hearsay, and the limitation of the former doctrine of parental immunity in personal injury cases.

In addition to his law school education and other continuing legal education courses, Gary is a graduate of the University of Virginia’s Institute of Trial Advocacy in Charlottesville, Virginia, and Gerry Spence's Trial Lawyers College. He has given presentations on personal injury trial practice and cross examination of expert witnesses to other lawyers.

ON THE RECORD

Larry S. Klein has been a staunch defender of injury victim rights for the last 39 years. His extensive experience spans the areas of personal injury, medical malpractice, insurance law, motor vehicle accidents and nursing home negligence.

Born in Cleveland , he attended Boston University , where he earned a B.A. in 1975 in Psychology and Accounting, graduating cum laude. He earned his J.D. in 1980 from Cleveland Marshall College of Law.

He is admitted to practice in all Ohio courts, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio and the U.S. Tax Court. He is a member of the Cleveland , Cuyahoga, Ashtabula, Ohio State and American Bar Associations; the American Association for Justice, the Ohio Association for Justice and the Cleveland Academy of Trial Attorneys. Larry S. Klein has received a Preeminent AV* rating from Martindale-Hubbell. This rating applies to those lawyers at the highest level of professional excellence.

Because he has demonstrated excellence in the practice of law, Larry is receiving an honor that is limited to no more than 5% of the attorneys within his state. Super Lawyers recognizes attorneys who have distinguished themselves in their legal practice. The selection process is rigorous and results in third-party validation of their professional accomplishments.

OFF THE RECORD

Larry is a first generation American, whose parents both immigrated to this country for a better life. His parents emphasized the importance of education, and sacrificed to make sure their son would attend quality schools. He was the first member of his family to attend college, and obtain an advanced degree. In his spare time, his favorite pastimes are golf and travel, and he is passionate about both. Larry enjoys golfing and travel with his wife of forty-one years, and spends as much time as possible visiting with their two grown children. Larry is active in the community and supports various religious and secular charities.

attorneys.name: David Knisley
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Building on a Family Legacy of Advocating for Injured Ohio Workers

David Knisley is an Attorney of Counsel at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Now semi-retired, David draws on a lifetime of career experience to support NRS Injury Law, the firm’s practicing attorneys, and clients.

Four Generations of Relentless Support for the Working Men and Women of Ohio

“My first job was as a sanitation worker, but my path to law started long, long before I was born,” David began when asked to reflect on the days and decisions that led him to a career as a workers’ compensation attorney. “My grandfather, my dad’s dad, was one of the first commissioners of the Industrial Commission in Ohio. He played a crucial role in helping injured workers in Ohio back in the early and mid-20th century when attorneys and politicians were still working out the details of what the state’s workers’ compensation system was going to look like.”

By the time David was born, grandfather Clarence Hugh Knisley and father Scott Knisley were already deeply involved in helping injured Ohio workers. David grew up in a family of lawyers who were dedicated to advocating for those who could not advocate for themselves, and the experience left an impression.

“I worked manual labor jobs as a youth and I joined the Marine Corps after a stint at a military prep school in Kentucky, but I couldn’t get away from a calling to pursue a career in law,” David said. David served his country as a Marine from 1978 through 1982. He went to law school in the mid-1980s, graduated in 1988, passed the bar in 1989, and took a job at the family firm where he practiced with other members of the Knisley family until 2017.

Establishing Connections and Winning Cases for Injured Workers in Southern Ohio

“Grandfather, father, and me plus my brothers, we were all attorneys, and that’s three generations, but you’re probably wondering where the ‘fourth’ generation part of the Knisley family of attorneys comes into play,” David says, grinning with pride. “In 2017, I left the family law firm and went into private practice with my brilliant and talented daughter, Samantha J. Brush. We practiced law together until Samantha joined NRS Injury Law in 2025. I came along and joined the firm in 2026, so I guess you could say I’m the one following in her footsteps now.”

Bolstering Ohio’s Largest Workers’ Compensation Law Firm in an Of Counsel Role

In his Of Counsel role, David provides invaluable advice and support to the firm’s growing cohort of workers’ compensation attorneys, particularly in the firm’s efforts to help injured workers in southern Ohio.

“I’ve practiced in multiple legal fields, from workers’ comp to personal injury, criminal defense, and social security,” David says. “But wherever I went, something always drew me back to southern Ohio, and whatever I practiced, I was always drawn back to workers’ comp law. It’s definitely been a calling.”

According to David, one of his greatest strengths is his ability to form connections with working families in southern Ohio and his unending loyalty to them. David says many of the families he represents today are in fact intergenerational working families whose fathers and grandfathers were represented by David’s father and grandfather. “Nothing connects you to a people and a place like showing up for your neighbors, be it at the mediation table or at trial,” said David.

Work/Life Balance

“It’s been a while, but I love to fly airplanes,” David says. “More recently I’ve been going up when a friend needs someone to fly with them. We fly all around the Midwest and visit places like Traverse City and other picturesque towns. It’s a great way to relax while also practicing a valuable skill.”

In addition to his time in the cockpit, David is an active and devoted grandfather. He frequently travels to Europe and other international destinations with his children and grandchildren.

David Knisley and NRS Injury Law

David’s lifetime commitment to truth and justice and his willingness to put in the hard work and show up for workers who have suffered an injury through no fault of their own are traits that align with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with the firm about your case, call 855.468.4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

David has always been committed to southern Ohio communities. In 2018, he ran for Ross County Common Pleas Court judge. Though he lost that race, the experience inspired him to become more involved in his community. Through legal representation and community activities, David maintains close ties with families in places like Bainbridge, Chillicothe, Portsmouth, and Columbus.

attorneys.name: Jesse E. Knowlden
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jesse Knowlden has a general practice with an emphasis in criminal defense and civil litigation. He has been a licensed attorney since 2019.

Jesse was born in Pennsylvania, attended Penn State University, and then spent three years working in the oilfield before moving to Cincinnati and attending the University of Cincinnati College of Law.

Jesse now dedicates his career to advocating for the accused and championing the claims of those who have been wronged. Jesse has successfully represented and defended clients facing a range of charges from minor misdemeanors to murder. Jesse works tirelessly to secure the best possible outcome for his clients and advocates for them inside and outside of the courtroom.

Jesse is an affiliated attorney with the Armed Citizens’ Legal Defense Network, which is an organization which provides its members with immediate criminal defense representation in the aftermath of a self-defense incident. Jesse has successfully represented clients who have used lethal and non-lethal force in self-defense. Whether you are a member of the Armed Citizens’ Legal Defense Network or not, call Jesse immediately if you have used force in self-defense.

In the civil context, Jesse has achieved favorable outcomes for his clients in a wide variety of litigation and business matters. Jesse has experience working with individuals, small businesses, and large corporations. Jesse uses his unique personal experiences to relate to his clients, no matter their status or claim, and identify efficient solutions for success.

Jesse was a law clerk with Cohen Todd Criminal Defense for two years before becoming an attorney. In law school, he served as a member of the University of Cincinnati Law Review and had two articles published. Prior to joining the firm, Jesse served as a fellow with the Ohio Innocence Project where he worked on post-conviction matters for individuals who were convicted of crimes that they did not commit.

Jesse is an avid outdoorsman and enjoys hunting, fishing, hiking, camping, and spending time with his wife, Alison.

Call Jesse at 513-333-5235 if you need help immediately, for a free consultation, or if you just have a question.

Representative Matters

Assisted in representation of individual indicted for Murder, Attempted Murder, and Felonious Assault with firearms specifications for shooting and killing one individual and shooting at another. Charges carried life in prison if convicted. Argued self-defense at trial. Not guilty verdict.

Represented individual charged with murder for fatally stabbing another individual. Argued self-defense. Charge dismissed.

Represented individual indicted for two counts of Felonious Assault and one count of Having Weapons While Under Disability for shooting one individual. Argued self-defense. Charges dismissed.

Represented individual indicted for seven counts, including first-degree felonies Aggravated Burglary and Kidnapping. Not guilty verdict on each indicted offense after a jury trial.

Represented individual charged with two counts of Rape and one count of Gross Sexual Imposition. Not guilty verdict after a bench trial.

Represented individual charged with two counts of felonious assault with gun specifications and one count of discharging a firearm on or near a prohibited premises. Charges carried a mandatory minimum of six years in prison if convicted. Argued self-defense. Not guilty verdict after a bench trial.

Represented individual charged with Driving Under the Influence and Improper Change of Course after an early morning car accident. Not guilty verdict after trial, administrative license suspension terminated, and all case records sealed.

Represented individual indicted for eighteen felonies, including nine first degree felonies. Conviction as charged carried over 120 years in prison. Negotiated a plea agreement to one misdemeanor, no incarceration, and no probation.

Represented individual indicted for twenty-five felonies, including twelve first degree felonies and eleven second degree felonies. Conviction as charged carried sentence of life without parole. Argued witness credibility issues. All charges dismissed.

Successful resolution of numerous serious personal injury claims on behalf of Plaintiffs, including multiple pre-suit settlements for policy limits.

Pre-suit policy limit settlement of $1,250,000 for serious personal injuries suffered in an automobile crash.

attorneys.bio:
Brad Koffel — Trusted Criminal Defense Attorney in Ohio

With over 30 years of courtroom experience representing clients in high stakes criminal litigation, Brad Koffel is among Ohio’s most experienced, well-connected, and trusted criminal defense attorneys. He has been recognized for his record of success in highprofile and complex criminal cases landing him national accolades including Best Lawyers in America since 2007, “Lawyer of the Year”, Ohio Super Lawyers, National Trial Lawyers Top 100 and was selected as one of the top 10 criminal defense attorneys in Ohio by the National Academy of Criminal Defense Attorneys (NACDA). Brad is a frequent contributor to iHeart Media as a Legal Analyst and presenter at CLE seminars.

Brad focuses his practice on Computer Crime, Sex Crimes, False Sexual Assault Allegations, Title IX Investigations, Serious Vehicular Crimes, and all Major Felony Cases. Brad’s team has been with him over 20 years. His team brings a rare and unique holistic approach of working with clients who have never been accused of a crime to make sure they can handle the emotional and mental load of being investigated and prosecuted. Brad’s goals are the same for every client: Avoid charges. Avoid conviction. Avoid prison. The mission is the same for every single client: prepare the case as if the only way to freedom is through a jury. Many clients are surprised at how many cases are indicted with insufficient admissible evidence to sustain a conviction.

If you’d like to talk to Brad about representation, call 614-884-1100, from 7:00 a.m. – 10:00 p.m ET every day of the year. If your matter is something that aligns with his practice, then the team will schedule with a consultation with him, most likely within a few hours. Brad and his team only accept about one or two new clients per week to keep our focus on our existing clients. Legal fees are always discussed and agreed to in advance of longterm representation and will be based upon the work that needs to immediately be done within a budget the client can reasonably afford. The Firm offers discounts and grants of time to members of the military and first responders.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Brad Koffel — Trusted Criminal Defense Attorney in Ohio

With over 30 years of courtroom experience representing clients in high stakes criminal litigation, Brad Koffel is among Ohio’s most experienced, well-connected, and trusted criminal defense attorneys. He has been recognized for his record of success in highprofile and complex criminal cases landing him national accolades including Best Lawyers in America since 2007, “Lawyer of the Year”, Ohio Super Lawyers, National Trial Lawyers Top 100 and was selected as one of the top 10 criminal defense attorneys in Ohio by the National Academy of Criminal Defense Attorneys (NACDA). Brad is a frequent contributor to iHeart Media as a Legal Analyst and presenter at CLE seminars.

Brad focuses his practice on Computer Crime, Sex Crimes, False Sexual Assault Allegations, Title IX Investigations, Serious Vehicular Crimes, and all Major Felony Cases. Brad’s team has been with him over 20 years. His team brings a rare and unique holistic approach of working with clients who have never been accused of a crime to make sure they can handle the emotional and mental load of being investigated and prosecuted. Brad’s goals are the same for every client: Avoid charges. Avoid conviction. Avoid prison. The mission is the same for every single client: prepare the case as if the only way to freedom is through a jury. Many clients are surprised at how many cases are indicted with insufficient admissible evidence to sustain a conviction.

If you’d like to talk to Brad about representation, call 614-884-1100, from 7:00 a.m. – 10:00 p.m ET every day of the year. If your matter is something that aligns with his practice, then the team will schedule with a consultation with him, most likely within a few hours. Brad and his team only accept about one or two new clients per week to keep our focus on our existing clients. Legal fees are always discussed and agreed to in advance of longterm representation and will be based upon the work that needs to immediately be done within a budget the client can reasonably afford. The Firm offers discounts and grants of time to members of the military and first responders.

attorneys.name: Chad G. Koop
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce, Dissolution, Collaborative Divorce Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
As a Partner at Stagnaro Hannigan Koop Co., LPA, Chad G. Koop represents clients in Ohio and Northern Kentucky in matters of family law, including divorce, dissolution, collaborative divorce, child custody, child support, spousal support, maintenance, post-decree modifications and enforcement, juvenile court matters, and mediation. While he is an experienced, successful trial lawyer, he also works with clients to find solutions to their problems before they are forced into the courtroom.

Chad received his bachelor's degree from the University of Kentucky in 2005, and then went on to complete his Juris Doctorate at the University of Dayton School of Law in 2008. Chad guides many families in Ohio and Northern Kentucky through their divorce, custody and family law matters. Chad focuses his practice in family law matters in Hamilton, Clermont, Warren and Butler Counties in Ohio; and in Kenton, Campbell and Boone Counties in Kentucky.

As a domestic relations and family law attorney, Chad thrives on helping people by finding creative solutions that fit their unique situations. His extended experience in the practice area and dedication to client interaction are major contributors to his continued success. He works very hard to develop a strategy catered to the client's individual needs and goals. Chad is confident and prepared to zealously advocate for his client's interests in the most complex, challenging, and high conflict situations.

While the majority of Chad's practice is spent in the courtroom litigating, he believes it is important to educate his clients on options to resolve conflicts outside of court. Through Chad's experience in practicing collaborative law and mediation, he has been able to help people respectfully negotiate creative resolutions, designed to meet their interests and objectives, in a manner that would be very difficult, if not impossible, for a court to do through traditional litigation.

Chad is recognized by the Ohio Supreme Court as a domestic relations mediator and a parenting coordinator. Chad completed the necessary training to be a parenting coordinator to better assist his clients involved in parenting coordination or who may be considering parenting coordination, but he is not actively accepting parenting coordination cases at this time.

attorneys.name: Andrew Koscianski
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Drawing on a Rich Legal Background and an Attorney-Client Teamwork Approach to Win Cases

Andrew Koscianski is an Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. From his first personal injury case, where he represented a badly hurt family member, to his current role advocating for injured workers, Andrew has always prioritized using the law to help others.

A Background Centered Around Service

“I’ve always worked, in some form or another,” Andrew said as he outlined his career background. “I started as a busboy at an old family-run Italian place in North Royalton, and then I painted houses for Neubert Painting for seven years while making my way through high school and undergrad. Once I got into law school, I started working in legal clinics for Cleveland-Marshall, which gave me a head start on my career in law.”

Andrew reminisced on how a youth spent in the service industry and the trades gave him an appreciation for hard work, while an upbringing in a family of intergenerational attorneys inspired him to ultimately seek a law degree and a career where he could use the U.S. justice system to serve others.

Every Day is an Opportunity to Use Our Justice System to Help Someone

Andrew’s first job out of law school was at the family law firm of Koscianski & Koscianski Co., LPA, and he described it as a trial-by-fire experience in which he was handed a highly diversified caseload that included anything from probate to family law, criminal defense, and personal injury. Andrew learned the ropes at the family firm, then went on to represent clients at a variety of firms, including helping one firm get off the ground, training a contingent of its paralegals and case managers, and wearing IT and management hats.

“By the start of my seventh year as a practicing attorney, I felt a calling to help others and hone my legal career towards a singular goal of service, towards using the justice system to help those who had been severely wronged,” said Andrew. “I had a few meetings with NRS Injury Law Co-Managing Partners Jerry Schneiberg and Dan Romaine, and I realized this firm is where I could do the most good.”

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not representing the firm’s clients, Andrew fills his time with hands-on activities like going to the gym, cycling, and hiking. Andrew and his wife love to travel and are on a mission to visit all of the national parks. On weekends, Andrew plays in adult soccer leagues and disc golfs with friends.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Andrew Koscianski

“This is a team that sticks around,” Andrew said when asked to describe why he took a position at NRS Injury Law. “This firm has attorneys who have been with the firm for decades, because not only does NRS Injury Law empower the attorneys to be the best versions of themselves in terms of representing clients, but the firm truly values their employees and understands the importance of creating a teamwork-based approach between the firm, the attorney, and the client. That’s how they became the largest workers’ compensation firm in Ohio.”

Andrew is laidback yet strategic, easy to talk to yet ruthless in his client advocacy. His hard work, tenacity, and detail-based case-building are essential traits that align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Andrew and the firm about your case, call 855.468.4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Andrew and his wife are passionate about adopting and fostering rescue animals. They are currently involved with the Cleveland Animal Protective League (APL). Andrew has also worked for the Cuyahoga County Board of Elections and is passionate about civic engagement.

attorneys.name: Roy Krall
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning, Probate & Trust Administration Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Roy A. Krall is a Shareholder with over three decades of experience, maintaining offices in both Akron and Cleveland. He is a certified specialist in Estate Planning, Trust, and Probate Law by the Ohio State Bar Association, and a valued member of the Cavitch Team. His practice focuses on estate planning, trust and probate law, and business law.

Roy was admitted to the Ohio Bar in 1989 and is also admitted to practice before the United States District Court, Northern District of Ohio, and the Internal Revenue Service.

A dedicated educator, Roy taught Estate and Gift Tax as an adjunct professor at the University of Akron School of Law in 1997 and 1998 and is a frequent lecturer and journalist on estate-related topics. In 2003, he was among the first in Ohio to be designated as a specialist in Estate Planning, Trust, and Probate Law by the Specialty Board of the Ohio State Bar Association. He has been a Fellow of the American College of Trust and Estate Counsel (ACTEC) since 2007 and a past Chair of the Estate Planning, Trust, and Probate Law Section at the Ohio State Bar Association. Currently, he serves as a Fellow of the Akron, Cleveland and Ohio State Bar Foundations and is an Associate Editor of the Probate Law Journal of Ohio, a bi-monthly publication intended to keep Ohio estate practitioners current.

Roy's distinguished career is further marked by numerous accolades. He holds a Martindale-Hubbell AV rating and has been recognized as an Ohio Super Lawyer in Estate Planning & Probate every year since 2007 by Law & Politics Media, Inc. Additionally, he has been named as one of the Best Lawyers in America for Trusts and Estates every year since 2006 and has been listed in Chambers High Net Worth since 2021.

Beyond his practice, Roy serves on gift committees for several area nonprofit organizations and continues to participate as a Member of the Council of, and several committees formed by, the Estate Planning Trust and Probate Law Section of the Ohio State Bar Association. Prior to attending law school, Roy gained valuable experience as an actuary for a year at Buck Consultants in New York City.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Charles W. Kranstuber, LPA
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Charles Kranstuber has been practicing the area of workers' compensation since 1982. He is a graduate of the Ohio State University where he received a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science. He received his law degree from the University of San Diego in 1979. He is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Columbus Bar Association, and the Ohio Academy of Trial Lawyers.

Upon graduation from the University of San Diego, he was employed by the Ohio Industrial Commission as a district hearing officer. The Industrial Commission is the state agency which handles the adjudication of contested matters in the workers' compensation system. After several years with the Ohio Industrial Commission, he was employed as an associate attorney at the law firm Agee, Clymer, & Morgan, where he worked through 1994. He then was hired by the law firm of Livorno & Arnett, where he served as a partner through 2006. Since that time, he has established his own law office, where his practice continues to consist of representing injured workers before the Ohio Bureau of Workers' Compensation and Industrial Commission of Ohio.

Charles Kranstuber has also been active in politics and local government. He served for 12 years as a city councilman in the City of Dublin and also served for 6 years as the mayor of the City of Dublin. In 2006, he was appointed by the governor as the injured workers' representative to the Workers' Compensation Oversight Commission, which is responsible for the Ohio Bureau of Workers' Compensation. The Oversight Commission's duties include making recommendations regarding premium rates, investments, and setting the rules and policies of the Bureau of Workers' Compensation.

Charles Kranstuber has been dedicated to serving the needs of injured workers in Ohio for over 30 years. He recognizes the deep trust placed by his clients and will strive to uphold that trust by working hard and fighting hard for you.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Charles W. Kranstuber, LPA
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Carley’s practice focuses on workers’ compensation and Social Security Disability law. A native of Dublin, Ohio, she earned her undergraduate degree from The Ohio State University before beginning her legal career as a legal assistant at a firm specializing in workers’ compensation and Social Security Disability/SSI matters.

In 2013, Carley enrolled in the evening program at Capital University Law School while continuing to work full-time. During law school, she served as a teaching assistant for the Legal Research and Writing Department, a peer advisor, and the Executive Articles Editor of the Capital University Law Review.

After graduating magna cum laude from Capital University Law School in 2017, Carley joined the Law Offices of Charles W. Kranstuber, LPA. She has presented throughout Ohio on a variety of workers’ compensation topics, including avoiding burnout, emotional labor in legal practice, parking lot injuries, and effective hearing room techniques.

Carley is passionate about advocating for injured workers and disabled individuals and represents her clients with empathy, energy, and dedication. She previously served as Chair of the Workers’ Compensation Section of the Columbus Bar Association for two years and currently serves on the Executive Committee of the Ohio Association for Justice.

Outside of her practice, Carley enjoys spending time with her family, cheering for the Cleveland Guardians and Ohio State Buckeyes, traveling the world, and exploring the vibrant Columbus community she calls home.

attorneys.name: Mark Kremser
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mark is an experienced trial lawyer and problem solver. Each and every client, no matter the controversy, deserves and gets Mark’s best. Mark takes both a personal and practical approach to representing his clients, which begins with getting to know each client and his or her personal and legal goals. A leader in the courtroom, the community, and the office. Mark works tirelessly to achieve optimal results for his clients. That is why Mark has an impressive record of success in commercial disputes and cases involving catastrophic injuries and professional malpractice.

A graduate of Brooklyn High School, Mark graduated summa cum laude from Bowling Green State University where he was inducted into the Phi Beta Kappa Honor Society. He earned his Juris Doctor from Case Western Reserve University in 1996, where he was inducted into the Order of Barristers, a national honor society recognizing achievement in advocacy. Upon passing the bar, Mark worked as Bill Wuliger’s associate for 8 years. He then sought new challenges working for larger plaintiff and defense litigation firms. While he grew professionally from those experiences, he missed the personal connection with clients that comes from working at a small firm. So, in 2014, Mark returned to his roots and rejoined Bill and Amy Wuliger.

When he is not practicing law, Mark is a devoted husband to his wife, Laura, and father to their children, Kyra and Connor. When he has time, Mark enjoys chasing golf balls in the woods and jamming 80’s hair metal on his Fender Precision bass guitar. He also does volunteer work for Autism Speaks and the Westlake Schools.

Kevin E. Kuehn, a Practice Group Leader with WH&E, is involved in all phases of the firm's practice. His expertise is in the areas of materials and mechanical technologies. Admitted to the Ohio Bar in 2003, Mr. Kuehn is registered to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office and before the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio. Kuehn joined the firm in 2007. He graduated cum laude with a B.S. in Ceramic Engineering in 1992 from The Ohio State University, a M.S. in Ceramic Engineering from Alfred University in 1995, and obtained his Juris Doctor degree from Capital University Law School in 2002.

Prior to receiving his law degree, Kuehn worked as a process and development engineer at a glass company in Columbus, Ohio. He is an active member of the Ohio and Cincinnati Bar Associations, as well as the American Intellectual Property Law Association. Kevin is the Practice Group Leader for the Chemical/Biotech/Materials patent prosecution practice group within the firm. He resides in Northern Kentucky with his children.

Awards and Honors

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Orange Village, OH
attorneys.bio:
Hans C. Kuenzi is one of the most respected small firm trial attorneys in Northeast Ohio. After serving as a trial magistrate in the Cuyahoga County Domestic Relations Court from 1985 to 1988, Hans established the firm and quickly rose to prominence representing clients in the areas of family law and personal injury. His peers and colleagues know Hans to be a superior litigator, who routinely achieves outstanding results on behalf of his clients. His experience allows Hans to provide compassionate and effective representation of his client’s interests. In recognition of his abilities, Hans has earned statewide distinction as a Certified Specialist in Family Law.

Only seasoned experience in the art of advocacy can provide the effective representation, confidence and insight that legal matters require, regardless of whether the case calls for litigation or settlement. With over fifty years of combined experience as trial attorneys, the attorneys at Kuenzi/Somogyi can provide you with high caliber legal representation that you require and that you deserve.

attorneys.name: Phillip A. Kuri
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mayfield Heights, OH
attorneys.bio:
Phil, a partner at Elk & Elk since 2012, focuses on injuries of a catastrophic nature including personal injury, medical malpractice, trucking, products liability and general tort law. He has won substantial verdicts and settlements on behalf of his clients.

In addition to his legal practice, Mr. Kuri maintains active memberships in the American Bar Association, and the Ohio State Bar Association. He is a member of the American Trial Lawyers Association - Top 100 Lawyers, Super Lawyers, Ohio Academy for Justice, American Association for Justice - Top 100 Trial Lawyers, and the Million Dollar and Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum. He is admitted to practice in Ohio, before the Northern and Southern U.S. District Courts of Ohio and before U.S. federal courts.

Settlements and Verdicts

$39 Million Jury Verdict – Wrongful death due to negligence of construction company (April 2014)

Case brought on behalf of a 41-year-old Ohio man struck by vehicle and died while working in a construction zone. A Cleveland jury awarded $19 million in compensation for wrongful death, and $20 million in punitive damages. Jury found 60% fault with construction company 30% fault of driver of vehicle and 10% to the Plaintiff. Case settled on appeal filed. Case tried with co-counsel.

$6.3 Million Jury Verdict – Hypoxia brain injury following minimally invasive surgery from drug interaction. (October 2009)

$3.65 Million – Truck accident where a floor mat (product defect) caused unintentional acceleration, causing severe and permanent injuries (January 2017)

$3.5 Million – Client undergoing heart surgery sustained permanent brain injury (2014)

$2 Million – Employer intentional tort results in serious injuries (March 2009)

While at work, a crane fell on the Plaintiff, resulting in serious injuries and lost wages. Plaintiff was admitted for intense rehabilitation and surgery.

$1.375 Million – Birth injury during delivery (April 2014)

Labor and delivery claim resulting in permanent, debilitating brain damage to the infant.

$1.15 Million – Death due to medical negligence by heart surgeon (December 2013)

Plaintiff’s heart was damaged during a surgical procedure. The surgeon failed to repair the damage properly, resulting in death.

$800,000 Jury Verdict – Medical Malpractice and Wrongful Death (September 2016)

The Decedent, age 69, was recovering in a nursing /rehab facility following bowel surgery. Plaintiffs alleged the Defendant physician negligently failed to appropriately order, manage and monitor the Decedent’s anticoagulation therapy resulting in a brain bleed and her death on August 3, 2011. (Hamilton County)

$785,000 – Slip and fall results in back injury (September 2009)

Plaintiff fell on a wet floor while shopping at a grocery store. The water was present on white flooring and was not visible by shoppers. Plaintiff suffered a lumbar strain.

$750,000 – Police officer struck by motorist, resulting in severe back injuries (March 2014)

Plaintiff was on the side of the road when a passing motorist veered into her, slamming her into a parked vehicle, causing her to suffer spinal injuries.

$750,000 – Medical malpractice results in patient’s death. (March 2012)

Plaintiff underwent surgery for the removal of a tumor. During the procedure, the surgeon damaged an artery, resulting in a massive stroke and death.

$650,000 – Serious injuries due to motor vehicle accident (April 2012)

A pregnant woman suffered multiple fractures to her hip, sacrum and back when a hotel employee lost control of a passenger shuttle and crashed.

$500,000 – Improper care results in diabetic coma and death (March 2012)

Woman dies in a rehabilitation center, due to improper monitoring of her blood sugar.

$450,000 – Nursing home resident injured during transportation (May 2013)

81-year-old Plaintiff was not secured properly while travelling in a vehicle and fell from her wheelchair, resulting in fractures to her knees and back.

$450,000 – (February 2011)

Nursing home staff members failed to follow safety protocols, dropping Plaintiff. The 77-year-old woman suffered lacerations and a hip fracture.

$430,000 – Employer Intentional Tort (September 2013)

Plaintiff’s fingers were severed while operating machinery due to her employer’s deliberate removal of a safety guard.

All lawsuits are different and Elk & Elk makes no representation or promises that it can obtain the same results in other cases. These results do not guarantee, warrant, or predict the outcome of any future legal matter. You should consult an attorney for advice regarding your individual situation.

attorneys.name: Corey J. Kuzma
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Providing Expert Counsel and Representing Clients with Strategy, Curiosity, and Compassion

Corey Kuzma developed an interest in storytelling, composition, case-building, and strategy from a very early age. As a student at Baldwin Wallace University, Corey thought his interests would lead him to film school, but an Introduction to Criminal Law course showed him his passion for methodical organization and compelling storytelling could be better utilized in a career in law.

Corey paid his way through college by managing a local restaurant for nine years, a critical role where he learned how to organize a team, strategize, execute, and meet expectations. While running the restaurant, Corey pursued a double major in political science and philosophy. This education prepared him for law school, teaching him how to theorize, debate, inform, analyze, and, perhaps most importantly, how to listen.

Entering the Legal Field

While attending Cleveland Marshall College of Law, Corey interned at the City of Cleveland Department of Law. The valuable experience he gained while assisting attorneys in the Department of Civil Litigation short-listed him for a position at NRS Injury Law. Corey took the bar in February of 2015, received his diploma in May, and had a job at the firm by July.

Within days of joining the firm, it became clear Corey had a unique ability to provide compassionate counsel for clients one day and then strategically and methodically build an unassailable case for them the next. “Once I started working for NRS Injury Law, I knew without a shadow of a doubt I was in the right place,” reflected Corey. “I was the kind of kid who loved grand strategy and storytelling in movies and books, hoping one day I could write interesting stories or shorts of my own. Now, as an adult, I find myself in a work environment where I apply those same organizational and creative skills to listen intently to clients and build compelling, winning cases for them.”

A Passion for Workers' Compensation Law

To Corey, workers' comp law is especially meaningful and important. “When I was a young child, my uncle lost his leg in a workplace accident, and workers' comp was essential in helping our extended family stay afloat,” says Corey. “That experience helped inspire me to go into worker's comp law, because in this field, you're representing everyday, hardworking people who've been injured in the line of duty, and who are often up against powerful institutions or corporations that don't want them to receive the compensation they need to get treatment, recover, and provide for their families.”

Corey distinguished himself in the firm’s workers’ comp department by listening intently to clients, asking the right questions, taking a vested interest in learning the details of their stories, and building effective cases to represent them. His charismatic nature and calm demeanor quickly made him NRS Injury Law’s go-to attorney for even the most complex and nuanced workers’ comp cases. “When clients come to me with their stories and questions, I like to have answers,” says Corey, reflecting on his role at the firm. “The unknowns of each case are always very interesting to me, which is why I endeavor to learn, learn, and learn as much as possible so I can provide answers while really getting to know my clients. At some point, I feel like I start walking in their shoes. I learn their story as well as they know it, which enables me to get results for them.”

Community Involvement:

Passionate about music, Corey can be found frequenting and supporting the budding music scene in the greater Cleveland area.

Work/Life Balance:

Corey lives in Lakewood with his wife, Emma, and their niece, Regina. Free time is limited, but Corey plays music with his niece, teaches her new instruments, and cultivates her musical interests. Corey takes his family to museums, aquariums, parks, and festivals on weekends and holidays. On the rare “down” day, Corey can be found at home spending time with the family dog and cat or singing karaoke in a jam session with Regina.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Corey Kuzma

Patient and persistent, Corey embodies the values of NRS Injury Law in his intentional, hands-on approach to each case and his interest in interacting with clients in a personal, invested manner. For him, the firm's mission of relentlessly pursuing the best possible outcome on behalf of every client comes naturally, as does the firm's vision to always live with compassion, strive for excellence, and take action with integrity, patience, and professionalism. To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Corey and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

attorneys.name: Kimberly A. Kyle
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Kyle is an attorney who seeks to efficiently and effectively resolve the disputes of her clients. At the outset of each claim or lawsuit, she investigates the relevant facts, law and desired outcome, and draws on the breadth of her experience to determine if there is an efficient and desirable manner in which to quickly resolve the dispute without drawn-out litigation, time and expense. If litigation is necessary, she develops an early and effective strategy to obtain success for her client. Ms. Kyle views herself and her clients as partners in resolving disputes in a manner most conducive to the client's business, personal interests and concerns.

She has extensive experience in evaluating and litigating insurance coverage issues involving personal injury, property damage, UM/UIM and other claims by first parties and third parties, as well as insurers' duties to defend and/or indemnify under homeowners policies, commercial general liability coverages, builders risk policies, inland marine coverages, auto policies and umbrella/excess policies. Her coverage opinions and declaratory judgment actions have provided guidance for insureds and insurers on the entire spectrum of today's insurance issues, in jurisdictions around the country.
