attorneys.bio:
Amanda C. May is an experienced estate planner who joined Cavitch Familo & Durkin in 2019 as an attorney. She is a valued member of the firm's Estate Planning and Business Practice Groups. Amanda's practice focuses on customizing and reviewing estate plans, as well as trust and estate administration. She also prepares various tax returns, manages corporate and real estate records, and researches complex tax and real estate issues. As a current member of the Estate Planning Council of Cleveland and The Cleveland Bar Association, Amanda is deeply committed to counseling clients on both proactive estate planning and probate matters. She is passionate about helping clients secure their family's future and achieve their long-term financial goals.

Amanda earned her Juris Doctor, Cum Laude, from the University of Akron School of Law, where she was active in the Akron Law Moot Court Honor’s Society team, served as a Contracts ASP Fellow/Student Teacher, and was a member of Phi Delta Phi Honors Society and the Immigration and Human Rights Legal Clinic. She holds undergraduate degrees in Political Science and Philosophy from Malone University. While attending Malone, Amanda was the captain of the women’s soccer team, an active member of Student Counsel, and the women’s soccer representative for the Student-Athletics Advisory Committee.

Outside of her professional life, Amanda is happily married and has a daughter, experiences that further fuel her dedication to helping families plan for their future. In her free time, she enjoys spending time with friends and family, and being outdoors.

attorneys.name: Zach Mayo
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Sandusky, OH
attorneys.bio:
Zach Mayo is an experienced criminal defense lawyer with a lengthy history of trials, dismissals, and not guilty verdicts for offenses of violence and sex offense.

With more than a decade of experience in the criminal defense world, he's quickly become the man to see for private criminal defense in the Delaware and Franklin counties.

Zach D. Mayo is an asset to the team at Ohio Legal Group Columbus as a Criminal Defense Attorney. He studied at Capital University earning his Bachelor’s degree in Psychology. Following completion, he continued his studies at Capital University to obtain his Juris Doctorate.

While working tirelessly on his Juris Doctorate, Zach accepted a position with The Law Office of Brian Jones as a Law Clerk. This position allowed him the ability to learn the ins and outs of the criminal defense field while simultaneously completing his education. After his graduation, the office had no questions in offering him a position as an Associate Attorney after seeing his dedication and passion for this field.

Zach exceeded all expectations in our office and had personal goals to grow and excel in his career, and to obtain a vast wealth of mastery in Law. After over 2 years with our office, Zach made the decision to expand on his experience and take a position at the Public Defender’s office to gain knowledge and a better understanding of Criminal Justice.

His time spent at the Public Defender’s office gave Zach additional perspective on his work and presented him with the ability to look at cases from many different angles. He is well-versed in a multitude of case types and has built strong relationships as well as a strong reputation in his area.

Zach has achieved numerous not guilty verdicts and dismissals on cases from traffic tickets to rape, all the way up to homicide charges. His background has given him the advantage to testify to the Ohio Legislature on criminal justice topics such as the violent offender registry as well as the stand your ground law.

Not only is Zach a board member of the Ohio Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, but he also holds a Membership Committee Chair. Zach is licensed to practice law in the state of Ohio and is admitted to the Federal District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.

attorneys.name: Michael P. Mazanetz
attorneys.firm_name: Heller, Maas, Moro & Magill Co., LPA
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Youngstown, OH
attorneys.bio:
To Michael P. Mazanetz, the greatest personal professional reward comes when a client's long wait for oftentimes badly needed Social Security disability benefits comes to an end with a decision in their favor.

"Some of those people have worked 25-30 years, and they've had some accident at work or at home or they've been diagnosed with a serious illness, and all of a sudden the money stops coming," he says. "It can be a long process to go through, so when they get that news, it's always a highlight."

Atty. Mazanetz is a Mahoning Valley native, raised in Newton Falls, where he still lives. As a boy, Michael knew that he wanted to be a lawyer who would help the kind of working people he knew - his father worked in a bearing factory - and he focused hard on his studies to achieve that goal.

He graduated magna cum laude from Mount Union College in 2005 with a B.A. degree in political science, and then attended the University of Akron School of Law, where he was associate editor of the Akron Law Review and graduated cum laude in 2008.

Atty. Mazanetz began working part-time at Heller, Maas, Moro & Magill starting the summer after his first year in law school, and after he got his J.D. in 2008, the firm immediately hired him as a full-time attorney.

His day-to-day practice focuses on Social Security disability law, ranging from initial case assessment through every stage of what can be a long process.

"Every Social Security disability claimant deserves to have their interest represented in a diligent, comprehensive, and personal manner," he says. "It is my goal to provide this exhaustive representation for each and every client I work with."

It's a process that requires patience by the claimants and a steady counselor role for himself.

"When somebody comes in and they've just suffered something traumatic in their life you see how much they're struggling, it can be difficult," he says. "But then when you get that decision that grants them Social Security disability benefits, and you hear in their voice or see how happy they are and it's the first good news they've had in a couple of years, it can be very rewarding."

When he's away from the office, Atty. Mazanetz contributes to his hometown of Newton Falls in two ways: He is an assistant coach for the Newton Falls High School Tigers varsity basketball team and also takes appointment work representing indigent criminal defendants in Newton Falls Municipal Court when scheduling permits.

His professional associations include membership in the National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives (NOSSCR), the Ohio State Bar Association (OSBA) the Trumbull County Bar Association, the Ohio Association for Justice (OAJ) and Portage County Bar Association.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
To Michael P. Mazanetz, the greatest personal professional reward comes when a client's long wait for oftentimes badly needed Social Security disability benefits comes to an end with a decision in their favor.

"Some of those people have worked 25-30 years, and they've had some accident at work or at home or they've been diagnosed with a serious illness, and all of a sudden the money stops coming," he says. "It can be a long process to go through, so when they get that news, it's always a highlight."

Atty. Mazanetz is a Mahoning Valley native, raised in Newton Falls, where he still lives. As a boy, Michael knew that he wanted to be a lawyer who would help the kind of working people he knew - his father worked in a bearing factory - and he focused hard on his studies to achieve that goal.

He graduated magna cum laude from Mount Union College in 2005 with a B.A. degree in political science, and then attended the University of Akron School of Law, where he was associate editor of the Akron Law Review and graduated cum laude in 2008.

Atty. Mazanetz began working part-time at Heller, Maas, Moro & Magill starting the summer after his first year in law school, and after he got his J.D. in 2008, the firm immediately hired him as a full-time attorney.

His day-to-day practice focuses on Social Security disability law, ranging from initial case assessment through every stage of what can be a long process.

"Every Social Security disability claimant deserves to have their interest represented in a diligent, comprehensive, and personal manner," he says. "It is my goal to provide this exhaustive representation for each and every client I work with."

It's a process that requires patience by the claimants and a steady counselor role for himself.

"When somebody comes in and they've just suffered something traumatic in their life you see how much they're struggling, it can be difficult," he says. "But then when you get that decision that grants them Social Security disability benefits, and you hear in their voice or see how happy they are and it's the first good news they've had in a couple of years, it can be very rewarding."

When he's away from the office, Atty. Mazanetz contributes to his hometown of Newton Falls in two ways: He is an assistant coach for the Newton Falls High School Tigers varsity basketball team and also takes appointment work representing indigent criminal defendants in Newton Falls Municipal Court when scheduling permits.

His professional associations include membership in the National Organization of Social Security Claimants' Representatives (NOSSCR), the Ohio State Bar Association (OSBA) the Trumbull County Bar Association, the Ohio Association for Justice (OAJ) and Portage County Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Haley McDaniel
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Haley brings a passion for family law and knew from her law school days that it was the only area of law in which she wanted to make a career. As a Columbus Family and Adoption Law attorney, Haley represents clients in a wide range of matters, including divorce, dissolution, child custody, grandparent visitation, prenuptial agreements, and all forms of adoption. Haley has spent years as a certified Guardian ad Litem on the Franklin County Domestic, and Juvenile Abuse, Neglect, Dependency lists.

Haley understands that family and relationship conflicts can be overwhelming and emotionally draining. She provides sensitive support to those who are navigating the arduous dissolution, divorce, and child custody processes. Haley takes the time to learn what is most important to her clients and guides them through the process to achieve the best outcome for their family.

Haley received her Juris Doctor from Capital University Law School and her Bachelor of Arts in Political Science from The Ohio State University. While in law school she received the Cali Award (recognizing the highest final grade in the class) for her academic achievement in Mediation. Haley was a Capital University Law School Moot Court Competitor during her second and third year of law school; competing in Buffalo and Brooklyn, New York. She now coaches for Capital University Law School's moot court program.

Haley was born and raised in Ohio and enjoys cycling, watching college sports, and spending time with her husband, Bryce and two dogs, River and Kava.

attorneys.bio:
Brian T. McElroy is the owner of McElroy Law, LLC. He focuses his practice on civil litigation and contract review and drafting. His practices areas include: business litigation, consumer protection, personal injury/negligence law, employment law, insurance law, small business, drafting employment and severance agreements, drafting sales contracts, and asset purchase agreements. attorneys.name: Amy M. McKinlay Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ms. McKinlay received her Juris Doctor, magna cum laude, from the Capital University Law School, Columbus, Ohio, in 1996. While in law school, Ms. McKinlay was a Member of Order of the Curia and the Capital University Law School Law Review, and finished in the top ten percent of her graduating class. She also served as a judicial extern in the Franklin County Court of Common Pleas, Division of Domestic Relations. Ms. McKinlay was admitted to the practice of law in the State of Ohio in 1996 and to the United States District Court, Southern District of Ohio, in 1997.

Since 2007, Ms. McKinlay has been certified by the Ohio State Bar Association as a Board Certified Specialist in Family Relations Law. She has also attained the Martindale-Hubbell AV rating (highest rating attainable).

In addition, Ms. McKinlay was named by Law and Politics as an Ohio Super Lawyer "Rising Star" six times between 2005 and 2011, a designation bestowed upon the top "up-and-coming" attorneys in Ohio. In 2015, Amy joined Law and Politics' list of Ohio Super Lawyers (a group comprised of approximately five percent of the total number of attorneys in Ohio). She has U.S. News & World Report: Best Lawyers rating. She also was selected in 2022, 2023, and 2024 as one of the Top 25 Women Lawyers in Columbus by Ohio Super Lawyers.

Ms. McKinlay is a member of the American Bar Association (Family Law Section), Ohio State Bar Association (Family Law Section), and the Columbus Bar Association (Family Law Committee). She has also lectured on a number of family law-related topics, including discovery procedure, settlement strategy, and valuation and division of complex assets.

attorneys.name: Sydney S. McLafferty
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Dublin, OH
attorneys.bio:
Sydney S. McLafferty has been representing injury victims and their families for over 20 years throughout the state of Ohio. Early in law school, Sydney learned that the civil justice system was weighted in favor of insurance companies and corporations with endless resources to deny justice to the individuals of Ohio. She has found it truly rewarding to be able to level the playing field for her clients by providing them access to justice and protection in an otherwise challenging atmosphere.

Sydney has spent a significant amount of her professional time in leadership roles at the Ohio Association for Justice which is a state-wide organization dedicated to protecting her client’s constitutional rights and access to the civil justice system. Her involvement with OAJ directly benefits her clients and the clients of other practitioners around the state.

Sydney was raised in Wyoming, Ohio (a suburb of Cincinnati) and moved to Columbus to attend The Ohio State University. Following in the footsteps of her grandfather and uncles, Sydney attended law school at Capital University Law School. Sydney and her husband, Scott, are raising their family in the Columbus suburb of Upper Arlington.

attorneys.name: R. Craig McLaughlin
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mayfield Heights, OH
attorneys.bio:
Craig represents people who have been seriously injured or killed as a result of motor vehicle crashes, medical negligence, defective products, and workplace incidents. He has served as lead counsel for an injured client in over 35 jury trials and obtained the highest verdict ($620,000) in Clermont County, Ohio for a personal injury motor vehicle crash case. He has been named a "Super Lawyer" every year since 2013 by Ohio Super Lawyer Magazine and was identified as a "Super Lawyer Rising Star" in 2009-2012. Craig has also earned the highest attorney rating from Martindale-Hubbell and AVVO and is a life member of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Million Dollar Advocates Forum.

Settlements and Verdicts

$7.1 Million – Motor Vehicle Crash – Indiana

Recovery for an Ohio woman who was rear-ended by a SUV at a high rate of speed on an Indiana highway. She suffered a traumatic brain injury, fractures in her middle back, herniated discs in her lower back, multiple rib fractures, and other injuries in the collision that prevented her from continuing her career as an administrative assistant.

Confidential Settlement – Motor Vehicle Crash – Ohio

Recovery for a man who was seriously injured when a commercial truck went left of center and hit his pick-up truck in a head-on collision. He suffered a fractured pelvis, fractured hip, and other injuries that kept him from continuing his career as a welder.

$1.25 Million – Motor Vehicle Crash – Butler County, Ohio

Recovery for a man who was seriously injured when a pick-up truck was negligently backed into a barn door and the door fell on him. He suffered a fractured back, fractured foot, multiple rib fractures, ruptured spleen, lacerated liver, and other injuries.

$1.085 Million – Motor Vehicle Crash – Allen County, Ohio

Recovery for a woman involved in a multiple vehicle crash on an Ohio interstate. She suffered a lacerated liver, rib fractures, ankle fracture, bruised lung, abdominal compartment syndrome and other injuries in the collision.

$1.05 Million – Motor Vehicle Crash – Geauga County, Ohio

Recovery for a man who was hit in a head-on collision by a speeding commercial truck. He suffered multiple fractures of his legs, lacerations to his spleen and kidneys, and other injuries in the crash. Co-Counsel: Todd Rosenberg

Confidential Settlement – Employer Intentional Tort – Ohio

Recovery for a factory worker who was scalped when his hair got caught on an unguarded rotating shaft on a machine. He also lost part of one ear and suffers from post-traumatic stress disorder.

$875,000 Verdict – Medical Malpractice – Court of Claims – Ohio

A baby from Lucas County suffered brain damage when the doctor negligently performed a C-section. The mother had scar tissue from a previous abdominal surgery and the doctor negligently failed to remove scar tissue before cutting into the mother’s uterus to deliver the baby. The doctor also failed to have a second experienced doctor present to assist her during this difficult delivery. A verdict on the issue of liability only was won in the Ohio Court of Claim and then the case was resolved at a settlement conference.

$800,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Hamilton County, Ohio

Recovery for a woman who was a passenger in a van that was struck by a truck that failed to stop for a red light. She suffered a fractured neck and herniated disk and was unable to work again.

Confidential Settlement – Motor Vehicle Crash – Ohio

Recovery for a female security guard who had her foot and ankle run over by a tractor trailer driver during an inspection of the trailer. She was unable to work as a security guard again.

Confidential Settlement – Medical Malpractice – Ohio

Recovery for an elderly man who now has advanced stage kidney disease because his family doctor failed to review and respond to abnormal blood tests that had been ordered for many years. Client will now likely need dialysis or a kidney transplant.

$700,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Erie County – Ohio

Recovery for a man who was hit from behind by a car while he was on a tractor driving down a country road. He suffered a fractured back and was unable to work again.

$650,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Miami County, Ohio

Recovery for the family of a truck driver who was killed instantly when his truck was hit by another truck.

$620,000 Verdict – Motor Vehicle Crash – Clermont County, Ohio

Jury verdict for a man who was injured when a truck clipped another car during an improper lane change, causing it to spin out and strike the client’s car. He suffered two herniated disks in his lower back that required multiple surgeries and left him unable to return to work. The last offer from the insurance company before trial was $50,000.

$575,000 – Personal Injury – Kentucky

Recovery for a delivery truck driver who suffered a fractured ankle that required multiple surgeries when a tow truck operator dropped a heavy slab of granite during unloading of a flatbed trailer.

$525,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Mahoning County, Ohio

Recovery for an elderly woman who was being transported in a nursing home van and suffered a fractured neck when another car ran a stop sign and struck the van.

$525,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Franklin County, Ohio

Recovery for the death of a 73 years old woman who was killed when her husband went left of center and crashed into another car. She died at the scene.

$500,000 – Medical Malpractice – Ohio

Recovery for the family of a veteran who went to the Cleveland VA Medical Center for hernia repair surgery. The surgeon perforated the client’s intestines during surgery then failed to detect the injury in a timely manner. The client died several months later due to complication from sepsis infection.

$500,000 – Medical Malpractice – Lucas County, Ohio

Recovery for the family of a nursing home patient who was dropped by a private ambulance attendant during transport back from a dialysis session. He fell and hit his head and suffered a brain injury. He died one month later.

$500,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Lucas County, Ohio

Recovery for a woman who was hit head on by a truck that went left of center. She suffered multiple fractures to her arms and legs, a very bad laceration to her leg, and other injuries.

Confidential Settlement – Personal Injury – Ohio

Recovery for a pipefitter whose foot was crushed when the operator negligently lowered outriggers on a mobile crane without warning.

$470,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Richland County, Ohio

Recovery for a teenager who was a passenger in a car where the driver lost control and struck a utility pole. Client suffered a fractured skull, moderate brain injury, and other injuries in the crash.

$460,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Muskingum County, Ohio

Recovery for a woman who was hit head on by a car that crossed over the median. She suffered a fractured foot, neck injury, and bruised ribs.

$425,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Kentucky

Recovery for a young woman who was a passenger in a pick-up truck that rear-ended a slow moving tractor on a dark country road that did not have appropriate lights and warning signs. She suffered a fractured nose, fractured wrist, fractured ankle, and other injuries.

$400,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Kentucky

Recovery for a man who was injured when another car ran a red light and struck his car while he was clearing the intersection. He suffered closed head injury, punctured lung, bruised lung and other injuries.

$400,000 – Motor Vehicle Crash – Allen County, Ohio

Recovery for female was seriously injured when a commercial truck failed to stop at a stop sign and crashed into the car in which she was a passenger. She suffered a fractured nose, fractured arm, fractured leg, multiple rib fractures, and other injuries.

$400,000 – Medical Malpractice – Ohio

Recovery for the family of an 82 years old nursing home resident who was totally dependent on nursing home staff for all of her needs, but was left unattended on a portable toilet. She fell and hit her head and suffered a brain injury. She died two days later.

$350,000 – Medical Malpractice – Ohio

Recovery for elderly gentleman after an optometrist failed to diagnose open angle glaucoma that resulted in permanent partial vision loss in both of client’s eyes.

$325,000 – Premises Liability – Knox County, Ohio

Recovery for elderly female who tripped and fell going down steps to a business that did not comply with safety codes. She suffered a fractured skull, traumatic brain injury, fractured right wrist, and other injuries.

Confidential – Medical Malpractice – Ohio

Recovery for the family of an elderly nursing home resident who was dropped and suffered a brain injury during a Hoyer lift transfer because the aide attempted transfer on her own instead of with two people as was required. Client died days after the fall.

$300,000 – Personal Injury – Delaware County, Ohio

Recovery for a young girl who suffered a fractured skull when a neighbor gave his young son a golf club and ball to play with in the backyard and then left the children unsupervised while he went upstairs to take a shower.

$275,000 – Medical Malpractice – Ohio

Recovery for a veteran after doctors and nurses at the Cleveland VA Medical Center failed to remove surgical towels from the client’s abdomen after surgery to remove his cancerous kidney. Client became very sick, needed multiple surgeries to fix the problem, and missed significant time from work.

$241,000 – Personal Injury – Medina County, Ohio

Recovery for a teenage female who suffered an avulsion of the patellar tendon in her knee and other injuries when a classmate stepped on her feet and knocked her to the ground during horseplay at school.

$225,000 – Dog Bite – Butler County, Ohio

Recovery for a toddler who was bit on the cheek by a friend’s dog at a Fourth of July party.

All lawsuits are different and Elk & Elk makes no representation or promises that it can obtain the same results in other cases. These results do not guarantee, warrant, or predict the outcome of any future legal matter. You should consult an attorney for advice regarding your individual situation.

attorneys.name: William J. McLoughlin
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Westerville, OH
attorneys.bio:
The primary focus of my law practice involves guiding individuals through the complex estate planning process and probate. I have more than thirty years’ experience in the preparation and administration of matters ranging from very basic wills to highly sophisticated wealth and family business transfers. I provide clients guidance with all areas of probate law and estate tax matters, including resolution of contested cases in Probate Court and the Internal Revenue Service.

I also counsel clients on the formation and operation of closely held businesses, corporations, limited liability companies and partnerships. Such advice involves preparation of shareholder/owner agreements, buy-sell agreements, employment and compensation agreements, and business sales and acquisitions.

I began my career as a Certified Public Accountant (inactive) having spent a considerable amount of his accounting practice assisting clients in the insurance, real estate development and retail food service industries.

My wife and I reside in Westerville, Ohio, and have two children. I am a member of the Westerville Sunrise Rotary and enjoy golfing and time with my family.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Martindale Hubbell - AV Rating, 1999 - Present

attorneys.name: Kevin McManus
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Cases Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
I had the privilege of growing up in Toledo and attending St. John's Jesuit High School. Following my graduation from the University of Notre Dame, I returned home and completed my studies at the University of Toledo College of Law. At that point, I joined forces with my father and brother to establish a general law practice, where we assist clients in a wide range of legal matters they may face.

I gained valuable experience in the courtroom while assisting our clients. Additionally, I learned the significance of effective communication, including actively listening and comprehending each client's unique needs. This is especially crucial as they frequently endure the most challenging period in their lives.

I am grateful for the chance to assist exceptional individuals who may require a bit more support. Several have been loyal clients of our firm for quite some time. Frequently, I am approached with inquiries about how to aid a family member who is experiencing mental decline or is unable to care for themselves. Additionally, many seek guidance in managing the affairs of a deceased loved one. I have found that few are acquainted with the legal system and often do not know where to begin.

Throughout my career, I have had the privilege of assisting individuals during challenging times. Some face the unavoidable consequences of cognitive decline, while others have sustained injuries and require assistance with their daily tasks. Irrespective of the specific circumstances, each client entrusts me with the utmost important aspects of their lives, and for that, I am deeply honored.

I prioritize individualized communication with every client. I make myself available to assist with everyday problems, even in the late hours of the night. Going above and beyond to ensure all their needs are met is essential to me. In these situations, I often find that I gain as much from the relationship as the client does. It's a collaborative effort between the client, their family and myself. Success is only achieved when we work together as a team.

I am a lawyer because I believe in the power of practicing law.

Feel free to reach out to me anytime at 419-346-3268. I am always available to answer your calls.

If you prefer, you can also contact me at the office on 419-242-1255. I offer free consultations, and I am here to assist you with any questions or concerns you may have. Rest assured, I will provide excellent care and support for you or your loved ones.

attorneys.name: Martin McManus
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Administration Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Since graduating from the University of Toledo College of Law in 1987, Martin J. McManus has been accompanying his clients into the state and federal courthouses in the Toledo area. Additionally, Marty has gained extensive experience practicing law in the southern Michigan area, appearing in both state and federal courts.

Marty was born in Toledo. He attended St. John's Jesuit High School and the University of Notre Dame. Afterward, he returned home to pursue law school and joined his father's law practice.

Marty is an experienced litigator who practices in various areas. He focuses on defending clients facing criminal charges and representing those with significant personal injury claims, such as wrongful death, car accidents and medical malpractice cases. Unlike many other lawyers, Marty is willing to take cases to trial, which greatly impacts the outcomes he achieves for his clients.

Marty is an attorney concentrates on protecting individuals and businesses during white-collar criminal investigations and prosecutions. He also represents adults and juveniles facing misdemeanor and felony charges, such as drug offenses and DWI/OVI offenses. Throughout his career, Marty has been devoted to defending the accused and advocating for those who have been unjustly harmed.

Marty has a clear strategy: treating each client as if they were his only client. This may sound straightforward, but Marty is determined to execute this plan for every client, regardless of the nature of their case. As a result of Marty's unwavering dedication, each client benefits greatly from his relentless efforts on their behalf.

Marty is available 24/7 at 419-351-1531 to provide protection for his clients. Feel free to reach out anytime you require immediate assistance. Rest assured, Marty will always be there to answer your call. Feel free to contact Marty at the office on 419-242-1255 whenever it is convenient for you. He is available for a complimentary consultation or if you simply have any questions.

attorneys.name: Jeff Meadows
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense/OVI/Traffic Lawyers in West Chester, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Meadows grew up in the Mason and West Chester area when both were essentially one-horse towns. Well maybe two horse towns for Jeff because his family had horses on their 5-acre mini farm in West Chester.

While his parents were Lakota grads, Jeff ended up graduating from Mason High School in 1982 where he was the senior class president. He then headed off to Oxford where he had a very robust social experience - so robust that Miami U. asked him not to come back after 2 ½ years of fraternity fun.

Shortly after the fun ended at Miami (of Ohio), Jeff became a father, got married and started working for American Airlines where he continued to work while finishing his undergrad at Univ. of Cincinnati. With a bachelor's degree in hand, Jeff headed off to Miami, Florida to attend law school at The U, while working third shift at the baggage claim area for American Airlines at the Miami Intl. Airport. After finishing law school, Jeff came back to Ohio to begin his law career.

Having established himself as one of the top OVI defense lawyers in Ohio, Jeff focuses his practice in SW Ohio (Butler, Hamilton, Warren and Clermont Counties) and is regularly found fighting DUI's in a multiple counties a day. In total, Jeff has practiced OVI defense in 26 of Ohio's 88 counties, including, but not limited to Brown, Adams, Preble, Madison, Greene, Montgomery, Fayette, Highland and Athens counties.

Throughout his 28+ year career, Jeff has handled well over 3500 DUI cases and has taken more DUI cases to trial than other Ohio attorney (at least that's how he gets introduced when speaking at OACDL events).

Additionally, his love for continuing his education has led him to be one of SIX lawyers in Ohio recognized by the American Chemical Society as a Lawyer-Scientist and this has helped him in defending OVI cases that involve blood or urine testing as well as drug possession/trafficking cases involving other substances such as methamphetamine, cocaine and various other drugs.

When not fighting for his clients, Jeff's real passion is SCUBA diving and he loves diving with sharks and other apex predators which includes 12 species of sharks and Salt Water Crocodiles. So when it's time to fight in the courtroom, no other attorney around matches his fearless and bold personality.

attorneys.name: Thomas D. Meeks
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Thomas decided to pursue a career in law at a young age and never changed his mind. Always the one to get straight to the issues and stick to the point, Thomas has a longstanding passion for advocacy and argument. His knack for dispensing with the distractions and getting to the heart of the matter served him greatly in his personal life, academic career, and now his professional career as a litigator.

Thomas has a strong work ethic, having an unbroken resume beginning at age 14 at Giant Eagle. All these childhood jobs, combined with profound life experiences including missionary work in Kenya, have given Thomas a unique and insightful perspective that continues to be one of his most valuable assets.

While pursuing his Bachelor of Arts in Law at the University of Arizona, and with some extra time on his hands during the COVID pandemic, Thomas earned his Paralegal II certification while in college. This opened up doors allowing Thomas to work for firms practicing in a wide range of practice areas - from immigration to personal injury - all before even applying to law school. This early experience and demonstrable passion earned Thomas a spot and a scholarship at the University of Cincinnati College of Law.

At UC Law, Thomas had the privilege of meeting Rick DeBlasis at a firm expo held at the school. While Rick was not there to hire anyone, the two hit it off and Rick brought Thomas on as a law clerk in 2024. After a successful run as a law clerk, and after Thomas passed the Bar with outstanding results, Rick hired Thomas as a full-time attorney in November 2025. With particularly honed research and writing skills, Thomas has distinguished himself in cases ranging from foreclosures, creditor rights, consumer rights, and more.

When he is not lawyering, Thomas enjoys reading about history, playing chess and golf, and taking his dog on hikes with his fiancée. If you are looking for a hardworking and driven attorney to solve your legal problems, Thomas is your man.

attorneys.name: Brooke Meneses
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Brooke Meneses’ practice encompasses all aspects of divorce, dissolution of marriage, child custody and support, parental rights and responsibilities, grandparents’ rights, and adoption. Brooke has a passion for helping clients navigate these difficult legal issues knowing that the outcome of these types of cases not only affect the here and now but the rest of a client and their loved ones’ lives.

Before becoming an attorney, Brooke spent her undergraduate years as an NCAA Division II volleyball player at Tiffin University. Thereafter, Brooke proudly served four years in the United States Marine Corps from 2014 to 2018 where she served as a Combat Engineer Officer at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. During her time in the Marine Corps as a Company Commander she trained, developed, and mentored hundreds of young Marines. Additionally, throughout her four years of service, Brooke served as a Uniformed Victim Advocate under the Marine Corps’ Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Program providing sexual assault prevention training to young Marines and 24/7 support and advocacy to all Marine, Sailor, and military dependent victims of sexual assault. After concluding her service in the Marine Corps in 2018, Brooke has remained dedicated to the veterans of our country by serving as a mentor to criminal justice involved veterans through the Stark County Honor Court and simultaneously, as a board member for The Honor Foundation of Stark County, Ohio, a non-profit organization that provides specialized financial and recovery service support to justice-involved veterans and their families.

Since earning her J.D. in 2022 from the University of Akron School of Law, she has been selected as a 2023 ystark! Twenty under 40 award winner – an award given to young leaders of Stark County who have demonstrated dynamic leadership and social responsibility; named a 2024-2025 Best Lawyer “One to Watch” for labor and employment law; and named a 2025 Super Lawyers Ohio Rising Star for the practice of Family Law.

Outside of work Brooke and her husband, Sergio, enjoy spending the majority of their day-to-day with their four children, Sawyer, Colt, Shiloh, and Cruz – constantly transporting and supporting their older children in the multiple different sports and activities they are involved in year-round. Although it can be hectic at times, she loves her family’s busy, active lifestyle. In her spare time, Brooke enjoys traveling, coaching her children’s basketball teams, playing in recreational volleyball leagues with friends, and has just started training for her first appearance in the Marine Corps Marathon in Washington, D.C this coming October.

attorneys.name: David L. Meyerson
attorneys.practice_type: Ohio Workers' Compensation Litigation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney David Meyerson heads our Workers' Compensation litigation department. He is considered one of Ohio's leading and most effective litigators in this area of law.

David further holds the Ohio State Bar Associations prestigious board certification in Ohio Workers' Compensation Laws.

My Story:

Dave Meyerson doesn't like to blow his own horn - but he is actually very good at it. Dave is a gifted trumpet player. He began taking lessons when he was in second grade and by the time he was 11 he packed his bags for the first of many enjoyable summers at the prestigious Interlochen National Music Camp in Michigan.

"Playing the trumpet was a wonderfully enriching experience for me," says Dave. "It fueled my lifelong love of music, and helped me meet and interact with many exceptional people from all walks of life. It also taught me how to be a good team member."

Nowadays listening to music provides a safety valve for Dave, particularly after a hectic day at the office. His musical tastes range from jazzy sets performed by Wynton Marsalis to the big band sounds of Glenn Miller, Duke Ellington and Count Basie. But it is classical music that soothes the "wild beast." "When I drive home I put on the classical music station and the stress of the day melts away," says Dave.

Although he could have been a music major at Ohio State University, Dave opted to major in criminal justice. But up until his senior year at OSU, becoming a lawyer was not on Dave's radar screen. Fortunately, a chance discussion with his roommate ultimately led to a law career.

"My roommate had taken the Law School Aptitude Test (LSAT) exam and reviewed his answers with me," says Dave. "I instinctively knew the answers to many of the test questions. We both agreed that I should take the LSAT on the next testing date and see how I would do."

Dave scored so well on the LSAT that when he applied to Cleveland Marshall School of Law he immediately secured a spot as a first-year law student. "I knew then I had found my correct career path," says Dave. "I've always believed in the importance of fair play and the Golden Rule and these principles are the basis of any good legal practice."

As a Workers' Compensation litigation attorney with Seaman Garson LLC, Dave's ability to see justice done for injured workers makes his job particularly rewarding. "I've always liked helping people," he explains. "Even though not all my clients personally say thank you, it's those clients who give me a hug or send me a nice note that make me feel that I have touched their lives in an important way."

Dave doesn't have to worry about effectively touching people's lives. His warmth, keen intelligence and lively sense of humor are greatly appreciated by his wife Cathy and their two children.

"It is my nature to make people happy," says Dave. "That's why I give it my all as a plaintiff's attorney at Seaman Garson LLC."

attorneys.name: Leah Michael
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Law Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Building on a Diverse Legal Background to Win Cases for Injured Workers

Leah Michael is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation. Since joining the firm in 2022, Leah has demonstrated a unique talent for getting to know clients and using care, creativity, communication, and profound legal strategy to loop clients in, make them a part of the team, and collaboratively build cases that win.

Lived Experience in Workers’ Compensation

Leah grew up in a working-class family in the manufacturing corridor of northwest Ohio. Her father worked in industrial hazardous waste management, and when Leah was still young, he suffered a bad workplace accident. After more than 30 surgeries, Leah’s father became permanently and totally disabled.

Leah spent much of her youth working at a locally owned restaurant to help make ends meet. Her father’s experience, plus the mentorship of a restaurant regular (a retired federal judge) led Leah to pursue a career in law. “I knew I wanted to help people,” Leah says. “And having known so many within our family and community who had been injured in the line of work, it just seemed natural to enter a field where I could give a voice to people who are often made to feel like they don’t have one.”

Leah attended undergrad and law school at the University of Toledo, wasting no time and jumping into the legal profession as a law firm’s paralegal while still completing courses towards her undergrad. Then Leah went to night school for her law degree, continuing to work full-time for law firms. The years of employment in the legal field before even completing law school and her excellent academic marks led Leah to successfully practice bankruptcy law, personal injury law, elder law, estate planning, asset protection, probate, social security law, and workers’ compensation law.

A Relentless Commitment to Working Ohioans

Leah’s strengths lie in her ability to get to know clients, understand their cases, empathize with them, and strategize how to tell their stories. “Attorneys are, at their core, storytellers,” Leah says. “Our job is to utilize the legal codes at our disposal and construct a compelling, strategic story around our client’s case, a story so powerful that we come out winners not by a hair, but by a mile.”

To accomplish this, Leah relies on her exceptional team-building skills and the immense resources available to her. “NRS Injury Law is the largest workers’ compensation firm in Ohio,” she said. “There are dozens of nuanced yet critical factors that go into building a strong workers’ compensation case, and the attorneys here are supported by the firm’s staff assistants, case managers, paralegals, research capacities, information sharing, and colleague assistance.”

Work/Life Balance

To Leah, hard work is best rewarded by taking a few moments here and there to tune out, relax, and recharge. Leah enjoys regular walks and snuggle sessions with her beloved French bulldog, Biscuit. On the weekend, Leah can be found playing tennis, golfing, and getting together with her friends to perform improv acting and comedy skits. During the holidays, Leah takes great pride in donning the “Favorite Aunt” title when visiting her nephews in Kansas.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Leah Michael

Both on the clock and off it, Leah’s core commitments and values align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Leah and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Leah Michael comes from an upbringing where helping one’s community is as natural as going to school or working a job. On a national level, Leah is active in the Workers’ Injury Law & Advocacy Group (WILG), a national organization of attorneys dedicated to improving worker protections. Leah is also deeply involved in her community at the local level. She is a member of the Charter Review Committee for her hometown of Toledo, where she reviews legislation brought before the City Council. Leah is also involved in voter protection efforts led by attorneys, and she volunteers for union shops in the Toledo area by helping them organize community events.

The years of employment in the legal field before even completing law school and her excellent academic marks led Leah to successfully practice bankruptcy law, personal injury law, elder law, estate planning, asset protection, probate, social security law, and workers’ compensation law.

A Relentless Commitment to Working Ohioans

Leah’s strengths lie in her ability to get to know clients, understand their cases, empathize with them, and strategize how to tell their stories. “Attorneys are, at their core, storytellers,” Leah says. “Our job is to utilize the legal codes at our disposal and construct a compelling, strategic story around our client’s case, a story so powerful that we come out winners not by a hair, but by a mile.”

To accomplish this, Leah relies on her exceptional team-building skills and the immense resources available to her. “NRS Injury Law is the largest workers’ compensation firm in Ohio,” she said. “There are dozens of nuanced yet critical factors that go into building a strong workers’ compensation case, and the attorneys here are supported by the firm’s staff assistants, case managers, paralegals, research capacities, information sharing, and colleague assistance.”

Work/Life Balance

To Leah, hard work is best rewarded by taking a few moments here and there to tune out, relax, and recharge. Leah enjoys regular walks and snuggle sessions with her beloved French bulldog, Biscuit. On the weekend, Leah can be found playing tennis, golfing, and getting together with her friends to perform improv acting and comedy skits. During the holidays, Leah takes great pride in donning the “Favorite Aunt” title when visiting her nephews in Kansas.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Leah Michael

Both on the clock and off it, Leah’s core commitments and values align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Leah and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Leah Michael comes from an upbringing where helping one’s community is as natural as going to school or working a job. On a national level, Leah is active in the Workers’ Injury Law & Advocacy Group (WILG), a national organization of attorneys dedicated to improving worker protections. Leah is also deeply involved in her community at the local level. She is a member of the Charter Review Committee for her hometown of Toledo, where she reviews legislation brought before the City Council. Leah is also involved in voter protection efforts led by attorneys, and she volunteers for union shops in the Toledo area by helping them organize community events.

attorneys.name: Todd T. Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Dayton, OH
attorneys.bio:
Biography

For over 30 years, Todd Miller has been representing injured workers. Whether it’s your first work related injury or if you have had prior injuries, the system can feel overwhelming. Todd is here to help!

Board Certified in Worker’s Compensation and chosen to be an Ohio Super Lawyer for multiple years, Todd has the experience and knowledge to guide you through the workers’ compensation system. When you hire Todd, you are hiring an attorney that will personally work on your case. Clients are treated with the respect and dignity they deserve. Despite being a “no fault” state, an injured worker can often feel that they are suddenly the enemy. Receiving multiple phone calls from different people working under the umbrella of the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation can be confusing. Statements can be taken out of context and even be used against you in the processing of your claim. Injured workers simply want to get fixed and get back to work as quickly as possible. Todd’s goal is to assist in that process against a system that often feels like it just doesn’t care.

Born and raised in Ohio, Todd has three adult children. Proud of them all, two have gone on to be lawyers helping injured people in other states. He enjoys reading, traveling and golfing as time permits.

When asked what has changed in the last thirty years, Todd responds:

A lot! Most people that come to see me simply want their life back. In a fraction of a second their life has changed. They have gone from being a provider for themselves and their family, to being injured and in pain. They want to be fixed and get back to work ASAP! It is difficult to be patient during this process.

If you have been injured at work, your remedy is an Ohio workers’ compensation claim. In most circumstances, the employer is given immunity from negligence. You cannot directly sue them. Workplace injuries must be reported through the Ohio workers’ compensation system. To report a work-related injury through your private insurance can, in some circumstances, be interpreted as insurance fraud.

A workers’ compensation claim can take time, especially if you don’t know where to begin. Sometimes employers can be helpful in steering you in the right direction, but often the injured worker is left to figure out the system by themself. Most employers have professional representation, you should too!

The system can feel informal but be careful. You can now phone in or appear through the internet for hearings before the Industrial Commission of Ohio. The hearing officers are making decisions about your life, your medical treatment, and your compensation. Why wouldn’t you want to be there in person? It is always the injured workers’ responsibility to prove that the injury happened at work and that the physician’s diagnoses are related to your injury. The fact that it happened at work is sometimes not enough. The hearing officers are looking for specific evidence in precise legal language. If you don’t have it, that can mean the difference between winning and losing your claim. You cannot assume that anybody at the hearing is on your side. The workers’ compensation system is often adversarial.

Representing injured workers is what I have devoted my career to over the last 30 years. I want to help injured workers not only understand the system but also get the treatment and compensation they deserve. It is sometimes harder than people realize and there are organizations working against the injured workers’ goal to get better and back to work.

Over the last 30 years, the workers’ compensation laws have changed and often not to the benefit of the worker. I have seen people trying to represent themselves in a system that can be stacked against them. Injured workers need to know their rights and responsibilities in a system that has become more complicated. Isn’t it worth your time to find out what you need to know? My consultation is free! Contact me today!

attorneys.name: Laura L. Mills Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Canton, OH
attorneys.bio:
For twenty-five years, Laura L. Mills has managed and provided a full-service litigation practice through the law firm of Mills, Mills, Fiely & Lucas. The law firm originated in Canton and provides service throughout the entire state of Ohio.

Laura is a litigator and has defended multiple murder/attempted murder trials successfully. She has managed and tried multi-million dollar medical malpractice claims, business litigation matters and partnership disputes. She is a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates, Super Lawyers, Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and has earned the highest possible rating in legal ability and ethical standards from the bar and judiciary.

She strongly and passionately advocates for individuals, especially in the realm of social injustice. She has appeared on national television (CBS, 48 Hours, Good Morning America, Dr. Phil, Fox News,) on behalf of her clients. She has appeared in LawNewz, and provided an interview podcast for Beth Karas as well as being featured in her hometown paper for her work and commitment to domestic violence and other social injustice.

Laura is admitted to practice in state and federal courts throughout Ohio as well as the District of Columbia. She has also tried jury trials in multiple other states and jurisdictions as well as family matters in multiple states across the country.

Laura is President of the Stark County Academy of Trial Lawyers and she is a member of the Ohio Bar Association and Ohio Association for Justice.

She assists clients in many areas of the law such as business formation, family law matters, medical malpractice, civil rights violations, corporate litigation, contract litigation, criminal defense and estate planning.

Laura is a graduate of Mount Union College with a Bachelor's Degree in Political Science and a minor in Secondary Education. She obtained her law degree from the University of Akron School of Law while employed full time by a large multi-state law firm. She championed the regional trial team at the University of Akron as the first women team to win at regionals.

attorneys.name: Howard D. Mishkind
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Beachwood, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Mishkind is President and Founder of the Mishkind Law Firm Co., L.P.A. His practice is concentrated primarily in the area of personal injury litigation, consisting of the representation of injured patients and their families in medical malpractice, legal malpractice and catastrophic injuries arising out of motor vehicle collisions. He has been a participant in numerous seminars locally and throughout the State of Ohio on matters relating to personal injury, medical malpractice and civil litigation. He has also made numerous appearances and presentations to various local schools and on several local radio and television stations.

Mr. Mishkind has chaired or co-chaired the Cleveland-Marshall Law Alumni Association Annual Recognition Luncheon from 1992 through 2012 and was honored as Outstanding Alumnus of the Year in 2003. He serves on various committees of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association, including the Court Rules Committee. He is also actively involved in issues concerning attorney ethics and has served as the Chair of the Cuyahoga County Certified Grievance Committee and is an active member of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association Certified Grievance Committee. He has investigated and litigated claims against attorneys involving violations of the Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct (formerly known as the Ohio Code of Professional Responsibility). He has served as an expert witness and has testified in Professional negligence matters as an expert witness.

attorneys.bio:
Clare Mitchell graduated from the University of Dayton in 1991 with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Psychology. She attended the University of Toledo evening law program and earned her Juris Doctorate in December of 2002. She was admitted to practice in May of 2003. She focuses her practice on Family Law including divorce, dissolution, domestic violence and custody issues in Lucas, Wood, Fulton, Henry and Hancock Counties. She has advocated for abused, neglected and dependent youth as a Lucas County court appointed Guardian Ad Litem for over 8 years, and is active in the Toledo Bar Association’s volunteer programs for both the Domestic Relations and Juvenile Court divisions. Her hobbies include running, cycling, scuba diving, traveling, and spending time with her daughters.

Clare has been an associate at Mahaffey & Associates since 2022.

attorneys.name: Mark Mockensturm
attorneys.practice_type: Taxation Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mark Mockensturm founded Mockensturm, Ltd in 1999. After graduating from law school in 1993, he worked for several firms in the Toledo area that specialize in employment litigation and real estate transactions. During that time people who learned of his training as a CPA sought his advice in their dealings with the IRS and other tax authorities. He was often able to help these people resolve their issues quickly and favorably. So in late 1999, Mark decided to offer his help to a list of people who recently received notice of IRS liens filings. The response was overwhelming and Mark soon found there was more work than he could handle on a part-time basis. Starting with one secretary, he started Mockensturm, Ltd. and moved into a building he purchased with a friend in downtown Toldeo. Within a couple of years, the practice outgrew that location and moved to its current location on Adams Street.

Mark believes that his success is due in large part to the excellent rapport he has built with his clients, the IRS and other tax agencies. He and his staff have built a reputation as effective and responsive representatives and this has earned them trust and cooperation from local tax authorities. However, those authorities also know that he and his employees will not hesitate to use every tool at their disposal to diligently represent their clients. There is no hesitation to use all available avenues of appeal, including litigation in US Tax Court and all Federal and State Courts.

Because of his success in tax representations, many of Mark's clients return for other legal services. Mark soon found that he needed additional legal staff to handle a range of other legal matters, including business transactions, real estate, probate, estate planning and many other financially relevant legal issues. Because he and his associates have a deep understanding of many economic issues, his firm soon earned the reputation as effective financial problem solvers.

As his practice has grown, Mark spends much of his time meeting and advising new clients and overseeing the work of his excellent staff. He considers himself extremely lucky to have brought together a group of smart, hardworking people who truly care about his clients and work together as a team. This approach ensures that all possible avenues of representation are thoroughly explored and the best, most cost-effective plan is implemented.

attorneys.name: John R. Mohr
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Matters Lawyers in Dayton, OH
attorneys.bio:
John is a business lawyer who graduated from The Ohio State University with a B.S. in Business Administration (Major Accounting) and a law degree from Moritz College of Law.

Before forming Gottschlich & Portune, John served as in-house counsel for several entities, including: a real estate developer; a large financial institution engaged in the business of financing large commercial projects in numerous states; a publicly-traded multi-national corporation where he handled real estate matters and later served as a member of management as senior vice president, general counsel and secretary with responsibility for all legal issues including, real estate, corporate financial issues, employment, international, corporate compliance and franchising.

John's primary practice includes real estate matters, corporate formation, business transactions, securities, private placements and franchising. His past experience working in-house provides a broad base of experience in real estate, corporate, franchising and general business transactions. He has extensive experience in ground leases, build-to-suit leases, leasing/subleasing and other real estate and title matters.

More recently, he represented the City of Clayton, Ohio in the sale of real estate to Caterpillar for development of a $65 million facility. He has also been involved in the redevelopment of real estate.

He is admitted to the Bar in Ohio and the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio.

attorneys.name: Jarrod M. Mohler
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jarrod is a partner in the firm's litigation practice group. He has experience representing both companies and individuals in a variety of matters, including business, commercial and contractual disputes, employment issues, personal injury claims, workers compensation, probate and estate litigation, aviation claims, and appellate practice. Jarrod regularly appears in trial courts, appellate courts, mediations, arbitrations, and administrative hearings in Greater Cincinnati, Dayton, Columbus and surrounding communities.

Jarrod was selected for inclusion on the 2011, 2012, and 2013 Ohio Super Lawyers "Rising Stars" list, which recognizes outstanding young lawyers based on peer recognition and professional achievement.

From 2006 to 2011, Jarrod served on the Cincinnati Bar Association's Certified Grievance Committee, which investigates and prosecutes grievances filed against local attorneys for violations of the Ohio Rules of Professional Conduct. In 2011, Jarrod was appointed to the Ohio State Bar Association's Legal Ethics and Professional Conduct Committee.

Jarrod is a graduate of the Cincinnati Bar Association's Cincinnati Academy of Leadership for Lawyers (CALL), Class XVI. Jarrod also volunteers to be a mentor to new lawyers through the Ohio State Bar Association's "Lawyer to Lawyer" Program.

Jarrod began his career as the staff attorney for the Honorable Thomas J. Grady of the Ohio Court of Appeals. Jarrod applies the knowledge and experience he gained at the Court of Appeals when handling many of the firm's appeals. Jarrod has been personally involved in appeals before the United States Supreme Court, the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, the Ohio Supreme Court, and Courts of Appeals throughout the State of Ohio.

Jarrod is committed to serving his clients' needs and efficient, practical resolution of disputes.

Jarrod is actively involved in volunteer activities both within the legal community and for the public at large. He is an Emeritus Member of the Board of Directors of Visionaries & Voices, a non-profit arts organization that provides studio space and instruction to artists with disabilities. Jarrod and his wife Sharon live in Cincinnati with their two young children.

attorneys.name: Jennifer Molnar
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law - Employee Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jennifer Molnar is an associate attorney at Cavitch, bringing a strong academic background and a wealth of hands-on legal experience to the firm. A recent graduate of Cleveland State University College of Law, she earned a Juris Doctor and was consistently named to the Dean’s List. Jennifer demonstrated exceptional legal aptitude by earning five separate CALI Excellence for the Future Awards in Contracts, Animal Law, Critical Race Theory, Estates and Trusts, and Pretrial Practice.

Prior to law school, Jennifer completed both a Master of Arts and a Bachelor of Arts in English from Cleveland State University, providing a strong foundation in critical analysis, research, and persuasive writing.

Jennifer was a Law Clerk at Schroth Law, LLC where she was responsible for researching complex legal issues, drafting a wide range of legal documents, and assisting with trial preparation and discovery. This role was complemented by her work in the Pretrial Justice Clinic at CSU Law, where she gained valuable experience interviewing clients, attending probable cause hearings, and preparing legal motions for the public defender.

Beyond client work, Jennifer is committed to legal education and mentorship, having served as an Academic Excellence Fellow for a contracts course and an Adjunct Instructor for first-year writing at Cleveland State University. She is the mom of two boys and lives with her family in Olmstead Township.

attorneys.name: Lindsay Moretta
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cuyahoga Falls, OH
attorneys.bio:
Lindsay completed her undergraduate studies at Walsh University, earning her B.S. in Education as an Early Childhood Intervention Specialist in 2006. She then attained her Master’s Degree in Special Education from the University of Akron in 2010. Lindsay attended the University of Akron School of Law, part-time while raising a family and working full time, graduating in 2020.

During her time in law school, Lindsay gained valuable experience by taking part in a variety of clinics the University of Akron has to offer. In the Re-Entry Clinic, she provided legal assistance to low-income clients looking to file applications to seal their criminal records, obtain Certificates of Qualification for Employment (CQE), and file clemency applications. She also worked on the Ohio Governor’s Expedited Pardon Project by screening potential pardon candidates and assisting qualified candidates with preparing a pardon petition to the governor. In the Civil Litigation Clinic, she assisted low-income clients who experienced housing problems. She interviewed clients, investigated cases, and prepared and represented clients in court. In the Domestic Relations Clinic, Lindsay handled family law matters in the Portage County Domestic Relations Court by advising clients on matters of dissolution, divorce, custody, and child support. She prepared filings, appeared in court, and participated in hearings via telephonic conference and zoom.

Lindsay had the opportunity to clerk for the City of Akron Prosecutor’s Office. In her capacity as a law clerk, she managed the docket for traffic court, ran traffic bench trials, and provided prosecutor coverage in the various Akron Municipal court rooms.

These experiences provided Lindsay with a vast and unique opportunity to sharpen skills both in and out of the court room, allowing her to effectively represent clients’ interests in many settings.

Lindsay is licensed to practice law in Ohio.

attorneys.name: Joseph A. Moro
attorneys.firm_name: Heller, Maas, Moro & Magill Co., LPA
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Youngstown, OH
attorneys.bio:
The son of a Youngstown steelworker, Atty. Joseph A. Moro is acutely aware of the challenges that working people face and the dire impacts that injuries and impairments can have on them and their families.

"I think I identify with a lot of our clients because of my own background, coming from a blue-collar family," he says.

In addition to being raised in a blue-collar family, Atty. Moro has his own experience working in the steel mills. He spent his summers during his undergraduate college years at Youngstown State University working at Republic Steel Corp. as well as at the General Motors' Lordstown assembly plant.

He knew then that he wanted to be a lawyer, and after getting his B.S. degree from Youngstown University in 1981, he enrolled at the University of Cincinnati College of Law. He received his J.D. there in 1985 and worked for a year in a law firm and another year in the City of Youngstown's Law Department before joining this firm in 1987.

From the start, his practice has focused on workers' compensation claims, but he has also been a trial lawyer handling both workers' compensation appeals and personal injury cases. Over the years, he has obtained a number of favorable jury verdicts on behalf of his clients.

To Atty. Moro, the greatest professional rewards come from being able to help people put their lives back together following oftentimes devastating setbacks.

attorneys.name: Mary Jo Morse
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Mary Jo Morse has over three decades of experience in the practice areas of Estate Planning, Trust Planning, and Trust and Estate Administration. Her educational background in accounting and business has served her clients well in the complexities of estate and asset management as well as tax matters.

Mary Jo served over ten years as a Trust Officer in a local bank Trust Department administering trusts for family and charitable beneficiaries designated in numerous Trust Agreements. Administering the Trust Accounts in every aspect, she developed close personal relationships with her clients as she carried out the terms of the agreements she was entrusted to uphold.

Her undergraduate college degree of a Bachelor’s of Business Administration in Accounting provides a solid foundation for estate and tax planning. She assists her clients in understanding the estate tax effects for their estate plan and for their beneficiaries. Her in-depth knowledge of trust planning helps clients develop the optimal estate plan for their needs. Each family is unique. Each estate plan developed by Mary Jo, whether straightforward or the most complex, is carefully crafted to meet the individual needs of the client.

The loss of a loved one is a difficult and emotional time. Knowing that the attorney can guide a family through the administration of the estate plan that had been personally developed is a comfort. For Mary Jo, it is rewarding to see that the terms of the legal documents established by a client actually fulfill the estate planning goals and needs of the family. Whether through Trust administration or Probate Court Estate Management, Mary Jo assists the family with the orderly distribution of assets.

Mary Jo and her staff provide prompt and professional representation of her clients in the estate and trust planning and estate administration.

attorneys.name: Donald K. Moser
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Fairfield, OH
attorneys.bio:
For over 20 years, I have been living and practicing law in the communities of Butler County Ohio. I truly enjoy being in private practice, dedicating my practice to family law and helping over 2,800 clients in matters related to marriage, family and children. I also represent clients in the areas of wills and estate planning and landlord/tenant matters.

Fully trained and qualified as a collaborative law lawyer in 2002.

I strive to provide every one of my clients with honest, compassionate and effective representation at a reasonable fee. I keep your best interests in mind during every phase of representation.

Butler County is my home and I believe in developing strong communities and supporting the families that are part of my community. I grew up in Butler County and my father was a lawyer for 25 years and a judge for 20, former Butler County Common Pleas Court, Judge John Moser. I am proud of what my dad has accomplished for the community and the Butler County judicial system. I enjoy sharing stories about my dad and the history of the Butler County court system.

In my own professional practice, I am involved in the Butler County Bar Association serving many roles from President (2011-2012) to chairing a number of committees. Currently, I am on the Board of Trustees. In 2013, I received the Professionalism Award from the Butler County Bar Association in recognition of my service to the legal profession as an attorney and community leader.

I also serve as Magistrate in the Fairfield Municipal Court which helps me keep involved with the community, Fairfield, where I live and have my office.

Licensed to practice law in Ohio and the United States Southern Ohio District. Currently, hold inactive licenses for the state of Virginia and Washington DC.

attorneys.name: Donnell Much Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Securities Arbitration Litigation Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Donnell Much (“Don”) is a Senior Attorney with the Firm. He focuses his practice on securities arbitration litigation, general complex litigation, and state and federal court securities litigation.

Before joining Meyer Wilson Werning, Mr. Much worked as Senior Counsel at two major independent broker dealers serving in both litigation and regulatory roles. Previously, Mr. Much worked as a Senior Associate Attorney at a prestigious, boutique law firm in New York City focusing his practice on securities litigation where he handled general and complex commercial litigation; securities arbitration cases filing suit against stockbrokers, broker-dealers, investment advisers, and Investment Adviser Representatives (“IARs”); and Plaintiff side state and federal court Ponzi scheme litigation. Mr. Much has also worked as a Securities Litigation Associate Attorney in the Securities Department of a large, national law firm in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania where he litigated state and federal securities cases and investigated public companies for violations of Section 11 of the Securities Act and Section 10 of the Securities Exchange Act. In addition, Mr. Much has worked at a highly reputable, full-service law firm in Devon, Pennsylvania. Mr. Much has been named a 2019 – 2020 and a 2020 – 2021 Pennsylvania “Rising Star” attorney in the area of securities litigation by Super Lawyers/Rising Stars, an attorney-rating service of Thomson Reuters.

Mr. Much is a 2014 graduate with Distinction of the Georgetown University Law Center’s LLM program, where he concentrated in Securities Regulation. While at Georgetown, Mr. Much worked as an intern at the U.S. Securities & Exchange Commission (“SEC”) in the Division of Enforcement – Market Abuse Unit and in the Division of Trading & Markets. While at Georgetown, Mr. Much also interned at the Commodities Futures Trading Commission (“CFTC”) in the Office of the General Counsel. Mr. Much is a 2008 graduate of Loyola New Orleans College of Law in New Orleans, Louisiana. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Much received his MBA from Saint Joseph’s University in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania where he concentrated in financial statement analysis. Prior to attending law school, Mr. Much worked as a Senior Consultant for a “big-four” accounting firm focusing his consulting practice in the areas of alternative funds and mutual funds. Mr. Much is a 2003 graduate of the University of Vermont, where he received his Bachelor of Arts degree.

Mr. Much is a member of the Delaware County Bar Association and the Delaware County Inn of Court.

Mr. Much is also a certified Sommelier by the Wine School of Philadelphia.

attorneys.name: Victoria Munson
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cuyahoga Falls, OH
attorneys.bio:
Tori graduated from the University of Akron in 2012 with her associate degree in criminal justice technology. She then attended the University of Toledo where she earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice in 2014. Tori continued her studies at the University of Toledo, where she earned her juris doctor with the University of Toledo College of Law in 2017.

Following her admission to the Ohio Bar in 2017, Tori spent three years as a staff attorney with the Stark County Public Defender, where she represented juveniles who were accused of committing delinquent acts, parents whose rights were challenged by the children services agency, and adults who were accused of misdemeanor crimes.

Tori took a break from criminal work to enhance her family law skills when she worked for a small law firm learning all the ins and outs of divorce/dissolution, custody, and other family law matters.

Tori is a qualified mediator as well as a parent coordinator.

Tori grew up in Barberton, Ohio, and in her free time she enjoys traveling, spending time with her wife and four dogs, and attempting to practice yoga.

attorneys.name: Leslie O. Murray
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Sandusky, OH
attorneys.bio:
There is nothing more satisfying than achieving a just result for my clients. It is an honor for me to spend my days working for people who otherwise may have no voice and no way to secure their rights. That is why we fight for justice for all people, including the most underserved among us.

I started my career in West Africa to implement the most basic human rights and rules of law. We can never forget the work we have done in our country to provide access to justice for all who need it. We must continue to work toward a more equal playing field where the strongest and richest do not win by default, simply as a result of their positions of power.

When I see a wrong, I believe it needs to be righted. That is why I practice law.

Leslie Murray: Leslie's background spans from graduating from the Case Western Reserve University Law School, to serving with the United Nations Mission in Liberia - Department of Peacekeeping Operations and the Office of the Prosecutor for the Special Court for Sierra Leone. She is past President of the Board of the Boys and Girls Club of North East Ohio and serves on numerous other boards in the community including the Sandusky State Theatre. She is also a native Sanduskian and attended Sandusky Central Catholic School.
