attorneys.name: Zachary J. Murry
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Maumee, OH
attorneys.bio:
Zachary J. Murry joined Barkan & Robon, Ltd. as an Associate in June, 2014. Zach was named a Partner in January, 2017. Zach is a graduate of Evergreen High School in Metamora, OH. He received his Bachelor of Arts degree in English from the Ohio State University. Zach earned his Juris Doctor from the Catholic University America, Columbus School of Law in Washington, DC in 2007. He is licensed to practice as an attorney in the States of Michigan and Maryland as well as in Ohio.

Zach has broad experience in representing businesses and individuals in a variety of legal matters. Focusing on business law and commercial litigation, Zach and Barkan & Robon, Ltd. have represented business and contractors in numerous litigation and arbitration proceedings along with providing representation and counseling in non-litigation matters including contract negotiations and litigation, labor and employment issues, EEOC and OCRC claims, trade secrets, and business formation and valuation. Zach has also served as litigation and arbitration counsel for Taft-Hartley Plans on ERISA issues encompassing fiduciary obligations and the appropriate investment and management of Plan assets.

Zach has represented numerous property owners in Eminent Domain proceedings. He aggressively represents property owners at both negotiation and trial proceedings to secure appropriate compensation for taken land. Zach also works to protect the rights of accident victims and persons injured as a result of defective products.

Zach is a member of numerous legal organizations including the American Bar Association, Federal Bar Association, Ohio State Bar Association, State Bar of Michigan, Toledo Bar Association, Ohio Association for Justice, Fulton County Bar Association and the American Association for Justice.

attorneys.name: Chandra M. Muster
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law/Domestic Relations Lawyers in Green, OH
attorneys.bio:
As a lifelong resident of Summit County, Ohio and a graduate of Manchester High School, Chandra earned her B.A. Magna Cum Laude in criminal justice and psychology from Baldwin Wallace College. While at Baldwin Wallace, Chandra found her love of law while interning at the Cuyahoga County Prosecutor’s Office. She earned her J.D. Cum Laude from the Cleveland Marshall College of Law in 2007.

After graduating law school, Chandra immediately began running a successful practice when she took over for her mentor William E. Howard, when he retired at the end of 2017. January 1, 2018, Howard, Muster, & Associates began. While engaging in solo practice, Chandra handled a multitude of legal matters, including but not limited to domestic, juvenile, criminal, landlord tenant, and bankruptcy cases. Chandra also worked as a Guardian ad Litem in the Summit County Court from 2010 – 2023.

Being at Melissa Graham-Hurd & Associates will allow Chandra to immerse herself again in domestic relations practice and gives Chandra an opportunity to guide clients through sometimes complex legal matters with caring and heart.

Chandra is a member of the Akron Bar Association and the Ohio Bar Association. She is also licensed to practice in the Northern District of Ohio, Federal Court. Chandra was recently certified as a Parent Coordinator.

In her spare time, Chandra enjoys spending time with family, her dogs, and reading.

Specialties and Certifications

Parent Coordination, 2023

attorneys.bio:
I was born in Birmingham, Michigan on August 17, 1961. I attended Youngstown State University, graduating in 1983 with degrees in Economics and Political Science. I went to law school at Ohio Northern University and received my law degree in 1987. Prior to joining Slater and Zurz LLP, I served as the Assistant City of Findlay, Ohio Law Director and Assistant Hancock County, Ohio Prosecutor. I was also in private practice while in Findlay.

I also invite you to contact me for a free consultation by calling me at the telephone number listed above our sending me a message to schedule a time to talk at your convenience. Spending a few minutes on the telephone with me may provide you with the answers you are looking for and calm your anxieties.

Like all the attorneys at Slater and Zurz LLP, I am focused on getting results for my clients while providing them with unparalleled service. I will respond to your questions promptly, provide you with complete explanations that are easy to understand and cover all options under the law. I will also thoroughly prepare and aggressively pursue your case to achieve the results you desire. By doing this, we will be able to effectively settle your case without the need for trial. In the event that a trial is necessary, I have extensive trial experience with a proven record of success.

My father's dream was to be a lawyer. He attended Harvard Law School but joined the U.S. Army during World War II and was never able to finish his legal education. I originally became a lawyer to fulfill my father’s dreams. However, my career is about so much more than that. I take great pride and satisfaction in helping others resolve their legal issues.

attorneys.bio:
Gage has represented clients in a variety of matters in state and federal trial courts throughout Ohio, the Ohio Courts of Appeal, the Ohio Supreme Court, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court. Gage has a practice focused on complex commercial and tort litigation, with an emphasis in appellate advocacy.

In 2012, Gage was victorious in the Ohio Supreme Court on behalf of the Knox County Commissioners and the County Risk Sharing Authority, in a case in which the Ohio Supreme Court held that the Ohio Constitution allows the use of motor vehicle and gas tax (MVGT) revenues to pay the portion of the county's insurance premium covering the county engineer's highway department. The Court's unanimous (7-0) decision reversed the Court of Appeals and effectively overruled the results of a prior 2006 decision. In that same year, Gage was part of the legal team that won a hard-fought appeal in the Sixth Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in favor of Columbus-based shoe retailer, DSW Inc -- a victory that resulted in an award of over $7.1 million against National Union Fire Insurance Company of Pittsburgh, PA. 2009, Gage was the lead counsel representing the Ohio Grocers Association in the Ohio Supreme Court in a constitutional challenge to Ohio's commercial activities tax, a case Columbus Business First called "one of [the court's] most important cases of the year." In 2010, Gage represented retail natural gas suppliers in the United States Supreme Court in a constitutional challenge to Ohio's taxation of natural gas sales. Gage has represented numerous clients in amicus briefs to the Ohio Supreme Court including three former Ohio attorneys general in an amicus brief to the Ohio Supreme Court in 2010 relating to the power and authority of the attorney general to represent the state of Ohio in matters pending before the courts. Gage has represented plaintiffs in high-profile defamation cases at both the trial and appellate level.

In 2012, Gage was designated a Best Lawyers® for Appellate Advocacy, and in 2019, was awarded Appellate Practice "Lawyer of the Year" for Columbus, Ohio. Prior to joining Arnold & Clifford in May 2011, Gage was a partner at the Columbus law firm of Chester Willcox & Saxbe LLP in their litigation section. He began his legal career in 1995, when he joined the Columbus office of Jones Day. Gage served four years as a judicial law clerk for Judge Cynthia Lazarus on the Ohio Tenth District Court of Appeals.

attorneys.name: Madilyn Maruna
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Madilyn (Madi) Maruna is a Shareholder at Cavitch Familo & Durkin, focusing her practice in the areas of employment and commercial litigation. Madi is uniquely positioned to represent both closely held businesses as well as employees in matters regarding Title VII (employment discrimination and retaliation), the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA), the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), and Ohio Revised Code 4112. With experience representing both employers and employees, Madi has gained a unique litigation perspective that allows her to offer creative solutions for her clients. She also has significant experience representing closely held businesses and individuals in non-compete matters, class/collective actions, commercial litigation, contract disputes, probate litigation, partnership disputes, and real estate disputes.

Her experience also includes regularly representing employers in administrative investigations and proceedings involving the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), the Ohio Civil Rights Commission (OCRC), the Department of Labor (DOL), the Ohio Department of Commerce (Wage and Hour Division), the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services (ODJFS – Ohio Unemployment), and other administrative agencies.

Madi spends much of her time counseling clients to keep them out of litigation by drafting comprehensive employment agreements, non-compete and non-solicitation agreements, policies and agreements to protect confidential information and trade secrets, as well as employee handbooks and operating policies.

Madi earned her Juris Doctor from Cleveland-Marshall College of Law, magna cum laude, and her undergraduate degree in Marketing, cum laude, with a minor in Entrepreneurship, from John Carroll University. Before law school, Madi worked for a financial compliance firm in Cleveland, Ohio, and a China-based manufacturer. Throughout law school, Madi was a member of Cleveland-Marshall’s flagship law review journal and externed for the Cleveland-Marshall Civil Litigation Clinic, where she assisted with representing clients in immigration and unemployment matters. Madi also served as a law clerk for Jackson Lewis, P.C., and Tittle & Perlmuter.

Giving back to the Cleveland community is important to Madi. She volunteers her time as the President of the Cleveland chapter of the Salvation Army’s young professional group, Echelon. She also serves on the National Echelon Leadership Council, which oversees all Echelon chapters nationally. Madi is a dog lover and a board member of One Health Organization, an organization promoting the human/animal connection by providing veterinary vouchers to low-income pet parents in Northeast Ohio. She is also very involved with the Cleveland Animal Protective League. In her spare time, Madi enjoys spending time with family, practicing yoga, cooking, and relaxing with her dogs, Hendrix and Intro.

attorneys.name: Gerhardt "Gage" Gosnell II
attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Gage has represented clients in a variety of matters in state and federal trial courts throughout Ohio, the Ohio Courts of Appeal, the Ohio Supreme Court, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, and the United States Supreme Court. Gage has a practice focused on complex commercial and tort litigation, with an emphasis in appellate advocacy.

In 2012, Gage was victorious in the Ohio Supreme Court on behalf of the Knox County Commissioners and the County Risk Sharing Authority, in a case in which the Ohio Supreme Court held that the Ohio Constitution allows the use of motor vehicle and gas tax (MVGT) revenues to pay the portion of the county's insurance premium covering the county engineer's highway department. The Court's unanimous (7-0) decision reversed the Court of Appeals and effectively overruled the results of a prior 2006 decision. In that same year, Gage was part of the legal team that won a hard-fought appeal in the Sixth Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals in favor of Columbus-based shoe retailer, DSW Inc -- a victory that resulted in an award of over $7.1 million against National Union Fire Insurance Company of Pittsburgh, PA. 2009, Gage was the lead counsel representing the Ohio Grocers Association in the Ohio Supreme Court in a constitutional challenge to Ohio's commercial activities tax, a case Columbus Business First called "one of [the court's] most important cases of the year." In 2010, Gage represented retail natural gas suppliers in the United States Supreme Court in a constitutional challenge to Ohio's taxation of natural gas sales. Gage has represented numerous clients in amicus briefs to the Ohio Supreme Court including three former Ohio attorneys general in an amicus brief to the Ohio Supreme Court in 2010 relating to the power and authority of the attorney general to represent the state of Ohio in matters pending before the courts. Gage has represented plaintiffs in high-profile defamation cases at both the trial and appellate level.

In 2012, Gage was designated a Best Lawyers® for Appellate Advocacy, and in 2019, was awarded Appellate Practice "Lawyer of the Year" for Columbus, Ohio. Prior to joining Arnold & Clifford in May 2011, Gage was a partner at the Columbus law firm of Chester Willcox & Saxbe LLP in their litigation section. He began his legal career in 1995, when he joined the Columbus office of Jones Day. Gage served four years as a judicial law clerk for Judge Cynthia Lazarus on the Ohio Tenth District Court of Appeals.

attorneys.bio:
I was born in Birmingham, Michigan on August 17, 1961. I attended Youngstown State University, graduating in 1983 with degrees in Economics and Political Science. I went to law school at Ohio Northern University and received my law degree in 1987. Prior to joining Slater and Zurz LLP, I served as the Assistant City of Findlay, Ohio Law Director and Assistant Hancock County, Ohio Prosecutor. I was also in private practice while in Findlay.

I also invite you to contact me for a free consultation by calling me at the telephone number listed above our sending me a message to schedule a time to talk at your convenience. Spending a few minutes on the telephone with me may provide you with the answers you are looking for and calm your anxieties.

Like all the attorneys at Slater and Zurz LLP, I am focused on getting results for my clients while providing them with unparalleled service. I will respond to your questions promptly, provide you with complete explanations that are easy to understand and cover all options under the law. I will also thoroughly prepare and aggressively pursue your case to achieve the results you desire. By doing this, we will be able to effectively settle your case without the need for trial. In the event that a trial is necessary, I have extensive trial experience with a proven record of success.

My father's dream was to be a lawyer. He attended Harvard Law School but joined the U.S. Army during World War II and was never able to finish his legal education. I originally became a lawyer to fulfill my father’s dreams. However, my career is about so much more than that. I take great pride and satisfaction in helping others resolve their legal issues.

attorneys.name: David E. Nager
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Making Ohio a Safer Place for Workers by Founding the State’s Largest Workers’ Compensation Law Firm

David E. Nager is the Founding Attorney of Nager, Romaine & Schneiberg Co., L.P.A. (NRS Injury Law). After joining a personal injury law firm in 1990 and becoming a partner in 1995, David opened his own law firm in 1999. In 2004, along with Dan Romaine and Jerald Schneiberg, David formed NRS Injury Law. David launched the firm with the goal of one day managing the largest workers’ compensation law firm in Ohio. David achieved this goal, and he credits service, compassion, empathy, and fierce loyalty to his clients and co-counsel as the values that helped him get there.

A Background Built on Service

“I remember when I delivered that first newspaper, I realized I was doing something meaningful in service to others,” David said when asked to describe his work background. “It taught me from a very young age how to run a business, be organized, and serve others.”

At age 10, David was spending his mornings going out at 5:30 a.m. to deliver Cleveland’s Plain Dealer newspaper to residents in his community. By age twelve, he was cutting lawns for a local landscaping company for $1.90 an hour and working 50 hours per week during the summer. “Our kids don’t believe us,” David said, referring to the stories he and his brother tell their adult children. “They’ve never heard of kids that age working odd jobs to help make ends meet. But that’s what we did.”

David learned two life-changing lessons at a young age. One was the importance of work ethic combined with good business practices. The other was the value of service. “My most memorable childhood job was selling flowers on street corners during holidays,” David said. “A friend of my father’s would set us up with several bouquets of flowers and my brother and I would stand on a street corner in Detroit and sell them to folks going to Memorial Day and Veterans Day services. Seeing the effects those flowers had on people during meaningful and sometimes emotional moments had an impact on us, as well.”

Entering Law

Most attorneys say their interest in law began early on, from watching iconic lawyer films or having an attorney in the family. But that’s not how David became interested in the profession. Though his father had always wanted him to become an attorney, David was a criminal justice major at Kent State from 1982 through 1987 with aspirations of becoming a police officer and serving his community that way. In his last year at Kent State, the University’s dean took David aside and convinced him to take the LSAT and consider law school.

“From there on, there was no looking back,” said David. He attended law school at Cleveland-Marshall College of Law while also managing a pizza parlor. While still in his first year at Cleveland-Marshall, David added a second job clerking at a workers’ compensation law firm so he could pay the bills. David took the bar and passed it in 1990. “I simply had to pass the bar that year,” recalls David. His wife Ellen was pregnant with their first child, and David had to pass the bar in order to support his growing family.

Shortly after David passed the bar and became an associate attorney at the firm he’d clerked for, his father experienced a horrific work injury that permanently changed his life. David successfully represented him in securing workers’ compensation benefits. “My parents almost lost everything because of that injury,” David said. “But I was able to get them benefits which enabled them to hold onto their house and keep their heads above water. The experience made me want to keep doing workers’ compensation for the thousands of other Ohioans I knew were getting hurt on the job every year.”

Constructing the Core Tenants of NRS Injury Law

“You tend to grow into what you’ve grown from,” David said when asked to describe the core tenants of NRS Injury Law. Then he listed them out, emphasizing each. “We’re about Knowledge, Experience, Service, Size, and a willingness to Litigate,” David said. “Our Knowledge base from the sheer Size of our client roll combined with our Experience winning thousands of cases every year since 2004 and our willingness to Litigate when others won’t means we have the edge needed to secure the results our clients need.”

“But most importantly, it’s about Service,” David concluded. “Many attorneys act like they sit on a throne. But I’ve always just wanted to be a man of the people, and I hire attorneys who have that same value. We’re all in this together, so we may as well treat each other with dignity and respect. We may as well serve one another, because in so doing we’re leaving this world a lot better than we found it.”

Making Ohio a Safer State for Workers

David Nager’s list of career accomplishments is long and storied. In addition to founding and growing the largest workers’ compensation law firm in the history of Ohio, David has personally helped thousands of injured workers obtain compensation and medical benefits. He’s successfully argued cases before every level of the Industrial Commission of Ohio, and he’s won cases at the Trial Level and all State Appellate Levels up to and including the Ohio Supreme Court. He’s secured compensation and medical benefits for his clients totaling hundreds of millions of dollars.

David has actively worked to improve the landscape in which injured workers seek compensation. David served on the Bureau of Workers’ Compensation (BWC) Nominating Committee, holding a central role dedicated to nominating individuals for the BWC’s Executive Board. David spent years meeting with BWC leadership to help direct the agency towards pro-worker policies that benefit injured workers in Ohio. David is involved in several organizations statewide and nationally that represent injured workers.

Community Involvement

Core to David’s ethos is a commitment to community, a lifestyle choice manifested in David’s frequent volunteer activities. David volunteers at the Cleveland Food Bank and local shelters, and he frequently hosts donation drives for hospitals and adopts families during the holidays. He also hosted the firm’s annual turkey giveaway during Thanksgiving. David has coached and sponsored multiple youth and adult sports programs, including The Miracle League, a baseball program for children and adults with serious physical and mental disabilities.

Work/Life Balance

David has been active in sports since his childhood. As an adult, he became a two-time state racquetball champion and a member of several nationally ranked men’s softball and hardball teams. When he’s not working, playing sports, or visiting his adult children, David can often be found working out in the gym, riding his bike, or going on long walks in his Cleveland neighborhood or traveling with his beloved wife of 30+ years and their three dogs.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from David Nager

Having built NRS Injury Law from the ground up, David Nager exemplifies the firm’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with David and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 (855-GOT-HURT) or fill out a convenient online contact form.

attorneys.name: Wesley Matthew Nakajima
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - General Lawyers in Lebanon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Matt Nakajima is a trial lawyer who stands with individuals and families touched by tragedy. After a catastrophic injury or the loss of a loved one, people are often left searching for answers, stability, and someone they can trust. Matt helps guide them through that uncertainty while holding those responsible accountable.

For nearly two decades, he has represented clients whose lives were permanently changed by negligence and corporate misconduct, taking on large corporations and insurance companies that refuse to accept responsibility. Matt understands that no amount of money can undo what has been taken—but he believes accountability and justice matter, both for his clients and for the safety of others.

Matt focuses his practice on catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases, including trucking and car collisions, defective products, insurance bad faith, and dangerous premises claims. He is known for meticulous preparation, creative trial strategy, and genuine, compassionate advocacy for the people he represents. Insurance companies know him as a lawyer who is prepared to take cases to trial when fairness is refused.

Throughout his career, Matt has secured more than forty verdicts and settlements of $1 million or more. Since 2025 alone, he has recovered over $100 million for his clients, including results of $28 million, $12 million, $11.25 million, and $11 million. Several of these cases have resulted in nationwide safety changes, particularly in corporate negligence and trucking collision cases—helping prevent similar harm to others.

Many of Matt’s cases are ones others considered too difficult or unwinnable. When insurance companies refuse to make fair settlement offers, Matt is known for obtaining extraordinary results:

• $6,000,000 jury verdict (2025) in a medical negligence case after the defense refused to make any settlement offer;

• $825,000 jury verdict (2021) in a disputed car crash case where the highest offer was $90,000;

• $3,000,000 jury verdict (2019) in a trip-and-fall case involving a fractured kneecap, after a pre-trial offer of $25,000;

• $1,028,317 jury verdict (2018) after rejecting a $20,000 offer for a serious shoulder injury.

Because of his courtroom experience and results, Matt is frequently invited to speak to trial lawyer organizations across the country on trial advocacy and litigation strategy. He has been recognized by his peers as a Super Lawyer and/or Rising Star every year since 2013.

Above all, Matt stands with his clients when it matters most—giving them a voice, standing up to powerful corporations, and securing results that help families move forward.

attorneys.name: Dominick Nardozzi
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Leveraging a Detail-Focused, Strategic Approach to Securing Results for Workers’ Compensation Clients

Dominick Nardozzi is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Highly methodical in his practice, Dominick secures results for clients by leaving no details uncovered and no avenue to victory unexplored.

A First-Generation Attorney Committed to Defending Injured Ohioans

Though no one in his immediate or extended family had ever practiced law, Dominick knew he wanted to be an attorney since age seven. “I’m a first generation attorney, and a first gen college graduate,” Dominick said, reflecting on the early years of his life that shaped his career path. “With my early years spent in a disadvantaged household led by a single mother, I experienced firsthand the injustices of larger systems designed to keep us down. I knew from an early age I wanted to pursue a career that would give me the tools to help families like ours.”

Dominick entered the workforce at age 15, diving headfirst into various working-class roles in the service industry and retail. Dominick worked through high school, undergrad, and law school, intent on providing for his family and their future. While studying at Bowling Green State University, Dominick’s affable character, superior communication skills, and detail-oriented mind secured him employment in the university’s IT department, a role he excelled at for several years before making the leap into law school.

A Commitment to the Details and a Willingness to Present Them in Court

“The details are everything,” Dominick says, laying out his approach to lawyering. “Growing up, it became clear to me that bureaucratic systems are made so overly complex that it’s difficult to get ahead, in everything from health insurance to student loans to food stamps to workplace injuries. The only way to beat these systems and win for clients is to become a master of the details, which is what I’ve aimed to do as a workers’ compensation attorney.”

Highly motivated and ambitious, Dominick is a fast learner, quickly sorting the details of a case into a nuanced legal strategy that will secure the best value possible for a client’s claim. The approach is smooth and calculating on the surface, but on a deeper level, Dominick’s commitment to his clients is driven by his fierce loyalty to working-class Ohioans who’ve been injured in the line of work and are now up against powerful insurance companies and complex bureaucratic institutions.

Work/Life Balance

Podcasts, cooking, reading, writing fiction, Dungeons & Dragons campaigns with friends, whenever Dominick isn’t practicing law, he’s actively engaged in other activities that stimulate his mind and keep his brain performing at peak efficiency. But not every day can be dedicated to cognitive fitness, and on the weekends, Dominick can usually be found hiking around Ohio’s parks and trails. He’s also fast becoming a big Ohio sports fan, and he’ll never say no to a snuggle session on the couch with his orange cat, Leo.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Dominick Nardozzi

Dominick Nardozzi joined NRS Injury Law in December 2023 with the intent to leverage his unique legal skills and his relentless commitment to helping others. Loyal to his core, brilliantly methodical and detail-minded, and always willing to go to bat for his clients, Dominick’s approach to workers’ compensation law aligns perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Dominick and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Dominick’s commitment to his community aligns perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to give back and be a part of the rising tide that lifts all boats in Ohio and beyond. When he’s not working, Dominick volunteers in a choir group that sings at nursing homes and local community events. Highly organized and a big planner, Dominick is also setting his sights on running for public office, starting with the school board and city council and with aspirations of melding his legal career with political advocacy on the state level.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey Nash
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Law Lawyers in Beachwood, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jeff Nash received a Bachelor of Science degree in 1980, and a Juris Doctor degree in 1984. He is admitted to the practice of law in the state of Ohio and Georgia and admitted to practice in the federal courts.

After gaining experience with a general practice law firm handling business and litigation matters, Jeff joined The Progressive Corporation in August, 1985, shortly before Progressive’s rapid growth to the third largest auto insurance company in the United States. Jeff initially managed this national carrier’s claims litigation, coverage and complex casualty matters for a 10-state region. In 1994, Jeff was selected to develop and lead a national approach to the management of policy drafting, regulatory relationships, speed-to-market product strategy, and regulatory compliance, in order to minimize and defend against market conduct violations, bad faith and class action risks, and to improve the brand image of the company as reflected by its policy, coverage and written communication to insured’s. This practice group within the Law Department grew to a team of 19 professionals under Jeff’s leadership, managing all forms, forms compliance and filings. In January 2003, Jeff left Progressive and formed The Nash Group, which has grown and thrived, providing a broad range of services from developing and managing insurance regulatory relationships, to product development, forms drafting, rule manual development and insurance regulatory compliance management.

Jeff is a valued resource used by insurance product management and marketing executives from many large national insurance companies, as well as some small regional companies focused on growth. He is well-acquainted with key staff in virtually every state insurance department and has extensive knowledge of insurance regulatory requirements, rating and rule restrictions, forms compliance requirements, and the fastest path to getting insurance products from concept to implementation. Recently, Jeff has become part of the leadership team of multiple insureTech start-ups.

Jeff is an experienced attorney with more than 20 years working with corporate law departments and chief legal officers of major insurance companies to supplement their working staff when they have need for additional experience and resources to meet their business objectives and service level. While Jeff maintains a national practice for the insurance industry, he also continues to advise small and medium size businesses planning for growth, with recent experience assisting small companies acquiring other business lines.

attorneys.name: Todd B. Naylor
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Todd's practice areas primarily include class actions, insurance litigation, products liability, antitrust litigation, toxic and environmental torts, personal injury, and wrongful death. He has appeared as lead counsel in courts across the United States representing clients at all stages of litigation and has lectured on various aspects of the legal profession at numerous seminars and at the University of Cincinnati College of Law.

Todd frequently represents large classes and entities. He represented the State of Ohio in a securities lawsuit relating to the merger of Exxon and Mobil. He has also represented multiple states, including Connecticut, in pharmaceutical pricing litigation. Todd served on the trial team in antitrust litigation involving the oriented strand board industry that resulted in an aggregate settlement of over $120,000,000. Additionally, Todd has served as lead counsel in multiple life insurance cases in which he has obtained contested class certification, ultimately resolving the cases for millions of dollars. One such case was filed on behalf of beneficiaries of the Federal Employees Group Life Insurance (FEGLI) Policy, the world's largest group life insurance program. Todd presently serves as lead and/or co-counsel in numerous multi-million dollar complex civil litigation cases throughout the State of Ohio and nationwide.

Todd has also represented many individuals in high-value litigation involving severe personal injuries and wrongful death. He recently acted as lead counsel in a case against the Montgomery County, Ohio dog warden for the warden's alleged failure to act to prevent the fatal mauling of a Dayton resident. The multi-million dollar settlement of that case, following Plaintiff's defeat of the Dog Warden's motion for summary judgment, is believed to be the largest settlement ever against an animal control agency. Todd also recently obtained a $10.3 million verdict against Ethicon for the alleged failure of one its surgical staplers to function as intended during a bowel resection. He then successfully defended the appeal of that verdict before the Second District Court of Appeals.

Todd is admitted to practice in the State of Ohio, the United States Supreme Court, the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, and the United States District Court for the Southern and Northern Districts of Ohio. He serves as an Attorney Mediator for the Southern District of Ohio, and an Arbitrator for the Clermont County Common Pleas Court and the Cincinnati Bar Association Fee Arbitration Committee. Todd is a Fellow with the Cincinnati Academy of Leadership for Lawyers.

attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Mike's legal practice is focused on representing investors and developers in a broad range of real estate matters, including acquisitions, developments, dispositions, commercial leasing, litigation, and opportunity zone consulting. Mike has experience representing clients in residential and commercial transactions, with a focus on representing clients in the acquisition of multi-family apartment properties. Since 2019, Mike has structured and closed over $1B in real estate transactions throughout the country. Mike regularly works with real estate partnerships by discussing the partners' goals before helping with the formation of their entity with all the necessary organizational documents. Mike then provides legal guidance through every step of the acquisition process, by assisting in the negotiation of purchase and sale agreements, due diligence review, and closing coordination.

Originally a native of Cleveland, Ohio, Mike moved to Columbus in 2012 where he attended Ohio State's Fisher College of Business and Capital University Law School. During his time at Capital, Mike participated in public service through two externships with the Ohio State Supreme Court and the United States District Court for the Souther District of Ohio. Mike was also the President of the Corporate and Business Law Society and awarded the Ohio State Bar Association's Real Property Section Scholarship. Mike is also an Ohio licensed title insurance agent.

Mike believes in making his community a better place and is an investor and developer of real estate with a focus on developing multi-family assets within Columbus' opportunity zones. Mike currently manages a growing real estate portfolio valued at over $20M, with an emphasis on acquiring multifamily complexes in the 40-100-unit range in the Midwest.

Mike has experience representing clients in residential and commercial transactions, with a focus on representing clients in the acquisition of multi-family apartment properties. Since 2019, Mike has structured and closed over $1B in real estate transactions throughout the country. Mike regularly works with real estate partnerships by discussing the partners' goals before helping with the formation of their entity with all the necessary organizational documents. Mike then provides legal guidance through every step of the acquisition process, by assisting in the negotiation of purchase and sale agreements, due diligence review, and closing coordination.

Originally a native of Cleveland, Ohio, Mike moved to Columbus in 2012 where he attended Ohio State's Fisher College of Business and Capital University Law School. During his time at Capital, Mike participated in public service through two externships with the Ohio State Supreme Court and the United States District Court for the Souther District of Ohio. Mike was also the President of the Corporate and Business Law Society and awarded the Ohio State Bar Association's Real Property Section Scholarship. Mike is also an Ohio licensed title insurance agent.

Mike believes in making his community a better place and is an investor and developer of real estate with a focus on developing multi-family assets within Columbus' opportunity zones. Mike currently manages a growing real estate portfolio valued at over $20M, with an emphasis on acquiring multifamily complexes in the 40-100-unit range in the Midwest.

attorneys.bio:
Born and raised in Cincinnati and a graduate of Wittenberg University (BA Psych/Poli Sci) and the University of Cincinnati (JD). Previous trial experience includes over 150 juries, including but not limited to aggravated murder, rape, arson, insurance fraud, burglary, robbery, domestic violence, aggravated vehicular homicide and literally over a thousand OVIs. I have two daughters, one of whom is a recent college graduate while the other is a junior at Loyola of Chicago. I live in Clifton with my wife, two dogs and two cats.

attorneys.bio:
Will Nesbitt — Top Criminal Defense Lawyer in Columbus, Ohio Will Nesbitt is an experienced and highly respected criminal defense attorney based in Columbus, Ohio, with over two decades of proven success defending clients throughout Central Ohio and across the state. Recognized as an Ohio Super Lawyer and one of Columbus Business First’s Top Lawyers, Will has built a reputation for strategic advocacy, sound judgment, and consistently favorable outcomes in complex criminal cases. Will’s practice focuses on DUI/OVI defense, domestic violence, federal criminal charges, theft, and serious felony cases. He has successfully obtained acquittals, dismissals, charge reductions, and significant sentence mitigations in both state and federal courts. A respected educator and legal authority, Will has taught at the Ohio Peace Officer Training Academy (OPOTA), the Columbus Division of Police, and numerous Continuing Legal Education (CLE) programs across Ohio. He also served as President of the Central Ohio Association for Justice (COAJ), the region’s leading trial lawyers’ organization.

Will Nesbitt is widely regarded for his experience, professionalism, and unwavering commitment to protecting the rights of the accused. His record reflects not only courtroom excellence but also a deep understanding of Ohio’s criminal justice system — from local municipal courts to federal jurisdictions.

attorneys.name: Rob A. Nestico
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Fairlawn, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Nestico has long had an interest in personal injury law. At the age of 15, he was injured in a car crash when another driver failed to stop an intersection resulting in a head-on collision with another vehicle, killing the other driver. Due to the incident, Nestico spent three months in the hospital recovering from injuries to both arms, one requiring a steel rod to be surgically attached.

During this time, Nestico says he and his family were vulnerable to the practices of insurance companies and were taken advantage of during one of the most difficult times in their lives. Thus, Nestico's passion for personal injury law had manifest and led him to become a personal injury lawyer.

Attorney Nestico received a Bachelor of Arts degree in 1990 and a Specialized Honors of Political Science in 1992, both from York University. He received his Juris Doctor of Law degree, graduating in the top five percent of his class and with honors, from Touro Law School in New York in 1999. During his time at Touro, Nestico completed two internships, one with a state judge and one with a federal judge. He then attended The University of Akron School of Law in Akron, Ohio, as a visiting student, where he still practices law today.

Nestico began his professional law experience with an insurance defense firm before switching to the plaintiff-side of personal injury. In 2005, along with Attorneys Kisling and Redick, Nestico became a founding partner of Kisling, Nestico & Redick, LLC. KNR has since grown from three to 26 lawyers, five to over 100 support staff, and have offices all throughout the state of Ohio.

Attorney Nestico has successfully tried cases to verdict and argued cases before the Ohio Supreme Court and 6th District Court of Appeals. He has represented over 200,000 clients in a class-action suit recovering over $27.5 million dollars and is a member of The Million Dollar Advocates Forum - an honor less than one percent of U.S. attorneys can claim. He has been recognized as a Rising Star and Super Lawyer several times by Super Lawyers Magazine and has also been voted as a Top 100 Trial Lawyer. Attorney Nestico is admitted to practice law in multiple Ohio courts and the U.S. Supreme Court and is trilingual in English, French, and Italian. He focuses his practice on personal injury and class-action lawsuits.

Attorney Nestico is a first generation American-Italian as both of his parents hail from Calabria, Italy. He lives in Summit County with his wife, Patricia, and their three children.

attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability and SSI Lawyers in Maumee, OH
attorneys.bio:
My name is David Newcomb. I am a Social Security Disability attorney, who prides himself on his accessibility to his clients. I'm not part of a national, faceless firm. I am locally based in Maumee, Ohio, which is a suburb of the Toledo, Ohio area. I'm available by appointment, to anyone who wants to come in and meet me. If the Toledo area is too far of a drive for you, I am willing to travel to my clients. Give me a call and we can work something out.

I am a true solo practice attorney. When you call my phone, you get to speak to me, not an answering service or a paralegal. When you call the attorney, you get the attorney. That is a point of pride for me, and to my business. I strive to achieve consistent availability for all my clients and perspective clients.

I have been representing Social Security Disability claimants since 2018. I started working in firms for other attorneys. As of July 2021, I have founded my own practice. Now, I am not only the attorney, but also the firm owner.

I look forward to hearing from you. Give me a call today. Let's talk about your case.

attorneys.name: Mark L. Newman
attorneys.firm_name: Mark L. Newman Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ compensation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Since 1989, Mark Newman has devoted his practice to helping injured and disabled individuals pursue claims related to workers' compensation, social security disability, and personal injury. As a result of his focus and dedication to these areas of law, Mark has developed a reputation for getting results for his clients in a timely and cost effective manner.

As a Cincinnati workers' compensation lawyer representing injured workers for 30 years, Mark has developed an understanding of the Ohio workers' compensation system allowing him to achieve results for his clients without exposing his clients to the complex and bureaucratic workers' compensation system.

Over his 30 years of representing injured workers and appearing before the Industrial Commission of Ohio on behalf of his clients, Mark has successfully obtained benefits for his clients including temporary total, permanent partial, wage loss, permanent total disability, and settlements.

In the area of social security disability benefits, Mark helps individuals navigate through the process of filing a claim and gathering the evidence necessary to have a successful outcome at the hearings. Mark understands that the process of filing a claim can be lengthy and wearisome. Mark and his team gives each client the personal attention and support they need through the process in order to keep them informed and ease their mind

Combining personalized service and insightful advice, Mark has been recognized by his peers as an Ohio Super Lawyer in 2006, 2011 and annually since 2015.

Mark grew up in Cincinnati and is very active in his community. He is President of the Isaac M. Wise Temple Brotherhood, and a board member of the University of Cincinnati Hillel. He also serves on the Operation Give Back finance committee. In the past he servesd as President of Sycamore Athletic Club, Youth Basketball Organization, and a member of the Board of Directors of the Mayerson JCC. Mark is married and has two young sons. He also coaches many youth sports teams including basketball, baseball, and soccer.

attorneys.bio:
Joseph A. Nigh, Esq.

Founder, The Nigh Law Group

Joseph A. Nigh is the founder of The Nigh Law Group and a highly regarded family law attorney based in Columbus, Ohio. Before establishing NLG in 2016, he served as a partner at two other Columbus law firms. Under his leadership, The Nigh Law Group has been recognized in the area of family law, including as a top-three finisher in Columbus CEO Magazine’s “Best in Business” for family law, listed in Best Lawyers in America, and named one of the “Best Litigation Attorneys in Columbus.”

Over the course of his career, Joseph has represented clients in nearly half of Ohio’s 88 counties, consistently achieving favorable results. His extensive courtroom experience allows him to evaluate cases effectively and provide clients with clear, strategic guidance. Known for his thorough preparation and dedication, Joseph is committed to securing the best possible outcomes for his clients.

In addition to his practice, Joseph serves as an adjunct professor at The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law, his alma mater, where he developed and teaches a course on Divorce Trial Practice. He is also a frequent lecturer, having delivered more than 40 continuing legal education presentations both in Ohio and nationally. His topics have included advanced child and spousal support calculations, the use of private investigators in family law cases, children as witnesses, and the role of experts in matters involving abuse or alienation allegations.

Joseph’s professional excellence has been recognized with numerous honors. He holds Martindale-Hubbell’s highest possible distinction, the AV Preeminent rating, for both legal ability and ethical standards. He has been named to Best Lawyers in America, selected to the Ohio Super Lawyers list for seven consecutive years (following 11 years on the Rising Stars list), and included in The National Trial Lawyers: Top 100. He also maintains a perfect 10 “Superb” peer rating and 5.0 client review score on Avvo.

Beyond his legal practice, Joseph has served the central Ohio community in numerous leadership roles. He spent six years on the Columbus Bar Association Professional Ethics Committee, three years as President of the CBA Juvenile Law Committee, and four years as President of the Lawyers’ Club of Columbus. He also served six years on the Dublin Board of Zoning Appeals, including terms as Chairman and Vice Chairman, and was appointed by Governor John Kasich to the Ohio Board of Dietetics, where he served for five years.

Above all, Joseph is committed to guiding clients through some of life’s most difficult challenges with compassion, clarity, and steadfast advocacy.

attorneys.name: Gregory Nitz
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Drawing on Teamwork and a Client-Forward Focus to Win Cases

Gregory “Greg” Nitz is an Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law at the firm’s Cleveland offices. A people person at heart, Greg is good at asking the right questions and even better at listening to their answers. He is a master at building carefully crafted cases and ardently representing his clients in litigation.

A Background Based in Client-Facing Roles

“One of the big jobs I had in undergrad was a pretty high-up customer service role at Bank of America,” Greg said, describing his lead-up to a legal career. “I took that job right before the COVID-19 pandemic began, and let me tell you, even when stress-levels are at the max for you and your clients, working a client-facing role teaches you real fast how to perform essential functions within a framework of rules and regulations while also getting results for your client.”

Bank of America may have been a highlight of Greg’s pre-law school career, but it was just one of many steps in a methodical, highly intentional stairway that Greg has been climbing since childhood. A newspaper delivery boy in the mornings and a hardworking student by day, Greg added activity after activity each year to improve the lives of those around him. He joined the Boy Scouts of America at a young age and rose to the rank of Eagle Scout, leading community service projects at every step. He volunteered in school programs, mentored others, and helped refugees and foreign torture survivors through his church.

Helping Ohio Workers No Matter the Case

After graduating from college and law school with a surplus of academic accolades, Greg launched a legal career. Today he focuses primarily on litigation, where he feels he can do the most good by advocating for clients. “I’ve always loved anything having to do with debate, argument, rhetoric, or simply making a case for something and standing by it,” Greg said.

Greg’s background in law has been immensely varied, including corporate law, civil litigation, transactional and business-related legal administration, and public defense. “Prior to working for the firm, I saw a lot of different types of legal cases in a relatively short time,” Greg said. “That’s immensely helpful, as no two cases are the same, and every case requires an open mind and a willingness to draw on different strategies and legal approaches.”

Work/Life Balance

“I enjoy cooking, setting up home networking systems, and hiking,” Greg said when asked what he does when he’s not serving clients at the firm. “I’m also really into baking, especially pizzas!” Greg added. A man of many hobbies, Greg has also achieved intermediate fluency in German and is at a beginner level in Russian.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Gregory Nitz

“Attorneys have to be willing to put in the work, but it’s not just about the work,” Greg said in closing. “You also have to apply yourself to the work in an organized and methodical manner.” Greg went on to describe the organizational structure of NRS Injury Law as being one that’s designed to assist each attorney in applying themselves to their craft in the best way they know how. “The ‘pod’ structure at the firm is unique and unlike other firms,” Greg said. “It’s so well organized, we’re able to focus on our clients to the best of our abilities.”

Greg’s affable, people-person character, his impressive work ethic, his love for process and methodology, and his knack for strategy and debate are all traits that align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Greg and the firm about your case, call 855.468.4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

As a boy and teen, Greg spent most of his free time in Boy Scouts of America, applying himself to his community wherever he could and ultimately attaining the rank of Eagle Scout. While in high school, Greg mentored and educated new marching band members as squad leader of the Anthony Wayne Marching Generals. Greg also served as Vice President for his school’s chapter of the National Honor Society. While in college, Greg volunteered for the Catholic Charities, the Summer Reading Club, and ZooTeen.

Brian brings a unique blend of global perspective, intellectual curiosity, and community spirit to his role at Oliver Law Office. He went on to receive his J.D. from The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law, where he honed the critical thinking and advocacy skills he now uses to serve clients with clarity and conviction.

Brian’s thoughtful approach to the law and strong commitment to his clients make him a trusted and compassionate advocate at Oliver Law Office.

attorneys.name: Joshua Nolan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law (Divorce / Custody/Adoption) Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Joshua Nolan has travelled a rather non-traditional route into the practice of law. He worked as a Press Operator in a Ford Motor Company factory to put himself through college before accepting a scholarship for law school. While attending the University of Cincinnati College of Law, Josh worked as a Legal Extern for Judge David Bunning, United States District Court, EDKY. After graduation in 2004, Josh worked in a medium sized law firm in Cincinnati, Ohio before joining a large Columbus, Ohio based law firm. During that time, Josh had the opportunity to work on a wide variety of complex commercial litigation matters, ranging from product liability claims to mass torts to $100 Million Dollar contract disputes. However, while Josh enjoyed this often complicated and challenging work, he wanted to use his skills to help individuals and small business rather than large corporations and insurance companies.

In 2011, Josh had the opportunity to return to the Toledo, Ohio area and open NOLAN LAW, LLC. Since opening in June of 2011, Josh has helped dozens of individuals and small business resolve a wide variety of legal issues, ranging from divorce and child custody matters to insurance coverage disputes to starting a new business.

Josh is also licensed to practice law in Michigan, where he has become one of the foremost experts on municipal zoning and/or licensing of industrial wind turbines. Josh has dedicated this portion of his practice to helping individuals and local government entities who are seeking protection from the dangers of improperly sited industrial wind turbines. In conjunction, Josh is one of the Directors and founding members of the Interstate Informed Citizens Coalition, Inc., a non-profit corporation dedicated to educating the public about the impacts of improperly sited industrial wind turbines.

At NOLAN LAW, LLC, we pride ourselves on giving individual attention and large law firm experience at small law firm rates. Call today to let us help you!

Awards and Honors

Honors

Order of the Barristers, 2004

In her estate plan practice, Esther focuses on helping clients put together all of the documents necessary not only to manage their assets after death but to transition individuals and families through the aging process. She has a wide range of experience in drafting Wills, Trusts, Financial Powers of Attorney and health care documents, including Living Wills and Health Care Powers of Attorney.

In Esther's adoption practice, she welcomes all prospective adoptive couples. She has recently represented multiple step-parents in Warren, Butler and Hamilton Counties through the process of adopting their stepchildren.

In Esther's business practice, she has counseled numerous small to mid-sized companies from their initial start-up through the succession planning. She advises and prepares operating agreements for different business entities and member/shareholder agreements where there are multiple business owners.

Outside of the office, Esther is busy with her family. She and her husband are active in their children's sporting and school activities. Esther volunteers regularly at her children's school and serves on the Leadership Committee of her Church's Cub Scout Pack. Esther also volunteers weekly as a personalized talking print reader for the Cincinnati Association for the Blind and Visually Impaired.

attorneys.name: Gregory O'Brien
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Gregory E. O'Brien is a Shareholder in Cavitch's litigation group and the chair of its Insurance Law Committee. He has extensive trial experience in the defense of complex business, tort, and insurance disputes in both state and federal court. He is an accomplished appellate practitioner who has briefed and argued over 100 cases to the U.S. Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, the Ohio Supreme Court, and numerous intermediate Ohio appellate courts. Greg's clients value his ability to provide prompt, early and insightful evaluation coupled with practical and efficient resolution strategies in complex litigation and business matters of all kinds.

Greg is one of only a handful of Ohio lawyers certified as a Specialist in Insurance Coverage and Bad Faith Law. He has extensive experience in all aspects of insurance law, including: examinations under oath; coverage opinions; reservations of rights and denials; and, litigating tort, breach of contract, declaratory judgment, bad faith, and other coverage disputes. Greg has extensive experience litigating claims under property, general liability, auto and other policies. Greg has tried cases arising out of premises claims, fires, thefts, auto and UM/UIM claims under both business and personal lines in cases asserting property damage, bodily injury/wrongful death, business losses, and bad faith.

Greg is an active member in numerous professional organizations, including: The Cleveland Metro Bar Association (Appellate Courts Committee, Chair 2003 - 2005; Insurance Law Section, Chair 2014-2015); the Ohio Bar Association (Appellate Courts Committee, 2004 - present; Appellate Law Specialty Board, Chair 2006-2015; Insurance Law Specialty Board, 2014 - present); Ohio Association of Civil Trial Attorneys ("OACTA"), (President, 2008; Board of Trustees, 1998 -2009; Awards Committee, Chair 2013 - present; Amicus Curiae Committee, Chair 2003 to 2005; Program Committee, Chair 1999 - 2000; Quarterly Review, Editor-in-Chief 1997 to 2002); Cleveland Association of Civil Trial Attorneys (1986 - present); Defense Research Institute ("DRI") (State Representative for Ohio, 2010-2013).

Greg is a frequent author and lecturer on topics related to his practice, and he has been awarded numerous honors throughout his career, including: Life Delegate to the Judicial Conference, Eighth District Court of Appeals (2007 - present); Martindale Hubbell, A/V Rating (2002 - present); Ohio Super Lawyer (Appellate Practice, 2004-2006; Civil Litigation Defense, 2009 - present); OACTA Distinguished Service Award (1999, 2001, 2005, and 2006); OACTA President's Award (2008); OACTA Frank Seth Hurd Member of the Year Award (2016); DRI Exceptional Performance Citation (2007, 2008, and 2013); and, DRI State Leadership Award (2013).

Greg is very involved in the community through organizations such as the St. Ignatius High School Father's Club (President, 2009-2010); St. Ignatius High School Crew Parents' Steering Committee (Treasurer, 2010-2012); Cleveland Rowing Foundation: Head of the Cuyahoga Regatta (Parking Committee, Chair 2011-2012); Rocky River Buc's Baseball (Coach, 2011-2015); Rocky River Youth Hockey Association (Board of Trustees, 2005-present; Advisory Council, 2002-2004); St. Christopher's CYO Athletics (Baseball Coach, 2012-2015; Basketball Coach, 2011-2013); Rocky River Little League (Coach, 2001-2002, 2004-2008, 2010); Rocky River Rec. Dept. T-Ball/Coach Pitch Baseball (Coach, 1998- 2004, 2007-2009); Rocky River Rec. Dept. Pony League Baseball (Coach, 2008, 2009); Rocky River Rec. Dept. Boys Basketball (Coach, 2009).

In 1986, Greg received his law degree from The Ohio State University College of Law and in 1983 he received a Bachelor of Arts degree in business administration (cum laude) from Walsh College. Greg also successfully completed the course of study at the International Association of Defense Counsel's Trial Academy in 1995.

attorneys.name: Michael W. O'Neil
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Setting a New Standard in Workers' Compensation Law Through Empathy, Experience, and Excellence

“Just about everyone can name moments in their life when everything changed,” says Michael O'Neil, reflecting on his path to practicing workers' comp law as an attorney with NRS Injury Law. “Sometimes it's for the better, sometimes it's for the worse. In workers' comp law, we're helping people who, within an instant, had everything change for them and their families due to a workplace injury.”

For Mike, his path to law began in the Armed Forces. From 1984 to 1990, Mike served in the United States Army, arriving there by way of the ROTC. He served with the 2nd Infantry Division in Korea and took stateside assignments at Fort Moore (formerly Fort Benning) and Fort Jackson. His time overseas and postings at Moore and Jackson gave him a deep appreciation for organization, teamwork, strategy, and case-building. His last assignment had him working as a supply officer. Mike was tasked with performing investigations and presenting cases regarding damaged or destroyed Army property to a Judge Advocate General. After transitioning out of the Army, that last role stuck with Mike, and he quickly enrolled at the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law.

Approaching Workers' Comp Cases with Optimism and Strategy

Mike began clerking at a law firm while attending law school. “A skillset with workers' comp soon became what I could bring to the table,” says Mike. “And it was coincidentally what I was most passionate about. Each case is different, and each involves someone whose life has been turned upside down from a workplace injury or illness. I committed to approaching each case with a glass-half-full mindset, and I soon found I had a knack for turning around the client's devastating life event and helping them secure a brighter future.”

After putting in the work clerking and going to law school, Mike took the bar, passed, and accepted a job offer at a firm where he continued his focus on workers' comp. The glass-half-full mantra carried on, and Mike's positive demeanor, infectious smile, and charismatic cheer proved invaluable in setting clients at ease and preparing them for case-building, deposition, mediation, and trial.

Committed to the Cause

Mike's career experience now includes more than two decades of diligent work in workers' comp. However, Mike still embodies the same youthful cheer, persistence, empathy, and optimism that were on display during his years as an Army supply officer and later as a law student/clerk. Mike dedicates several hours each day to finding ways to maximize efficiency, strengthen his strategies and arguments, and optimize the nuances and finer details of each case that comes before him. “I've seen thousands of cases in my time,” Mike said. “Each is different, and each requires me to draw on my experience and find unique and compelling ways to argue that case.”

In addition to his casework, Mike has taken on a mentorship role at the firm, where he advises new attorneys on their workers' comp cases. To excel in mentorship, provide maximum value to the firm’s clients, and set a good example for the firm’s attorneys, Mike also dedicates significant time each year to continuing his education as a workers’ compensation attorney. As a result, Mike has earned his Workers’ Compensation Certified Specialist certification with the Ohio State Bar Association. Read more about Mike’s certification experience on the firm’s blog page.

Community Involvement:

Pursuing a career in workers' comp law means committing oneself to a life of service, and that mindset doesn't end when Mike clocks out for the day. Passionate about helping his community, Mike has been involved in several programs that give back. For example, since 1993, Mike has been a team leader on the Sunday lunch ministry at Cleveland's Trinity Cathedral. The program provides meals to the homeless and food-depraved community members. Mike's son is now an Eagle Scout, but in previous years, Mike served as Assistant Scout Master in the local troop.

Work/Life Balance:

Mike lives in Rocky River with his wife Tamzin, who is also a practicing attorney. Between their dedicated careers, two dogs, and two cats, the pair stays more than busy. When they have some free time, they can be found heading over to Kent State University to spend a weekend with their son Aidan, a business management major with aspirations of joining the ROTC as his father did.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Mike O'Neil

“NRS Injury Law provides clients with the best opportunity to maximize their workers' compensation claim,” Mike added in closing. “The large complement of staff enables us to leverage our individual skills and get results for clients, without any of the employees ever feeling spread too thin. Everyone has their role, and they're great at it. Our processes are streamlined, comprehensive, and thorough. We're able to proceed with constant compassion, ever-present excellence, integrity, patience, and professionalism. In my time, I've never seen a firm operate in such a strategic way, and it makes a difference.”

To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Mike and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

attorneys.name: John P. O'Neil
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mayfield Heights, OH
attorneys.bio:
John P. O'Neil joined Elk & Elk Co., Ltd. in 2012 as an equity partner. He is one of the firm's leading medical malpractice and personal injury attorneys, whose practice focuses primarily upon death and catastrophic loss cases. Prior to joining Elk & Elk, John spent 14 years at one of Ohio’s top defense law firms, where he served as a practice area chair and member of the firm's management committee and executive group. He also spent time working as a successful prosecutor in the Dade County State Attorney's Office. Over the years, John has successfully tried more than 80 jury trials in various areas of law, including medical malpractice, transportation, legal malpractice, premises liability and others. John's first chair jury trials are in state and federal courts, and he has argued in the Eighth District Court of Appeals, Ohio Supreme Court and Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals.

John practices with the Ohio firm of Elk & Elk Co., Ltd., located in Mayfield Heights. He received his undergraduate degree from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio and his law degree from John Marshall Law School in Chicago, Illinois.

John is married and has four children.

Settlements and Verdicts

$5 million settlement – Loading/unloading accident in Indiana, which caused catastrophic brain injury.

$4.75 million settlement – Truck crash, which caused catastrophic orthopedic injury.

$4.5 million settlement – Case involving a truck striking an elderly pedestrian causing orthopedic and neurological injuries.

$3.65 million settlement – Truck accident where a floor mat (product defect) caused unintentional acceleration, causing severe and permanent neurologic injuries.

$2.3 million settlement – Highway crash, causing significant permanent orthopedic and neurologic injury.

$2.0 million settlement – Medical malpractice in Florida of failure to properly diagnose an abscess leading to lower extremity paralysis.

$1.1 million settlement – Intersection collision which resulted in a permanent foot drop.

$1,035,000 million settlement – Shooting range accident which caused serious internal injuries.

$787,500 result – Bicycle accident case that caused the death of an adult male.

$585,000 settlement – Negligent security case on a college campus.

All lawsuits are different and Elk & Elk makes no representation or promises that it can obtain the same results in other cases. These results do not guarantee, warrant, or predict the outcome of any future legal matter. You should consult an attorney for advice regarding your individual situation.

attorneys.bio:
Detached reflection cannot be demanded in the presence of an uplifted knife.

– Oliver Wendell Holmes, Jr., Brown v. U.S. (1921) No. 103, 256 U.S. 335

Those were the first words of John’s closing argument in his client’s trial for shooting an unarmed man twice. A conviction meant a mandatory minimum eight years in prison. John argued self-defense and his client was found Not Guilty. John’s client legally defended himself from his attacker at the scene and John successfully defended his client from the government at the trial. John’s client is a free man today.

Biography

John is available day or night at 513-300-4012. Call any time you need help immediately.

John is a lawyer who goes to court. He handles criminal, white collar, DUI/OVI ("drunk driving"), and juvenile defense; and civil litigation involving serious personal injury and wrongful death claims.

He was named to the Super Lawyers Top 50 lawyers in Cincinnati for 2012 through 2025 and the Super Lawyers Top 100 lawyers in Ohio for 2013, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021 & 2025.

John was just named the 2025 Cincinnati Criminal Defense “Lawyer of the Year” by The Best Lawyers in America. This after he was voted by his peers to be the 2015 and 2023 The Best Lawyers in America Cincinnati Criminal Defense “Lawyer of the Year”. And John was The Best Lawyers in America 2018 Cincinnati Criminal Defense: White Collar “Lawyer of the Year”.

John has a perfect 10.0 rating from AVVO.com.

John O’Shea represents clients in southwest Ohio in the State and Federal Courts. He has established himself as a lawyer dedicated to tirelessly spending himself in the worthy cause of protecting his clients as a true Man in the Arena.

John served as the lead trial and appellate lawyer on the case invalidating Cincinnati’s illegal attempt to criminalize firearm possession. In 2023, Cincinnati passed a law making it a crime to have a firearm that was not always locked away when anyone under 18 was present. John argued the challenge to that law to the Trial Court, which agreed that Cincinnati’s attempt to criminalize the constitutional right to bear arms violated Ohio law. The City appealed that decision. John argued the case to the Court of Appeals, which unanimously agreed that Cincinnati’s attempt to criminalize gun ownership was illegal and ordered that the law be immediately revoked.

At 5:22 a.m., John was called by the mother of two young men in police custody accused of an early morning homicide. John was at the police department before sunrise. He coordinated defense for both, which included immediately securing co-counsel. John spent the day negotiating with the police, who ultimately charged both with Murder. Within minutes of that charging decision, John reached an agreement with the prosecutor for bail and both were released less than two hours after being charged. The case was investigated and negotiations with the prosecutor continued, which included presenting evidence of self-defense. The Grand Jury then dismissed all charges, exonerating both. John then had all the case records sealed.

John is a designated attorney of the United States Concealed Carry Association's Critical Response Team, which provides 24-hour insurance backed benefits, including immediate criminal defense representation for USCCA members.

He defended a USCCA member indicted for Murder, Attempted Murder and Felonious Assault for shooting and killing one and shooting at another. A conviction as charged carried a mandatory life prison sentence. John argued self-defense at trial, after which his client was found Not Guilty of all charges. All defense costs were paid by the USCCA.

At 3:45 a.m., John was called by the USCCA Critical Response Team to defend a USCCA member in police custody after being involved in a shooting. The USCCA member had defended himself by returning fire and shooting the assailant. The USCCA member was unharmed. John immediately responded to the police department where his new client was being held for questioning. John protected his client through the investigation. His client’s attacker was charged with Felonious Assault. John’s client was released without being charged. All defense costs were paid by the USCCA.

Before joining Cohen Todd Criminal Defense in 1994, John was an assistant prosecutor in the Juvenile, Municipal and Common Pleas Court criminal trial divisions of the Hamilton County Prosecutor’s Office. During that time, John was also appointed by the Ohio Attorney General to serve as a special prosecutor to the Ohio Organized Crime Investigations Commission. While in private practice, John was twice appointed as a special prosecutor by the Hamilton County Courts.

Today, John uses his decades of courtroom experience to effectively defend individuals and businesses in white collar criminal investigations and prosecutions, as well as adults and juveniles charged with misdemeanor and felony criminal offenses of every type, including drug offenses, and driving under the influence charges. John actually tries cases when few lawyers will. That makes an enormous difference in the results John gets for his clients.

In civil matters, John has successfully advised and represented business clients on various corporate matters, disputes and litigation. He has won significant awards for clients in numerous personal injury and wrongful death cases.

John is a trusted advocate who around the clock puts his clients first. John’s unwavering commitment to his clients is a testament to his character and to the mark he is leaving on the local legal community.

Call at your convenience for a free consultation or if you just have a question.

Call John on 513-300-4012 at any time – day or night – if you need help immediately.

attorneys.bio:
Commercial litigation, business contracts and counseling, non-profit organization, and healthcare law. Martindale-Hubbell AV Rated since 2005.

Joe has spent his entire legal career with Bieser, Greer & Landis but law was not his first profession. After graduating from Harvard with a degree in Economics in 1987, he went to work for Emerson Electric's Copeland Corporation in Sidney, Ohio, where he held both finance and marketing positions. Leaving Copeland was a difficult decision but in 1992, Joe made the choice to enroll in law school in what had become his hometown, graduating from the University of Dayton School of Law in 1995 with honors.

Most of Joe's time as an Associate with the firm was spent litigating civil cases, most dealing with business and professional issues. Joe's business experience and economics and finance background give him insights that many lawyers may not have. In only ten years, Joe earned Martindale-Hubbell's highest rating and was subsequently named a Best Lawyers in America Commercial Litigator and Super Lawyer. Joe still litigates cases on behalf of individual and business clients but now also devotes time organizing businesses, drafting contracts and counseling clients on matters relating to all facets of business, both for-profit and non-profit.
