attorneys.name: Erin Schmidt
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
A Life-Long Legal Career Dedicated to Advocating for Injured Workers in Ohio

Erin Schmidt is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Having spent multiple years representing clients in Social Security Disability claims, Erin draws on a rich background in plaintiff law where a knack for details, an eye for strategy, and an ability to counsel injured clients were essential in building winning cases.

Diverse Legal Skills Honed Through Years of Client Representation

“I wanted to be an attorney since I was seven years old,” Erin said, retracing the steps she took that brought her to a career in law. Coming from humble beginnings in rural, working-class Illinois, Erin worked after-school jobs in retail, record-keeping, market research, and finance when she wasn’t playing sports, but she always knew she’d one day take the LSAT, go to law school, pass the bar, and become an attorney.

Erin passed the bar in 2006 and immediately began working with clients who had Social Security Disability claims. “From how the cases are constructed to how the laws govern both the administrative and litigative sides of the cases, social security law is very similar to workers’ compensation law,” Erin said. By working at plaintiff’s law firms and at times working under her own name, Erin represented thousands of cases in legal fields including disability, family law, real estate, criminal law, bankruptcy, consumer defense, and estate planning from 2006 to 2022. Since 2022, Erin has shifted her focus to advocating for Ohio workers who have been injured on the job.

Working Closely with Clients to Help Them Understand How to Win Workers’ Compensation Cases

To Erin, the key to building a winning case is harnessing institutional knowledge, informing clients so they become active team members on the case, and deftly helping clients set aside the emotions that often come with stressful workplace injuries. “We’re here to win victories,” Erin says. “NRS Injury Law holds the keys to the greatest body of institutional knowledge in the state of Ohio when it comes to workers’ compensation cases, and the firm is willing to innovate and do whatever it takes to help our clients succeed.”

Erin continued: “With the sheer degree of support we attorneys have at NRS Injury Law, we don’t have to go outside the firm to get help or to get complicated questions answered. I know workers’ comp cases can be stressful at times, both for the client and the attorney, but with the immense support we have at the firm, we’re able to smooth the road out in front of us, counsel our clients effectively, and work with them as a team to build compelling, logic-and-fact-driven cases that win.”

Work/Life Balance

When she’s not representing injured workers at the firm or volunteering, Erin is an avid gardener. She likes to go fishing from her kayak, and takes frequent summer trips to Wisconsin and Michigan to fish on inland lakes. Erin also sews, cross-stitches, and crochets. She enjoys visiting Northeast Ohio’s botanical gardens and natural history museums.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from Erin Schmidt

“My goal is to advocate for my clients in such a way that I help them remove the emotion from the case,” Erin said in closing. “I’m trying to help guide my clients to a point where the heartache and loss connected to their injury, their frustrations associated with it, those feelings are left by the wayside. That way, we can simply examine the facts with logic and strategy so that we may, as a team, build a winning case.”

Erin’s dedication to everyday working people and her unique ability to help clients focus on their cases and build strategies that win in court all come together and align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Erin and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Erin has been deeply involved in numerous causes, community efforts, and volunteering campaigns, often centered around social services and education. For example, Erin has taken a leadership role in multiple organizations seeking to end preeclampsia, including the Preeclampsia Foundation and EndPreeclampsia. She has served as State Coordinator and Forum Moderator, actively answering and moderating a group of over 25,000 women who have suffered from preeclampsia, eclampsia, and HELLP Syndrome. Erin has also advocated for patients with auditory processing disorder, ADHD, and the need for comprehensive special education services. As a result of her diligent work in these spaces, Erin has earned numerous licenses and certifications. She is a Maternal Mental Health Advocate, a guardian ad litem, she holds the VA Disability Accreditation, and she is a member of the League of Women Voters.

Specific to her role as an attorney, Erin has spent a great deal of her free time sharing the knowledge she has accrued over the course of her career. For example, she has delivered several CLE (Continuing Legal Education) presentations. Some of these have included the Social Security and Workers’ Compensation Crossover CLE (2018), the Five Day Rule CLE (2017), the IDEA Basics CLE (2016), and the Social Security Disability Practice CLE (2014). She has also published her legal writings about workers’ compensation and social security payments in the Attorney at Law Magazine (2016). She also published her writings about Social Security Disability Practice in the American Bar Association’s Solo and Small Firm Magazine (2014).

attorneys.name: Jerald A. Schneiberg
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Co-Managing Ohio’s Largest Workers’ Compensation and Personal Injury Law Firm

Jerald (Jerry) Schneiberg is Co-Managing Partner at NRS Injury Law, heading the workers’ compensation litigation groups. Alongside Dan Romaine, who heads the firm’s personal injury and auto accident departments, Jerry directs Ohio’s largest workers’ compensation and injury law firm in its daily activities, including serving clients in every county across Ohio from the firm’s offices in Euclid, Cleveland, Columbus, Toledo, Dayton, and Cincinnati.

Finding a Path to Law in the Service of Others

From a young age, Jerry felt a call to serve others. His first job was at a family restaurant, the “Old Barn Out Back” in Lima, Ohio. Once in college, Jerry spent his summers working for Nickles Bakery, a union shop providing baked goods to restaurants. Jerry pursued accounting in college and took a job at National City Bank after graduating from Ohio University in 1988, but he soon realized the banking industry wasn’t for him.

“There I was, sitting in a glass-walled office in a high rise that many would dream of working in, yet I knew I was in the wrong career,” Jerry said, reflecting on what he refers to as his “silly, fresh-out-of-college years.” After careful consideration, Jerry left the banking industry and enrolled at Cleveland-Marshall College of Law.

A Life’s Dedication to Helping Injured Ohioans

Following an externship during law school that saw Jerry shadow renowned federal court judge, John Michael Manos, Jerry passed the bar in 1993 after winning the prestigious Lawyers’ Co-op Award for Outstanding Achievement in Administrative Law. Jerry spent the next few years working for personal injury and workers’ compensation firms, including Yulish, Twohig & Associates; Peltz & Birne; Davis & Associates; and Crosby O’Brien & Associates.

“I went to law school because I wanted to help people, so I was naturally drawn to the plaintiff’s side of injury law right away, but most of the jobs I was offered in the 90s were on the defense side,” Jerry said. “Those early years gave me an in-depth knowledge of how companies try to defend themselves against personal injury and workers’ comp claims, a knowledge I began putting to use as soon as I joined NRS Injury Law.”

Leading a Workers’ Compensation Law Firm that Does Things Differently

When asked about the driving principles behind NRS Injury Law and what makes the firm different, Jerry reached for a laminated copy of the firm’s Vision Statement and began to read aloud. “We put a lot of thought into this,” he began with a smile. “NRS Injury Law is the largest workers’ compensation law firm in Ohio. Our elite team zealously advocates for justice for every client by practicing the art of constant compassion, striving for excellence, and acting with integrity, patience, and professionalism.”

Jerry elaborated, describing the firm as being about the client and their journey. The firm is constructed entirely around the client, from their initial consultation to their case’s final result. Workers’ compensation cases are complicated and nuanced, requiring multiple steps, so Jerry designed the firm’s approach to accommodate. As Ohio’s largest workers’ comp firm, NRS Injury Law has the resources, support structure, assistants, medical experts, research potential, evidence-gathering help, and colleague advice the firm’s attorneys need to build winning cases.

“It’s also about the foundation,” Jerry added. “We built a law firm that’s unlike any other, because we built it on a unique foundation. The foundation is our great attorneys and the structures they operate in. Each attorney is supported by their own case manager, paralegal, and legal assistant. The associate attorneys themselves are organized into ‘pods’ with a partner attorney mentoring the associate attorneys in each pod. The result is a streamlined, perfected, and proprietary system that optimizes results for our clients.”

Work/Life Balance

When Jerry isn’t co-managing NRS Injury Law or volunteering in the Cleveland community, he enjoys skiing during winter and golfing during summer. Year-round hobbies include traveling and spending time with his beloved wife, Kim, and their four adult children. Jerry is also a former marathon runner, having completed races in Columbus, Cincinnati, Chicago, and Philadelphia. An avid outdoor enthusiast, Jerry can often be found scanning travel blogs, searching for the next big family adventure.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Jerry Schneiberg

Thoughtful, determined, an empathetic listener during one-on-one client counsel, and a ruthless advocate in court, Jerry epitomizes the traits written into the firm’s mission statement. “We are zealous in our client advocacy,” reads the mission statement on Jerry’s wall. “Our elite team cares deeply, providing empathetic and patient service to every person who calls our firm. We relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting our collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work each and every day.” Drawing on decades of dedication to Ohio workers and utilizing a collaborative, results-driven, and empathy-first model, Jerry has won thousands of cases for injured workers. To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Jerry and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

As Co-Managing Partner, Jerry takes a lead role in the firm’s philanthropic and community-oriented endeavors, particularly the firm’s involvement with the Miracle League, a baseball league for children and adults with permanent disabilities. Jerry is also involved with the firm’s volunteer efforts at the Cleveland Food Bank.

Outside the firm, Jerry serves as President of the Board of Directors of Open Doors Academy, a year-round out-of-school program for children designed to protect, inspire, nurture, and challenge youth to reach their full potential. Always open to opportunities to encourage new generations of workers’ compensation plaintiff attorneys, Jerry has served as keynote speaker at events hosted by the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association, Ohio Association for Justice, National Business Institute, AFL-CIO Workers' Compensation Institute, Ohio State Bar Association, and the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law.

Formerly, Jerry served as the author of the Ohio Association for Justice’s quarterly newsletter. Jerry also coached youth basketball, served on the Board of Directors for the Shaker Heights Youth Hockey Association, and was an active parent in the Shaker Heights PTO.

attorneys.name: Theodore J. Schneider
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Health & Safety Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ted has years of regulatory legal and technical knowledge and in-plant experience as an environmental engineer, safety professional and attorney. He employs his technical background and experiences into a thriving EHS auditing, compliance and legal practice, which includes multi-media EHS compliance auditing as a mainstay.

As a certified IRCA EHS auditor, Ted has audited facilities in nearly every business sector throughout the United States and in more than 25 countries. He has performed gap analyses for the automobile and auto parts manufacturing industry, battery production, foundries, stamping facilities, wire assembly, utilities, metal finishing and electroplating, electrical component, paper coating, can coating, printing, health and beauty care, pharmaceutical, research and development, pulp and paper production, chemical manufacturing, food and beverage, other heavy manufacturing industries, a variety of waste treatment, recycling and disposal facilities, and corporate social responsibility audits in China, South Korea, India, Mexico, Ireland, and Italy.

In addition, Ted has been responsible for a broad array of corporate and industrial plant environmental and safety compliance programs including air and water pollution permitting, emissions monitoring and testing, hazardous waste management, underground storage tank installation, closure and corrective action, industrial ventilation design and installation, wastewater treatment plant operations, waste minimization studies, noise control design and installation, noise monitoring, compliance auditing, emergency response and contingency plan preparation, employee training and regulatory reporting, and has developed complete safety programs.

Finally, Ted’s legal and technical EHS background provides a significant advantage in representing clients in their defense against enforcement actions. Using these skills, Ted can skillfully negotiate to reduce or remove agency orders, citations, and penalties. He can also support complex purchase and sales agreements in merger and acquisition activities.

attorneys.name: Sam Schneider
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Health & Safety Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Sam has performed many EHS audits in several of the U.S. states and is developing his skills as a well-rounded regulatory EHS auditor. At the same time, he is also developing a strong expertise in performing lockout, guarding, confined space, fall protection surveys, noise monitoring, industrial hygiene monitoring and in developing related and necessary corrective actions to address the gaps he finds in these programs. He has performed gap analyses for clients in the auto parts manufacturing, battery production, utilities, food and beverage, recycling and disposal facilities, and other heavy manufacturing industries. He has an added advantage in that he possesses in-plant / field experience as a pipe welder providing him with insight into how maintenance and manufacturing functions interact and how to get the best out of both.

Sam has developed health & safety facility-specific compliance programs and procedures for several clients in the following regulatory areas: the control of hazardous energy / lockout tagout, fall protection, hazard communication, machine guarding, emergency response, and confined space entry. He has also delivered new employee orientation training, performed hazardous waste accumulation area and SPCC inspections, and documented air pollution control equipment and emergency generator monitoring data and opacity readings. Sam’s education, technical and professional EHS background provides a significant advantage toward improving manufacturing plant compliance and protecting clients against enforcement actions.

Sam is an Eagle Scout and holds TIG and arc welding certifications for pipe and structural steel welding.

attorneys.name: Michael Schroth
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Avon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Michael T. Schroth focuses his legal practice in the areas of employment law, estate planning and probate law, business law, and real estate law. During his career, Mr. Schroth has represented individuals, families, small businesses, large companies, municipalities, and boards of education in hundreds of cases throughout Ohio. Mr. Schroth is sensitive to his clients' concerns and counsels with them to achieve the best possible outcome. He believes in finding cost-effective and cooperative solutions to complex problems. However, he also recognizes that some legal issues can only be resolved through litigation.

Mr. Schroth has a wealth of experience advocating for his clients in various settings. He has successfully argued cases before trial courts and appellate courts throughout Ohio, as well as the Ohio Civil Rights Commission, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the Industrial Commission of Ohio, the Ohio Unemployment Compensation Commission, local Boards of Revision, and the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals. Mr. Schroth also has broad experience assisting his clients put together their estate planning documents, form businesses, buy and sell commercial and residential property, buy and sell businesses, administer probate estates, and prepare all manner of legal contracts.

Mr. Schroth is licensed to practice law in the State of Ohio. He is a member of the Ohio Bar Association, the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association, and the Lorain County Bar Association. He also serves as a volunteer attorney for Hospice of the Western Reserve. Mr. Schroth obtained a B.A. from Brigham Young University and his J.D. from the Cleveland-Marshall College of Law. A graduate of Westlake High School, he resides with his wife and three sons in Avon, Ohio. His office is located in the historic Clifton House in Avon, which was built in 1834.

attorneys.name: Neal Darwin Schuett
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Oxford, OH
attorneys.bio:
Neal Schuett is one of the rare breeds of criminal defense attorney that is willing to go to trial and also knows how to protect his client's appellate rights. Since moving to southwest Ohio in 2010, Neal has successfully handled hundreds of criminal and DUI/OVI cases, including not guilty verdicts in both bench and jury trials. For example, Neal received not guilty verdicts for a man accused of high-level felonies. In that same time, Neal has also fought to protect the rights of his clients through his criminal appellate work. In one case, Neal's appellate advocacy skills convinced the Twelfth District Court of Appeals to overturn its prior ruling on felony OVI sentencing laws.

Neal has never been shy about being in a courtroom. From a young age, he could be found in the peanut gallery of the Polk County Courthouse watching his father testify as a Des Moines Police Department officer. His interest in trial-work lead him to join the University of Iowa mock trial team where he won All-American honors and back-to-back national championships. In law school, Neal was selected to compete in the University of Iowa College of Law's prestigious Van Oosterhout Moot Court Competition and to represent the College of Law on its trial advocacy team. As part of that team, he earned a bid to compete at TYLA's Trial Advocacy National Championship tournament. Neal continues to teach competitive trial advocacy as the program director and head coach of Miami University's nationally-ranked mock trial program. In 2018, he helped coach Miami Mock Trial to its first national championship title in seventeen years, and second overall.

Neal has turned his interest in trial-work into a successful criminal law practice. Prior to joining Rittgers & Rittgers, he has worked as a municipal prosecutor, a felony public defender, and as an associate for Haughey & Niehaus, LLC in Oxford, Ohio. Neal has been named to Super Lawyer's Ohio Rising Stars list in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, and 2019. He is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association, the Cincinnati Bar Association, and the Butler County and Warren County Bar Associations. Since 2009, he has also been on the board of directors for the American Mock Trial Association.

Neal is licensed in Ohio and the Southern District of Ohio (federal).

attorneys.name: Donald K. Scott
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Dayton, OH
attorneys.bio:
Don Scott didn’t grow up with everything being handed to him. For 16 years, Don drove a Dayton Daily News truck while in school in order to pay for law school. His goal from day one was to help people, and he does that by working as a Workers’ Compensation lawyer here at Hochman and Plunkett. He has been in practice since 1994, and in 1998 he became one of the first attorneys in Ohio to become certified as a specialist in Workers’ Compensation Law by the Ohio State Bar Association.

Don is very caring and believes that everyone has rights and they should get what they deserve in a case. He has a passion for Workers’ Compensation and said that he wouldn’t want to work anywhere else.

Don speaks about a case that he remembers most:

I was once contacted by a relatively young woman whose husband had just been diagnosed with lung cancer. She was convinced that the lung cancer resulted from her husband’s occupation as a printer’s helper. Her husband had one of his lungs removed, he was in very poor health and he was in a nursing home. I met her husband at the nursing home and spoke with him about his work. He described how many inks and chemicals he breathed all day working around large printing presses. He also described how he would blow his nose after coming home from work, and the color of the ink he was working with that day would come out on his handkerchief. I agreed to take the case. He died soon after that from lung cancer, and the case proceeded as a widow’s benefit case under Ohio workers’ compensation law.

I worked closely with another attorney in the office to prepare the case for trial. We shot video of the inside of the printing plant to show the working conditions. We went through a listing of the hundreds of inks and chemicals used in the printing plant to find those that could cause lung cancer. We found what we were looking for. I found a printing press expert who testified how the printing process resulted in a fine ink/chemical mist that workers were exposed to and breathed. A toxicologist testified that the chemicals and inks had carcinogenic properties. An occupational medicine doctor testified that the inks and chemicals used by the printing company caused the husband’s lung cancer. The husband’s cancer doctor also testified at the trial.

Finally, my client, the lady who had first contacted me months earlier, had her chance to testify. It was very emotional for her, but she did a great job. The verdict of the court was that her husband’s lung cancer resulted from his work as a printers’ helper. She would now receive a widow’s benefit for the rest of her life. The money she received was important to her, but I believe what was more important to her was that she had proved that her husband’s death need not have occurred. That was the most important thing for me too. The sincerity of her thanks to me at the conclusion of the case made everything worthwhile and is something I’ll always remember.

attorneys.name: Peter Scranton
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Peter J. Scranton is a Partner at Bowen, Scranton and Olsen, where he works primarily in criminal defense. He has handled cases throughout the country and in 83 of the 88 counties in the State of Ohio. He has represented clients in over 200 jury trials in the last 20 years.

Mr. Scranton graduated from the Moritz College of Law at The Ohio State University and began his legal career as a prosecutor with the Columbus City Attorney’s Office. He gained experience handling cases that ranged from OVI to domestic violence. He also spent three years as the environmental prosecutor for the Columbus City Attorney’s Office working on criminal cases involving animal abuse and neglect.

Mr. Scranton went on to work for The Ohio State University representing students and faculty in a wide range of criminal and civil matters. He taught courses at the school as part of the Ohio States’ First Year Success Series and STEP programs. He has taught courses with both high school and college mock trial programs and as part of a program by the Interfraternity Council, he speaks to fraternities and sororities on campus on subjects ranging from hazing to knowing and understanding their criminal rights.

Mr. Scranton has presented at several National Legal Aid & Defender Association’s national conferences on defending the rights of clients and was also the feature presenter at the Ohio State’s Leadership Awards Banquet. He is certified by the Columbus Division of Police in Standardized Field Sobriety Testing and by the Ohio Department of Public Safety in advanced detection, apprehension, and prosecution. He has handled appeals both in prosecuting and defending clients throughout the different districts in Ohio and the Supreme Court.

He has also been an advisor for several Buck-I-Serv trips that take a group of 10 or more Ohio State students for a week around the country to do community service work. He has helped with hurricane relief in New Orleans, Louisiana and Biloxi, Mississippi, building homes on Native American reservations in North Carolina, assisted at animal shelters in South Carolina, and worked with K-12 students at the public schools in Vinton County, Ohio. Mr. Scranton dedicates over 100 hours a year to community service.

attorneys.name: Donald P. Screen
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Donald P. Screen's experience includes partnership and service as a senior litigator at major Cleveland law firms and as a federal law clerk to United States District Judge Ann Aldrich. Screen has developed a strong record in both business and tort litigation, and has represented dozens of policyholders and insurers in complex coverage litigation. Screen has fought both for and against major banks, manufacturers, retailers, and service providers. His cases, both individual and class action, have involved civil rights, contract disputes (UCC and other), consumer rights, antitrust and intellectual-property matters, real estate, ERISA and employment-discrimination-and-retaliation disputes, and environmental compliance.

Screen's recent successes include winning an injunction and obtaining a favorable settlement against a major newspaper over its abandonment of healthcare benefits for retirees; a victory in the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals on behalf of a commercial policyholder; a unanimous defense verdict, obtained after a five-day jury trial, in a seven-figure insurance-fraud lawsuit; numerous other motion, trial, and appellate victories; management of an extensive docket of insurance and tort cases for numerous corporate clients, including a big-three automobile manufacturer; and assisting in designing and implementing a commercial general-liability insurance program for the automobile manufacturer. Screen has also been active in the firm's civil-rights, employment, and First Amendment practices.

Screen is a graduate of the University of Virginia School of Law. Before embarking on his legal career, Screen earned his Ph.D. in philosophy, and served as an assistant professor, at the University of Virginia. He has written and lectured on a wide variety of subjects in both law and philosophy.

attorneys.name: Dennis M. Seaman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Dennis Seaman is the founder and managing partner of Dennis Seaman & Associates Co., L.P.A. Dennis has had over 38 years of experience handling cases involving motor vehicle accidents, construction site accidents, premises accidents, defective product claims, medical and professional malpractice claims, nursing home negligence claims, wrongful death claims, workers' compensation claims, job site accident claims, and claims against employers for intentional acts.

Dennis has dedicated his entire legal and personal life adjudicating and protecting the rights of injured workers and citizens. In addition to his professional career of protecting the rights of injured consumers, he has assisted the general community through his involvement in many civic organizations.

My Story:

Coming from a solid working class family Dennis Seaman has a real understanding of the lives of hard working people he represents. He is at his best when he is working for those who need a strong voice to protect their best interests within the legal system.

"I enjoy being an advocate for the downtrodden," says Dennis. "Every life is important to me, no one is insignificant in my eyes. That is why I treat my clients equally, fairly and am proud to call many of them my friends. I get up every day and it is David versus Goliath, and I'm grateful I can provide justice for the people I represent."

It is this sense of responsibility for others that has been the hallmark of Dennis's life. He has selflessly devoted himself to running neighborhood youth groups for the past 30 years. He has taken teens on educational trips overseas, and has personally funded scholarships for needy students.

"I strongly believe in volunteer work and giving back to the community," says Dennis. "It's not always about writing checks. It's about rolling up your sleeves and pitching in. It's a great feeling when you are doing something that you know will have a positive, long lasting impact."

Dennis, a partner in Seaman Garson LLC, is also known to follow a different drummer. "I admire Winston Churchill because he was a statesman, not a politician and said things that he believed in, even though it was not politically expedient for him to do so," Dennis explains. "I've lived my life based upon my own principles, regardless of what anyone thinks about me. I've always been in the minority and that doesn't bother me, as long as I know I am doing the right thing and following my conscience."

Although Dennis enjoys hiking, swimming and the great outdoors, nothing gives him greater pleasure than his nine grandchildren. "One of the most wonderful bonuses my wife and I got from our three children is our grandchildren," he says. "I go to all their plays, baseball and basketball games, piano and dance recitals and soccer practices. As busy as I am, spending time with my grandchildren tops everything else. They make me feel forever young."

attorneys.name: Kaitlyn G. Settergren
attorneys.practice_type: Patents Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
With a foundation in chemistry and biology and hands-on patent experience, Kaitlyn Settergren brings a scientist’s curiosity and a lawyer’s precision to her work at Wood Herron & Evans. She partners with inventors, entrepreneurs, and businesses to help transform complex technical concepts into protected intellectual property assets that support innovation and growth.

A graduate of the University of Cincinnati College of Law and a member of the Ohio Bar, Kaitlyn gained early experience in patent law through the University of Cincinnati Patent & Trademark Clinic, where she conducted prior art searches, prepared patentability memoranda, and guided clients through filing provisional patent applications. That experience sparked her commitment to helping innovators understand the strategic value of IP protection from the very beginning of their journey.

Before joining Wood Herron & Evans, Kaitlyn served as a Law Clerk with Laufman & Napolitano and Spitz, The Employee’s Law Firm, sharpening her skills in legal research, document drafting, and litigation strategy. Earlier, she worked at the intersection of science and technology as a Chemistry Teaching Assistant at Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis (IUPUI) and as a Biomedical Engineering Laboratory Assistant at the Roudebush VA Medical Center, where she supported 3D bioprinting and tissue engineering research.

Kaitlyn earned her B.S. in Chemistry with a Minor in Biology from IUPUI. Outside her practice, she remains dedicated to community engagement through her long-time volunteer work with the Feast of Plenty Food Drive in Greenfield, Indiana.

attorneys.name: Joseph W. Shea III
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Lebanon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Joe is one of the most successful and experienced trial attorneys in the Midwest. Over the past several decades, Joe recovered record breaking verdicts in several local counties for victims of medical malpractice and their families – including verdicts of $8.3 million in Hamilton County, $6.5 million in Butler County, and $5.4 million in the Eastern District of Kentucky Federal Court in Kenton County. In two of these three listed cases, other attorneys and law firms declined to pursue the matter because they did not believe they could win the case. In most of Joe’s cases, favorable settlements are reached to help families cope with lifelong injury and loss. Joe is also called upon at times by the Ohio Attorney General (OAG) over the past decade. When he is called in by the OAG, it is to represent the state of Ohio as lead counsel in complicated litigation matters under the designation of “Special Counsel to the OAG”. In the past decade he recovered more than $6.5M in just two cases alone.

Based on his advocacy for his clients and their families, Joe has numerous accolades including listings in the following publications: “Leading Lawyer” by Cincy Magazine each year for more than a decade, Best Lawyers in America in fields of Personal Injury and Medical Malpractice each year for more than two decades, “Best Lawyers in the Tristate” by Cincinnati Business Courier each year for more than a decade, and Ohio Super Lawyers “Top 50 Cincinnati and/or Top 100 Ohio” more 20 times since the designation began. Joe also received the Ohio State Bar Association’s Ritter Award, which is given annually to only one of Ohio's 50,000 lawyers or alternatively to one law-related organization for the accomplishment of the highest degree of professionalism, ethics, and contribution to the legal profession.

Joe and his wife have three children and in his spare time he enjoys boating on the Great Lakes and road biking.

attorneys.name: Robert B. Sherwood
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Robert’s practice specializes in complex civil and class action litigation. He has nearly 20 years of experience representing both plaintiffs and defendants, in state and federal courts, at both the trial and appellate court levels, in consumer fraud, product liability, insurance coverage, antitrust, securities, and commercial disputes.

Prior to joining Goldenberg Schneider, LPA, Robert was an associate with a large Cleveland-based corporate law firm and, prior to that, a small Philadelphia-based boutique firm specializing in antitrust class actions.

Robert has served as a member of legal teams prosecuting multi-million dollar class actions throughout the United States, including F-150 Spark Plug and 5.4 Liter Engine Defect Litigation, Mercedes Diesel Emission Fraud Litigation, Continental Casualty Long Term Care Insurance Litigation, City of Cincinnati Pension Litigation, Vitamix Blender Litigation, U.S. Bank Mortgage Satisfaction Litigation, Honda Odyssey Infotainment Litigation, Acura RDX Infotainment Litigation, Plantronics Headphones Litigation, Bose Soundsport Headphones Litigation, Navy Federal Credit Union TCPA Litigation, Hill’s Dog Food Litigation, In re Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) Antitrust Litigation, In re Carbon Black Antitrust Litigation, and In re OSB Antitrust Litigation.

Robert received his Bachelor of Arts in 1999 from Bucknell University, from which he graduated magna cum laude with Phi Beta Kappa honors. After earning his Juris Doctor from the University of Pennsylvania in 2002, he subsequently served as law clerk to the Honorable Jerome O. Herlihy of the Superior Court of Delaware. Robert is admitted to practice in the State of Ohio and the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, the United States District Courts for the Southern District of Ohio and Eastern District of Pennsylvania.

attorneys.name: William D. (Bill) Sherman
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Bill Sherman is a partner at Robbins, Kelly, Patterson & Tucker. Bill has been with the firm his entire career, starting as a law clerk in 1992 and is currently the President of the firm.

Bill's practice is focused on estate and personal planning as well as estate and trust administration. Bill has an expertise in estate tax planning and business succession planning. He has been involved in the successful business transition planning for RKPT clients transferring ownership in operating businesses. This planning involves a thorough review of both tax and non-tax issues, including asset protection, to ensure the success of the transition.

Bill has been active in working with many charitable organizations, including previously serving on the planned giving committees of the Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Gardens and the University of Cincinnati Foundation as well as serving on the Project Paradise Committee at McNicholas High School. Bill is currently involved as a member of the advisory board for a local non-profit, May We Help and is also serving on the Cincinnati Children's Hospital Foundation Board.

Bill practices from the firm's downtown Cincinnati office, but is also available in the firm's Mason office.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Meet Attorney Tyler Shroyer, a dedicated and experienced lawyer with a passion for helping those in need.

After earning his law degree from the Catholic University of America, Tyler began his career as a county prosecutor, where he honed his skills as a trial lawyer and developed a deep understanding of the criminal justice system.

In his time as a prosecutor, Tyler handled a wide range of cases, from minor traffic offenses to serious felonies. He was known for his tireless work ethic and his commitment to seeking justice for victims of crime.

Today, Tyler uses his extensive legal knowledge and trial experience to help those who have been injured by the negligence of others. As a personal injury and medical malpractice attorney, he fights tirelessly on behalf of his clients to help them secure the compensation they deserve.

Tyler is a dedicated and compassionate advocate who is committed to providing his clients with the highest level of legal representation. He is licensed to practice law in Ohio and is a member of the Ohio State Bar Association.

When he is not working, Tyler enjoys spending time with his family, traveling, and playing golf with friends.

attorneys.name: David I. Shroyer
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
David Shroyer was born on June 2, 1955 in Middletown Ohio. He attended the Ohio State University and graduated in 1977. He attended Capital University Law School and graduated cum laude in 1980. He grew up in Troy Ohio and graduated from Troy High School in 1973.

''Assistant Franklin County Prosecutor''

He was an Assistant Franklin Prosecutor from 1980 until April 1982. In 1981 he was assigned to assist Senior Assistant Prosecutor Tom Beal to investigate and prosecute Dr. Donald Plotnick. Dr Plotnick, a podiatrist, with a past record of gun charges was indicted on arson charges relating to lighting a drug dealer on fire in the attempt to collect a drug debt. The prosecution resulted in a guilty verdict in spite of the victim developing sudden amnesia at trial. In 1982 David was hired as an Assistant United States Attorney assigned to the Southern District of Ohio.

''Assistant United States Attorney''

He served as an Assistant United States Attorney from 1982 to 1989. He prosecuted federal crimes involving drug conspiracies, organized crime, counterfeiting activity, white collar crime and political corruption. He prosecuted major drug conspiracy cases under the RICO statute that resulted in substantial prison sentences and forfeitures of property and money to the government. His political corruption prosecutions included: the city manager of Upper Arlington Ohio and associated contractors, the city law director and fire chief of Steubenville Ohio, and police narcotic detectives in Dayton Ohio. His organized crime prosecutions included a bombing over a gambling territorial dispute. As an AUSA he tried over 50 criminal prosecutions to verdict.

During his tenor as an the Assistant United States Attorney in the Southern District of Ohio he often taught at the Attorney General's Advocacy Institute in Washington DC instructing other AUSA's on trial advocacy techniques. He also taught FBI agents on how to survive cross examination at the FBI's Quantico, Virginia training facility. He received the Attorney of the Year Award in the Southern District of Ohio in 1988.

Trial Attorney with Colley Shroyer Abraham

David joined Michael F Colley as a trial lawyer in 1989. Michael F Colley is the Past President of the American Trial Lawyers of America and ABOTA. Mr Colley also served as Chairman of the State Republican Party and long time Franklin County Chairman. The firm was renamed Colley Shroyer Abraham in 1998. As a trial lawyer David Shroyer has tried over 75 civil jury trials to verdict. He primarily limits his practice to medical negligence prosecutions. He has argued three cases before the Ohio Supreme Court involving issue of immunity and trial procedures.

He has obtained numerous medical negligence jury verdicts in excess of $1,000,000. His jury verdicts include: an $8,600,000 jury award in a medical negligence case for a woman who lost partial vision from pseudotumor cerebri; a $3,200,000 jury in a medical negligence case resulting in an award for a woman you lost part of her arm due to a blood clot; a $1,800,000 jury verdict for the wrongful death of a 32 year old mother of two who was killed in an auto accident; a $1,600,000 jury verdict for the wrongful death of a grandmother in a head on collision; a $1,800,000 jury verdict n a medical negligence case for involving the death of a young man relating to a subdural hematoma, a $2,700,000 bench verdict in a medical negligence case for a young child who suffered loss of limbs from untreated meningitis, an $828,000 jury verdict in a medical negligence case for injury to the median nerve, a $374,000 jury verdict for an arm injury due to failure to properly interpret an x ray, a $506,000 jury verdict in a medical negligence case for a 60 year old man for failure to diagnosis a bladder obstruction, a $500,000 jury verdict for a woman who suffered an injury from an intubation.

Mr Shroyer has also settled numerous substantial medical malpractice claims including a $9,700,000 settlement against Ohio State University and it's physician for negligence that caused a brain injury and persistent vegetative state of young girl who was recovering from Guillain Barre Syndrome. Other significant settlements include $2,000,000 for a patient who contracted undiagnosed Wernicke's encephalopathy, $1,200,000 legionella case against Ohio State University, $975,000 wrongful death settlement due to respiratory arrest from indiscriminate use of dilaudid by nurses, $1,200,000 in prejudgment interest against a medical malpractice insurer who failed to negotiate in good faith, $1,000,000 for a woman who suffered partial paralysis from a nerve ablation, $950,000 for the 18 month wrongful imprisonment of a teenager wrongfully accused of murdering his twin, $1,500,000 settlement against city for failing to properly respond to a 911 call resulting in the death of a 10 year old girl suffering an allergy attack, $1,200,000 settlement for loss of vision in an infant due to failure to monitor retinopathy of prematurity, $1,000,000 settlement for failure to do genetic testing of leukemia patient, $1,700,000 wrongful death due failure to diagnosis leukemia, $2,250,000 form loss of vision, $2,000,000 for wrongful death of a mother after an outpatient plastic surgery and hysterectomy, $1,000,000 for a wrongful death after breast augmentation and plastic surgery.

Adjunct Professor

David Shroyer has served as an adjunct professor of law teaching trial advocacy at Capital University Law School since 1986. He has taught nearly 1000 students how to try lawsuits. His students have gone to become trial lawyers and state court judges and many have been involved important litigation in Ohio and across the United States. David regularly lectures on the subject of trial advocacy. In December 2009 he presented a seven hour legal education seminar on "Cross Examination". In 2012 he presented a four hour presentation on the "Principles of Cross Examination" to 100 lawyers at the Franklin County Courthouse. In 2013 he lectured at the Ohio State Bar Association to attorneys on the "Anatomy of a Medical Malpractice Case" From 1989 to present he has routinely demonstrated trial advocacy skill in the "Master in Trial" CLE sponsored by the American Board of Trial Advocates.

Author

He is the author of "Mastering the Principles of Trial Advocacy". This is a 360 page book dealing with all aspects of trial advocacy.

Memberships and Legal Service

David Shroyer served as President of the Ohio Chapter of American Board of Trial Advocates. He was also elected twice to serve on the board of commissions for the Columbus Bar Association. In addition Mr Shroyer belongs to the American Association for Justice, the Ohio Association for Justice and the Central Ohio Association for Justice. Appointed by Senator Brown to serve on the screening and recommendation committee for federal judicial nominees for the Northern District of Ohio. He served on the Ohio Supreme Court Rules Committee for two terms.

Personal Life

He is married to Judge Susan Brown, a Court of Appeals Judge in the 10th District of Ohio. They enjoy traveling the world including recent trips to Myanmar, China, Cambodia, India, Dubai and Egypt. In 2001 he and his wife traveled to China on a Capital University Judicial delegation to meet with and teach principles of American law to Chinese judicial officers in Shanghai and Beijing. In 2015, they traveled to the Hague to attend a CLE conference on the inner workings of the United Nation's War Crimes Tribunal. They have one son, Tyler, who is an attorney at the Franklin County Prosecutor's Office.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
David Shroyer was born on June 2, 1955 in Middletown Ohio. He attended the Ohio State University and graduated in 1977. He attended Capital University Law School and graduated cum laude in 1980. He grew up in Troy Ohio and graduated from Troy High School in 1973.

''Assistant Franklin County Prosecutor''

He was an Assistant Franklin Prosecutor from 1980 until April 1982. In 1981 he was assigned to assist Senior Assistant Prosecutor Tom Beal to investigate and prosecute Dr. Donald Plotnick. Dr Plotnick, a podiatrist, with a past record of gun charges was indicted on arson charges relating to lighting a drug dealer on fire in the attempt to collect a drug debt. The prosecution resulted in a guilty verdict in spite of the victim developing sudden amnesia at trial. In 1982 David was hired as an Assistant United States Attorney assigned to the Southern District of Ohio.

''Assistant United States Attorney''

He served as an Assistant United States Attorney from 1982 to 1989. He prosecuted federal crimes involving drug conspiracies, organized crime, counterfeiting activity, white collar crime and political corruption. He prosecuted major drug conspiracy cases under the RICO statute that resulted in substantial prison sentences and forfeitures of property and money to the government. His political corruption prosecutions included: the city manager of Upper Arlington Ohio and associated contractors, the city law director and fire chief of Steubenville Ohio, and police narcotic detectives in Dayton Ohio. His organized crime prosecutions included a bombing over a gambling territorial dispute. As an AUSA he tried over 50 criminal prosecutions to verdict.

During his tenor as an the Assistant United States Attorney in the Southern District of Ohio he often taught at the Attorney General's Advocacy Institute in Washington DC instructing other AUSA's on trial advocacy techniques. He also taught FBI agents on how to survive cross examination at the FBI's Quantico, Virginia training facility. He received the Attorney of the Year Award in the Southern District of Ohio in 1988.

Trial Attorney with Colley Shroyer Abraham

David joined Michael F Colley as a trial lawyer in 1989. Michael F Colley is the Past President of the American Trial Lawyers of America and ABOTA. Mr Colley also served as Chairman of the State Republican Party and long time Franklin County Chairman. The firm was renamed Colley Shroyer Abraham in 1998. As a trial lawyer David Shroyer has tried over 75 civil jury trials to verdict. He primarily limits his practice to medical negligence prosecutions. He has argued three cases before the Ohio Supreme Court involving issue of immunity and trial procedures.

He has obtained numerous medical negligence jury verdicts in excess of $1,000,000. His jury verdicts include: an $8,600,000 jury award in a medical negligence case for a woman who lost partial vision from pseudotumor cerebri; a $3,200,000 jury in a medical negligence case resulting in an award for a woman you lost part of her arm due to a blood clot; a $1,800,000 jury verdict for the wrongful death of a 32 year old mother of two who was killed in an auto accident; a $1,600,000 jury verdict for the wrongful death of a grandmother in a head on collision; a $1,800,000 jury verdict n a medical negligence case for involving the death of a young man relating to a subdural hematoma, a $2,700,000 bench verdict in a medical negligence case for a young child who suffered loss of limbs from untreated meningitis, an $828,000 jury verdict in a medical negligence case for injury to the median nerve, a $374,000 jury verdict for an arm injury due to failure to properly interpret an x ray, a $506,000 jury verdict in a medical negligence case for a 60 year old man for failure to diagnosis a bladder obstruction, a $500,000 jury verdict for a woman who suffered an injury from an intubation.

Mr Shroyer has also settled numerous substantial medical malpractice claims including a $9,700,000 settlement against Ohio State University and it's physician for negligence that caused a brain injury and persistent vegetative state of young girl who was recovering from Guillain Barre Syndrome. Other significant settlements include $2,000,000 for a patient who contracted undiagnosed Wernicke's encephalopathy, $1,200,000 legionella case against Ohio State University, $975,000 wrongful death settlement due to respiratory arrest from indiscriminate use of dilaudid by nurses, $1,200,000 in prejudgment interest against a medical malpractice insurer who failed to negotiate in good faith, $1,000,000 for a woman who suffered partial paralysis from a nerve ablation, $950,000 for the 18 month wrongful imprisonment of a teenager wrongfully accused of murdering his twin, $1,500,000 settlement against city for failing to properly respond to a 911 call resulting in the death of a 10 year old girl suffering an allergy attack, $1,200,000 settlement for loss of vision in an infant due to failure to monitor retinopathy of prematurity, $1,000,000 settlement for failure to do genetic testing of leukemia patient, $1,700,000 wrongful death due failure to diagnosis leukemia, $2,250,000 form loss of vision, $2,000,000 for wrongful death of a mother after an outpatient plastic surgery and hysterectomy, $1,000,000 for a wrongful death after breast augmentation and plastic surgery.

Adjunct Professor

David Shroyer has served as an adjunct professor of law teaching trial advocacy at Capital University Law School since 1986. He has taught nearly 1000 students how to try lawsuits. His students have gone to become trial lawyers and state court judges and many have been involved important litigation in Ohio and across the United States. David regularly lectures on the subject of trial advocacy. In December 2009 he presented a seven hour legal education seminar on "Cross Examination". In 2012 he presented a four hour presentation on the "Principles of Cross Examination" to 100 lawyers at the Franklin County Courthouse. In 2013 he lectured at the Ohio State Bar Association to attorneys on the "Anatomy of a Medical Malpractice Case" From 1989 to present he has routinely demonstrated trial advocacy skill in the "Master in Trial" CLE sponsored by the American Board of Trial Advocates.

Author

He is the author of "Mastering the Principles of Trial Advocacy". This is a 360 page book dealing with all aspects of trial advocacy.

Memberships and Legal Service

David Shroyer served as President of the Ohio Chapter of American Board of Trial Advocates. He was also elected twice to serve on the board of commissions for the Columbus Bar Association. In addition Mr Shroyer belongs to the American Association for Justice, the Ohio Association for Justice and the Central Ohio Association for Justice. Appointed by Senator Brown to serve on the screening and recommendation committee for federal judicial nominees for the Northern District of Ohio. He served on the Ohio Supreme Court Rules Committee for two terms.

Personal Life

He is married to Judge Susan Brown, a Court of Appeals Judge in the 10th District of Ohio. They enjoy traveling the world including recent trips to Myanmar, China, Cambodia, India, Dubai and Egypt. In 2001 he and his wife traveled to China on a Capital University Judicial delegation to meet with and teach principles of American law to Chinese judicial officers in Shanghai and Beijing. In 2015, they traveled to the Hague to attend a CLE conference on the inner workings of the United Nation's War Crimes Tribunal. They have one son, Tyler, who is an attorney at the Franklin County Prosecutor's Office.

attorneys.name: Matthew Shupe
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security Disability Lawyers in Mentor, OH
attorneys.bio:
Matt is an experienced disability litigator selected by his peers for SuperLawyers' annual Ohio Rising Stars recognition every year for the past 8 years. The Rising Stars list recognizes no more than 2.5 percent of attorneys in Ohio. To be eligible for inclusion in Rising Stars, a candidate must be either 40 years old or younger, or in practice for 10 years or less.

Why does Matt practice disability law?

I started practicing disability law because I enjoy fighting for the little guy and I can relate to how a person's health can derail an entire family. I come from a solidly blue-collar background and did not even know what a lawyer was when my uncle was in a terrible accident in 1993 that left him permanently disabled. I remember how confused we all were when the government denied his application for Social Security Disability benefits after many months of waiting. It was pretty clear to our family that a person who could not walk to the bathroom without severe pain could not be expected to work a full-time job. Thankfully, a lawyer working for the Legal Aid Society stepped in to help my family navigate the application process. Recently, my dad needed to apply for Social Security Disability because his body wore out after 40+ years of heavy labor. I took great pride in being able to assist my dad when he needed help the most. So, I’ve personally experienced the fear folks feel upon losing their livelihood and want to help.

What is Matt's role at the firm?

Although my primary focus is creating good legal precedents for disability claimants through federal litigation, I also frequently meet with new clients at many of our eight offices located throughout Northern Ohio and represent clients at their administrative hearings. Balin Law, LLC is here to service all of Ohio with Social Security Disability Insurance and SSI claims. We pride ourselves on compassion and client convenience with offices in Ashtabula, Beachwood, Canton, Cleveland, Cuyahoga Falls, Sheffield Village, Mentor [Our HQ], Toledo, and Youngstown.

attorneys.name: Michele Simonelli Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Rocky River, OH
attorneys.bio:
With more than two decades of experience practicing law in both the private and public sectors, Michele Simonelli brings extensive legal knowledge, strategic insight, and compassionate representation to every client she serves. She focuses her practice on family law, including divorce, dissolution, child custody, child support, parenting time disputes, and other emotionally complex domestic relations matters.

Michele previously served as a Judicial Staff Attorney for the Ohio District Courts of Appeals for both the Eleventh and Seventh Districts, where she researched and drafted judicial opinions for a three-judge panel in a wide range of cases, including criminal and civil matters. This appellate experience sharpened her legal analysis and writing skills and gave her a strong foundation for navigating high-stakes litigation.

In private practice, Michele has spent over a decade representing clients in high-conflict family law cases, including custody disputes, parental alienation, and complex divorce matters involving closely held businesses, hidden assets, or financial misconduct. She also has a strong background in cases involving LGBTQIA+ families and is committed to providing inclusive, respectful representation to all clients.

Michele approaches every case with discretion, empathy, and a deep understanding of how legal challenges affect the personal lives of her clients. Her background in psychology and counseling allows her to communicate effectively and build trust with individuals navigating what may be one of the most difficult times in their lives.

In addition to practicing law, Michele teaches courses on First Amendment and Privacy Law at Kent State University. Her outside interests include cycling, kayaking, hiking, and urban exploring.

attorneys.practice_type: Immigration Law Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Rea Singh is an Associate Attorney at The Nigh Law Group, where she primarily practices family law. She graduated from The Ohio State University in 2017 and earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Cincinnati College of Law in 2020.

Prior to joining the firm, Rea largely practiced immigration law, gaining extensive experience advocating for individuals and families navigating complex legal systems. Through that work, she developed a strong understanding of the significant intersection between immigration and family law, particularly in matters where family relationships directly impact immigration status and stability.

Passionate about helping people through some of the most challenging times in their lives, Rea is committed to serving her clients with compassion, diligence, and unwavering advocacy. She strives to protect her clients’ best interests while providing clear guidance and effective solutions tailored to their unique circumstances.

In addition to practicing family law, Rea intends to continue handling immigration matters, allowing her to offer comprehensive representation to clients whose legal needs span both areas.

attorneys.name: Louis H. Sitler
attorneys.practice_type: Mechanical & Aerospace Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Louis Sitler is an Associate with Wood, Herron & Evans and is part of the Mechanical and Aerospace practice group. Louis counsels clients on all aspects of intellectual property law, and primarily focuses on patent matters including U.S., international, and foreign patent preparation and prosecution, as well as patentability, infringement, and clearance investigations. Louis has experience in a variety of technology areas with a primary focus on matters in the mechanical arts.

Louis also has experience in post-grant proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. With a strong technical foundation, he represents both patent owners and petitioners in establishing positions before the PTAB for patents that are often in patent litigation.

Louis received his B.S. in mechanical engineering from the University of Dayton, where he graduated with a concentration in renewable energy systems. He earned his J.D. from the University of Dayton School of Law, where he was part of the Program in Law and Technology and served as president of the Intellectual Property Law Society.

attorneys.name: David W. Skall
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
David's interest helping medical malpractice and personal injury victims started early in life when his mother passed away of breast cancer. Aside from deep sadness, his family felt that her doctor made mistakes and should have detected her cancer earlier. The event got him thinking about what the doctor should have done and, more importantly, all that his mom and family lost from the mistake. Wanting to understand how the law worked in taking care of people who suffer life-changing events from the mistakes of others, the event ultimately lead him to law school and has stuck with him throughout his years of practice.

He joined a small personal injury firm out of law school to get immediate experience in preparing and conducting trials in auto accident cases and others involving medical errors. To better craft his trial skills, he moved to a large Cleveland area firm where he worked for 7 years defending hospitals, physicians, nursing homes and medical device makers in cases of alleged malpractice. His cases often involved people who unfortunately died or were disabled as the result of errors in medical care, and even infants and children who suffered crippling injuries at birth or early in life. This work allowed him to gain expert trial training in matters involving the most severe injuries, where the damages sought were often several million dollars.

In 2008, David got back to representing injury victims and their families when he joined a firm in Virginia that represented railroad workers throughout the country who were either killed or disabled from accidents they suffered at work. Despite several great trial successes in representing injured railroaders, David and his wife missed their extended families and hometown friends, and later decided to relocate back to Ohio, where he joined the formidable team at the Becker Law Firm in 2012. Like the Becker Law Firm, David's approach to helping personal injury victims involves two things: (1) intense client communication; and (2) relentless preparation during investigation and throughout a lawsuit. By understanding his clients' experiences as if they were his own, he is able to best teach trial juries about accident victims and their families, their hardships, the wrongs of the events that cause them, and how his clients' lives are forever changed.

INTERESTS/HOBBIES

When he is not working, you can generally find David either working in his yard tinkering with some repair, at a youth soccer game, or out at a park walking the dog with his family. He also considers himself a seasoned "Pitmaster", and enjoys grilling and preparing meals with his wife, Heather, who runs her own food service business and is an outstanding cook!

Awards and Honors

Honors

"Rising Star," Law & Politics, Ohio Super Lawyers Magazine, 2007

Invited Delegate, Eighth District Judicial Conference on Legal Policymaking in Ohio, 2006

She brings to the firm experience in complex domestic litigation; motions and trial practice; mediation and settlement negotiations; and contract drafting. She also enjoys the challenges of financial investigations and novel questions of law. A proud step-parent, Julia particularly values opportunities to help clients as their families grow and change.

attorneys.bio:
Archie W. Skidmore (1926–2025)

Founder (In Memoriam)

Skidmore & Associates Co., LPA — Akron, Ohio

Status:

In Memoriam — Retired from the practice of law upon his passing on October 2, 2025.

Biography

Archie W. Skidmore was the founder of Skidmore & Associates Co., LPA and practiced law in Akron, Ohio for nearly 70 years. Born in 1926 in West Virginia and raised in Akron, he devoted his life to serving the legal needs of families, individuals, and businesses throughout Summit County. Archie began his legal career in 1955 and continued practicing with unwavering commitment, integrity, and professionalism until shortly before his passing in 2025.

Archie was the recipient of the Akron Bar Association’s Distinguished Professionalism Award, a recognition reserved for attorneys who embody the highest standards of ethical practice and service. For decades, he was known for his meticulous preparation, principled advocacy, and deep respect for the practice of law.

He became a mentor to countless Akron attorneys — including each of his three sons, who proudly followed him into the profession and continue the family firm today.

His legacy endures through the continued work of:

Eric E. Skidmore, Family Law & Domestic Relations

Brian K. Skidmore, Real Estate & Construction Law

Thomas Skidmore [Thomas A. Skidmore Co.,L.P.A.] Personal Injury and Business Litigation

Spiros Vasilatos, Jr., Probate & Estate Planning

Skidmore & Associates honors his life’s work, his service to the Akron legal community, and the extraordinary example he set.

Professional Legacy

Nearly seven decades of continuous legal practice

Founder of Skidmore & Associates Co., LPA

Akron Bar Association Professionalism Award recipient

Pioneer of a multi-generational family law practice

Respected mentor to attorneys throughout Northeast Ohio

Known for integrity, preparation, and unwavering dedication to clients

Archie believed the purpose of practicing law was to solve problems with compassion, fairness, and careful analysis. His values continue to shape the firm’s culture and approach.

In Memoriam

Archie’s passing in 2025 marked the conclusion of an extraordinary legal career, but not the end of his influence. His legacy lives on through his children, his colleagues, and the firm he built — and through the countless families and clients he served with distinction over nearly 70 years.

Akron Divorce & Family Law Attorney | Complex Assets | Custody | Support

Eric E. Skidmore is a family law attorney with more than 35 years of experience representing clients in divorce, dissolution, custody, parenting plans, spousal support, and the division of complex marital assets throughout Summit County and Northeast Ohio. Born and raised in Akron, he continues the legacy of his father, Archie W. Skidmore, who founded the firm in 1955 and practiced law for seven decades.

Eric focuses his family law practice on:

Divorce and dissolution

High-asset and complex property division

Business and professional practice valuation

Executive compensation, stock options & RSUs

Retirement account division (QDROs & DOPOs)

Child custody & shared parenting

Temporary orders and emergency relief

Post-decree enforcement and modifications

His early career representing real estate developers, commercial creditors, condominium associations, and business owners gives him unique expertise in complex asset division and financial analysis.

Approach

Eric provides steady, analytical, and solution-focused representation. He guides clients through the emotional and legal challenges of divorce with clarity and preparation. His philosophy is rooted in the belief that while a marriage may end, family bonds — particularly between parents and children — must endure.

Local Court Experience

Eric has decades of experience in Summit County Domestic Relations Court, and he understands the local procedures, judicial expectations, and practical strategies that help clients achieve stable long-term outcomes.

Education & Background

Practicing law since 1989

Extensive experience in complex civil, commercial, and domestic litigation

Multi-generational Akron attorney dedicated to service and professionalism

Eric considers it an honor to represent individuals during pivotal moments in their lives and to help clients move forward with strength, stability, and confidence.

Eric offers a comprehensive initial consultation for a flat fee of $250, which covers a 45–60 minute strategy session!

During this meeting, we will:

• Review your legal situation in detail

• Identify key legal issues and potential risks

• Provide preliminary guidance on property, custody, and support matters

• Outline next steps and strategic options

If you choose to retain our firm within 30 days, this consultation fee will be credited toward your retainer.

attorneys.name: David Slepski
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Combining a Blue-Collar Upbringing with a Knack for Law to Advocate for Injured Workers

David Slepski is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Building on an upbringing in blue-collar Ohio and drawing from a background in the trades, service sector, and workers’ compensation law, David combines an essential mix of working-class relatability and impressive legal knowledge and strategy to get results for injured Ohio workers.

From the Trades to Law School to Workers’ Compensation Law

Born and raised near Youngstown, David is the son of a teacher and a medical worker. With all four grandparents working in auto and steel manufacturing, David grew up around blue-collar workers who faced a high risk of injury simply by showing up to work every day. Throughout high school, undergrad, and law school, David worked as a cashier at Sam’s Club, a gas station clerk, and a Sherwin-Williams paint store associate. He served as an intern in the U.S. and Ohio State Houses, and provided clerking and receptionist services for law firms.

“As I went through high school and college, I felt drawn towards law,” David says. “Given my work background and my upbringing near Youngstown, I learned early on that my calling was to become a workers’ compensation attorney so I could advocate for those who have been injured in the line of work.”

David graduated from the University of Cincinnati with a bachelor’s degree in international relations. He earned his law degree from Capital University and his Essential Legal Research license and certification through Thomson Reuters.

Working Closely with Clients to Win Fair Compensation

David represents NRS Injury Law’s clients from the firm’s Cincinnati office, though he has connections with doctors and providers in Columbus, Dayton, Cleveland, Youngstown, and across the state. “I’ve always wanted to help people,” David mentioned, reflecting on the trajectory that brought him to his role at NRS Injury Law. “I realized pretty early on that the legal field was my best vehicle for being hands-on with my goal to improve others’ lives and secure tangible results for them.”

David works closely with his clients throughout every step of the workers’ compensation process. He fully understands the emotional and psychological costs of being injured at work, costs that go well above and beyond the physical injury. “I understand what my clients are going through because their lived experience is my background and upbringing,” he said. “Being able to relate to my clients, stand on equal footing with them, and work cohesively as a team, those aspects being in place allow us to work together to craft winning cases that will get them the benefits they’re entitled to.”

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working at the firm’s Cincinnati office or traveling throughout Ohio to meet with clients, David spends his free time with his wife and their daughter. David is a lifelong Cincinnati Reds and Bearcats fan, but as much as he loves a good evening attending a sports game, he also enjoys quality time at home with the family. David also cherishes family trips to Mauritius to visit his wife’s parents and extended family.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from David Slepski

To David, one of the most critical puzzle pieces in building winning cases for injured workers is harnessing institutional knowledge while simultaneously leveraging connections with physicians, examiners, and other industry experts throughout the state. “Whether or not you have the resources you need will often make or break your case,” David says. “NRS Injury Law is the largest workers’ compensation law firm in Ohio and has done what no other firm has: fostered meaningful connections with doctors, examiners, legislators, hearing officers, judges, justices, and every possible opinion leader you can imagine in the workers’ compensation space. The firm’s vast institutional knowledge combined with its statewide outreach makes it unstoppable when it comes to representing injured workers and ensuring they receive the compensation they deserve.”

David’s work ethic, tenacity, and attention to detail align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with David and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

He fully understands the emotional and psychological costs of being injured at work, costs that go well above and beyond the physical injury. “I understand what my clients are going through because their lived experience is my background and upbringing,” he said. “Being able to relate to my clients, stand on equal footing with them, and work cohesively as a team, those aspects being in place allow us to work together to craft winning cases that will get them the benefits they’re entitled to.”

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not working at the firm’s Cincinnati office or traveling throughout Ohio to meet with clients, David spends his free time with his wife and their daughter. David is a lifelong Cincinnati Reds and Bearcats fan, but as much as he loves a good evening attending a sports game, he also enjoys quality time at home with the family. David also cherishes family trips to Mauritius to visit his wife’s parents and extended family.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from David Slepski

To David, one of the most critical puzzle pieces in building winning cases for injured workers is harnessing institutional knowledge while simultaneously leveraging connections with physicians, examiners, and other industry experts throughout the state. “Whether or not you have the resources you need will often make or break your case,” David says. “NRS Injury Law is the largest workers’ compensation law firm in Ohio and has done what no other firm has: fostered meaningful connections with doctors, examiners, legislators, hearing officers, judges, justices, and every possible opinion leader you can imagine in the workers’ compensation space. The firm’s vast institutional knowledge combined with its statewide outreach makes it unstoppable when it comes to representing injured workers and ensuring they receive the compensation they deserve.”

David’s work ethic, tenacity, and attention to detail align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with David and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.
