attorneys.name: Catherine Twohig
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Helping Injured Workers Secure Compensation

One must be well versed in their field to successfully represent injured workers and help them secure compensation from large, powerful corporations. Katie Lietzke fits that description perfectly. She provides exemplary service for her clients by excelling in all areas of workers’ comp law, including workplace injuries, occupational diseases, safety code violations, permanent and total disability claims, loss of use awards, and death claims.

A Life of Service to Injured Workers and Their Families

Katie joined NRS Injury Law in 2013, building on a legal career that began in 1996. When she accepted a position as Associate Attorney at the firm, Katie began a chapter in her legal career that would see her represent hundreds of injured Ohio workers. Katie has argued cases at all levels of the Industrial Commission, including the full Industrial Commission in Columbus.

Katie has worked closely with her fellow attorneys, paralegals, and case managers at NRS Injury Law to successfully argue workers’ compensation mandamus actions and workers’ compensation cases at the Ohio Supreme Court.

Leveraging Comprehensive Knowledge and Decades of Experience in Workers’ Compensation Law

When asked what inspires her in her career as a workers’ compensation attorney, Katie spoke of her work representing Ohio firefighters. “There was a time when firefighters could rarely secure workers’ compensation for cancer illnesses they sustained as a result of their work,” says Katie. “One of my greatest victories has been successfully arguing for the allowance of cancer in workers’ comp claims.”

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Katie Lietzke

While following in her father’s footsteps as a career attorney and while also being the mother of three children, Katie is passionate about her family’s intergenerational commitment to working people. She is hardworking, diligent, thorough, and committed to securing client results.

Katie’s approach to her cases aligns perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Katie and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

attorneys.name: Kevin C. Urtz
attorneys.practice_type: Family and Juvenile Law Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Kevin C. Urtz is a senior associate attorney at Mockensturm, Ltd. with a primary focus in civil litigation, family and juvenile law, probate administration/estate planning, real estate transactions, and employment law - employer. Kevin represents clients in Ohio and Kentucky state and federal courts in a wide array of civil matters, including contract and business disputes, tax controversies, real estate, tort claims, probate litigation, and employment contract or discrimination claims.

Kevin is a graduate of The University of Akron School of Law. He graduated cum laude and in the top 23% of his class. During law school, he received the CALI Excellence for the Future Award for achieving the highest grade in family law. While in law school, Kevin clerked for two Akron/Cleveland area law firms, volunteered at the Akron Law Expungement Clinic, and served as the Treasurer for the Sports and Entertainment Law Society.

Prior to joining Mockensturm, Ltd., Kevin worked for a law firm in the Cleveland area where he represented clients throughout Northeast Ohio in employment, personal injury, domestic relations, and general litigation matters. He practiced before state courts, federal courts, and administrative agencies, including: the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, Social Security Administration, Ohio Industrial Commission, Ohio Civil Rights Commission, and Department of Veterans Affairs. Kevin was also a certified CASA/Guardian Ad Litem, where he represented and advocated for children in court proceedings, and he was accredited by the Department of Veterans’ Affairs to handle claims for VA disability and pension benefits.

Prior to attending law school at the University of Akron, Kevin received his Bachelor of Arts degree in criminal justice from Seton Hill University in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, where he also played baseball for four years. Kevin currently works out of our Toledo and Louisville locations. When he is not working, Kevin enjoys watching Pittsburgh sports and spending time with his wife and son.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey W. Van Wagner
attorneys.firm_name: Bonezzi Switzer Polito & Hupp Co. L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Health Care Professional Liability Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey Van Wagner is the Managing Shareholder of BSPH. His career as a litigator and trial attorney has now spanned three decades. He is a 1979 graduate of Case Western Reserve School of Law and has extensive litigation and trial experience in the areas of nursing home liability, medical malpractice defense of physicians and institutions and product liability. He has extensive experience in defending physicians and institutions where opioid prescription practices are at issue and is well familiar with the nuances of the learned intermediary doctrine as applied to the sales and marketing of prescription medications.

Mr. Van Wagner's full-service endeavors for his clients also include providing claims and risk management services and presentations for clients, interactions with state and federal agencies, participation in civil and criminal investigations, and pre-suit evaluation and assessment of potential claims. He recently worked with physicians and pharmacists at a major medical provider in Cleveland to develop a pain management protocol for use of opioids in general and methadone induction specifically.

The author of various articles and a frequent presenter to medical, nursing home and insurance clients, he has extensive experience with trials in courtrooms throughout the northern tier of Ohio.

Mr. Van Wagner is a member of the Ohio State Bar as well as the United States District Court of Ohio (Northern and Southern Districts), the Sixth and Fifth District Courts of Appeal.

Mr. Van Wagner was selected as an Ohio Super Lawyer for twelve straight years (2007 through 2018). In 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2018 he was also named as a Cleveland Top 50 and Ohio Top 100 Ohio Super Lawyer. He was also named to "The Best Lawyers in America" for 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2018, the 19th through the 24th Editions in the fields of Medical Malpractice Defense and Health Care Law. Mr. Van Wagner further enjoys an AV Preeminent Five Star rating with Martindale-Hubbell.

David R. Vance joined Zashin & Rich Co., L.P.A. in 2008. David is a member of the firm's Employment and Labor Group and can counsel you through your public and private employment related issues. He understands the intricacies of the employment relationship and has the experience and expertise to solve your legal problems. His clients cover an array of industries and range from national employers with thousands of employees to local employers with only a handful of employees. He regularly practices in state and federal court and is experienced with arbitration and in handling matters before various state and federal agencies.

David was named a 2011 Rising Star in the area of employment and labor law by Super Lawyers. He is editor of the firm's newsletter and regularly contributes to the firm's blog. He is a member of the American Bar Association, the Ohio State Bar Association, the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association, and the West Shore Bar Association.

David received his Bachelor of Business Administration, cum laude, from Ohio University. Prior to practicing law, David worked as a contracting officer for NASA drafting, negotiating, and administering multi-million dollar contracts. David earned his law degree (J.D.) from The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law where he was a Barton Scholar and member of moot court. He was born and raised on the west side of Cleveland where he lives with his growing family.

Asset protection strategies

Elder law issues

His familiarity with Summit County Probate Court allows him to efficiently navigate procedural requirements and streamline the administration process.

Experience

With decades of practice in Akron, Spiros has become a trusted advisor to families seeking stability, protection, and clarity in planning for the future.

attorneys.name: Thomas M. Vasvari
attorneys.practice_type: Car Accidents Lawyers in Poland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Tom Vasvari was born in Struthers, Ohio, where his family worked in steel mills and were active in politics. Tom decided to become an attorney in grade school and has never waivered from this ambition as he has now been practicing law for over 20 years.

After his first semester of law school at Case Western Reserve University, Tom served as a law clerk to a group of prominent Youngstown attorneys. From that experience, he knew he wanted to represent injured people and the "underdogs" who needed an attorney to level an unfair playing field.

After law school, Tom was invited to practice with the same attorneys who employed him as a law clerk. He was also invited to serve as a staff attorney in Ohio's Seventh District Court of Appeals. There he learned from the best (and worst) attorneys as they argued their most complex cases to the appellate court.

Since leaving the Court of Appeals, Tom tried many cases with his mentor and former law partner, Clair M. Carlin. Carlin was president of the Ohio Academy of Trial Lawyers and Tom benefited greatly from serving on the board of trustees and as co-chair of the negligence law committee of that organization. In that capacity, Tom frequently planned and spoke at seminars designed to help attorneys sharpen their trial skills. It was during this time that Tom gained perspective through his role as acting judge in the Struthers Municipal Court. There, he was required to make rulings and decisions on civil and criminal cases.

In 2002, Tom began practicing law with Gary Kisling, Rob Nestico, and Robert Redick. He quickly found they shared a passion for representing injured people who simply need help and for doing what it takes to provide that help. He has since tried many cases with Kisling, Nestico and Redick and has had the opportunity to argue before the Ohio Supreme Court on behalf of Ohio auto insurance consumers.

In 2007, Tom was privileged to take on the opportunity of managing the Youngstown office of KNR - the role in which he currently serves.

attorneys.name: Gayle P. Vojtush
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Gayle Vojtush has handled detailed complex and high stakes cases in personal injury, litigation, and social security areas. She has knowledge and experience with mediations, arbitrations, alternative dispute resolution, bench trials, jury trials, default hearings and administrative law hearings. Gayle is honored to have been selected by The National Trial Lawyers as one of the top 100 Civil Plaintiff attorneys in the United States.

Gayle does incredible work for accident victims because she understands the mechanics of the accident, the medicine behind the injury, the law related to liability, and the damages to the victim. She has handled every kind of injury case imaginable with outstanding results. Gayle will go to trial, and has done so many times for clients. Every attorney would prefer to settle cases, but if the other side is simply being unreasonable during settlement, then Gayle is as comfortable in the courtroom as she is in the boardroom. Gayle's advantage over an attorney that will not go to trial is that she forces the person responsible for your injury to be reasonable, or face a jury.

Gayle believes in giving back to the community, where people value her commitment to the law and levelheaded judgment. Gayle taught the civil trial process as a part time professor at Lakeland Community College in Kirkland, Ohio. She taught Civil Law and Law Office Management and Procedures. Gayle served on the Board of Trustees for Big Brothers & Sisters of Greater Akron, Ohio where she was appointed as one of the Trustees for the Rules and Compliance Committee, and Fund Raising.

Gayle received her law degree from the Cleveland Marshall College of Law, Cleveland, Ohio, where she had Dean's List honors, served on the Moot Court Team, including serving on the Moot Court Board of Governors, and was a member of the Phi Alpha Delta Law Fraternity. She received her undergraduate degree at the University of Akron, Akron, Ohio, where she received a B.S. in Political Science, and an A.A.S. in Criminal Justice Technology.

Phillips Law Firm, Inc. is extremely proud of the work that Gayle has done for clients that need help with their personal injury cases. When you have been injured, you need to talk to Gayle. When you hire an attorney that has been designated as one of the top 100 lawyers in the United States, you can expect outstanding representation.

attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Paul Vollman has been practicing in the area of complex medical malpractice actions at the trial and appellate levels for over 22 years. He is licensed in Ohio, Kentucky, and Florida, in addition to the United States District Court for the Southern District of Ohio and the United States Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals.

Recently he has developed an area of expertise on the issue of subrogation of past medical expenses in tort actions. He has written papers on this topic which have been peer reviewed and appeared in the Kentucky Defense Bar Journal "Common Defense" as well as the DRI National Blog.

Outside of litigation, Paul loves spending time with his wife Sarah and his twin boys Grant and Owen. Paul is also a fine artist represented by galleries locally and regionally.

attorneys.bio:
After graduating from high school, Wayne was a foreign exchange student in Stockholm, Sweden where he met his wife, Christina. Wayne pursued his undergraduate studies at the State University of New York and graduated cum laude in 1979 with a major in Psychology. He graduated from the University of Dayton School of Law, cum laude in 1982. Wayne served on the law review and worked at the school's legal clinic. While in law school, Wayne completed an internship at the City of Kettering Law Department. After graduating from law school, Wayne worked for several years in the corporate law department for Miami Valley Hospital. Thereafter, he served as Vice-President of Human Resources and General Counsel for Fidelity Health Care before entering private practice with the prestigious law firms of Beiser, Greer & Landis and Freund, Freeze and Arnold. As a trial lawyer, Wayne participated in a wide range of cases including medical malpractice, employment and business litigation. During his distinguished career, Wayne has a special interest in probate law and estate planning and has also litigated several probate will contest and undue influence cases. Wayne is licensed to practice in all Ohio State Courts, including Federal Courts in the Southern District of Ohio, the Federal Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals and the United States Supreme Court.

In addition to being active in his local church, he has served as the co-founder and Chairman of the charitable organization Shoulder to Shoulder providing medical, education and nutrition services for resource poor individuals in rural Honduras. In that capacity, Wayne has negotiated and obtained contracts with the Honduran Government to provide health care to over 70,000 Hondurans. He has also negotiated contracts with the Honduran Department of Education for the first public bilingual school in Honduras. Shoulder to Shoulder has deployed computer assisted learning tablets to over 15,000 students in more than 50 public schools. Prior to the pandemic, Shoulder to Shoulder provided micro-nutrient supplementation to over 3,000 children, between 6 months and 6 years of age who were at the risk of malnutrition. That program now provides fresh eggs daily to 300 at risk children. More information about Shoulder to Shoulder may be found at www.shouldertoshoulder.org.

In his free time, Wayne enjoys general aviation. He is a private instrument rated pilot with over 450 hours of flight time. He also serves as an adjunct professor for Sinclair Community College teaching Aviation Law.

Wayne's area of practice includes medical malpractice and personal injury, probate law, business law, aviation law, and municipal law. He has a reputation of a seasoned litigator and problem solver. Wayne is a member of the Greene County, Miami County and Dayton Bar Associations.

He currently resides in Xenia, Ohio with his spouse, Dr. Christina Waite.

attorneys.name: Joshua Waters
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Droder & Miller
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Joshua Waters enjoys helping clients as they make important decisions in life’s journey.

Being trial lawyer requires passion, and he has become known as someone who will fight for justice on behalf of individuals and families harmed by negligence as well as in numerous other areas of law.

Josh has secured millions in verdicts and settlements for his clients. He strives to be a formidable advocate in the courtroom, where he has tried numerous cases to verdict in a wide range of practice areas.

Josh is honored to have been trusted to represent many victims of nursing home negligence, where he has successfully litigated cases involving abuse, neglect, and substandard care that led to severe harm or wrongful death. Holding nursing homes accountable is special because not only has he had victories that compensate families, but it may change the bad care the client received for future residents.

Josh brings the same level of dedication to medical malpractice cases, where he has represented patients and families of patients harmed by healthcare provider negligence. From surgical errors, delayed diagnosis, misdiagnoses, to delayed or improper treatment, he collaborates with medical experts to uncover if the providers provided substandard care. Similar to the work involving long term care facilities, he pushes to hold doctors, hospitals, and clinics accountable while providing clients with the resources needed for recovery and rehabilitation.

Beyond personal injury, Josh has become a trusted advocate in family law matters, having tried high-stakes divorce cases and child custody cases. He guides clients through the emotional and financial complexities of ending a marriage, including asset division, alimony / spousal support, while prioritizing equitable outcomes and protecting long-term stability for those involved.

Licensed in OH and KY, Josh serves clients in a variety of areas, including medical negligence, nursing home abuse & neglect, personal injury, divorce & custody issues, disputes with insurance coverage, business litigation, UCC issues, real estate disputes, & contract disputes.

Aside from his professional career, originally from East Tennessee, Josh lives with his family in Northern Kentucky. Life is constantly busy having young children and in addition to raising their children, they are also foster parents. Many have said, for Josh, the most important “unimportant” thing in his life is the University of Tennessee Volunteers. However, Josh has taken the 5th on that statement.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Matt is a partner and founder of Hutchinson & Webster. He grew up in Columbus and Galloway right here in central Ohio where he graduated from Westland High School. A bachelors of science in mechanical engineering from Case Western Reserve University propelled him to success in the aerospace and power generation industry.

While a student at Case Western Matt worked as a mechanical engineer intern and coop with Ward Engineering in Columbus, Alcoa in Cleveland, and Parker Hannifin in Phoenix. Following his engineering degree Matt was a mechanical engineer and project manager at Parker Hannifin in South Carolina, manufacturing fuel nozzles for gas turbine engines. Matt was awarded a masters degree in business administration from Capital University. While working toward his M.B.A., he completed a year long project with the Economic and Community Development Institute providing local entrepreneurs with marketing and business advice about their start-up companies.

He received his juris doctorate from Capital University Law School. While in law school he worked as a law clerk, at the Ohio House of Representatives for the Minority Legal Counsel and a state representative, and in the Legal Research Department at the Ohio Industrial Commission. He also worked in Capital’s law library throughout his three years of law school. Matt now lives in central Ohio with his wife and son, and is dedicated to serving H&W’s clients’ needs. Matt is admitted to practice in the state of Ohio. Additionally, he serves as of-counsel attorney to the firm of Wildman & Associates, LLC in London, Ohio.

While I entered law school with hopes of practicing environmental law, I began my legal career in St. Louis, Missouri, working for Brown & James PC, a large regional firm, in its construction law and toxic tort departments. From there, I joined a national firm, Polsinelli PC, primarily focusing on business litigation, telecommunications law, and trademark disputes in state and federal courts. Working in St. Louis, Missouri, and Overland Park, Kansas, I obtained law licenses in Missouri, Illinois, and Kansas. After working full time as a litigation attorney, I made the decision to scale back from hours and spend time with my growing family. I worked part-time for an attorney who mentored me most of my career and worked for him until he was confirmed as a U.S. District Court Judge for the Eastern District of Missouri.

Life brought me to Cleveland, Ohio, and good fortune introduced me to The Becker Law Firm. I am licensed to practice law in Ohio and I am honored to be working with the attorneys at The Becker Law Firm while we advocate for our clients who have suffered devastating losses from catastrophic injuries, birth injuries, and medical negligence. Working for our clients brings more meaning to my legal career than I have ever had – I believe The Becker Law Firm fights the good fight.

Outside of the firm, I spend my time raising my two sets of twins – one boy and three girls – and driving them to and from practices and games. For fun, I teach group exercise classes, binge watch Netflix with my children, and every so often find time to sit down with a good book.

attorneys.name: Kyleigh A. Weinfurtner
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Kyleigh Weinfurtner is the Managing Partner of Zashin Law. Her practice is focused on strategically navigating clients through all areas of family law matters.

Kyleigh has a particular strength in handling matters involving complex financials, such as executive compensation, business valuations and diversified investments. Her experience and knowledge in these matters allow her to comprehensively advise clients, whether representing the participant or the spouse. Kyleigh has handled a variety of financially complex matters, including, estates in excess of $500M, compensation and estates of professional athletes, business valuations of publicly and privately held interests, tracing premarital assets, and determining the fair market value of contracts pertaining to executive compensation. In addition to her sophisticated knowledge of finances, Kyleigh also focuses her practice on challenging parenting matters. She has successfully litigated matters of parental alienation to terminate a parent’s rights to custody and parenting time. Kyleigh does not shy away from litigation but preaches strategy over reaction in the handling of matters.

Kyleigh is frequently sought after to lecture at continuing education seminars on various topics. She was appointed as an Adjunct Professor of Law at Case Western Reserve University in 2020 and enjoys the opportunity to work with future professionals.

Kyleigh and her family enjoy life in a small township, prioritizing their time together and all things sports. She is an avid fan of her beloved New York Giants, a season ticket holder for the Cavs and has an inherited passion for the Tribe. She loves hosting friends and family and cooking far more food than appropriate. She has an extensive bourbon collection and can frequently be found playing golf with her husband.

attorneys.name: Michael D. Weisensel
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Lebanon, OH
attorneys.bio:
Driven Advocacy for the Injured

Michael Weisensel has dedicated over two decades of his legal career to one mission: leveling the playing field for the "little guy." With a career defined by an aggressive stance against powerful insurance corporations and their legal teams, Mike has successfully represented thousands of individuals who have suffered life-altering injuries due to the negligence of others.

Proven Litigation Excellence

Mike’s extensive courtroom experience sets him apart in the field of personal injury. He has served as lead counsel in dozens of first-chair jury trials and has navigated countless contested hearings, securing tens of millions of dollars in settlements and verdicts for his clients. His practice is comprehensive, encompassing high-stakes cases involving:

Wrongful Death & Catastrophic Loss

Commercial Trucking & Motor Vehicle Accidents

Complex Premises Liability & Dog Bite Litigation

Strategic Leadership & Client-First Approach

Before joining Rittgers Rittgers & Nakajima, Mike served as the Managing Attorney for the Dayton office of a prominent regional personal injury firm. While he excelled in high-volume environments, Mike transitioned to Rittgers Rittgers & Nakajima to return to his roots: hands-on, individualized representation. By maintaining a selective caseload, he ensures that every client receives the rigorous attention, investigative resources, and strategic planning their case deserve.

Academic Foundation & Community Roots

A native of Rochester, New York, and the son of a firefighter and a schoolteacher, Mike was raised with a deep-seated respect for public service and hard work. He earned his Bachelor of Science, cum laude, from the State University of New York at Brockport in 1992, followed by his Juris Doctor from the University of Akron School of Law in 1996.

Personal Life

Outside of the courtroom, Mike is a proud resident of Southwest Ohio. He is a devoted cheerleader to his three college-aged children, an avid traveler and loves to read. A lifelong enthusiast of his childhood sports teams, he is a vocal and resilient Buffalo Bills fan who cherishes game days as a time to connect with family and friends.

attorneys.name: John C. Weisensell
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
John C. ("Jack") Weisensell is licensed to practice law in Ohio, Florida, the United States District Courts for the Northern District of Ohio, Southern District of Ohio, Eastern District of Michigan, and Northern District of Illinois, the United States Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States Supreme Court.

Jack graduated from The College of Wooster in 1981 and from The Cleveland-Marshall College of Law at Cleveland State University in 1985. Following graduation from Cleveland State, Jack accepted a position as a law clerk to the Honorable Paul C. Weick with the United States Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals.

After completion of his one year term with the Sixth Circuit, Jack took a position with Amer Cunningham Brennan, Co., LPA and remained at the firm for eighteen years earning partner status in 1994.

In 2004, Jack left Amer Cunningham to join the firm that is now Weisensel & Corgan, LLC. Jack's practice has been primarily focused on civil litigation and appellate practice, in both state and federal courts. He has tried personal injury, medical malpractice, and commercial litigation matters in dozens of counties in the State of Ohio as well as many other states.

Notably, Jack briefed, argued, and won a case in the United States Supreme Court. He is Board Certified in Civil Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy. Jack is recognized as an Ohio "Superlawyer", a peer reviewed recognition, and he has had that designation for several years now. Jack is also a member of Litigation Counsel of America, a close-knit, peer-selected, and aggressively diverse honorary society of 3,500 of the best trial lawyers you will find anywhere. Less than one-half of one percent of American lawyers, vigorously vetted for skills, expertise, and service; an invitation-only collegial network of lawyers who effectively represent clients across North America and around the world. He is also a member of The National Trial Lawyers Top 100, and he has an AV rating by Martindale-Hubbell meaning that he has reached the highest level of professional excellence and is recognized for the highest level of skill and integrity

Jack has also lectured both locally and statewide on issues related to trial tactics and ethics. He has also authored for Ohio Trial and has been guest legal commentator on radio shows in Cleveland, OH, Akron, OH and on Long Island.

Jack has served as President of the Akron Bar Association, President of the Summit County Trial Lawyers Association nka Summit County Association for Justice, and has served on the Board of Trustees of the Ohio Academy of Trial Lawyers, the Akron Bar Association, and the Akron Bar Foundation.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Ethan A. Welch is committed to helping families with vulnerable loved ones preserve their resources and plan for the years ahead. His primary areas of focus are elder law, Medicaid planning, and special needs planning. He also practices in the associated areas of estate planning, trust and estate administration, and probate. Ethan's extensive knowledge of elder law and special needs planning ensures that his clients' rights are protected. His compassion and understanding bring his clients peace of mind, and his experience guides them in finding unique solutions as they plan for their future.

Ethan is a member of The National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys (NAELA), the Ohio State Bar Association, and the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association. He is also a board member and the Treasurer of Council Gardens, an affordable senior housing facility located in Cleveland Heights, Ohio. He finds his work with this organization very rewarding and feels privileged to serve older adults in our community. Ethan graduated magna cum laude from Bowling Green State University and received his law degree from Ohio Northern University.

Ethan, his wife and two daughters live in Brecksville, Ohio. Avid sports fans, they enjoy cheering on all Cleveland area teams and exploring the Cuyahoga Valley National Park.

attorneys.bio: Jack Welsch is an attorney and Certified Professional Environmental Auditor (CPEA). He has 20 years of experience working with environmental, health, and safety issues in both the private and public sectors. He has participated in and led EHS audit teams in a wide variety of industries including: chemicals manufacturing, food processing, electronics assembly, consumer products, administrative offices and others. Jack has had considerable international experience. In addition to living and working in Belgium for two years, he has been involved in audit projects in Brazil, Canada, Chile, Egypt, Germany, India, Kenya, and Russia. Prior to joining Goldenberg Schneider, Mr. Welsch managed the Washington, DC office of Enhesa, leading its auditing and environmental consulting practice in North America. He has also served as an Enforcement Specialist with the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality and as EHS Regulatory Counsel for Stateside Associates. Mr. Welsch holds a Juris Doctor and Masters Degree in Environmental Law from Vermont Law School and a BS in Environmental Biology from Ohio University.

attorneys.name: Blanca N. Wheeler
attorneys.practice_type: Tax Lawyers in Toledo, OH
attorneys.bio:
Blanca N. Wheeler is a senior member and owner attorney at Mockensturm, Ltd., focusing on business, collections, litigation, and tax law.

Blanca graduated magna cum laude from the University of Toledo College of Law, finishing in the top 13% of her class. During her studies, she earned honors from The Order of Barristers and was recognized as the Best Oralist at the BFSU-Wanhuida Intellectual Property Moot Court Competition in Beijing, China. She also served as a teaching assistant for Contracts 1 and competed in several moot court competitions, including Criminal Law Moot Court and the Attorney General of Ohio Public Service Mock Trial Competition. Additionally, she participated in Law Review for two years as both an Associate Member and Contributing Symposium Editor. Blanca holds a Bachelor of Arts in social psychology from Dartmouth College and a Master’s in Liberal Studies from the University of Toledo.

With over 18 years of experience at the Wood County Department of Job and Family Services specializing in Fraud and Investigations, Blanca has also worked at the Ohio Attorney General's Office and the Civil Advocacy Clinic at the University of Toledo.

Fluent in Spanish and conversant in French, Blanca actively participates in TBA committees and serves on the boards of various organizations. She regularly engages in panel discussions at UT Law events, such as the Launch Into Law and Practice-Area Speed Networking, where she shares insights about her practice with law students.

Blanca finds great fulfillment in her work as an attorney, particularly in helping clients navigate difficult situations. She is passionate about providing solutions that empower her clients. She takes pride in her ability to simplify complex legal issues and advocate for her clients’ needs, ensuring they feel supported and informed throughout the process.

In her free time, Blanca loves spending quality moments with her family. She has a passion for art history and enjoys exploring different cultures through their art, food, and music, which fuels her love for traveling to various countries.

attorneys.name: Terrence T. Wheeler
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Columbus, OH
attorneys.bio:
Terry Wheeler is a partner of the law firm and has been licensed to practice law since November 4, 1985. Terry began his career as a staff attorney for the Franklin County Municipal Court, then joined the Ohio Commission on Dispute Resolution & Conflict Management as associate director, and then became a director for the Center for Dispute Resolution at Capital University Law School. Terry joined ADW in June 2001 and became a partner on January 1, 2009. Since joining ADW, Terry practices law primarily in the areas of employment, criminal, and civil litigation. He also serves as a mediator.

Terry continues his involvement with dispute resolution at Capital University Law School by serving as a director for the Center for Dispute Resolution and adjunct professor of law teaching negotiation, mediation and mediation clinic. He serves as an adjunct professor for the Mortiz College of Law at The Ohio State University.

Terry is a former president of the board for the Association for Conflict Resolution. He has been mediating since 1983 and has been actively involved in the development of the Uniform Mediation Act and the Model Standards of Conduct for Mediators, as well as many other state and national initiatives. In addition, to teaching and training, Terry serves as a private mediator.

Hi, my name is Catherine M. White. Not only am I an attorney, but I am a wife to my wonderful husband who I have shared the past 20 years (plus) of my life with. I have 5 beautiful children and you can often find me watching one of their sporting events out in my community.

There are many things in life I enjoy; however one thing I really love is my work. I spend my days helping people - real people with real everyday problems.

When you come to me, you are probably facing one of the most difficult moments in your life. You may be overwealmed and confused. Your child may be in trouble; your marriage may be in trouble. One thing you can count on is that you do not have to face these circumstances alone. You can come see me and know that you can expect real, honest guidance and representation.

I practice law because it is what I love to do. It is a priviledge to have the honor to step into someones life and assist them with their legal issues. I went to law school later in life to do just that - to help people. Together, we will work to solve your problems effectively and affordably.

attorneys.name: Maury White Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Collaborative Law Lawyers in Mason, OH
attorneys.bio:
Maury White, JD, is certified by the Ohio State Bar Association as a Specialist in Family Relations Law. Maury earned his degree of Bachelor of Science in Commerce at the University of Virginia in 1975, and his law degree at the University of Cincinnati in 1978. Maury's practice is limited to Mediation and Collaborative Law. Maury's professional leadership roles have included chairmanship of the Cincinnati Academy of Collaborative Professionals 2006-2008; and chair of the Ohio Supreme Court's Sub-committee on Alternative Dispute Resolution: Collaborative Law. Maury has presented on Collaborative Family Law at the Ohio State Bar Association, and has been published in Thomson Reuters' Inside the Minds series, "Understanding Collaborative Family Law"; the World of Collaborative Practice magazine; and, the Ohio Association of Civil Trail Attorneys' Quarterly Review, Volume 5, summer 2012. With fellow Ohio IACP members Elaine Buck, Esq. (Columbus, Ohio) and Brian Urban, Esq. (Cleveland, Ohio) Maury was instrumental in attaining passage of the Ohio Collaborative Family Law Act, Ohio Revised Code Sections 3105.41 to 3105.54, eff. March 22, 2013. He is listed in Martindale Hubbell's Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers with their highest AV-rating in legal ability and ethical standards, as well as Best Lawyers in America for Collaborative Law.

attorneys.name: Margaret Whitmore
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Euclid, OH
attorneys.bio:
Winning Trial Victories for Clients Through Impeccable Organization and Skilled Case-Building

Margaret Whitmore-Ribeiro is a Senior Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation. A self-starter, highly organized, a fast thinker, and an expert strategist in case-building, Margaret constructs winning trial arguments through her in-depth knowledge of the nuances of medicine and workplace injuries. With her ever-present interest in people, their stories, and how she can find the best possible way to represent them, Margaret fulfills an essential role on the NRS Injury Law team.

Building on a Background in Medical Law

Margaret developed a rich understanding of her chosen field at a young age, which empowered her to achieve notable trial victories early on. In fact, Margaret began preparing for a career helping injured workers before she joined NRS Injury Law. While in college, she was a legal extern in the Compliance & Ethics Department at University Hospitals. She earned a Certificate in Health Law from Cleveland-Marshall’s Center for Health Law & Policy and was given an ABA-BNA Award for Excellence in Health Law.

After law school, Margaret worked at a small firm in Fairview Park, Ohio, where she developed skills in multiple legal areas, including personal injury, nursing home negligence, wills, trusts, and estate planning and administration. When she came to NRS Injury Law in 2018, Margaret’s in-depth knowledge of medicine as it pertains to injury law made her a perfect fit as a workers’ compensation plaintiff attorney.

“I spent much of my youth shadowing a prominent personal injury attorney who I happened to babysit for,” Margaret said, taking us back even further to her teen years. “Despite having no one in my family in the legal profession or anyone around me who was even all that familiar with the field, that attorney took me under his wing and showed me the ins and outs of personal injury law. He also showed me that attorneys can be kind, genuine, affable, charismatic, and empathetic and still be very good at their job.”

Working with the NRS Injury Law Team to Produce Results for Clients

Drawn to trial work and an expert litigator, Margaret credits the structure of the NRS Injury Law firm with the results she and other attorneys are able to secure in court. “Workers’ comp is more than just a hearing,” Margaret says. “Each case has numerous aspects and administrative details. Lots of firms either won’t handle workers’ compensation cases because of that, or they’ll only take on certain cases. NRS Injury Law is the largest workers’ comp firm in the state, empowering their attorneys with the resources, support structure, assistants, medical experts, research potential, evidence-gathering help, and colleague advice they need to build winning cases.”

Beyond the teamwork approach that NRS Injury Law is known for, Margaret also credits the firm’s ability to loop clients in as a part of its formula for success. “We at the firm are encouraged to fully bring clients in and make them a part of the team,” Margaret says. “We (the clients and their attorneys) are in this together, and the best cases are built with clients who feel like they’re a part of the process. We build great cases together because the firm encourages us to bring clients up-to-date, inform them, and coach them on what they must do to maximize their results. NRS Injury Law is unique in its inclusion of clients to this degree.”

Work/Life Balance

Margaret and her husband have put down roots and started a family in Lorain County, so Margaret’s time away from work is usually spent managing the home, planning childcare, and accomplishing essential tasks. During her free time, Margaret enjoys running, exercising, taking yoga classes, and visiting her parents and seven siblings.

Don't Wait to Seek Legal Help from Margaret Whitmore-Ribeiro

From her day-to-day work ethic in the office to her relentless advocacy for injured workers in court, Margaret’s core commitments and professional values align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with Margaret and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

A young mother, dedicated daughter, and an active, present sister to her seven siblings, Margaret still manages to set aside time to give back to her community. She helps improve the legal landscape for injured Ohio workers through her membership in the Ohio State Bar Association and the Ohio Association for Justice, and she is a superb team player at NRS Injury Law. For example, Margaret takes every opportunity to train new staff and answer any questions the legal assistants, paralegals, and case managers may have.

Awards and Honors

Honors

Super Lawyers: Rising Star (2024 – 2025)

attorneys.name: Ian Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Ian is a very reputable and respected attorney in the Northern Kentucky/Greater Cincinnati Area. His practice focuses on all-things civil litigation -- primarily car accidents, trucking accidents, dog bite, and catastrophic injury cases. His passion is helping those who are hurt and injured while going about their every-day life, and he is dedicated to working with people who do not have access to or experience with the legal process. He believes that by putting his client's needs first, he can effectively recover what his clients are due and owed. In addition to personal injury, Ian counsels people who do not get a fair cut when dealing with big insurance companies and corporations.

As one of the fastest up-and-coming attorneys in the personal injury world, Ian easily passed the universal bar exam in July 2024. He graduated from Chase College of Law with a wide array of skills and experiences making him a fierce advocate, counselor, and trial attorney. At Chase, Ian founded the intellectual property club, and he has written numerous critical analyses on various topics ranging from animal attack laws to the intricacies of federal and state privacy laws. He has been immensely successful in the courtroom and is active in numerous professional organizations, soaking up the advice and testimonies from other successful, seasoned attorneys.

Outside of the courtroom, Ian loves to play, learn, and stay active. He is constantly trying a new recipe, going out for a hike, working in his yard, or exploring events and festivals around Kentucky and Ohio. Ian plays soccer and pickleball all the time, and as a Kentucky native, he is a huge University of Kentucky basketball fan. He also has become a big FC Cincinnati fan and enjoys watching the Bengals (sometimes). Ian considers himself a life-long student, and he loves learning a new subject and refining the skills he already has. He is confident that having a well-rounded life will make him the best advocate for his community.

Best Lawyers 2009 Toledo Personal Injury Litigator of the Year Marty Williams

Best Lawyers, the oldest and most respected peer-review publication in the legal profession, has named Martin W. Williams as the Toledo Best Lawyers Personal Injury Litigator of the Year for 2009.

After more than a quarter of a century in publication, Best Lawyers is designating Lawyers of the Year in high-profile legal specialties in large legal communities.

These specialties are Banking Law, Bet-the-Company Litigation, Corporate Law, Family Law, Personal Injury Litigation, and Real Estate Law and only a single lawyer in each specialty in each community is being honored as the Lawyer of the Year.

Best Lawyers compiles its lists of outstanding attorneys by conducting exhaustive peer-review surveys in which thousands of leading lawyers confidentially evaluate their professional peers. The current, 15th edition of The Best Lawyers in America (2009), is based on more than 2.5 million detailed evaluations of lawyers by other lawyers.

The lawyers being honored as Lawyers of the Year have received particularly high ratings in our surveys by earning a high level of respect among their peers for their abilities, professionalism, and integrity.

Steven Naifeh, Managing Editor of Best Lawyers, says, We continue to believe as we have believed for more than 25 years that recognition by one's peers is the most meaningful form of praise in the legal profession. We would like to congratulate Martin W. Williams on being selected as the Toledo Best Lawyers Personal Injury Litigator of the Year' for 2009.

With warm regards,

Steven Naifeh

attorneys.name: Riley A. Williams
attorneys.firm_name: Hickman Lowder Lidrbauch & Welch Co., L.P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Special Needs Estate Planning Lawyers in Independence, OH
attorneys.bio:
Attorney Riley A. Williams has always been inspired to help vulnerable individuals, especially those who may be overlooked and in greatest need of assistance. She joined the firm as an attorney in October 2024 and will concentrate her practice on special needs estate planning and asset protection as well as Elder Law, including Medicaid planning, guardianship, and trust and estate administration.

Riley has been a dedicated law clerk at Hickman Lowder since April 2023, with a specialized focus on special needs estate planning. Drawing from a unique background in caregiving, Riley brings a compassionate and understanding perspective to her work, having worked closely with children and families with both behavioral and academic challenges. This experience drives her commitment to helping families to collaboratively design comprehensive plans that protect their loved ones and ensure financial stability. At Hickman Lowder, Riley is passionate about empowering clients to make informed choices for a well-protected, secure future.

Riley earned her law degree in 2024 from Cleveland State University College of Law, where she was a member of the Health Law Society and the Women’s Law Student Association. She graduated from Ohio University in 2021 with a Bachelor’s of Science degree.

Riley lives in Strongsville, Ohio and enjoys spending time with family and friends, traveling, baking, trying new foods and restaurants, and watching Cleveland sports.

attorneys.name: Mark C. Willis
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
Since the beginning of my legal career, I have dedicated my skills to obtaining justice for injured individuals and families. My typical client finds his or her life turned upside down as a result of someone else's carelessness, negligence, recklessness, or greed. Injuries are not always just a physical component. Often they create financial and emotional stress as well.

I have successfully represented clients against insurance companies, banks, mortgage companies, real estate companies, trucking companies, Fortune 500 companies and local businesses as well as other individuals. I have been on the cutting edge of obtaining insurance coverage for clients where insurance companies have claimed no coverage existed. I have had success in making insurance companies pay more than they claim they have in coverage. I have had success against these interests at the Common Pleas, Appellate, and Supreme Court levels. Obtaining justice for clients against the insurance industry and other big business interests has always been rewarding. With over 20 years experience in litigating cases, I have the experience and the resources to obtain justice for my clients.

I graduated from high school in rural West Virginia and went on to college in West Virginia. I moved to Akron, Ohio in 1983 to attend law school. I began working at age 13 and by the age 17, I was working full-time. I worked full-time the remainder of high school and all the way through college and law school. I have always had a strong work ethic and I work hard for my clients.

attorneys.name: Matthew R. Wilson Esq.
attorneys.bio:
Matthew R. Wilson is a principal with the firm.

Matt Wilson prosecutes the firm's class action cases. He serves as counsel for certified and putative classes in cases pending throughout the country involving defective products, privacy of medical information, violations of the federal telephone consumer protection statute ("TCPA"), mortgage problems, securities fraud, and deceptive advertising.

Recently, Matt has been court-appointed class counsel in numerous cases across the country in which the defendants were alleged to have made unauthorized calls and sent text messages to cellular telephones through the use of an automated telephone dialing system and/or an artificial or pre-recorded voice, in violation of the TCPA. The TCPA class settlements - over the last four years alone - in which Matt has been class counsel total over $200 million in cash for consumers.

Several of Matt's cases have resulted in nationwide settlements for consumers that are among the largest since the TCPA was enacted in 1991, including In re: Capital One Telephone Consumer Protection Act Litigation, 1:12-cv-10064 (N.D. Ill.) ($75.5 million - largest all-cash TCPA class settlement) (final approval granted February, 2015); Wilkins v. HSBC Bank Nevada, N.A. et al., 1:14-cv-00190 (N.D. Ill.) ($39.9 million - third-largest all-cash TCPA class settlement); Rose v. Bank of America Corp., 5:11-cv-02390-EJD (N.D. Cal.) ($32 million - largest all-cash TCPA class settlement at the time final approval was granted in 2014); and Arthur, et al. v. Sallie Mae, Inc., No. 10-cv-198-JLR (W.D. Wash.) ($24.15 million - largest all-cash TCPA class settlement at the time final approval was granted).

In another recent matter, Matt was co-lead counsel in Yarger v. ING Bank, fsb, 1:11-cv-00154-LPS (D. Del.), representing consumers who alleged that ING breached its promise to allow them to refinance their home mortgages for a fixed flat fee of $500 or $750, and instead charged a higher fee. In 2012, the court certified a class of consumers in ten states who purchased or retained an ING adjustable rate mortgage. In October 2014, the court approved a $20.35 million all-cash class settlement.

Before joining Meyer Wilson Werning in 2006, Matt spent four years with the international law firm Jones Day, and two years prior to that with Vorys, Sater, Seymour & Pease LLP. During those six years, he defended many of the world's largest corporations in class actions, wage and hour collective actions, and a wide variety of other types of complex civil litigation.

Matt graduated magna cum laude, Phi Beta Kappa, in Philosophy from Denison University in Granville, Ohio. He received his law degree from the University of Virginia Law School in Charlottesville, Virginia. Matt is admitted to practice in the courts of California and Ohio; the Sixth, Seventh, and Ninth Circuit Courts of Appeals; the Northern and Southern Districts of Ohio; the Central and Northern Districts of Illinois; the Central, Eastern, Northern, and Southern Districts of California; and the Eastern and Western Districts of Wisconsin.

Since 2007, Matt has been the chair of the Central Ohio Association for Justice Class Action Committee, and he is a member of the Class Action Preservation Project Committee with Public Justice. He is frequent speaker on class action law and practice.

attorneys.name: Andrew J. Winkel
attorneys.practice_type: State and Local Tax Issues Lawyers in Westerville, OH
attorneys.bio:
My practice involves assisting clients with state and local tax issues, audit defense and tax appeals, real property valuation & exemption, and matters of state and local governmental law, including the representation of the firm’s municipal clients. I strive to provide clients with legal guidance that draws upon my experience working within the legislative and administrative processes of state and local governments. I pride myself on distilling, describing, and discussing complex matters in a practical and understandable way that enables my clients to choose the approach that results in the best possible legal outcome for them.

I have worked in multiple roles where I collaborated with elected and appointed officials on high-profile legal, administrative, and legislative matters. Prior to coming to Metz, Bailey & McLoughlin, I led the Ohio Department Taxation’s (ODT) Division of Tax Equalization and worked closely with county auditors and local taxing authorities to ensure that real property in Ohio was accurately and uniformly valued, levied, and exempted. Before working in the Division of Tax Equalization, I led a team of attorneys who were responsible for handling the administrative appeals for nearly every major tax that ODT administers and consulted with Ohio Attorney General’s Office on appeals before the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals and the Ohio Supreme Court. I have also worked as an aide in the Ohio Senate and ODT’s Legislative Affairs & Legal Divisions where I drafted administrative rules and legislation and developed strategies to successfully advance them.

I have also served on Bexley’s Board of Tax Review and presented multiple times at the Ohio’s Annual Tax Conference as well as before the County Auditors Association of Ohio and County Commissioners Association.

A few personal facts: My wife, Jaime, and I have a son (9) & daughter (7); I coach multiple youth sports teams, including football, lacrosse, baseball, and basketball, and, while we don’t always win or elevate scholarship-chances or draft stocks, the kids learn fundamentals, teamwork, and make friendships; I lead my daughters 1st Grade Daisy Troop; I was a Disc-Jockey and Board Manager at WOUB in Athens, Ohio.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey T. Witschey
attorneys.practice_type: Alternative Dispute Resolution Lawyers in Akron, OH
attorneys.bio:
Jeff takes on the firm’s litigation matters for its regular clients and clients of other law firms who often refer Jeff their litigation matters. In his role as a litigator, Jeff handles litigation matters in the real estate and business settings. Matters range from zoning and land use disputes to complex litigation in business, trade secret, and partnership breakup matters. He practices in both state and federal courts. He also focuses on related appellate work. Jeff’s accomplishments include a jury award of $5.5 Million along with recovery of his client’s attorney fees in excess of $2 Million after a 6-week jury trial. In another matter he secured a settlement returning a $37 Million Dollar facility back to a local government.

Jeff balances the stresses of litigation with a diverse background in business and real estate transactional law. In this part of his practice he focuses on business start-ups, mergers, acquisitions, risk management, and strategic planning. His litigation experience informs his transactional work helping clients prepare contracts and business transactions that are as litigation proof as possible and his transactional work informs his business litigation practice allowing insights to client cases that most trial lawyers do not have.

Jeff is a graduate of Bowling Green State University and the University of Akron School of law where he graduated cum laude and was an excelling member of its nationally recognized mock trial team. He is a member of the United States Supreme Court Bar, the Northern District of Ohio Bar, the Ohio State Bar, the Akron Bar, and the Medina County Bar. He has been selected by his peers as an "Ohio Super Lawyer" in litigation practice by Law & Politics Magazine and Cincinnati Magazine/Cleveland Magazine.

Jeff is a native of Wadsworth, Ohio, is active in his local community, and serves on the board for St. Genevieve’s Church located in Holmes County and named an Ohio historical landmark. He is a contributing member of the Akron Bar Foundation. He now lives in Sharon Township where he and his wife Elianna have focused on raising their three children. He and his wife enjoy their children’s activities, the outdoors and traveling together to near and far away destinations.

attorneys.name: David Wolfram
attorneys.practice_type: Workers’ Compensation Law Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Drawing on a Diverse Legal and Professional Background to Help Injured Ohio Workers

David Wolfram is an Associate Attorney at NRS Injury Law, focusing on workers’ compensation law. Methodical, process-oriented, and possessing a knack for research, details, and case-building, David helps injured Ohio workers by crafting compelling, data-driven case strategies that result in injured workers obtaining the compensation they deserve.

Combining a Diverse Career Background in Helping Others via Workers’ Comp Law

After over two decades of serving in various corporate positions, David went to law school in his 40s to live out his ambition of becoming an attorney and giving back to others as others have helped him. His path into and through law school was influenced by his early years. “We experienced adversity when I was a child,” David said. “Some days it got so bad our utilities would be shut off. Thankfully, there were a lot of people in the community who helped us, and those experiences impacted me and planted the seed of being a service-minded person. Additionally, when my mother was injured at work, a workers’ comp attorney made a big difference in our lives. The attorney helped guide her through the process, advocated for the needed surgical treatment, and was the instrument to her getting her life back.”

David worked in the trades after graduating high school, then went on to become a first-generation college graduate. After building up an impressive resume in the business world, David watched as his mother went to college to achieve her degree in social work. Inspired, David returned to academia by attending law school, intent on entering the legal field to help others.

Leveraging a Mind for Research and a Knack for Strategy to Win Cases for Injured Workers

After working as a family law attorney, David now represents Ohioans injured in the line of work. He spends much of his time studying, researching, examining cases, and generating solutions based on his findings. Building on his background in business leadership roles, David knows how to craft a compelling strategy and execute it successfully. Bolstered by his deep empathy and ability to relate to injured workers in Ohio, David brings these skills and capacities to bear daily in his work for NRS Injury Law.

“The founding members are truly committed to helping others,” David said when asked why he took a job with the firm. “This firm embodies my values of helping others. It’s not a legal firm that operates as just another business. NRS Injury Law is a center of advocacy for injured workers in Ohio. The firm delivers the best possible service to its clients that it can, and thanks to the size of the firm, the dedication of its employees, and the resources it brings to bear, that service is above and beyond what most expect from a legal firm.”

Work/Life Balance

When he’s not representing injured workers as an attorney, David enjoys remodeling his home and finding other ways to work with his hands, be it on his projects or projects for community members. David also collects coins, reads, and studies new ways of solving problems. When the weather’s right, he enjoys exploring Cleveland Metroparks.

Don’t Wait to Seek Legal Help from David Wolfram

After taking numerous clinics in law school, competing in moot court, and excelling in client counseling competitions, David took the Universal Bar Exam (UBE) in 2022. He passed it on the first try, enabling him to practice law in any UBE jurisdiction. As a practicing attorney, David’s problem-solving and process-driven nature combined with his lifelong interest in helping people all align perfectly with NRS Injury Law’s mission to: “Provide empathetic and patient service to every person who calls the firm, and to relentlessly pursue the best possible outcome on behalf of every client by putting collective experience, knowledge, and passion to work every day.” To retain an effective legal team with a proven track record and to speak with David and the firm about your case, call 855-468-4878 or fill out a convenient online contact form.

Community Impact

Coming from an upbringing where the good graces of others were, at times, essential, David understands the importance of giving back. Before he became an attorney, David spent his free time volunteering at homeless shelters. David’s carpentry experience helped him immensely when volunteering on Habitat for Humanity projects. Today, David helps people with their home projects, and he assists others with brainstorming business and product ideas and strategies. Given his background in family law, he’s interested in philanthropic and volunteer activities that help others have better opportunities in life.

attorneys.name: Scott P. Wood
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Lancaster, OH
attorneys.bio:
A lifelong resident of Lancaster, Scott graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa from Ohio University, with a degree in Political Science, History, and Philosophy. He attended The Ohio State University College of Law, where he received his law degree, with honors, in 1994. While in law school, Scott was a member of The Ohio State Law Journal on Dispute Resolution and served as a judicial extern with Ohio Supreme Court Justice Craig Wright.

Scott is an experienced trial attorney and litigator, aggressively representing individuals accused of committing felonies, misdemeanors, traffic offenses and juvenile offenses. Scott also represents the rights of individuals who have been seriously injured and families who have suffered a wrongful death.

Scott is certified as a specialist in Criminal Trial Advocacy by the National Board of Trial Advocacy, and he is the only certified specialist in Fairfield County and only one of seven in the entire state of Ohio.

Scott has successfully argued two cases before the Supreme Court of Ohio on behalf of his clients and has tried over 100 jury trials in his career. He also is a certified criminal trial attorney by the Ohio Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Scott belongs to numerous professional associations and has served on and chaired numerous volunteer boards, including chairing the Fairfield County United Way Board of Review. He is a past president of the Fairfield County Bar Association and since 2012, Scott has been selected by his peers as one of the top lawyers in the State of Ohio by Super Lawyers and the National Trial Lawyers.

attorneys.name: Amy A. Wuliger
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Cleveland, OH
attorneys.bio:
Amy started the practice of law as a public defender in Washington, DC. Eventually, she branched out into civil practice, representing clients in both state and federal courts in a wide variety of matters including fraud, commercial and contract disputes, securities law, domestic relations, personal injury, and legal malpractice.

Amy was born in Cleveland and raised in Northeast Ohio by a single father – also a lawyer (and former public defender) – who taught her to always fight for the underdog with tenacity and persistence. After college, she moved to Washington, DC where she worked at a trade association promoting U.S. agricultural exports. Nevertheless, her fascination with the legal system never waned. She attended law school in the evenings at Georgetown University and, following in her father’s footsteps, became a public defender. She tried – and won – her first case just six weeks after being admitted to the DC Bar. In 2012, Amy left the Washington, DC metropolitan area and returned to Cleveland with her husband and three children. When she and her father decided to start their own firm in 2016, their vision was to create a full-service law firm with a “small firm” atmosphere.

Amy is an active member of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association and has served on several committees, including as past Chairman of the Ethics & Professionalism Committee. She has also written multiple articles for the local bar journal and been a speaker at numerous continuing legal education seminars.

Amy has extensive trial experience, both criminal and civil, and has participated in countless evidentiary hearings in federal and state courts located in Ohio, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Florida, and the District of Columbia. She has also handled dozens of cases in federal and state courts of appeals. Her efforts have contributed to the award of over $65 million in settlements and judgments for Wuliger & Wuliger’s clients.

Amy started the practice of law as a public defender in Washington, DC. Eventually, she branched out into civil practice, representing clients in both state and federal courts in a wide variety of matters including fraud, commercial and contract disputes, securities law, domestic relations, personal injury, and legal malpractice.

Amy was born in Cleveland and raised in Northeast Ohio by a single father – also a lawyer (and former public defender) – who taught her to always fight for the underdog with tenacity and persistence. After college, she moved to Washington, DC where she worked at a trade association promoting U.S. agricultural exports. Nevertheless, her fascination with the legal system never waned. She attended law school in the evenings at Georgetown University and, following in her father’s footsteps, became a public defender. She tried – and won – her first case just six weeks after being admitted to the DC Bar. In 2012, Amy left the Washington, DC metropolitan area and returned to Cleveland with her husband and three children. When she and her father decided to start their own firm in 2016, their vision was to create a full-service law firm with a “small firm” atmosphere.

Amy is an active member of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association and has served on several committees, including as past Chairman of the Ethics & Professionalism Committee. She has also written multiple articles for the local bar journal and been a speaker at numerous continuing legal education seminars.

Amy has extensive trial experience, both criminal and civil, and has participated in countless evidentiary hearings in federal and state courts located in Ohio, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Florida, and the District of Columbia. She has also handled dozens of cases in federal and state courts of appeals. Her efforts have contributed to the award of over $65 million in settlements and judgments for Wuliger & Wuliger’s clients.

attorneys.name: William S. Wyler
attorneys.practice_type: Intellectual Property Lawyers in Cincinnati, OH
attorneys.bio:
Bill Wyler moved his practice to Flagel and Papakirk in 2016, after more than 25 years at another firm, because of F&P's fast growing reputation as an outstanding law firm with a concentration on solving business related legal issues.

Bill's practice focuses on (1) the protection of intellectual property and (2) technology licensing and transfer. His protection of intellectual property practice includes registration and licensing of trademarks and copyrights; prosecution and defense of trademarks, trade secrets, and copyrights involving infringement and misappropriation claims, both administratively and in court; and in drafting, prosecuting and defending non-compete, non-solicitation and non-disclosure agreements.

His technology licensing and transfer practice includes drafting and negotiating, often complex, development, acquisition, licensing and hosting agreements. In each of these practice areas, Bill is a leader in the field, helping to develop the strategies and methods that are in common use today.

He has chaired both the Ohio State Bar Association Computer Law Committee and the Board of Governors of the Intellectual Property Section. He has also chaired the Cincinnati Bar Association Computer Law Committee. He has received an AV rating (the highest possible rating) from Martindale-Hubble, the rating service used most by lawyers, for 18 consecutive years. He has been named by American Lawyer Media, as a "Top Rated Lawyer in Intellectual Property," every year since 2013, and a "Top Rated Lawyer in Technology," every year since 2012. He has also previously been named a "Super Lawyer." He served for ten years on the Cincinnati Bar Association's grievance committee, which investigates attorney misconduct and makes recommendations for discipline to the Ohio Supreme Court.

He was appointed, by Chief Justice Thomas Moyer, to the Ohio Supreme Court's Advisory Committee on Court Technology and he served on the Board of the Center for Information Technology and the Law, which was a joint project of the University of Cincinnati College of Law and the School of Business. He taught Computer Law at both the University of Cincinnati College of Law and Salmon P. Chase College of Law. He is invited to speak regularly at both legal and business seminars.

He is admitted to practice law before the Supreme Court of the United States, all courts in the State of Ohio, the United States Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit, for the D.C. Circuit and for the Federal Circuit. He is also admitted to practice before the U.S. District Court of the Southern District of Ohio and the Eastern District of Kentucky.

attorneys.name: Melissa A. Yasinow
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mentor, OH
attorneys.bio:
Melissa Yasinow is a fierce advocate for her clients in all legal settings. Trained as a litigator, Melissa has successfully represented students in all manner of disciplinary proceedings across Ohio and the United States. Melissa’s experience includes defending students in Title IX investigations as well as proceedings concerning student misconduct, professionalism, and academic integrity. Her years of litigation experience complement Balin Law’s Social Security Disability practice, helping her to assess SSDI/SSI cases and other claims on behalf of our clients.

Melissa is particularly proud of her work defending students with disabilities, including Depression, ADHD, Anxiety, and Autism Spectrum Disorder.

Melissa’s experience includes:

Successfully appealed a fourth-year medical student’s dismissal from an Ohio public university for alleged academic underperformance.

Successfully defended an Ohio high school senior in a Title IX investigation after he had been suspended without due process.

Successfully defended a college senior against claims of sexual misconduct at a private college in New York.

Successfully resolved a sexual misconduct case at a New Jersey public university where both students had Autism Spectrum Disorder.

Successfully defended a pre-med student at a private Ohio university accused of cheating on a physics exam.

Successfully resolved a disciplinary matter ensuring that an Ohio high school sophomore could return to school and the soccer team after a mental health crisis.

Successfully appealed the suspension of an Ohio public university student from his pharmacy program after the university failed to provide mandatory due process.

Successfully appealed a sexual misconduct ruling against a rising senior at a public Indiana university.

Successfully resolved a disciplinary matter for a high school student after private writings were circulated without his knowledge or consent by former friends.

Successfully resolved a dispute between a dual-degree graduate student and an Ohio private university where the university had attempted to overbill the student and deny her shared-course credit.

Advised healthcare professional of her rights under the Public Student Loan Forgiveness Program and helped her get confirmation from her nonprofit employer that over $100,000 in student loans would be forgiven.

Secured disability-related housing accommodations for a visually impaired student at an Ohio public university after he had previously been denied requested housing.

Melissa is also proud to help individuals with disabilities in all legal settings, including before Social Security.

Civic Involvement

Melissa previously served as a Councilmember and Vice Mayor in the City of Cleveland Heights. When Melissa first joined Cleveland Heights City Council, she was the youngest ever elected official in the city’s history.

Melissa completed Ladder Down Cleveland (Class of 2021), Cleveland Bridge Builders (Class of 2019) and the Mandel Leadership Symposium (Class of 2017). She is also a past Board Member of the Anti-Defamation League in Cleveland.

Melissa is a member of the Cleveland Metropolitan Bar Association.

Honors & Awards

Melissa was recognized as a Top Rated Attorney 3 years in a row, making the Super Lawyers Rising Stars list in 2019, 2020, and 2021; an honor granted to no more than 2.5 percent of attorneys in the state.

Named one of the “Most Interesting People” by Cleveland Magazine in 2018 and “12 Under 36: Member of the Tribe,” by the Cleveland Jewish News in 2018.

Recipient of a Fulbright Grant to the Republic of Korea where she represented American interests from 2006 to 2007.
